News.title: Temperatures plunge to -6C on coldest night of the season as Brits wake up freezing and cold health alerts in place
News.content:
COLD SNAP Temperatures plunge to -6C on coldest night of the season as Brits wake up freezing and cold health alerts in place







Next

BRITS slept through the first cold snap of the season last night, with the mercury dropping to -6C and weather warnings blanketing the country.

The UK Health Security Agency issued a yellow cold health alert on Tuesday which is due to remain in place until midday on Saturday.



The warning covers the North West and West Midlands, with temperatures expected to drop below average by the end of the week.

Last night was the chilliest night of the season so far, with many waking up to frosted windscreens and icy morning walks, the Met Office said.



Pictures show parks coated in frost and fields covered in icy mists on Friday morning.

The public has been advised to check in on eldery relatives amid the cold snap, as health and cares services brace themselves for icy conditions.





People with pre-existing conditions and those sleeping rough are also particularly vulnerable, the UKHSA said.

Rural and frost-prone areas could see temperatures drop as far as -6C and -7C as the Arctic blast moves across the UK.

Despite frosty beginnings, Friday will largely remain dry with plenty of sunshine across England and Wales.

Some showery spells are expected near the North Sea coastline, and in the far north.



Tonight will see much of the nation blanketed in widespread frost again, turning cloudier in the south as the evening progresses.

Saturday will be largely dry, although cloudier than before, with some rain and hill snow expected in Scotland and showers hitting the southwest.



Dr Anya Gopfert, consultant in public health at UKHSA, said: “This is the first cold health alert of the winter, but we can expect more as we move further into the season.

“We’re reminding people to take simple steps to stay warm and look after their health as temperatures begin to fall.

“Keeping homes heated where possible and dressing warmly can help people stay safe and well during colder weather.”

The agency is urging people to heat rooms they spend most of their time in to at least 18C.

Draught excluders and tightly sealed windows are also recommended for keeping homes warm.



It is also suggested wearing multiple thin layers as opposed to a single thick layer.

As temperatures plunge, many Brits have been speculating about the possibility of snowfall.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Some weather experts have hinted at a severe cold snap, due to the effects of El Nino, a super-sized natural climate pattern originating in the Pacific.

It comes after the spiralling winds of the polar vortex high above the Arctic weakened and reversed, leading to colder conditions in the UK.

News.title: DC gunman made eerie remark about victim’s daily routine & chilling Luigi Mangione reference before deadly shooting
News.content:
Next

A CRAZED doctor who shot dead his building manager in a horror rampage chillingly revealed he knew his victim’s daily routine before the attack.

Matt Lambert, who opened fire inside a luxury Washington, DC, apartment building on Thursday, was previously locked in a bitter feud over his mold-infested $1.1 million penthouse.



During that dispute, he also made disturbing references to accused UnitedHealthcare CEO killer Luigi Mangione.

The gunman killed building manager James Stuart shortly after 8am inside a ground-floor gym before shooting four others and turning the gun on himself following an intense standoff with cops.



But chilling details have now emerged about Lambert’s behavior in the months leading up to the bloodbath, including an eerie exchange in which he revealed exactly when Stuart could be found at the gym.

“If you want to see the building manager he comes in the gym about 8 o’clock,” Lambert allegedly told another resident who was also waiting for repairs to his apartment.

The disturbing remark was revealed by journalist Michael Brice-Saddler, who had previously interviewed Lambert about his bitter battle with the homeowners’ association at the swanky Metropole building in Logan Circle.

Writing for The Washington Sun, Brice-Saddler also recalled how the doctor had invoked Mangione and the chilling words associated with the murder of UnitedHealthcare boss Brian Thompson.



“What are they called? Delay, deny, defend … the Luigi three?” Lambert reportedly asked the journalist during a conversation last December.

The phrase echoed the words inscribed on ammunition linked to Thompson’s December 2024 murder in Manhattan.

Lambert had also publicly referenced Mangione in an October 1 post on X while accusing his building’s management of dragging its feet over repairs.

“After months of ‘Luigi’ tactics (delay, deny, defend) by the HOA, we were finally able to submit an independent engineering report into the record,” he wrote.

“The report addresses 704, the facade rehabilitation more broadly , and lists other units affected. When the time is right, I will share the report on X, with other Metropole owners, and with Logan Circle realtors.”



The increasingly bitter dispute reportedly began after Lambert discovered black mold and other problems inside his seventh-floor home.

He sued the homeowners’ association last year, claiming the unresolved issues had turned his life upside down.

Speaking to Brice-Saddler in December, Lambert described the bitter legal battle as “psychological warfare.”



He claimed it had “affected every part of my life — my sleep, dietary habits.”

“I pride myself on my resilience, and I’ve been kind of surprised at how much it has been affected,” he said.

In another chilling exchange, Lambert referenced Sun Tzu’s famous military strategy book, The Art of War, while discussing his determination to continue fighting.



“Do I keep fighting? Do I not fight?” he questioned.

“And ‘The Art of War’ talks about, you know, the battle’s won before it’s ever fought.”

“It says if you’re going to commit, don’t half commit, fully commit,” he added.

The doctor also accused the building’s management of trying to financially ruin him.

“They’re trying to make me quit. They’re trying to make me go broke,” he claimed.



“If I come out of this and I don’t get a satisfactory outcome, I won’t have a bunch of money, but I can live with that better than rolling over. … They don’t have my permission to treat me this way.”

Just moments before Thursday’s bloodshed, Lambert posted a lengthy statement on X detailing his grievances with the building.

The apparent manifesto cited an engineering report describing “suspected microbial growth,” water intrusion and costly repairs needed to rehabilitate an exterior wall.

Shortly after 8am, Lambert allegedly entered the building’s Vida Fitness gym and fatally shot Stuart.

He then reportedly opened fire from his apartment balcony, wounding four other people – two men and two women – who were rushed to hospital.



Cops descended on the luxury complex, sparking an hour-long standoff with the gunman.

During the confrontation, Lambert reportedly continued ranting about his dispute with the homeowners’ association before fatally shooting himself inside his penthouse.

“There had been an ongoing dispute between the suspect in this case and the building homeowner’s association regarding maintenance issues [and] mold,” Metropolitan Police Department Interim Chief Jeffery Carroll confirmed at a Thursday press conference.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Carroll said Lambert had also spoken about “the HOA and challenges” with it during the standoff.

Police have not publicly established whether the chilling remarks made months earlier were connected to any plan to carry out the deadly attack.

News.title: Tragic details revealed after boy, 2, fell to death from window of Cyprus hotel – as dad spared jail over his death
News.content:
FATAL FALL Tragic details revealed after boy, 2, fell to death from window of Cyprus hotel – as dad spared jail over his death







Next

A TWO-year-old boy who fell to his death from a Cyprus hotel died from multiple severe injuries, an inquest heard today.

Jaxon Foster plunged nearly 40ft from the fourth-floor window of the five-star King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort.



His dad Joshua pleaded guilty to causing death by a rash, reckless or dangerous act and was spared jail.

Essex Coroner’s Court heard today Jaxon suffered fatal injuries to his head, vital organs and body in the horror on July 12.



His provisional cause of death was given as “severe craniocerebral injuries and multiple injuries of the body and vital organs” due to a fall from height.

Lincoln Brookes, Essex’s senior coroner, said it was a “particularly tragic” case.

Outlining the tragedy, he added: “This two-year-old child was on holiday with his family in Paphos in Cyprus.

“He sadly fell from a window on the fourth floor of the hotel the family were staying at and, sadly, his death was confirmed that same day at the hospital.”

The coroner adjourned the full inquest until January 6 as he offered his condolences to Jaxon’s family.

Foster’s sentencing hearing was told the dad had placed Jaxon on a windowsill to show him the view of a waterpark.



Tragically, he did not realise the window was open in what his lawyer called a “momentary error” with “fatal consequences”.

The Essex dad was arrested following the tragedy, which took place on a family holiday.

His lawyer had pleaded with the Cypriot Attorney General to have the case thrown out on humanitarian grounds – but the top official ruled it was to go ahead.

Foster spent eight days in jail and was forced to tell his young daughter about the tragedy over FaceTime.

He fought back tears as he was fined £2,500 at Paphos District Court last month.



District Judge Froso Christodoulidou said: “The window did not appear to carry markings that would necessarily have alerted the defendant to the fact that one section was open.”

She also found there was no evidence Foster “deliberately exposed the child to danger”.

In a statement, the family previously said: “Our son was deeply loved and will be forever missed.

“His loss is something we carry with us every day.”

News.title: At least six dead after eight-storey building collapses in Nairobi – as five pulled from the rubble during rescue op
News.content:
COLLAPSE TRAGEDY At least six dead after eight-storey building collapses in Nairobi – as five pulled from the rubble during rescue op







Next

AT least six people have been killed after an eight-storey building collapsed, crashing down on construction workers.

Workers are feared to be trapped under the rubble after the tower suddenly gave way.



Many remain missing, but five were pulled alive from the rubble after the horror collapse around 9.50am on Friday morning near Nairobi, Kenya.

Local official Bramwell Simiyu confirmed the deaths as rescuers scoured the site in Mlolongo for survivors.



He said: “Three bodies were retrieved during the initial morning operations, while three more were recovered later from the debris.

“All six victims were middle-aged men.”

It is not yet known how many people were working at the site at the time of the collapse.

All five workers rescued alive are were treated by paramedics.



The Kenyan Red Cross confirmed several were hospitalised.

Dramatic photos show twisted metal and workers searching desperately for their colleagues in the rubble.

The cause of the collapse is not yet clear, with preliminary reports from emergency teams suggesting its top slab gave way.



Authorities urged members of the public to keep away from the area, near Mombasa Road.

It comes after eight people were killed when another unfinished building violently collapsed in Kenya last month.

Shocking footage showed the 12-storey construction site catastrophically implode, with debris showering across the streets of Nairobi.

Terrified pedestrians could be seen running for their lives as a tsunami of dust swallowed everything in its path.

And days before that, another building collapsed in central Nairobi, sparking concern about construction practices in the Kenyan capital.



There had been 24 workers at the site, with four sustaining injuries.

Three received treatment at Kenyatta National Hospital, while all workers were eventually accounted for.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Building collapses are a recurring problem in Nairobi.

County officials responsible for issuing building permits have been accused of failing to conduct adequate inspections to ensure developers comply with safety guidelines and construction standards.

News.title: Furious Kemi slams ‘betrayal of women of Piddington’ after Labour push through migrant camp – as locals vow legal battle
News.content:
Next

KEMI Badenoch has blasted the “betrayal of the women of Piddington” after Labour pushed through plans for a controversial migrant camp.

Locals have vowed to launch a legal battle after the Government used emergency powers to green-light housing 1,250 foreign men in the Oxfordshire village.



In September, 285 villagers voted to leave the UK, with just 26 against and one spoiled ballot in a symbolic “independence” referendum.

Women told how they fear being attacked on their doorstep if the migrants, almost four times the local population, are moved nearby.



Angela Rayner yesterday green-lit plans to convert the ex-military base MoD Bicester, which is expected to cost an estimated £250 million.

And Mrs Badenoch has today slammed local government boss Ms Rayner for “betraying” women and girls in the picturesque hamlet.

The Tory leader wrote: “This is a betrayal of the women of Piddington, but emblematic of Labour and Angela Rayner’s disregard for the law and women and girls’ safety.

“When I visited Piddington I met a village terrified of what was about to land on their doorstep.



“The government said it was listening, instead it’s completely ignored this community’s concerns.

“The 1,000+ male migrants that Labour are about to deposit in Oxfordshire are in Britain illegally.

“They should be deported as soon as possible, not housed in areas completely unsuitable for the task.



“Only the Conservatives have a thorough plan to leave the ECHR and ensure that every illegal migrant is removed from our country as swiftly as possible.”

Parish council chairman Tim McNally warned ministers should “absolutely” be braced for a legal challenge.

There is now a six-week window in which the villagers can challenge the decision.

Mr McNally, who has been leading the campaign against converting the former RAF site, said he was “massively disappointed” by the decision.

The furious council boss fumed that any migrant sexual assaults in the tiny village will be on Andy Burnham’s head.



Speaking on Sun show Harry Cole Saves the West, he blasted: “I’m sorry, Andy Burnham, you’re responsible for this.

“If any sexual violence happens, it will be on your head.

“Andy Burnham, the great Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, has come out and basically accused the media industry of sexual assaults against women.

“And yet he’s actually giving the approval to open up a site from where we’re going to have a whole number of problems.”

Village officials previously estimated that male asylum migrants will outnumber women in Piddington by 10-1.



Fearful women in the area have resorted to self-defence lessons ahead of the influx of asylum seekers.

Ministers admitted residents at the camp will be free to roam the local area, but claimed small country lanes would hinder their movements.

After the independence vote, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he understood the “strength of feeling” displayed by residents.

Local mums told The Sun they would be too scared to take their children to the park if plans were approved — a fear that has now become reality.

However, local Conservative MP Greg Smith, from the neighbouring Mid-Buckinghamshire constituency, said that was nonsense.



“There are 11 villages in my constituency where it’s straightforwardly walking distance,” he told The Sun’s show.

The furious Tory added: “I’m genuinely scared for the safety of my constituents, particularly my female constituents.

“We’re talking about a cohort of people who even this government’s Home Office has deemed they have to give a leaflet to informing them that rape is not acceptable in the United Kingdom.

“And they’re going to be walking distance from my constituents.”

A Home Office spokesperson said: “Planning permission allows us to continue to progress the use of MoD Bicester.



“However, a final decision to proceed is yet to be taken.

“The Government is working on a fairer distribution of asylum accommodation across the country, with over £1 billion saved in costs since the election.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This includes closing all asylum hotels and moving to alternative accommodation, including former military sites.

“These are designed to be self-contained, with 24/7 security and CCTV, to minimise the impact on the local community.”

News.title: Mum, 35, and sons, 5 & 8, killed after truck driver ‘watching YouTube’ ploughs into car on way to airport
News.content:
FAMILY TRAGEDY Mum, 35, and sons, 5 & 8, killed after truck driver ‘watching YouTube’ ploughs into car on way to airport







Next

A MUM and her two sons were killed after a truck driver allegedly watching YouTube ploughed into their car on the way to the airport.

Olga Sorbalo, 35, and her boys Luis, eight, and Samir, four, died after their family minivan was struck from behind by a huge heavy-duty truck.



Her husband and their two-year-old son survived the deadly crash but were rushed to hospital with serious injuries.

Truck driver Eldar Skander, 39, has since been charged with three counts of first-degree involuntary manslaughter over the tragedy.



Investigators allegedly discovered a tablet lying on the floor of his cabin with the YouTube app open.

Cops also found Velcro on the back of the device which matched a strip attached to the truck’s dashboard.



The family, from Vancouver, Washington, had been visiting relatives in Kansas City and were heading to the airport to catch a flight home when disaster struck.

Their Honda Odyssey minivan was caught in slowing traffic on US Highway 71 on Monday, November 9, when the truck allegedly slammed into its rear.

Prosecutors revealed there was no evidence the trucker had attempted to brake before the deadly collision.

In a statement, the Jackson County Prosecutor’s Office said: “As vehicles were slowing and coming to a stop in traffic, the semi struck a black Honda Odyssey, causing a chain reaction.



“There were no signs of emergency braking by the semi.”

The force of the impact sent the family’s minivan crashing into a Honda CR-V, a Ford Explorer and a FedEx truck.

Both young boys were pronounced dead at the scene, while their mum later succumbed to her injuries in hospital.



Olga’s husband, Liviu, their youngest son and Liviu’s sister were also inside the vehicle when the truck struck.

All three suffered serious injuries and were rushed to hospital.

Two other motorists driving the Honda CR-V and Ford Explorer were also seriously hurt in the devastating pile-up.

The FedEx driver escaped the carnage unharmed.

Olga’s brother, Daniel Cosovan, described the family’s final moments before the crash.



He told local station KGW8: “They were stuck in traffic, and a truck hit them from the back at a high speed.”

A dashboard camera was also recovered from inside the vehicle and could hold crucial evidence of the fatal smash.

The probable cause statement reads: “Officers also located a dash camera inside the semi-truck cabin that may have captured the incident.”

Skander, from Chicago, Illinois, suffered minor injuries in the collision.

Authorities revealed he refused to speak to investigators after being discharged from hospital.



The 39-year-old is being held at Jackson County Detention Centre on a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainer, according to local outlets FOX4 KC, KMBC and KCTV.

A judge has set his bond at £114,000 ($150,000) cash only.

It remains unclear whether he has entered a plea or appointed a lawyer.

Meanwhile, the shattered family is facing the heartbreaking task of bringing Olga and her two sons home for their funerals.

Olga was the daughter of Alexei Cosovan, a church minister in Vancouver.



A GoFundMe page has been launched to help cover funeral costs and support her surviving husband as he battles to recover from his injuries.

The fundraiser reads: “Liviu Sorbalo lost his beloved wife and two precious young children. This heartbreaking loss has left their entire family, relatives, friends, and church community in deep sorrow.

“No amount of money can replace the lives that have been lost, but together we can help ease the financial burden and surround this family with love and care.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The couple’s youngest son has since recovered enough to return to Washington with relatives.

But his grieving father remains in hospital in Missouri, facing a “long road to physical recovery, requiring ongoing medical treatment and is expected to be unable to work for an extended period”.

News.title: Former MP, 37, facing jail after raping boy, 13, in car park toilet after meeting him on ‘adults-only’ website
News.content:
Next

A FORMER MP is facing jail after raping a 13-year-old boy in an underground car park toilet.

Australian politician Rory Amon, 37, met his victim on an “adults-only” website and arranged to meet believing the boy was at least 17 years old.



He was found guilty on Friday of one count of sexual intercourse with a person aged between 10 and 14 and indecently assaulting a child.

The court heard the pair exchanged explicit pictures before meeting in the carpark under the boy’s apartment block in 2017.



A police report was filed when the teen told a teacher about what had happened.

At the time he first contacted the teen, Amon was working for federal Mackellar MP Jason Falinski.



The politician claimed he thought the boy was 17.

Amon would go on to represent Pittwater in New South Wales, after serving two terms on Northern Beaches Council.

But he was expelled from the Liberal party and resigned as he was hit with charges in 2023.

Friday’s conviction was Amon’s second Supreme Court trial after another jury acquitted him on eight separate charges of child sexual offending in March.



All charges related to the same 13-year-old victim.

That jury had been unable to reach a verdict over the two counts he was convicted of on Friday.

In March, the court heard that the pair met on a gay dating app.

Amon said he was innocent of all charges.

He did not dispute sexual activity, but claimed he held an honest and reasonable belief the teen was over the age of 16.



The former politician has been allowed out on bail and is set to be sentenced on November 27.

Amon has become the third ex- New South Wales MP to be found guilty of sexual offences in recent years.

In 2025, former minister Gareth Ward was jailed for sexually abusing two young men.

His victims included a political staffer, who had been intoxicated after an event at Parliament House.

And in 2023, Milton Orkopoulos was convicted of sexually abusing teen boys while serving as a state Labor MP.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

He was found guilty of 26 charges of sexual offending against four underage boys as well as supplying them with drugs over the course of a decade.

News.title: Shocking moment thug kicks and strangles whimpering dog after branding terrified pooch a ‘f***ing p****’ in attack
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a thug kicked and strangled his whimpering dog in a brutal attack.

Kyle Menham, 27, was captured branding cane corso Zee a “f***ing little p****” as he lashed out in the kitchen of his home in Swindon, Wiltshire.



Vile footage showed him attempting to put Zee in a cage before booting the dog in the side and dragging him by his tail.

The terrified dog can be heard whimpering in pain as it cowers on the floor during the sick attack.



A relative saw the harrowing footage and alerted the RSPCA, who launched an urgent investigation.

Officers seized Zee and rehomed him while Menham was charged with animal welfare offences.

He has now been convicted of causing unnecessary suffering to his dog and was handed an 18 month community order.

Menham was also ordered to complete 200 hours unpaid work and pay £2,383.70 costs and £114 victim surcharge.

Swindon Crown Court heard Zee would have suffered “acute pain” by the kicks, as well as “intense fear and anxiety due to the violence directed at him”.

A vet said: “Zee can be seen to exhibit fearful body language in the manner in which he tries to escape around his owner following the kicks.



“Being dragged by the skin of the lower back and tail head would have been extremely painful.

“Zee can clearly be heard crying and whimpering in distress as he is pinned down to the floor while being shouted and sworn at.

“The owner can be heard shouting and swearing at Zee following the first kick and then again, even more aggressively, during the period he has pinned the dog to the floor.



“In my opinion this violence was avoidable and so the suffering was clearly unnecessary and that no reasonable dog owner would abuse their dog physically and verbally in this manner.”

The court heard Menham failed to seek veterinary attention for any injuries the dog may have suffered during the attack.

He was also banned from owning animals for five years.

Former RSPCA Inspector Steph Daly, who investigated for the animal welfare charity, said: “The footage shows what Zee experienced. No animal deserves to be kicked and slapped.

“We’d plead to all pet owners to always show animals kindness and to reach out for help and support if they are struggling with training or behavioural issues they feel need to be addressed.



“It’s never acceptable to lose your temper and take it out on a defenceless animal.”

News.title: Watch: 'I feel it's a sign of what's to come' - office workers on Microsoft disruption
News.content:
Microsoft users across the world are being affected by an outage to tools like Outlook, Teams and Copilot.

With more than 430 million people known to use the Microsoft product, the side effects will be far reaching.

BBC Radio 5 Live's Nicky Campbell spoke to two insurance brokers in London, who shared how their jobs had been interrupted by the outage.

News.title: Firm offers to fake artworks for wealthy migrants seeking UK 'talent' visas - BBC investigation
News.content:
Companies are offering to help migrants pose as talented artists and tech experts to make fraudulent UK visa applications under a fast-track immigration scheme, the BBC has found.

The UK government's Global Talent visa was launched in 2020 to attract the "brightest and best" scientists and researchers from around the world. It is also open to creative artists.

Following our investigation, the Home Office is now revoking visas issued to two Nigerian men who claimed to be fine art photographers, because it believes they were obtained by deception.

Applicants for Global Talent visas are not interviewed. People granted them need to prove they are exceptionally talented or promising in their field. They can then bring their families to the UK and there is a potentially quick path to permanent residency - in three or five years.

We have discovered that wealthy migrants looking to cheat the system are being offered fake art portfolios which they can pass off as their own work for a large fee.

A consultant from one company in London told our undercover reporter - who was posing as a potential client - that his firm could supply artwork produced in China, as well as arrange exhibitions, media coverage and letters of recommendation.

No clients taking the "fully inclusive" package - costing more than Â£100,000 - had ever been refused a Global Talent visa, he said.

In the case of the two Nigerian men, our investigation was alerted to apparently faked newspaper articles reviewing their artistic work.

A well-known Nigerian art critic told us her name had been attached to online reviews praising the work of the two seemingly obscure artists.

"There is a real problem whereupon fake articles are being implanted onto newspaper websites using bylines of reputable culture journalists," said Molara Wood.

News.title: Piddington to bring legal challenge over asylum base plans
News.content:
McNally told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that the village could also apply the new Hillsborough Law.

Once passed, the law would create a legally enforceable duty of candour which compels public officials and authorities to act transparently when investigations and inquiries take place.

McNally told the programme: "Last night, [Prime Minister] Andy Burnham was on a podium talking about the violence, sexual violence towards women, and bringing it upon the media industry as their responsibility to manage.

"But the reality is, is that this is exactly what the government is doing to us here."

Asked how the village would respond, he said: "There's going to be many actions, you will see. We will disclose that as we move forward.

"Today is a day of reflection, and we'll work out where we plan to go from this point. But I will say, the Hillsborough Law is there for a reason, and we're going to apply it."

Asked if ministers should be braced for a legal challenge, he said: "Absolutely, absolutely."

Piddington symbolically voted to leave the UK in September over the planned use for the site, and last month the group Wrong Plan Wrong Site appealed for a judicial review into the proposals.

A government report said the decision received 3,177 representations against and one in support.

It also said Rayner had ruled permission via an Urgent Crown Development application should be granted because "national demand for asylum accommodation remains high".

The permission allows for demolition of existing buildings, the building of new modular accommodation, and provisions for health and welfare facilities.

News.title: Water firm pleads guilty after four killed in blast
News.content:
A water firm has pleaded guilty to health and safety charges after an explosion at one of its sites killed four workers, including a teenage apprentice.

Luke Wheaton, 16, Ray White, 57, Brian Vickery, 63, and Mike James, 64, died in the blast in a silo at Wessex Water's treatment site in Avonmouth, Bristol, in December 2020.

An Avon and Somerset Police investigation into manslaughter was dropped in 2024 but the Health and Safety Executive (HSE) undertook its own investigation to determine if criminal offences had been committed under health and safety laws.

At a hearing at Bristol Magistrates' Court earlier, Wessex Water pleaded guilty to three charges under the Health and Safety at Work Act.

News.title: Doctor burnout putting maternity patients at risk, says regulator
News.content:
Training doctors working on maternity wards are experiencing high rates of burnout which could have a "critical impact" on patients, a regulator is warning.

The General Medical Council (GMC) says the fully qualified doctors, who are still training in obstetrics and gynaecology, are reporting more feelings of overwork and sleep deprivation than similar trainees in any other field of medicine or surgery, and are also more wary of escalating concerns.

Author Adam Kay, who left medicine in 2010 after dealing with a traumatic birth incident, says the report "makes for miserable reading" and says "nothing has been done" to improve workplace culture.

The Department for Health and Social Care said ensuring every maternity unit "meets the highest standards" was a priority.

The GMC analysed figures from its national training survey, which in 2026 was completed by 68% of trainee doctors, which includes registrars, representing almost 52,000 people.

It found:

Almost one in three trainee doctors working in obstetrics and gynaecology felt hesitant or apprehensive approaching a senior colleague about a patient, compared with one in five across all specialties

They were also more likely to be at moderate to high risk of burnout - 70% versus 61% across all specialties

One in three said they regularly suffered from sleep deprivation compared to one in five across the wider pool of trainees

Charlie Massey, head of the GMC, said having doctors who feel they cannot speak up, could have a critical impact on patients.

"Creating environments where staff are supported, listened to and feel able to raise concerns is essential."

He told the BBC: "Sadly, when we see when things go wrong, it is it is very often because of failures in terms of culture and leadership."

News.title: The school where white working-class pupils defy the odds
News.content:
Two years ago, I stood in a school hall in Sunderland on GCSE results day and watched the pride and surprise in the faces of teenagers as the envelopes were opened.

Even after years of covering results days, I was emotional to see a set of outstanding results in a school facing so many challenges. Almost half of the school's pupils receive free school meals, meaning their parents are on low incomes. In fact, the results in the ex-mining town of Hetton-le-Hole were as strong as the most affluent parts of southern England.

This summer, Hetton Academy hit another milestone, with 80% of its pupils getting a pass of at least a grade 4 in maths and English. A grade 4 is roughly equivalent to a 'C' under the old system, and is seen as a passport to jobs and further education.

Another striking detail about Hetton is that almost all of its pupils are from a white, working-class background, a group that's been in the spotlight for some time. This week saw the launch of the second phase of an independent inquiry, led by former Cabinet minister Baroness Morris, into why children from those communities lag behind their peers at school. Education Secretary Lucy Powell said: "Right now, too many white, working-class children are falling behind at every stage of their education."

But Hetton Academy seems to have defied the odds. The school's principal, Vicky Pinkney, refuses to accept low incomes should mean low results. "I don't think we should be accepting less just because of the community you work in," she says.

News.title: Brand will face 'hell on earth' in Wandsworth prison, says former inmate
News.content:
Russell Brand will face "hell on earth" inside HMP Wandsworth, a former inmate at the London prison has said.

Brand, 51, was convicted a week ago of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, and was sentenced on Monday to 10 years and six months in prison.

He is currently being held at the South London jail, which is one of England's largest Victorian-era prisons.

Chris Atkins, who served eight months at HMP Wandsworth for tax fraud, described the prison as "hell on earth".

He continued: "The first month is hands-down the worst. The mental shock is absolutely colossal. It was colossal for me and it's going to be 10 times worse for him because of the nature of his offences and the height from which he's fallen.

"He has to come to terms with it and the pure physical shock of suddenly being trapped in a dungeon for weeks on end with nobody to talk to most of the time is ghastly."

News.title: GPs, police and pharmacies among UK services affected by Microsoft outage
News.content:
GPs, police and pharmacies are among UK services affected by a global outage on some Microsoft platforms.

NHS England said patients should still attend appointments unless told otherwise, while several large police forces are urging members of the public to call if they want to make a report. MPs have also been affected.

Microsoft has said the problem was caused by a higher-than-usual stress on its servers but that systems were now showing "early signs of stabilisation" as work continued on a fix.

Major airports and UK intelligence services have been unaffected by the outage, while a minister said officials were assessing the extent of the impact on government services.

Sir CiarÃ¡n Devane, chief executive of the NHS Alliance, which represents the healcare system in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, said the outage was affecting some NHS services including emails.

NHS trusts in England were enacting measures to minimise disruption to critical services, a spokesperson said.

Patients have been told to continue to use 999 in an emergency and otherwise contact 111, 111 online or their local pharmacy.

Some GP surgeries have urged patients not to submit messages via their website while the problem remains. Practices in Hampshire and Shropshire have told patients to phone them or come into the surgery if they have an urgent need.

News.title: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU
News.content:
Andy Burnham said he believes a "win-win" deal can be agreed with the European Union, adding it could be "more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for" in 2016.

The prime minister is exploring closer ties with the bloc and is expected to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility at a UK-EU summit on 20 November.

Speaking after meeting European leaders in Ireland on Thursday, Burnham said he hopes a deal could help lower prices and boost the UK economy. He predicted the negotiations could "go down to the wire".

The Conservatives have previously said Labour are "dragging us into the European Union via the back door with their EU reset".

While Burnham has argued that Brexit has done "more harm than good", he has ruled out major changes to the UK's relationship with the EU before the next general election.

Labour's 2024 general election manifesto pledged there would be "no return to the single market, the customs union, or freedom of movement", and Burnham has committed to this.

The manifesto also said the party wanted to "make Brexit work" and reset the UK's relationship with the EU.

Former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer struck a deal in May 2025 covering fishing, trade and other areas and next week's summit will see the UK government seek to agree further changes.

Burnham has also made clear he wants to examine the "pros and cons" of the options for Britain's long-term relationship with the bloc.

News.title: Blink-182 to make Download debut as 2027 festival headliners
News.content:
Blink-182, Evanescence & Bring Me The Horizon have been announced as headliners of next year's Download Festival.

The trio are among more than 100 rock and metal acts set to play the event at Donington Park, Leicestershire from 9 to 13 June.

Other acts on the bill include The Prodigy, 5 Seconds of Summer and a special performance by heavy metal legends MÃ¶tley CrÃ¼e.

US pop-punk band Blink-182 will be making their Download debut, while Evanescence will become the festival's second female-fronted headliner.

The American rock band were founded by singer Amy Lee in the mid-1990s and had a UK number one with their best-known single Bring Me to Life in 2003.

It's the second year in a row a female-led band has headlined the festival, after Linkin Park topped the bill in 2025.

The nu-metal group have reformed with Emily Armstrong as their lead singer, after the death of former frontman Chester Bennington, who took his own life in 2017.

The choice of Emily upset some fans, who pointed to her alleged ties to the Church of Scientology and past support for convicted rapist Danny Masterson - someone she distanced herself from.

News.title: MI5 will need proof to be believed in future, says Leveson after BBC investigation
News.content:
In his first interview about the case, Lord Leveson said he stood ready to assist the police if asked.

He said that "MI5 have a great distance to go" with courts in the future.

He added the BBC investigation's reach "has been far greater than if this had never happened. So you can take some pride in that."

Lord Leveson said there was also a change in the way that agents, also known as covert human intelligence sources (CHIS), were managed.

Because of the Agent X case, there is a new policy relating to agents and domestic violence, and coercive control.

"There is no doubt that concern is now being focused not merely on the activity of the CHIS, but the impact of the CHIS on other aspects of his or her life.

"I think that everybody learns from disasters, and this for MI5 has been a very serious matter."

The Ipco chief executive, Richard Thompson, now attends meetings of an internal board in MI5, created to oversee changes because of the Agent X case, including changes in culture within the service.

In addition, MI5 must change the way it prepares and gives evidence, after the High Court case.

Lord Leveson said intelligence service chiefs from around the world had contacted him about the case.

They had expressed concern about whether something similar could happen in their organisations, he said.

The Agent X case had "done a great service to everybody", Lord Leveson said

The Ipco investigation examined how MI5 gave false evidence to three courts about having kept to its core secrecy policy - known as "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) - about the agent status of the violent neo-Nazi informant.

The government took the BBC to court in 2022 in a failed attempt to block our investigation into Agent X, but won him legal anonymity. His ex-partner Beth then sued MI5 at the Investigatory Powers Tribunal, and in 2024 she sought a review of a ruling at the High Court.

MI5 claimed it had maintained NCND and, consequently, the courts allowed it to keep information secret from Beth and everyone else, leaving her at a serious disadvantage.

But what MI5 said was untrue. It had, in fact, disclosed the man's agent status in phone calls to me, as it tried to persuade me not to investigate him in 2020.

A senior MI5 officer had tried to cover up for the man, falsely saying he was not an abusive misogynist nor a real extremist. He even wanted me to meet the agent. In doing so, he repeatedly departed from the NCND policy.

That officer was found to have repeatedly lied by the IPCO investigation. He has resigned from MI5 since the BBC exposed what happened.

News.title: Man charged over multiple sex assaults at university
News.content:
A 29-year-old man has been charged with sexually assaulting seven women in and around the University of Huddersfield.

West Yorkshire Police said officers were called to the university on Tuesday evening following reports of a man approaching and sexually touching women.

The force said, following an investigation, Sophan Akbash, from Huddersfield, had been charged with nine counts of sexual assault and is due to appear at Leeds Magistrates' Court later.

Prof Tim Thornton, the university's deputy vice-chancellor, said the university was working closely with police and that "the safety and wellbeing of our students, staff and visitors is our highest priority".

Earlier this week, Det Insp Sarah Bradley said: "We continue to work closely with our partners at the university to provide reassurance to students and staff and remain fully committed to supporting victims and safeguarding those who live, study and work in Huddersfield."

News.title: England thrashed by Australia in first ODI
News.content:
First one-day international, Perth

England 131 (33.4 overs): Atkinson 29*; Beardman 6-24

Australia 132-3 (23.3 overs): Marsh 50, Connolly 27

Australia won by seven wickets

Scorecard

England meekly offered Australia respite from the ongoing sandpaper scandal by being bowled out for 131 in a seven-wicket thrashing in the first one-day international in Perth.

Hours after Pat Cummins emphatically hit back at Usman Khawaja's comments, Harry Brook's England folded as 21-year-old fast bowler Mahli Beardman emerged with a stunning 6-24 on his ODI debut.

Beardman nicked off Brook in his second over for his first international wicket. Less than two hours later, bowling accurately and at good pace, he had the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut.

His second ODI wicket was the prized scalp of Joe Root for 17 and he also dismissed Jordan Cox and Sam Curran in an opening spell of five overs that returned figures of 5-18.

Ben Duckett, Tom Banton and Root, plus Beardman's later victims Liam Dawson and Jofra Archer, fell driving in Perth â dismissals familiar from England's wretched start to last winter's Ashes series on the same ground.

This was another Perth surface offering pace and bounce and England had no answer.

Talk of the sandpaper scandal still swirls around the game - the day began with David Warner accusing Cummins of throwing Khawaja "under the bus" on the Australian TV coverage - but England missed the chance to apply more misery to their oldest foe.

Captain Mitchell Marsh, who repeatedly dodged questions about ball tampering in his news conference on Thursday, thrashed a 29-ball fifty as Australia chased their target with a massive 26.3 overs to spare.

The second of three ODIs is on Sunday in Adelaide (03:30 GMT) with England, who suffered damaging defeats in the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka last month, desperately needing a response as they attempt to build towards next year's World Cup after four defeats in their past five matches.

News.title: Police officers sacked for 'despicable' on-duty filming of vulnerable people
News.content:
Two male Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) officers have been sacked for taking videos and photos of 18 vulnerable people they had been sent to help.

In one video, a woman with learning difficulties was filmed in bed and asked about her sex life.

The two officers, identified as Officers A and B, had been tasked to her house in 2021 after a report of concern for her safety.

Police Ombudsman Jacqui Durkin said their behaviour had been "utterly despicable".

Some of the videos and pictures taken by the officers were shared on WhatsApp, including with a member of the public, and contained "sexualised, derogatory and demeaning commentary".

Their actions came to light during an investigation into Officer A, who was accused of having a relationship with a woman he met during the course of his duties.

His home and workplace were searched and electronic devices were seized for examination.

He was found to have taken videos and pictures of people who had requested assistance, reported crimes, were intoxicated or considered at risk of self-harm.

Some were filmed in people's homes, others in hospitals and in police vehicles.

They spanned a period between 2016 and 2021.

Five videos found on Officer A's phone featured an elderly and apparently vulnerable man, filmed in his home and on a street from a police car.

They show the poor state of his living conditions and included the officer making mocking comments about his sex life.

Two other videos were recorded of women who had been involved in a neighbour dispute, one of whom was intoxicated.

Officer B took photos of two vulnerable women, which he shared with Officer A, along with messages which referred to the women in derogatory terms.

News.title: Bride jilted at the altar gives marriage another go - on Friday 13th
News.content:
A bride who was jilted at the altar says "everything has fallen into place" as she prepares for her second wedding in four years.

Kayley Stead became a social media sensation in 2022 when she decided to go ahead with the celebrations despite her fiancÃ© not turning up.

But after reconnecting with an old university friend, she was able to find love again, and the pair are set to tie knot on Friday 13th.

Referring to the mysterious superstition that the day is considered unlucky, Kayley, from Swansea, said she "loves a risk" and is feeling great about their big day.

"It just feels right, and it feels completely different from the last time when I was planning it," she said.

Kayley said she is feeling prepared to marry her fiancÃ© Richard Perrott who she met when they were on the same course in university a decade ago.

"Luckily, I learned all the dos and don'ts last time and what to prep for," she told Radio Wales Breakfast.

"But the nerves are definitely coming in, which I think is normal."

She said "everything has fallen into place" this time around and she feels that, despite the emotional rollercoaster she went on a few years ago, it happened for a reason.

News.title: Experts explain what happens to your pension when you die
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

While retirement planning often centres on maximising income, the fate of someone’s pension after death is a frequently overlooked element of estate planning.

The state pension typically ceases when someone dies, making understanding different pension types and potential survivor benefits essential.

For instance, the basic state pension, available to those aged 66 or over with sufficient National Insurance contributions, is generally not inheritable.

However, complexities arise with the Additional State Pension, applicable to men born before 6 April 1951, and women born before 6 April 1953.

This additional component may have different rules regarding inheritance, highlighting the need for personalised advice.

A surviving spouse's own National Insurance contributions and any deferred pension payments can also influence what, if any, benefits continue after a death.

open image in gallery The state pension generally is not inheritable ( Getty/iStock )

For clarity on your individual situation and to ensure your estate plan accurately reflects your wishes, contacting the Pension Service directly is highly recommended. They can provide tailored guidance based on your specific circumstances.

Here, experts explain what generally happens to your pension after death.

A few scenarios to consider

Inheritance rules regarding the state pension can be complex, varying depending on individual circumstances. While the state pension generally isn't inheritable, certain situations allow for spouses or civil partners to receive additional benefits.

If death occurs before reaching state pension age, a surviving spouse or civil partner who hasn't yet reached pension age may be eligible for additional pension benefits.

For those who pass away after reaching state pension age, the rules differ depending on the pension system. Under the pre-2016 system, if the deceased received the Additional State Pension, their partner might inherit a portion of it. Those on the post-2016 system may be entitled to increased pension payouts.

If the state pension was deferred and hadn't been claimed before death, the surviving spouse or civil partner may receive a lump sum payment or increased payments on their own pension.

It's important to note that the state pension is typically linked to an individual's National Insurance contributions and therefore doesn't automatically transfer to a spouse or partner upon death.

What happens to private pensions when you die?

Private pensions work very differently, and in many instances can be passed on to a beneficiary or beneficiaries in the event of your death. There are two kinds of workplace pensions, however, and it’s important to understand what they are, how they work, and how passing them on can differ.

“Workplace pensions come in two main types: defined contribution (DC) and defined benefit (DB),” explains Fiona Peake, personal finance expert at Ocean Finance.

open image in gallery Income tax likely needs to be paid by your beneficiaries on DC pension withdrawals if you die after the age of 75 ( Getty )

“With a DC pension, it’s all about the pot of money you’ve built up. If you pass away before age 75, your beneficiaries can usually access this money tax-free, as long as it’s paid out within two years. After 75, they’ll likely need to pay income tax on any withdrawals at their own rate.”

An important element here is whether beneficiaries have been nominated.

If they have, either by informing your pension provider or by naming beneficiaries in your will, they will typically receive your DC pension under the conditions Ms Peake has explained.

In cases where no beneficiary has been named, the pension provider may decide where it goes on your behalf and it will typically be endowed to your estate. Under these circumstances, the funds would be eligible for inheritance tax, depending on the total value of your estate.

If you’ve already begun drawing your private pension, the ways it can be passed on will be affected by how you decided to access it.

If you chose a drawdown option, in which the bulk of your money remains invested while you withdraw what you need, anything remaining in your fund can usually be inherited by a beneficiary.

“Lump sum payments or setting up an income for beneficiaries are both common options,” says Ms Peake.

For those who opt for annuities, however, the terms can be more limiting.

“If you’ve bought an annuity with your pension, it’s important to check the terms,” Ms Peake continues.

“A basic annuity stops paying out when you die, but if you’ve got a joint or guaranteed term annuity, there might be payments that continue to your spouse, partner, or dependants.”

That’s defined contribution pensions covered, but what about defined benefits pensions?

DB pensions, sometimes known as final salary pensions, provide a continued, guaranteed income rather than a money pot from which to draw.

“When you pass away, some schemes might pay a percentage of this income to your spouse, partner, or dependants,” explains Ms Peake.

“The exact rules depend on the scheme, so it’s worth checking with your provider to see what applies.”

If you have a DB pension in place but your spouse or civil partner is not listed with it, it will typically stop upon death unless that particular scheme allows for continued payments to your children or other dependants. Regardless of the type of private pension you have, it’s important to name your beneficiaries and keep that information up to date.

“One area where people can sometimes lose out is forgetting to nominate a beneficiary for their pension,” says Ms Peake.

“Most workplace pensions let you name who you’d like to benefit from your pension when you die, and it’s something you can usually update if your circumstances change. For example, if you’ve divorced or remarried, you might want to revisit this to make sure it reflects your wishes.”

Looking forward

Pension rules face a significant overhaul in April 2027, impacting how they are taxed after death, according to Joshua White, Head of Growth at Level.

Currently, most unused pension funds are exempt from inheritance tax, but this will change. From April 2027, these funds will be included in the value of an estate for inheritance tax purposes.

This change will particularly affect individuals on defined benefit schemes. Those on defined contribution pensions will be less impacted.

The shift also has broader tax implications, especially concerning "fiscal drag", where frozen tax thresholds pull more people into the tax system due to wage inflation.

“Given current property prices and fiscal drag, we at Level estimate that around one million UK properties currently just below the inheritance tax threshold could become liable due to these changes. As property is often the main asset in an estate, this will bring many estates into the scope of inheritance tax for the first time,” Mr White says.

“It’s clear from HMRC’s consultation notes that this change is designed to prevent pensions from being used as a tax-planning tool rather than a means of providing for retirement. Executors and beneficiaries need to be aware of the potential tax implications and plan accordingly.”

It is important to be abreast of upcoming changes and how they will impact upon your situation.

If you’re ever in doubt or need further guidance, it’s never too late to get in touch with a financial adviser or pensions expert to assist with understanding your own circumstances, your options, and how you can pass on your pension when the time comes.

News.title: Pakistani teenager mauled to death by lion while filming TikTok video
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A Pakistani teenager was mauled to death by a lion during the shooting of a TikTok video at a private breeding farm in Lahore.

The 19-year-old victim, identified as Taha, reportedly worked at the farm in Lahna town.

The incident took place at around 5pm local time on 11 November.

Noman Hassan, who has around 2.5m followers on Instagram and 928,000 on TikTok, arrived at the farm and called Taha to make a video with the lion for social media, the BBC reported, citing a police complaint.

Mr Hassan allegedly “took the lion out of the cage and started making a video”. That was when the lion suddenly attacked the teenager, according to the complaint filed by his father Munir Ahmed.

Mr Hassan took Taha to a local private hospital, but the teenager succumbed to his injuries.

Police later arrested Mr Hassan and the owner of the farm, identified as Fayyaz, and sealed the facility.

Police claimed the arrested men had made attempts to hide the truth and presented the incident as a dog attack. “A passion for TikTok cannot be more important than a human life," a spokesperson for the Lahore police said.

"No one can be allowed to put human life at risk in the name of a hobby or entertainment. The attempt to hide the facts and every aspect of negligence will be investigated."

Police said they were investigating whether the facility had the permit to keep the big cat and followed safety protocols.

Mr Hassan’s social media accounts are filled with hundreds of videos showing him interacting with big cats, at times engaging in rough play with the animals.

In Pakistan, owning lions, cheetahs, tigers, pumas, and jaguars is seen as a status symbol and is legal, provided the animals are registered and a one-time fee of 50,000 rupees (£129) is paid. Regulations, however, require such animals to be kept outside city limits.

In January, an eight-year-old boy lost his arm after being attacked by a pet lion at a private breeding farm in the Sabzazar area of Lahore.

In another incident, a girl suffered injuries when a pet lion being transported on a rickshaw escaped.

Last year, authorities launched a crackdown on the illegal keeping of lions as pets, following an incident in Lahore where a lion escaped and injured a woman and her two children.

News.title: Walking 10,000 steps a day is a myth. Here’s how many scientists say you really need
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Research suggests older women could significantly cut their risk of early death by simply walking just 4,000 steps a day.

Crucially, this protective effect, which reduces the chance of premature mortality by over a quarter, holds true even if these steps are completed just once or twice a week.

The study underscores that the overall volume of steps taken, rather than the frequency of activity, is the key determinant in lowering death rates and mitigating the risk of heart disease.

This finding challenges the widely accepted benchmark of 10,000 steps daily, with experts concluding there is “no ‘better’ or ‘best’ pattern” for achieving health benefits through walking.

They said moving is important and “individuals can undertake physical activity in any preferred pattern”.

The study found that, compared with women who were fairly sedentary, those who achieved 4,000 steps per day on one or two days a week had a 26 per cent lower risk of death from any cause and a 27 per cent lower risk of heart disease.

Researchers from Harvard University suggested new physical activity guidelines for older women after conducting the study ( PA )

Achieving this on three days a week had more benefits, including a 40 per cent reduced risk of early death and a 27 per cent lower risk of heart disease.

Even more exercise than that (5,000 to 7,000 steps) led to more declines, but these were more modest.

Here, there was a 32 per cent lower risk of death but there was a levelling out in the risk of a cardiovascular disease death, at 16 per cent.

The researchers, including those from Harvard University in the US, said the study found that “the number of steps per day, rather than the frequency of days/week achieving a particular step threshold, is important” for cutting the risk of early death and heart disease in older women.

They added: “Physical activity guidelines in older women should consider recommending at least 4,000 steps per day on one to two days per week to lower mortality and cardiovascular disease risk.”

The study, published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine, included 13,547 women free from heart disease and cancer at the start of the trial, who were typically aged around 72.

The women wore devices for seven consecutive days to measure their step count and were tracked for nearly 11 years.

During this time, 1,765 women (13 per cent) died and 781 (5.1 per cent) developed heart disease.

The team concluded that a “greater number of steps, regardless of daily patterns, is associated with better health outcomes”.

News.title: Malcolm in the Middle star ‘grateful to be walking’ after horror car crash
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Malcolm in the Middle star Frankie Muniz says the car crash which landed him in hospital has “put everything into perspective”.

The actor and racing driver was injured during the “pretty bad wreck” at Daytona International Speedway in the US on Wednesday.

He had been practising for the Proud to Honour Veterans Day Classic benefit race at the time.

Muniz, 40, has since been discharged and updated fans on his health in an Instagram post, saying he is “doing okay”.

In a video, he said: “What is up, everybody? I just wanted to give a quick update.

“I’m sure a lot of you saw the news that I was involved in a pretty bad wreck yesterday at Daytona International Speedway for Ford’s Proud to Honour event that they were hosting.

“I first of all want to say I’m doing okay. I’m extremely sore, but fortunately no major injuries.

“I’m not 100 per cent sure how that’s the case, but that’s just a testament to how well built the Ford Mustang Dark Horse cars are, and to their safety.”

The US star thanked car manufacturer Ford for “giving me the opportunity to race” during the event, which he was “really looking forward to”, adding: “I’m really sorry to have had that happen.”

“I want to say thank you to everybody who has reached out,” Muniz said.

“Wishing me well and all their thoughts and prayers – I can honestly say that I’m grateful to be walking right now.”

He said: “I’m forever grateful for all of you reaching out, and to the safety team.

“It was tough getting me out of the car. We had to cut the roof off, but got me out safely.

“Got me to the hospital, and all is well. I’m recovering now, and I’ll be back on the track soon. I can’t wait.

“Thank you to everybody for reaching out and being concerned. I’m feeling good.”

In the same update, Muniz said he is “extremely sore” but “grateful to be walking”.

The post was flooded with comments of support, and Muniz wrote in the caption: “Yesterday at Daytona was one of those moments that puts everything into perspective.

“First and foremost, thank you to everyone who’s reached out with messages, calls, and prayers.

“The support has been overwhelming in the best way, and it means more than I can put into words.”

Frankie Muniz began professional racing in 2006 ( Getty )

Muniz also said he is “still processing it all”, but reiterated that he was “okay and already looking forward to getting back on the track soon”.

Muniz rose to fame on Malcolm In The Middle, and was nominated for an Emmy and two Golden Globe Awards for his work on the US sitcom.

One of the best-known child actors of his time, he has also appeared in films such as Big Fat Liar, Deuces Wild, Agent Cody Banks and Racing Stripes.

According to his website, Muniz took a break from the entertainment world in 2006 to pursue professional race car driving.

He began competing in the Formula BMW USA Championship and later went on to race in the Champ Car Atlantic Championship from 2007 to 2009.

Muniz has since competed in the Nascar Craftsman Truck Series, chalking up his best career finish of 10th at Daytona in 2025.

News.title: BBC Radio 1 appears to suffer ‘technical glitch’ during Microsoft outage as Charlotte Church plays on repeat
News.content:
BBC Radio 1 appeared to suffer a “technical glitch” as a Charlotte Church song was left to play on repeat.

The funny moment happened on Friday’s breakfast show (13 November) as presenter Greg James discussed the current Microsoft outage affecting people across the globe.

James told listeners: “At times like these you rely on radio to keep everyone up to date with everything. When the servers are down, you can just rely on us”, just as a funny sound interrupted him.

Charlotte Church’s Crazy Chick then started playing.

“What’s happened, what’s happened there?,” James asked, as he then tried to play a song by Zara Larsson, before Crazy Chick started playing again.

It remains unclear whether the apparent technical glitch was genuine or part of a joke.

News.content:
From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging.

At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story.
