News.title: The Microsoft outage means no incessant email chimes or message pings, but still we stayed online
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

It was the sound of e-silence.

No Microsoft Outlook email chimes, no Teams message pings, no new notifications and, very possibly, no work getting done.

Microsoft 365 teetered on the edge of becoming Microsoft 364 as the global outage stretched from Thursday into, ironically (or fittingly, depending on your personal outlook), Friday the 13th. The disruption has impacted an unknown number of netizens, but the total could be as high as 430 million — the figure the tech giant touts as the number of people who use Microsoft 365 apps.

Many of us were doing the same thing: Refresh, refresh, refresh.

But what really happens when an essential workplace tool goes quiet and the silence is heard around the world?

Sadly, it seems, the extended break online did not mean that we went outside — or even offline. Thousands used the 21st century technology of social media to complain about the 20th century invention of email. Memes sprang up across the internet as brands like airlines rushed to capitalize early Friday on an unexpected long weekend.

“Emails can wait. The world has been waiting long enough,” Air India wrote on X. “Consider this your cue to plan that getaway.”

The airline's post featured a photo with a view out an airplane window with the quip, “A change of outlook we'd highly recommend.”

Burger King instead opted for a message directed at Microsoft: “whoever’s troubleshooting and working on the outage rn…take your time. go out and get a Whopper.”

The World Health Organization, meanwhile, valiantly pitched some healthy offline ideas like taking a break from screens or stretching and walking.

We could do that. We could take advantage of a world and a workday where our inboxes don't demand all of our attention. We could savor the unexpected serenity of an enforced e-silence. We could take a walk! Really, we could.

Or we could stay inside, tethered to our laptops and desktops and smartphones, drafting hot takes instead of emails.

And again: Refresh, refresh, refresh.

For some unfortunate souls, Teams sadly still worked. Others were forced to pivot to alternate forms of communication.

“Having meetings on WhatsApp now instead,” one Redditor wrote.

“My boss pointed out the program that has our training on still works,” someone else posted.

Still more turned to other screens for entertainment: “Feet up on the sofa, coffee in hand and playing a bit of xbox, wonderful start to the day,” another said. “Hopefully outlook is down for the remainder of the day.”

But the outage also brought a nostalgia not seen since the 1900s.

“It’s actually been quite fun in the office," another Redditor wrote. "It feels like a bit of a social event — everyone is chatting, we’ve ordered breakfast in, planning a pub visit this afternoon if it continues. Is this what the 90s felt like?”

But for many of us, the Internet Age is all-consuming. Even if our ears got a break for a few hours from the constant dings and pings of notifications, our fingers remained ready to reply-all at a moment's notice.

Refresh, refresh, refresh.

___

The Associated Press uses several Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. The outage gave Dazio some peace and quiet to write this report.

___

AP journalist Chan Ho-him in Hong Kong contributed to this report.

News.title: All the major organisations affected by the Microsoft outage
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A major global Microsoft outage has left millions of people around the world without access to emails and other key digital services.

The Microsoft 365 issues have affected users of Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, 365 and Copilot AI, as well as multiple connected services.

Microsoft said the issue affects “Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region”, with some experts warning it could rank among the most economically damaging technology outages in history.

It is the second breakdown of Microsoft’s 365 services this year, leading to concerns that repeated failures could cause clients to question its reliability.

Here’s a full round-up of all the major organisations, corporations and sectors impacted by the Microsoft outage.

Government agencies

Government departments in Australia, Japan, Singapore and the United States all reported being affected by the disruption.

The US House of Representatives said that it was working directly with Microsoft engineers to restore email and workspace access.

In Australia, the federal agencies impacted included the country’s intelligence agency ASIO, as well as the Australian Federal Police.

Japan’s Deputy Chief Cabinet Secretary Masanao Ozaki confirmed that parts of the government’s IT infrastructure had been hit by the outage, while government agencies in Singapore reported service disruptions on Friday morning.

Health services

The UK’s NHS said on Friday that some patients may struggle to get medications due to the Microsoft outage.

A spokesperson for the National Pharmacy Association said the outage “affects a pharmacy’s ability to communicate with GP practices and some patients”.

The NHS has also said that staff emails are also down across multiple regions, though patient appointments should be able to continue as planned.

AI firms

Anthropic and OpenAI both suffered issues because their services are integrated with Microsoft’s systems.

Claude creator Anthropic reported elevated errors and slow responses on requests for Claude for Outlook, which affects mail, calendar and search tools.

OpenAI reported similar problems, saying that it was working to resolve the issues.

“We’re investigating an issue with Microsoft connectors where new connections may be broken, and tools are not working as expected,” the ChatGPT creator said in a status report.

Schools and universities

Several schools and universities have reported disruption as a result of cloud-based administration services going down.

In the UK, the University of Manchester advised staff to use telephone calls and text messages for urgent communications, and to save any important work directly to their computers rather than the cloud.

Teachers at an Australian university expressed frustration at the impact the outages were having on their classes.

Ali Yavari, an associate professor at Swinburne University of Technology, also warned that the “consequences can outlast the outage itself” due to the measures taken to continue working.

“Out of frustration or urgency, employees may turn to personal email accounts, unmanaged devices or unapproved messaging and file-sharing services to keep working,” Professor Yavari told local outlet ABC News.

He added that this could potentially lead to future data losses or privacy breaches.

This article will be updated as the full extent of the outages becomes clear, with disruption reported across 74 countries

News.title: England’s batting capitulates in defeat to lift Australia’s spirits
News.content:
“We weren’t quick enough to adapt to the conditions, we talked extensively leading into the game about the surface here at Optus,” Brendon McCullum, England’s coach, said. “It’s a bit like batting on a trampoline, there are certain shots that are very difficult to execute. We talked about trying to put those away.”

McCullum called for his team to scrap a bit more, and at least acknowledged this time that driving on the up was unwise.

“KP has got such a nice manner about him,” he said. “He sees his role to get the talent to perform on the world stage. His message will be measured but firm – adapting to conditions, what could we have done, trying to drive the ball on the up is not wise. Next time we hit a surface like this we have to try and work it better.”

After a quiet start, both openers fell tamely. Ben Duckett prodded Johnson to point, then Banton had a booming drive at Bartlett and was caught behind.

Enter Beardman. When he came on to bowl the 10th over of the innings, there was palpable excitement from his home crowd, who had watched another West Australian, Mike Hussey, present his ODI cap before the toss. Later in the day, Hussey was probably glad he rebuffed England’s recent approach to work with their Test batsmen.

Beardman, who is a mentee of Dennis Lillee and has a gorgeously rhythmical action that helped him touch 90mph, started with a maiden to Root, then found just another movement away from Brook to invite the edge. On the occasion of his 200th ODI, Root had been dropped badly on three off Bartlett, and his only boundary came when Beardman found his an inside edge and the ball flew past his stumps.

The pressure told, and Root edged a big drive behind, where Josh Inglis took the third of his five catches. That sparked a collapse of five for 10, with Jordan Cox edging behind prodding in defence, before Curran was caught on the fence hooking for nought. Beardman’s five-fer was completed when Liam Dawson – selected ahead of Adil Rashid again – skewed a flat-footed drive to backward point. Overton followed in the next over, leaving England 65 for eight, with their lowest ever ODI score, 86, inevitably recorded against Australia in 2001, appearing a distant possibility.

A stand of 37 from Will Jacks and Gus Atkinson averted that particular indignity, and the fear of being bowled out for double figures. But the total was never enough and, despite Atkinson bowling Head first ball, the chase was painfully routine thanks to Marsh’s early barrage.

News.title: Kane bends game to his will on record-breaking night
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of England vs Croatia in the Nations League, with the hosts’ captain Harry Kane set to become the country’s most-capped player.

The 33-year-old has enjoyed a memorable few weeks, becoming the first English Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years and following it up with a new Bayern Munich contract, and an appearance at Wembley tonight will take him clear of Peter Shilton’s record of 125 England caps.

Kane scored twice in his record-equalling appearance against Czech Republic at Wembley last month, extending his international tally to 91 goals – a total that is unrivalled for England.

“It’s not about me – it’s about the team,” Kane said before tonight’s landmark moment. “I love coming to every England camp. I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible.”

The 3-0 home victory over Czech Republic left England on nine points after four Nations League group games, with a 2-0 win in the away contest and a 7-0 thumping of Croatia coming after a 3-2 defeat against world champions Spain.

Thomas Tuchel will be hoping that his side can inflict another heavy defeat on Croatia this evening, but a draw will be enough to book their place in the quarter-finals, with the group’s top two teams progressing.

While Kane will collect plaudits for his 126th cap, attention will also be on a potential first, with Jude Bellingham’s younger brother, Jobe, included in a senior England squad for the first time.

The two Bellinghams appearing together in a senior match would be a new experience for them, while it would be the first time that brothers have taken to the field together for England in 19 years.

“I can’t ignore it, but obviously with Jude being here too, it’s a great, great feeling for the family,” Jobe said on the Football Association’s England app. “It’s quite special, to be honest. It’s such a huge bonus on top of something that’s already so special and so great.”

News.title: Experts hail a “milestone” as TB deaths fall by more than a third in 10 years
News.content:
The number of people dying from tuberculosis has dropped by more than a third over the last 10 years but progress against the disease is still too slow, according to the World Health Organization.

Figures from WHO’s annual TB report showed that the lung disease took the lives of an estimated 1.13 million people in 2025, down from 1.7m in 2015, a drop of 35 per cent.

While WHO hailed this as a major milestone in achieving global targets - albeit five years too late - it said that progress in wiping out TB was still too slow.

Africa and Europe have made the greatest progress in reducing deaths, with numbers halving on both continents over the 10-year period. India and China - countries that have high burdens of the disease - also cut deaths by 35 per cent.

The report also showed that an estimated 10.6million people contracted the disease in 2025, a reduction of just 75,000 since 2024.

TB - still the world’s leading infectious disease killer - is preventable and curable, and is caused by the bacillus Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is spread when infected people cough or sneeze.

The disease has been around for centuries, and has been described as the quintessential disease of poverty as it spreads in areas of low quality housing, among people with poor nutrition and immunity. It is a particular risk to people who are HIV positive.

Treatment requires a six-month long regimen of medication, and while treatments have become less toxic in recent years, they still take a heavy toll on patients and have a range of side effects, including at the most extreme deafness. Adherence to medication is also a problem.

News.title: Low-cost parenting app halves rates of sexual violence amongst teenagers in Tanzania
News.content:
A low cost parenting intervention has more than halved rates of sexual violence among teenage girls in Tanzania, a study has shown.

The ParentApp digital parenting programme for families is aimed at reducing rates of violence experienced by teenagers of both sexes.

Researchers found the programme helped bolster family relationships and enabled mothers and fathers to better communicate with their children at what is often a tricky stage of their development.

The programme, led by Oxford University and the University of Cape Town in partnership with the Tanzanian government, the World Health Organization and Unicef, combines in-person and mobile parenting support.

Parents have an introductory session with a facilitator and then undertake 12 weekly sessions online. They also join a WhatsApp group with other parents where they can discuss problems and support one another.

The randomized controlled trial, published in The Lancet, included 2,396 children aged 10–17 and 2,396 parents and carers across 80 urban and rural areas.

Families were randomly assigned to receive either ParentApp or a comparison app focused on safe water and hygiene. Researchers analysing the results did not know which app each family received.

At the 14-month follow-up, girls in families participating in the ParentApp initiative reported a 67% reduction in sexual violence; a 54% reduction in sexual exploitation and an improvement in parent-child relationships. The successes were less marked in boys, however.

Violence against children is widespread globally: Unicef data shows that around one in five girls and women and one in seven boys and men globally have experienced sexual violence as children.

Lucie Cluver, professor of child and family social work at Oxford University and one of the authors of the study, said the intervention was aimed at helping parents and children talk to one another and discuss situations before they arise.

In Tanzania, for example, teenage girls might get a motorbike taxi late at night, potentially putting them in a dangerous situation.

“What you’re doing is making plans and problem solving ahead of these risky situations that teenagers end up in. And you’re building trust and the relationship so you can have these difficult conversations,” said Prof Cluver.

She said she was surprised at how big an impact the intervention had on sexual violence: teenage girls reported that because the app helped improve communication with their parents and carers they did not feel the need to go out as much.

The programme cost around $6 per family but researchers calculated that it goes up to around $10 per family if 20% are given smartphones. A traditional in-person parenting intervention generally costs around $120 per family.

Engagement in the sessions was high - around 70 per cent of participants completed the course - and some parents kept in touch with one another after the programme.

However, the authors of the study stressed that while the app focused on families there remains a need to prevent violence against children in other settings, such as schools and religious institutions. There also needs to be a broader societal push to address the scourge.

“The app isn’t the answer to everything - it’s just one part of the puzzle,” said Prof Cluver.

Prof Cluver said she hoped future versions of the programme would include greater focus on digital harms and test whether parents could take the lead themselves.

The programme is being rolled out in other countries, including Mexico, Panama and South Africa, and is easily adaptable for different contexts.

“Tanzania only has 20% smartphone use and we thought if it works in one of the hardest places to do a digital intervention it could work anywhere,” she said.

She said the study showed how parenting was a universal experience, with the majority focused on what is best for their children.

“Parents feel powerless. We live in a world where our kids are facing risks and parents just want to help,” added Prof Cluver.

News.title: AI fuels fastest economic growth in two years
News.content:
The Prime Minister and the Chancellor should not claim credit for the AI-fuelled expansion of Britain’s economy in the third quarter, a think tank said.

Julian Jessop, economics fellow at the Institute of Economic Affairs, said the 0.7pc expansion in the economy was “a tribute to the resilience of the private sector in the face of the energy shock and policy headwinds”.

He said: “This resilience is despite rather than because of anything the Government has done. In particular, the persistent weakens of the construction sector underlines the failure of flagship policies to boost housebuilding and infrastructure spending.

“The Government’s clumsy interventions are also continuing to add to labour and housing costs, including rents. Instead, the key driver of growth and business optimism has been the rollout of AI. This is an area that the Government has not got round to messing up, though that may yet be coming.

“In the meantime, the Government is still borrowing more than expected and the labour market remains weak.

“The full impact of higher inflation and higher interest rates has also yet to be felt. Early surveys for the fourth quarter already show that consumer confidence, retail spending, private sector hiring and housing market activity are all starting to slide again.

“2026 will still be a year when the economy performed much better than expected – at least in terms of GDP. But the new year will start with further increases in energy bills and high levels of job insecurity, which will matter far more to most people.”

News.title: Bird flu viruses ‘gaining function’ through natural mixing, warn scientists
News.content:
The bird flu virus’ resurgence began with an 11-year-old. In February 2023, the schoolgirl was admitted to a hospital in Phnom Penh with severe pneumonia – within a day, she was dead.

Tests soon revealed that she had contracted avian influenza: Cambodia hadn’t reported a human case of bird flu since 2014, but the hiatus was over. Since then, 39 more people have been infected and 15 have died in the Southeast Asian country – a case fatality rate of roughly 40 per cent.

Researchers have been scratching their heads as to why, after nine years, this particular stain of H5N1 suddenly started jumping from birds to people again. The strain or clade called 2.3.2.1 had been circulating for almost a decade without spilling into humans. What changed?

Now, a paper in Emerging Infectious Diseases offers clues.

Scientists say the apparent rise in human cases has coincided with the virus gaining new genetic material and, potentially, new powers of infection, from a second flu virus via a process known as “reassortment”.

News.title: The country where diabetes is more feared than HIV
News.content:
Furthermore, even when antiretrovirals suppress the virus, the immune system can stay chronically activated, causing a low-grade inflammation that damages organs and blood vessels. The Lancet HIV Commission reported that, by one measure of biological ageing, people with HIV appeared about five years older on average than peers without the virus.

HIV also makes other infections more dangerous. For example, those living with the virus are more likely to contract human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer, and they are less able to clear HPV from their bodies.

“With HIV, you don’t channel your mind into dying,” Ms Shongwe said. “But when I got to know that I have cervical cancer, I thought it was the end of the world.”

In 2018, Ms Ginindza moved from the Ministry of Health’s HIV programme to its NCD programme, but almost immediately, she asked to go back to her old job. “There is nothing here,” she recalled, “no tools, no data collection system, no guidelines”.

Even today, the ministry doesn’t have any dedicated NCD posts. While there are hundreds of people working on HIV, there are just 10 NCD staff, all borrowed from other programmes, Ms Ginindza said.

Although latest figures show that NCDs account for almost half of Eswatini’s deaths the government’s programme for NCDs, injuries and mental health received about one million emalangeni - roughly £45,000 - or 0.03 per cent of the health budget.

Foreign aid hasn’t filled the gap: international partners cover about five per cent of NCD spending, Ms Ginindza said, compared with 60 per cent of the HIV response. Donors “cannot give you money when they also need that money to address their own NCDs”, she added.

So, when it comes to these chronic diseases, patients struggle to get diagnosed, obtain their medicines or see a specialist for complications. In a 2024 government survey, fewer than 30 per cent of people with high blood pressure were on medication, and only 14 per cent had their hypertension under control.

The government’s own NCD report puts the stock-out rate for key medicines at 79 per cent, and the public system has no nephrologists, endocrinologists or cardiologists, Ms Ginindza said, relying instead on private specialists and Taiwanese medical missions to provide these services.

Faced with one of the worst HIV epidemics, Eswatini poured almost everything into fighting it. “The focus was HIV,” Ms Ginindza said, “so we forgot about the other conditions.”

Fighting on two fronts



Now, Eswatini is trying to turn its HIV machinery towards chronic diseases.

Since 2020, a government-led scheme has delivered NCD medication refills, blood pressure checks and glucose tests in hundreds of community settings, integrating this with existing HIV services. As it once did with antiretrovirals, the ministry is also shifting NCD care from hospitals to local clinics, Ms Ginindza said, aiming to train at least two nurses at each.

For Mr Mamba, that means he sees the same clinician for his HIV, diabetes and blood pressure. It saves time, he said, since he can get everything under one roof.

The challenge is not just extending HIV services to NCD patients but finding the money to sustain both. The Eswatini government aims to increase NCD funding to 20 million emalangeni, or £900,000, by 2028.

But last year, the Trump administration gutted the US President’s Emergency Plan for Aids Relief (Pepfar), the backbone of Eswatini’s HIV response.

In December, Eswatini signed a five-year deal with the US to restore some HIV funding - on the condition that the government shoulders more of the cost itself. So, as the country scrambles to protect its HIV gains, NCDs risk remaining a secondary priority.

With his diabetes and blood pressure medicines so often out of stock, Mr Mamba has come to dread his check-ups, convinced each one will show his numbers have climbed again - and that his luck is running out.

Many of his neighbours have the same conditions and probably share these fears, he said, but much as people once kept quiet about HIV, they rarely discuss such things.

Over 30 years ago, Ms Gwebu contemplated suicide after being diagnosed with HIV. But today, she hopes Eswatini can sustain its hard-won progress against the virus without leaving those with other diseases behind. “What is going to kill our people,” she said, “is not going to be HIV.”

News.title: Ebola could be raging in DRC for another year, expert warns
News.content:
The Ebola epidemic currently raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo could last at least another year, a leading UK epidemiologist has warned.

Experts have struggled to contain the current outbreak since the first cases of the rare Bundibugyo strain of the disease were reported in May.

There have so far been almost 11,000 cases including 5,000 deaths, making it the second largest outbreak in history, after the devastating West Africa epidemic of 2014-16. Cases have also been reported in Nigeria and Kenya, although transmission has not been widespread.

The outbreak is taking place across a vast area of DRC - North Kivu and Ituri - where conflict and widespread mistrust of authorities, including health workers, have hampered the response.

Neil Ferguson, professor of epidemiology at Imperial College, London, told a press briefing that at the current rate of disease spread that the epidemic could still be ongoing at the end of next year.

“Controlling Ebola outbreaks takes a long time so it is highly likely we’ll still be seeing transmission in a year’s time,” he said.

“We’re ticking over at about 70 confirmed cases a day at the moment and that’s almost certainly quite a significant underestimate of the true number of infections,” said Prof Ferguson, who rose to prominence at the beginning of the Covid pandemic when he advised government on the likely trajectory of the outbreak.

Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s true feelings on seven Man Utd players including Marcus Rashford

With Mauricio Pochettino set to soon be unveiled as the manager of Manchester United, seven current Red Devils have been earmarked as players he would like

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has been struggling with injuries this season (Image: 2026 DeFodi Images)

Marcus Rashford will be one of seven Manchester United players Mauricio Pochettino will "like". The manager of the United States of America is expected to soon be unveiled as the next Red Devils head coach.

‌



Pochettino, 54, will replace the recently sacked Michael Carrick, who was given his marching orders after a meeting with club CEO Omar Berrada at United's Carrington training base. The next Red Devils boss is set to inherit a side who are languishing in 18th position in the Premier League.

Their performances have been widely criticised for lacking intensity and desire, having shipped 15 goals in Carrick's final five matches in charge. However, one source close to the South American believes there are seven stars Pochettino will relish working with, including Rashford.

The ex-Tottenham manager knows Shaw well having managed him during his time at Southampton. Meanwhile, goal-scoring attacking midfielders like Fernandes have often fared well under Pochettino, with the likes of Cole Palmer and Dele Alli enjoying their best goal-scoring seasons under him.

Rashford has been troubled with a groin and hip injury throughout this season. He has not featured since the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid at the start of last month.

View 3 Images Fernandes is another player who has been tipped to thrive under Pochettino (Image: Getty Images)

He is currently on the road to recovery and United are optimistic he will be fit for Pochettino's first match as manager, which will be against Liverpool after the international break. Meanwhile, Fernandes has also claimed Pochettino wanted to bring him to Spurs in 2019, telling the Athletic: "The [Tottenham] manager, Mauricio Pochettino, was the one who wanted me there.

"It was a good offer but Sporting tried their best to keep me. The president spoke with me, but he spoke with me on the wrong day. It was the day after they decided to refuse the offer from Tottenham and I was really angry.”

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers hits back at 'nonsense' Cole Palmer claims: "It's a lie!"
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers hits back at 'nonsense' Cole Palmer claims: "It's a lie!"

Cole Palmer was left out of England's latest squad by Thomas Tuchel, while Chelsea teammate continues to impress for the Three Lions scoring against Croatia

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers has backed his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer

Morgan Rogers has rubbished suggestions that his Chelsea teammate Cole Palmer isn't committed to playing for England.

‌



‌



Rogers was on the scoresheet as the Three Lions beat Croatia at Wembley to set up a Nations League group decider with Spain on Sunday. But Thomas Tuchel’s squad will head to Madrid without Palmer, after he was a notable omission for the final fixtures of 2026.

‌



Since Tuchel was appointed as Gareth Southgate's successor in 2024, Palmer has featured just three times and after some patchy form for Chelsea, he missed out on the World Cup squad.

‌



He was named in Tuchel’s first squad after that, but pulled out despite playing every Chelsea league game up to that point. Speaking after leaving him out this time around, Tuchel suggested he “misses too many opportunities to impress”.

‌



That led to some questions over his commitment towards the national side, an insinuation Rogers branded a lie. In an interview with BBC Radio 5 Live, Rogers said: "He wants to be here. He wanted to get called up and he wanted to come and represent his country as he always has done.

"He was in quite a low place with his injuries last year and didn't feel 100% himself on the pitch, so he wants to be here and he wants to be the best version of himself.

‌



"But he also has to look at his body. He wants to play for 10 or 15 years, he also has to manage himself. If he has to manage himself in the short term for the greater good then he has to do that and you have to fully support it.

View 3 Images Rogers scored his third England goal in the win over Croatia

‌



"It has nothing to do with England or not wanting to play with England. It's a nonsense really that people are questioning someone that wants to play for England. It's a lie.

"You see the joy and smile on his face, how much he loves the game, so I honestly don't get it and he doesn't get it."

‌



As well as hinting towards his previous absence as a reason, Tuchel also stated there were enough players in his position and he was remaining loyal to those he picked last month.

He said: "We have enough number 10s and we stick to the guys who were in the previous camp because we were happy with the two and a half weeks we had together.

‌



View 3 Images Thomas Tuchel left Palmer out of his latest England squad (Image: Getty Images)

"I guess everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

‌



"We are speaking now about a player that is not in camp. It counts when you are in camp and I just said last time that he misses too many opportunities to impress."

"It's not personal. We will never assume Cole is in the mindset never to come to the camp. Cole is always in our mindset but the competition is on."

Sports.title: Premier League VAR panel is a nonsense distraction tactic that feeds modern controversy cycle
Sports.content:
Premier League VAR panel is a nonsense distraction tactic that feeds modern controversy cycle

The Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel is a sign of the time - a worthless show which feeds the perpetual controversy cycle the division feeds off

View 4 Images Jurrien Timber pulling Alexander Isak's shirt became the main talking point of Arsenal's 1-0 win over Liverpool

Football loves panels. Anyone remember the Pools Panel? Actually, it is still going and has Michael Owen and Rachel Brown-Finnis amongst its members.

‌



‌



The Pools Panel was not actually created by the game’s authorities but by companies such as Littlewoods, Vernons and Zetters. A forerunner of fixed-odds betting on football, the pools was, essentially, about predicting results. The aim was to pick eight score draws.

‌



During the Big Freeze of 1962-63, fixtures were decimated by the weather so the pools companies assembled a panel who ‘decided’ the outcome of fixtures.

‌



The original panel consisted of six men - former England players Tom Finney, Tommy Lawton and Ted Drake, former Scotland defender George Young, former World Cup referee Arthur Ellis, and John Theodore Cuthbert Moore-Brabazon, 1st Baron Brabazon of Tara.

In his late seventies when joining the panel, Brabazon was a former Tory MP, who became the first person to qualify as a pilot in the United Kingdom.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

In 1909, he put a small pig in a wastepaper basket and tied it to the wing of his biplane for a short voyage, proving that pigs could fly.

‌



He was the first man to go up in a hot air balloon, was the first Commodore of the House of Lords Yacht Club, introduced the golf trolley to Britain, was captain of the Royal and Ancient Golf Club and won toboggan’s Cresta Run Coronation Cup.

And also helped decide if the postponed Wolves v Manchester City fixture would have been a draw.

‌



You can assume none of the five people on the Premier League’s Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel - and, presumably, those five people change from time to time - are as colourful as Baron Brabazon, but it would not matter a jot if they were.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 4 Images Liverpool players protest with referee Andy Madley during the defeat to Arsenal

What, exactly, is the point of the KMI Panel? In case you are unaware of its existence, it is - according to the Premier League website - an independent body used to review and assess major refereeing decisions and VAR interventions.

‌



The panel typically consists of five members. Three former players or managers, one Premier League official and one official from Pro Ref (formerly PGMOL).

They look at contentious decisions and have a vote on whether or not the referee and/or VAR got it right or wrong. The result of that vote is announced. And that’s it.

‌



But the findings are announced some time after the incidents. Hence, on Wednesday - November 11 - we had the KMI panel’s verdict on the Jurrien Timber-Alexander Isak incident, which took place in the Liverpool-Arsenal game on November 1.

View 4 Images VAR controversy has taken over the game (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

‌



And the verdict? Four members of the KMI panel believed on-field official Andy Madley should have given a penalty for Timber’s shirt tug (was Baron Brabazon the fifth panel member?).

Three members believed video assistant referee Stuart Atwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the VAR monitor but two members believed he was right not to intervene.

‌



To which there is one quick response. So what? It’s like people agreeing and disagreeing in a bar. We all saw what happened.

Yet the shirt-pulling incident - which would have been a strictly minor one in pre-VAR days - is still newsworthy 10 days on.

‌



And perhaps that suits the Premier League. Perhaps the Premier League - its officers and the 20 clubs and their executives who make up the private members club - are not bothered about the contentious elements of the game that have been exacerbated by VAR.

View 4 Images Arsenal's win at Anfield wasn't the best spectacle (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

‌



After all, Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Anfield was a terrible watch. Three shots on target in a match between what are supposed to be two of the competition’s blue-chip teams.

Thanks goodness for Madley, Atwell and VAR for giving us something to talk about. Perhaps that is how the Premier League saw it. And the KMI panel can keep the pot bubbling.

Article continues below

It is a conspiracy theory, for sure. But such is the drudgery of a lot of today’s Premier League football that the competition has a vested interest in keeping VAR in the headlines.

And their panel helps them do just that.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes 'REJECTS second Man Utd contract offer' casting doubt over his future
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes 'REJECTS second Man Utd contract offer' casting doubt over his future

Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes will see his current contract expire in June and talks over fresh terms are yet to bring a breakthrough amid turmoil at the club

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is unhappy with the terms offered by Manchester United (Image: Ed Sykes/Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes has reportedly rejected Manchester United's second offer of a new contract.

‌



‌



Fernandes' current deal is set to expire in June 2027 and United are eager to tie their captain down to fresh terms. But the Portuguese international has snubbed the club's second offer, with both the salary and contract length an issue.

‌



The Athletic reports that talks have been ongoing since the summer between Fernandes' representatives and the club, but a compromise is yet to be reached. And the latest development comes at a time of serious turmoil for United, plunging Fernandes' future into doubt.

‌



If the impasse continues, the 32-year-old midfielder would be able to speak to foreign clubs in January about a free transfer when his deal expires on June 30. However, United do hold the option to extend his contract by 12 months and they want him to stay.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



The news comes on the same day that United sacked Michael Carrick. Club chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday and pulled the trigger on Carrick the following morning.

The club are now pushing ahead with a deal to hire Mauricio Pochettino from US Soccer as Carrick's replacement. Pochettino has already agreed personal terms and United will pay his £7.4million release clause to land the former Tottenham boss.

‌



Pochettino may be dismayed to discover the situation surrounding Fernandes, who has been club captain since the summer of 2023 and has been the team's stand-out player almost since he arrived from Sporting Lisbon for £47million in January 2020, contributing 113 goals and 111 assists in 341 appearances.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes' future is now in doubt (Image: Getty Images)

United sit 18th in the Premier League after winning just one of their opening 10 league matches and their dreadful form won't help persuade Fernandes to stay put, especially after his recent public criticism of the club, which saw him dropped by Carrick.

‌



"Everyone at the club must understand that it’s no longer the same,” Fernandes said after the defeat by Como last month. “We’re no longer in the past and we must look to the future. We must create something different in the present."

Fernandes was offered a lucrative three-year contract by Al-Hilal last summer, with the Saudi Pro League side willing to hand him a package totalling £200m. He chose to snub the offer and stay with United, but - like many of his team-mates - his form has dipped of late.

‌



"It's not a question of loyalty," Fernandes said in May when asked about his decision. "I could have gone two years ago, I could have gone three years ago, I could have gone last season, but I really like to be here.

"I think that being successful at this club is something that I can never get at another club. The joy and everything I get, the day I get what I want from this club, I don't think I will get that from any other club in the world."

Sports.title: Jack Grealish issues public statement after Everton decision and disciplinary breach
Sports.content:
Jack Grealish issues public statement after Everton decision and disciplinary breach

Jack Grealish was dropped from the Everton squad in the Toffees' last Premier League match in a decision which was supported by David Moyes

View 3 Images Jack Grealish featured in a behind closed doors friendly for Everton (Image: Tony McArdle/Everton FC via Getty Images)

Jack Grealish has apologised for the behaviour which resulted in him being dropped from Everton's last three Premier League matches.

‌



‌



After being left out of the club's 3-1 win over Newcastle United in the League Cup and the following Premier League match against the Toon, which saw Everton win 1-0, David Moyes also did not include him in the squad for the Toffees' 3-1 win over Coventry City at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

‌



However, Grealish has since been re-integrated into the squad. The club also decided to deploy him in a behind-closed doors friendly against Derby County; a clear sign they are in the process of forgiving his behaviour.

‌



On an Instagram story, Grealish also issued a public apology on social media. He said: "Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks. I love playing for this club and I can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon."

Everton confirmed Grealish's omission in a blunt statement on social media. After he was left out for the second match in a row, the club publicly said: "Jack Grealish is not match fit and therefore not part of tonight’s squad.”

‌



View 3 Images Grealish uploaded this message to social media (Image: Instagram/jackgrealish)

Grealish had also missed the 2-0 away defeat to Arsenal through illness. A "breach of club discipline" and a lack of fitness were used as justifications for his absence for the next three matches.

‌



Moyes refused to answer any questions about Grealish's absence when asked if he was going to play against Coventry. Instead, the ex-Manchester United manager said: "You probably know I'm not going to give any details. It's a club decision, it's something I don't want to speak too much about."

Last weekend, the Liverpool ECHO stated Grealish returned to training at the Toffees' Finch Farm HQ to undertake a tailored training programme. He played 90 minutes against Derby, which ended with Moyes' side emerging as 4-1 winners.

‌



View 3 Images Grealish has not featured for Everton since the 2-0 home defeat to Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Gralish's Instagram apology came soon after the match. It's now possible he will be involved for the club after the international break.

‌



Everton travel to Brentford on Monday, November 23 before hosting Liverpool in the Merseyside Derby on November 29. Grealish will also hope to be available when the Toffees visit his former side, Aston Villa, on December 2.

Grealish is on loan from Manchester City until the rest of the season, when his contract with City expires.

Sports.title: James Milner confirms Liverpool return and reveals delight in 'pulling on red shirt again'
Sports.content:
James Milner confirms Liverpool return and reveals delight in 'pulling on red shirt again'

James Milner spent eight years with Liverpool between 2015 and 2023 before making the move to Brighton and Hove Albion, but is set to grace the pitch of Anfield once more next year

View 2 Images James Milner is set to play in the Liverpool Legends match (Image: Getty Images)

James Milner has explained that he's "thrilled" at the chance to "pull on the red shirt again" after being confirmed as the first home team player for next year's Liverpool Legends charity match. The 40-year-old retired from the beautiful game at the end of 2025/26, having made 658 appearances in total across Leeds, Newcastle United, Aston Villa, Manchester City, Liverpool and Brighton and Hove Albion.

‌



‌



However, the midfielder is set to grace the pitch of Anfield once again in March 2027, having been confirmed for the annual LFC Legends game. A statement from Liverpool confirming his participation read: "Former Reds vice-captain Milner, who recently brought the curtain down on an outstanding 24-year Premier League career, is the first confirmed player for the home team.

‌



"The midfielder spent eight successful years with Liverpool after joining on a free transfer from Manchester City in 2015, making 332 appearances and playing an integral role in one of the most successful eras in the club’s history.

‌



Liverpool star at centre of angry row after Andoni Iraola left 'sobbing' READ MORE :

"A model of consistency, versatility and professionalism, Milner helped Liverpool lift six major honours, including the Champions League in 2019 and the Premier League title in 2020."

Speaking about the honour, meanwhile, Milner explained: "I’m thrilled to have the chance to pull on the red shirt again and step back out at Anfield. It’s a special place, and playing there in front of the supporters is a feeling like no other.

"What makes the legends match so special is that it’s about more than football. It’s a chance to give something back to the fans while supporting the work of the LFC Foundation. I’m delighted to be the first to sign up and can’t wait to be part of it."

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 2 Images James Milner won the Premier League with Liverpool (Image: Paul Ellis/PA Wire)

‌



The rest of the LFC Legends will be announced in the coming months, while the game will get underway at 3pm on March 27, 2027. There, Liverpool's former stars will face Inter Milan's heroes of days gone by.

The James Milner Foundation has been in support of the LFC Foundation for a decade, helping over 2,000 children enjoy fun activities over the course of the school holidays.

‌



It recently backed four weeks' of free football and multi-sport camps across Anfield and Toxteth, with LFC Foundation coaches teaching over 800 children.

A total of 10 legends games have been held to date, raising over £10million for community projects across Liverpool. This year's clash - which took place on March 28 - saw Liverpool battle to a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund, and also marked Jurgen Klopp's return to the sidelines of Anfield, acting as an assistant coach for the Reds.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd start date emerges as Michael Carrick's staff learn their fate
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino's Man Utd start date emerges as Michael Carrick's staff learn their fate

Manchester United are still trying to iron out details and logistics with Mauricio Pochettino, with the Argentine set to swap the United States for Carrington after Michael Carrick was sacked

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino will oversee two more matches with the United States before leaving (Image: Omar Vega/Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino will oversee the United States' matches against Haiti before taking over as Manchester United boss.

‌



‌



Pochettino is lined up to replace Michael Carrick as United manager following his sacking on Thursday morning. But while personal terms have already been agreed, with Pochettino keen on the job he's coveted for years, there remain details to iron out.

‌



The United States are preparing for their two-legged Concacaf Nations League quarter-final with Haiti and Pochettino intends to fulfil his obligations with his current employers before jetting over the Atlantic. The USMNT play the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica, on Saturday before hosting Haiti in Cincinnati on Wednesday.

‌



As reported by Manchester Evening News, Pochettino will leave straight after the second leg, flying from Cincinnati to Manchester. He will begin work with his new team on Thursday, giving him just three days to prepare for the trip to Anfield to play Liverpool on Sunday, November 22.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick sacked LIVE: First Man Utd player breaks silence as Pochettino payments revealed READ MORE :

Harry Maguire first Man Utd star to comment after Michael Carrick sacked for Mauricio Pochettino READ MORE :

Having finally dismissed Carrick on Thursday morning following a meeting in Monaco between Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox, United are now focusing on his replacement. The club will have to pay US Soccer $10million (£7.4m) to release Pochettino from the four-year contract he signed in August.

‌



United will also have to fork out further compensation to hire Pochettino's coaching staff, including long-time assistant Jesus Perez. There has been a clean sweep of the coaching staff at Carrington, with just one coach keeping his job in the wake of Carrick's dismissal.

Assistant goalkeeping coach Connor King the only member of the first-team coaching staff to stay put, with Carrick's team of Steve Holland, Jonathan Woodgate, Jonny Evans, Travis Binnion and Craig Mawson all leaving.

‌

Pochettino will speak to the media at the US training centre just outside Atlanta on Friday when things will become clearer. He only signed a new deal with the USMNT in August after exiting the World Cup in the last-16 at the hands of Belgium.

But despite committing his future to the team, Pochettino has never shied away from his desire to one day return to the Premier League. The 54-year-old has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea in the league and has long been considered a future United boss.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire first Man Utd star to comment after Michael Carrick sacked for Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire first Man Utd star to comment after Michael Carrick sacked for Mauricio Pochettino

Michael Carrick was sacked by Manchester United on Thursday morning following a meeting by the club's hierarchy in Monaco, where it was decided to hire Mauricio Pochettino

View 2 Images Harry Maguire sent a farewell message to Michael Carrick (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Harry Maguire has paid tribute to Michael Carrick after he was sacked by Manchester United following a miserable start to the season.

‌



‌



Carrick was finally sacked on Thursday morning after chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox met with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday. The United hierarchy believe he has been drastically underperforming with the players at his disposal and have lined up Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement.

‌



United sit 18th in the Premier League, having taken just eight points from their opening 10 matches. They have won just three matches in all competitions so far this season and have the joint-worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

‌



Carrick was handed the reins on a permanent basis in May after a successful spell as interim boss. But, having guided United to third in the Premier League after Ruben Amorim's sacking, he couldn't sustain that form.

Despite the dreadful form, he remains popular among the club's fans - and among the players, if Maguire's message is anything to go by. Alongside a picture of him shaking hands with Carrick, the defender posted on Instagram: "Will always be a legend. Respect. Thank you."

‌



Carrick continued to take United training this week during the international break, even after it became clear he would be sacked and that Pochettino would leave his role as United States boss to replace him.

"Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach," United said in a statement.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

"After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

‌



"Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

"The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible."

United will have to pay the United States £7.4million to release Pochettino from the contract extension he signed in August following the World Cup. The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager's coaching staff will require further payments.

Pochettino is expected to arrive at Carrington in time to take charge of United's next match in the Premier League against Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

Sports.title: Cameron to reignite Mayer rivalry in rematch on Jake Paul bill
Sports.content:
Chantelle Cameron and former world champion Mikaela Mayer will meet in a rematch on the Jake Paul vs Cedric Doumbe bill on Christmas Eve.

Unified super-welterweight world champion Cameron will share the ring again with Mayer in Dubai just four months after she defeated the American in a thrilling fight in Birmingham.

In a fight of the year contender, Cameron claimed a hard-fought unanimous decision victory following a fiery build-up, and she is relishing the opportunity to face Mayer in a rematch on a huge Most Valuable Promotions show as Paul returns to the ring for the first time since his fight with Anthony Joshua.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mayer and Cameron got into a war of words following their super-welterweight fight with Mayer believing she should've been victorious

"We agreed to the rematch before the first fight, so we both kept our word," said Cameron.

"And now the rematch is on the biggest stage in boxing."

After the first fight, Mayer claimed she should have been awarded the win, accusing Cameron of being "lucky in her little back yard".

The 36-year-old American is now looking to reclaim her world champion status.

"Although I don't feel I performed to my highest potential, I've been working hard to fix the mistakes I made and I will 100 per cent come back stronger," she said.

"I'm taking my belts back on Thursday, December 24."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jake Paul and his opponent Cedric Doumbe face-off for the first time ahead of their boxing match on December 24th.

The Paul vs Doumbe bill also features undefeated US Olympian and 2021 amateur world champion Jahmal Harvey (5-0, 4 KOs) who faces Scotland's Craig Morgan (15-1-1) in an eight-round lightweight bout at 135 lbs.

Nakisa Bidarian, CEO of Most Valuable Promotions, said: "Chantelle Cameron vs Mikaela Mayer 2 marks MVP's latest seismic pound-for-pound clash with two of the world's top ten fighters meeting again in their prime.

"Their first meeting just a few months ago was a clear 'Fight of the Year' contender and both immediately called for the rematch following the fight - a testament to both being willing to take on the hardest challenges.

"Now the stakes rise even higher for Chantelle as she puts three titles on the line against a hungry Mayer, one of the sport's biggest faces in her own right and a US Olympian.

"They are joined by USA's knockout sensation and future face of the lightweight division Jahmal Harvey. Topped by an unmissable Jake Paul vs Cedric Doumbe main event, MVP's Christmas Eve spectacle only gets bigger and better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Jake Paul’s new opponent, Cedric Doumbe, leave Kylian Mbappe stunned with this nine-second knockout in the PFL.

Paul and former Glory kickboxing champion and PFL star Doumbe will face off in an eight-round cruiserweight professional boxing match at the Coca-Cola Arena in Dubai.

Doumbe, a former two-time Glory welterweight kickboxing champion, boasts an impressive 75-7-1 record in kickboxing, including 45 knockouts.

He is also 6-1 in mixed martial arts and 1-0 as a professional boxer, having beaten Mohamed Fodil on points in his sole boxing appearance back in 2015.

Sports.title: England crumble in Perth again as Australia win first ODI
Sports.content:
England capitulated in Perth for the second year running as an Australia side engulfed by the 'Sandpapergate' storm cruised to a seven-wicket victory in a series-opening ODI in which debutant Mahli Beardman recorded a six-wicket haul.

England's raft of rash strokes in last November's first Ashes Test at Optus Stadium led to them losing that game inside two days en route to a harrowing 4-1 series defeat.

Unlike the previous winter, the tourists played a proper warm-up game at another Perth venue in The WACA, beating a Western Australia side by 92 runs last Saturday as 21-year-old pacer Beardman went wicketless from 10 overs.

Fast forward six days and Beardman bagged the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut - his 6-24 from 7.4 overs topping Tony Dodemaide's 5-21 versus Sri Lanka in 1988 - with his five-for on his home ground coming in 28 balls as England slumped to 132 all out, a total Australia eclipsed in 23.3 overs.

Score summary - Australia vs England, first ODI, Perth England 131 all out in 33.4 overs (put in to bat): Gus Atkinson (29no off 32 balls), Will Jacks (25 off 47), Tom Banton (25 off 27); Mahli Beardman (6-24), Spencer Johnson (3-42), Xavier Bartlett (1-46). Australia 132-3 in 23.3 overs (target 132): Mitchell Marsh (50 off 30 balls), Cooper Connolly (27 off 30), Matt Renshaw (26no off 38); Jamie Overton (1-35), Gus Atkinson (1-40), Jofra Archer (1-48),

Harry Brook (1), who became Beardman's first wicket when he poked behind in the 12th over, saw his side bundled out in just 33.4 overs with Joe Root (17), playing his 200th ODI, one of a number of players to perish on the drive, the sort of shot that had got England in all sorts of bother during their Test trouncing here a year ago.

Brook's men rallied somewhat from 65-8, passing their lowest-ever ODI score of 86 and reaching three figures thanks to Will Jacks (25) and Gus Atkinson, who top-scored with 29 not out from 32 balls from the No 10 spot and hit England's sole six.

But a target of 132 was never likely to trouble Australia, despite Atkinson bowling Travis Head - who had slammed a match-winning hundred in that Ashes clash in Perth in 2025 - for a golden duck in the second over and so it proved, as stand-in captain Mitchell Marsh tonked a 29-ball fifty before holing out with 65 runs needed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mitchell Marsh declined to comment on 'Sandpapergate' ahead of the series-opening ODI against England

Marsh's eight-boundary onslaught (four sixes, four fours) came a day after dead-batting all questions about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town, which has been catapulted back onto the news agenda following the release of Usman Khawaja's book.

Beardman the star after Cummins hogs the headlines

Marsh is leading Australia in this three-match series in place of the rested Pat Cummins - but the latter was, along with Beardman, the undoubted story of Friday as he held an extraordinary, 68-minute press conference to address Khawaja's comments.

Cummins insisted Khawaja's claims that every member of the Baggy Greens dressing room back then was aware of the plot to alter the ball using sandpaper to be "100 per cent untrue" and "utter nonsense" before lauding "really exciting prospect" Beardman.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Australia Test captain Pat Cummins described allegations from ex-team-mate Usman Khawaja that every Australian player knew about using sandpaper to tamper with the ball in South Africa in 2018

As fans and media digested Cummins' startling response to Khawaja's accusations, a couple of hours later they were hailing Beardman's record-breaking ODI bow, where he displayed accuracy, speed and skill and offered a glimpse into the future.

The seamer nicked off Brook, Root and Jordan Cox (2), bounced out Sam Curran (0), had Liam Dawson - once again preferred in the England XI to fellow spinner Adil Rashid - caught at backward point for a duck and ended the innings when last man Jofra Archer (11) was athletically pouched by a diving Jack Edwards in the gully.

An Australia attack missing Cummins and two other rested fast-bowling stalwarts in Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazelwood excelled with left-armer Spencer Johnson's 3-42 including Ben Duckett (9) caught square driving to backward point after England lost the toss and new-ball partner Xavier Bartlett (1-46) removing Tom Banton (25).

Image: Tom Banton trudges off after being dismissed by Xavier Bartlett

England took a few scalps in the chase in Head, Marsh and Cooper Connolly (27 off 30) but Australia eased to victory and will now look to wrap up a series win with a game to spare in Adelaide on Sunday ahead of next Wednesday's final game in Hobart.

Brook's team are not at full strength - they are shorn of the injured Jacob Bethell (knee), Jos Buttler (hamstring) and Josh Tongue (toe) - but neither are Australia, so this defeat, following swiftly on from their tri-series travails in Pakistan last month when they lost three of their four matches, leaves England with plenty to ponder.

Beardman 'outstanding' but England didn't 'execute well enough'

England captain Harry Brook, speaking at the presentation:

"We have been in Perth for a week and a half and prepared extremely well [but] Australia bowled extremely well.

"Beardman was outstanding. He put the ball in the right areas and got enough out of the surface to dismiss us.

"We have spoken a lot about adaptability. We want to adapt to different surfaces and we knew certain shots weren't going to work on this pitch. We probably didn't execute our skills well enough.

"The bigger picture is that there is a World Cup in South Africa in 12 months' time and these experiences - we try to bank them and learn from them as much as we can. We are not out of this series."

"He is a fantastic young kid - I would love to live my life like him: carefree, loves the ocean, loves learning about fast bowling.

Sports.title: 'It's the match people wanted' - Pegula to face Andreeva at WTA Finals
Sports.content:
Jessica Pegula saved a match ‌point en route to a gritty 7-6 (7-2) 4-6 7-5 win over Linda Noskova to advance to the semi-finals at the WTA Finals and ​send fellow American Coco Gauff packing from the season-ending championships.

Pegula enjoyed a career-high 16 aces while Wimbledon champion Noskova suffered a career-high 15 double faults in a see-saw battle that spanned a remarkable two ​hours and 45 minutes in one of the matches of the year.

Noskova had already reached the semi-finals but Pegula's victory eliminated Gauff despite her 6-4 7-5 victory against Ukrainian Marta Kostyuk earlier.

Gauff, Pegula and Noskova all finished the group stage 2-1. Noskova went 5-2 in sets to win the group, followed by Pegula at 5-3 and Gauff at 4-3.

"I've learned that sometimes the serve feels good and sometimes it doesn't, and how to manage ​the days when it doesn't and to ride it when you are serving well," Pegula told reporters.

"I don't think I served that well in my first couple matches and I served great today. Sometimes there's no ​rhyme or reason."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jessica Pegula was caught on WTA livestream calling Mirra Andreeva a 'diva' and saying the 19-year-old needs to be 'humbled'

The win sets up a grudge clash between Pegula and teenager Mirra Andreeva in ‌the semi-finals on Saturday.

"It's the match people wanted, well now you are going to get it," said Pegula.

Pegula called Andreeva "a diva" who "needs to be humbled" but the American didn't realise that her remarks were being livestreamed during ‌a practice session before the tournament.

Pegula also praised the world No 3, although she later apologised to those involved.

"She's fast, she has a great serve, she's strong, she hits the ball pretty hard and she's smart," Pegula said.

"I'm going to do my best."

WTA chair Valerie Camillo later apologised to Pegula for the "regrettable" incident.

Noskova, meanwhile, will face the winner of Friday's round-robin match between Aryna Sabalenka and Elina Svitolina.

Gauff beats ‌alternate but misses semi-finals

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Coco Gauff against Marta Kostyuk from the WTA Finals

Earlier, Gauff rallied to beat Kostyuk on a sun-soaked Stadium Two at Indian Wells.

After sealing the first set with a volley ​that sent fans leaping to their feet, Gauff ​rallied from 1-5 down in the second, winning six games in a row.

"I was fully prepared ​to play a third set there," said Gauff, who needed treatment on her back during the second ⁠set.

"It's the last tournament of the season so I just wanted to finish it on a high note and give myself the best chance to play the semi-finals. Either way, I didn't want to be sad walking off the court."

Before Pegula and Noskova took the court, Gauff said she had a back-up plan for Saturday in Los Angeles, where Tyler, the Creator's Camp Flog Gnaw Carnival is taking place this weekend.

"But I'm hoping not to be there," Gauff said.

Kostyuk, who won ⁠the Madrid title and reached the French Open semi-finals, was ​already eliminated coming into her match having lost to Noskova and Pegula.

Kostyuk joined the ​eight-player tournament as an alternate after world No 1 Elena Rybakina withdrew due to illness, but failed to win a set in her three matches as she struggled with a ‌wrist injury.

Sports.title: Las Vegas GP: UK schedule and how to watch on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Formula 1 heads for the bright lights of Las Vegas with both 2026 titles settled, but the competitive picture at the front of the grid tighter than it has been at any other stage of the season.

The Las Vegas Strip Circuit opens the triple header of events that conclude the campaign with the race on the streets of Sin City quickly followed by a fortnight in the Middle East for the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix.

Last time out at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Mercedes completed a title double by sealing the Constructors' Championship a week on from Kimi Antonelli becoming F1's youngest ever world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Despite closing out both championships, Mercedes are actually enduring their most difficult period of the season, with their rivals regularly outperforming them.

McLaren's Lando Norris claimed his third win of the season in Brazil, while Ferrari may well have claimed a one-two the weekend before in Mexico had Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc not clashed on the first lap.

Max Verstappen has featured on the last eight podiums, a run which has moved the Red Bull driver 17 points clear of Antonelli's team-mate George Russell in the battle for second in the standings, with Hamilton just a point further back.

The race for third in the constructors' standings is also very much on, with Red Bull just 17 points clear of McLaren. The duel for seventh is also tight with Haas only three points ahead of Audi.

That will ensure there is plenty to play for as F1 makes its fourth appearance at the stunning street circuit since Las Vegas returned to the sport's calendar in 2023.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix in the USA

With all track sessions running in the late afternoon or evening local time in Vegas, which is eight hours behind the UK and Ireland.

Sky Sports F1 viewers need to set their alarms - or, in the case of first and final practice, perhaps just stay up late - to watch the weekend's sessions live. Qualifying and the Grand Prix itself both start at 4am GMT.

Full F1 session re-runs will also be shown on Sky Sports F1 and Main Event each morning, while there will also be highlights available to watch on the Sky Sports website and app.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen, Lando Norris and George Russell are driven to the podium in a pink lego Cadillac by White Chicks star Terry Crews - only in Las Vegas!

Las Vegas GP track - Las Vegas Strip Circuit

Considered F1's most ambitious project to bring racing to the heart of Las Vegas and the city's world-renowned Strip, the street track runs to 3.8 miles in length and features 17 corners.

The layout winds past some of Vegas' most famous landmarks, such as the Venetian, the Bellagio Fountains and the Eiffel Tower at Paris, and features a 1.2-mile flat-out blast down the Strip.

With an average speed of 150mph across Russell's dry-weather pole position lap in 2024 (2025's qualifying was wet), Vegas represents F1's second-fastest street track after the Jeddah Corniche Circuit in Saudi Arabia. It has also proved itself to be good for racing, with plenty of overtaking and action over the first three years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson and Jenson Button talk you through the Las Vegas Grand Prix Strip Circuit

Las Vegas GP weather

With the race again taking place late in November, the 2026 edition is set to follow the pattern of the first three events in terms of weather conditions.

Day-time temperatures in the mid-high teens are set to be followed by chilly evenings as temperatures drop towards single figures in Nevada's Mojave Desert. No rain is currently forecast during track days.

Sports.title: England and Ireland's points battle, the return of Jones and France's Springboks clash
Sports.content:
The second weekend of Nations Championship Tests brings an England-Ireland points battle, Eddie Jones’ return to Twickenham and an injury-hit France facing the Springboks.

Points race for England and Ireland

Heading into the fifth weekend of six Nations Championship rounds - split between July in the southern hemisphere and November in Europe - England and Ireland have near-identical records.

Even with bonus points in play, Steve Borthwick's side and Andy Farrell's Ireland are set for a close finish, with their final standings potentially determining who reaches the title decider.

Both currently sit on 15 competition points, but England are 42 points better off in terms of points difference at the moment, owing to the fact they beat Fiji 73-8 in July, and added to that with a handsome 45-22 home success over Australia last week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Maro Itoje gives a passionate defence of Steve Borthwick after England's defeat of Australia at Twickenham

England's Nations Championship fixtures and results South Africa 45-21 England July 4 Fiji 8-73 England July 11 Argentina 24-31 England July 18 England 45-22 Australia November 8 England vs Japan Saturday, November 14 (4.40pm) England vs New Zealand Saturday, November 21 (2.10pm)

In July, Ireland edged a high-scoring win over Australia to claim a bonus point, followed it up with another bonus-point victory over Japan (despite winning by just 16 points), before losing to the All Blacks at Eden Park without securing a bonus point for either a narrow defeat or scoring four tries

On home soil, Ireland then dispatched of Argentina 42-12 last week, but failed to score a point in the final quarter of the Test, which they may yet pay for.

Ireland's Nations Championship fixtures and results Australia 31-33 Ireland July 4 Japan 20-36 Ireland July 11 New Zealand 40-21 Ireland July 18 Ireland 42-12 Argentina November 6 Ireland vs Fiji Saturday, November 14 (8.10pm) Ireland vs South Africa Saturday, November 21 (4.40pm)

For England, they lost to South Africa at Ellis Park without banking any losing bonus points, then annihilated Fiji in Liverpool and held on to win in Argentina with a crucial bonus point.

Last week's morale-boosting win over Australia has now given England a great chance of at least finishing second and facing one of South Africa or New Zealand on finals weekend at Twickenham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England captain Maro Itoje has warned his side need to be 'alive' when facing Japan at Twickenham on Saturday

For Ireland to overtake England, they must outperform them across the final two rounds. That means beating South Africa in Dublin while hoping New Zealand defeat England at Twickenham, or securing more bonus points in defeat to the Springboks than England manage against the All Blacks.

With comfortable wins expected for England and Ireland against Japan and Fiji respectively this Saturday, the Irish are unlikely to make significant inroads into England's substantial points-difference advantage.

Instead, it is likely to come down to bonus points.

Jones stoking the flames on his return as Japan seek huge shock

Former England head coach Eddie Jones is plotting a historic upset, backing Japan to stun England at Allianz Stadium on Saturday.

The Brave Blossoms have lost all six previous Tests against England and are 40-1 outsiders to pull off a seismic Nations Championship shock.

But Jones, who coached England from 2016 to 2022, is preparing a few surprises for his former side.

"It's a big week for Japanese rugby," Jones said this week. "We realise England are a nation we've never been able to beat.

"Everyone knows the record and we want to do something a bit different this week and we've trained like that, so I'm really pleased with the team.

"We've had really good training to prepare us for the game we are expecting against England.

Image: Former England head coach Eddie Jones, now in charge of Japan, has been speaking to media this week ahead of his side playing at Twickenham

"We had two days of very settled and pretty training but Wednesday was quite dirty. We had to adapt to certain situations and in the end we did it really well.

"I was really pleased with the players, really pleased with their effort, really pleased with the way they adapted to the situations.

"I'm looking forward to going to Twickenham with this young Japanese team that's going to play the house down."

Jones remains England's most successful coach by win rate, with 72 per cent, having won two Six Nations titles, including the 2016 Grand Slam. He also guided England to the 2019 World Cup final, but his tenure ended acrimoniously, with his side booed by fans in 2022.

"If you look at the stats, they stand the test of time," Jones said. "So there's no reason why I shouldn't be pleased to go back to Twickenham."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Alex Coles looks ahead to England's Nations Championship Test against Japan, and chats memories of Jones' 'tough love'

The 66-year-old has been doing the media rounds this week, also saying his Japan side are aiming to "make the Twickenham sky fall in on" Steve Borthwick's "distracted" charges in Saturday's Test.

Injury-hit France welcome Springboks to Paris in blockbuster

Two of the world's top sides go head-to-head on Friday as France host South Africa.

The Springboks insist they have no special plans to contain Antoine Dupont at fly-half, instead trusting their defence to limit the space available to the French playmaker.

With Romain Ntamack injured and Matthieu Jalibert already ruled out, Dupont will wear the No 10 jersey, with Maxime Lucu at scrum-half.

Both are more accustomed to playing at nine but have featured at fly-half for their clubs, and South Africa expect the pair to interchange positions during the match.

Image: France's Antoine Dupont is having to play at fly-half vs South Africa due to an injury crisis ruling out Matthieu Jalibert and Romain Ntamack

"He's [Dupont] played at 10 before for his ​club [Toulouse], and we saw the game where he played there. He was very good," captain Siya Kolisi told reporters on Thursday.

"I mean, he can play almost anywhere ​on the field, so I don't think it is a surprise to ⁠see him there.

"Obviously, nobody wants injuries, ⁠but every team experiences them and you have to adjust. He's a good enough player to do it. He's shown ‌that over the years."

Carrick and his backroom staff were dismissed on Thursday, with Pochettino expected to bring his trusted lieutenants from previous roles with him. It will cost United £7m in compensation to secure the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss. Share

2h ago 04.20 EST A Poch timeline for you. The official announcement is expected later today but Pochettino won’t arrive at the club until next Wednesday. Here’s how the next 10 days look: Friday 13 November: United are set to confirm his appointment.

Saturday 14 November: He takes charge of the USA in the first leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti in Miami (9.30pm UK time).

Tuesday 17 November: He leads the USA for the last time, in the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati (midnight UK time).

Wednesday 18 November: He flies to Manchester to meet his new bosses.

Thursday 19 November: He takes his first training session with the players.

Sunday 22 November: His first game in charge is Liverpool away at Anfield (4.30pm). Gulp! Share Updated at 04.24 EST

The stats say yes: only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Pochettino.
