Sports.title: David Warner unloads on Pat Cummins for throwing Usman Khawaja 'under the bus' over Sandpapergate - as he links the saga to his wife Candice's miscarriage: 'Life punishment'
Sports.content:
David Warner has accused Australian Test captain Pat Cummins of throwing Usman Khawaja 'under the bus' over Sandpapergate, as he opened up about the miscarriage his wife Candice suffered in the aftermath of the ball-tampering scandal.

Earlier on Friday, Cummins dismissed Khawaja's claim that the entire Australian team knew about the plan to use sandpaper in South Africa in 2018 as 'complete and utter nonsense'.

He also accused his former teammate of being 'casual with lives and reputations' and insisted there had been no team meeting to discuss collective responsibility and no 'masterplan around using illegal methods'.

Warner defended his childhood friend Khawaja while commentating on Fox Cricket before Australia's one-day international against England at Perth's Optus Stadium on Friday.

He spoke about the toll the scandal had taken on his family, saying he and his wife had paid the heaviest price and linked it to her miscarriage.

'Yes we accepted it, but at the end of the day my wife and I copped the greatest price; we lost a baby during that time, and that's why it really hurts me the most until the truth is accepted,' he said.

He described Cummins' response to his friend's claims in Khawaja's recently released biography as 'very well prepared'.

'I still stick by what Uzzie's written in that book; it's the truth,' Warner said.

David Warner accused Australian Test captain Pat Cummins of throwing Usman Khawaja 'under the bus' on Friday while commentating for Fox Cricket

David Warner and his wife Candice lost their unborn child a week after they returned home following the Sandpapergate scandal in South Africa

'I support him [Usman] and I actually feel for him at the moment.

'I actually feel that the captain today threw Uzzie under the bus and I'm very, very disappointed.'

Warner, former Test captain Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft received lengthy bans from Cricket Australia over their involvement in the scandal.

'All three of us have paid a big price - I hadn't spoken about it in eight years, but at the end of the day we have to live with these consequences daily, and we've been served a life punishment.

'When other people talk about [being affected] by it, there's nothing worse than for me, Steve and Cameron who have to walk out there every single day and cop abuse.'

Warner said he had spoken to Khawaja and Bancroft and that both were 'quite upset' by what had transpired.

'In the eight years since, not one of those people in that changeroom have spoken to us about it… the mateship that we talk about, the honesty that you have with each other, there's been no contact or questions about it,' he said.

'We're all adults and we're open to conversation; I've played golf with Pat Cummins a couple of times, I've been in changerooms and we've won a couple of World Cups, and its just never been questioned.'

Warner said that he and his wife Candice paid the heaviest price over Sandpapergate.

He addressed Cummins' claims while commentating for Fox Cricket on Friday

'At the end of the day Pat's not going to agree with me (and) I'm not going to agree with him; he's obviously spoken about what he thinks about Uzzie and his book, but I stand by Uzzie's comments.'

When Fox Cricket co-commentator and Aussie cricket great Adam Gilchrist asked if another investigation by CA was required, Warner noted that CA boss Todd Greenberg 'squashed that the other day'.

'It's been very difficult because the way it was handled in the first place, it was hard to go back and give more evidence,' Warner said.

'It felt like it was a botched investigation; it was a quick one to get it over and done with. Some of the questions were quite challenging in the way it was planted on us and we had to move on and just accept responsibility (the three of us).'

Former England captain Michael Vaughan asked Warner if he had 'absolute proof' that more players knew about the sandpaper tactics.

'There will be conversations behind the scenes after all this,' Warner said.

Warner commentated during the match alongside Alyssa Healy, who is married to his former teammate Mitchell Starc. Starc has previously denied any knowledge of the sandpaper tactics.

Warner's wife, Candice, previously revealed she had suffered a miscarriage a week after the couple and their young daughters returned to Sydney from South Africa following the scandal.

Australian Test captain Pat Cummins has broken his silence on Usman Khawaja's explosive 'Sandpapergate' claims

Left to right: Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon and Starc, all four bowlers who played in the Cape Town Test match and have denied they knew sandpaper was being taken onto the field

Khawaja and Cummins together on the sidelines during a Test match in 2018

'I woke up feeling pretty ordinary. I called Dave to the bathroom and told him I was bleeding. We knew I was miscarrying and we held one another and cried,' Candice told Nine's Now to Love at the time.

'The miscarriage was a tragic consequence, a heartbreaking end to a horror tour. Like so many families who've experienced a miscarriage, it's just really sad.

'The entire ordeal, from the public humiliations to the ball tampering, it had taken its toll and, from that moment, we decided that no sport, nothing will ever impact our lives like that again.

'At the time, I felt like I'd let us down – that my body had let us down – but I've come a long way since then. I'm a very spiritual person and I truly believe it wasn't their time to be with us. Despite our terrible loss, I do know without any doubt that my calling in life is to be a mum.'

The Warners welcomed their third daughter a year after the miscarriage.

Earlier on Friday, Cummins reiterated the statement he put out in 2021 with fellow bowlers Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon denying all knowledge of the plans.

'When Khawaja says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100 per cent wrong,' he told reporters.

'I've said that consistently for the last eight years.

'[Usman] says that I and others were architects of a scheme to ball tamper with sandpaper. That's complete and utter nonsense.

'It's something I've actually been grappling with the last couple days... Usman is a friend, but I think the way he's been quite casual and flippant with people's lives and reputations... I don't think that's okay, and I don't think that's what friends do.'

A reporter then asked: 'So, one of you is not telling the truth, which one of you is not telling the truth?'

Cummins replied: 'Well, that's my story. So, I think [Usman's] wrong,' adding that he wouldn't be pursuing legal action over the claims.

Sports.title: Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Why England were unremarkable on Harry Kane's big night, the Ben White problem - and established star whose place could be under threat from Morgan Rogers, writes IAN LADYMAN

England will head to Spain on Sunday for a Nations League shoot out with the World Champions. A win in Madrid could see Thomas Tuchel's team progress to the quarter-finals next March as group winners.

It wasn't always easy on Harry Kane's big night at Wembley against Croatia, though. Indeed this was probably England's worst performance since losing to Argentina in the World Cup semi-final last July.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the key issues emerging from last night's tight squeeze.

Self-defeating abuse of White is madness and must stop

In case nobody has noticed, England are not over stocked with competent right-backs.

Trent Alexander-Arnold isn't wholly trusted in big games by Thomas Tuchel, Reece James is always injured and Tino Livramento has also struggled to be available. Why, then, is a significant section of the England support so determined to drive Ben White away from the international scene?

White plays for Arsenal, the champions of England. He is a fine, versatile defender who would be gratefully received and appreciated by fans of most national teams in world football. He had issues with the previous England management regime and does not apologise for that.

Ben White was booed when he came on. The abuse towards the defender must stop

He spoke about it this week and made it clear he didn't wish to reopen old wounds. All that matters now is that he is willing and available. But – despite a plea from Tuchel before this game – England fans still booed him when he came on as a substitute last night.

It's a disgraceful way to treat a footballer who can be an asset to his country going forwards and it's something the England manager cares deeply about. Do we want to win the next Euros or not? Do we want our best players motivated and driven and part of the squad? Or do we want to faff about harbouring old grudges related to a situation in Qatar four winters ago that none of us really know that much about?

The choice is clear. If we are not careful, we will drive a good footballer away from the England set-up for good. It's madness.

Big night for Kane but questions for England

They came to celebrate Harry Kane and the England captain got his goal. Number 92 for the striker. Beneath all the fuss over England's talisman, however, this came perilously close to being a step backwards for Thomas Tuchel's England.

The England manager has been saying since the last international break in September and October that he wanted his team to go to Madrid on Sunday in with a shout at knocking Spain from the top of this Nations League Group. Had Croatia been a little smarter in front of goal at Wembley last night, England would have been heading for a dead rubber against the world champions.

Harry Kane scored on his big night as England edged out a 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley

It was a night to remember for Kane as he was honoured after receiving his record 126th cap

Three times in the last ten minutes of this game, Croatia had good opportunities to score a second goal and take a point from the game that would have been perfectly justified. So England crawled over the line but there was little here that was impressive with questions emerging once again about how capable really are when they don't have the ball.

Kane put it well himself afterwards when he said: 'You can't always expect things to be perfect. Of course, we know we can improve on a few bits and we will need to if we want to win on Sunday.'

Tuchel himself will perhaps have quiet concerns. One of the German's worries about this England team is that they sometimes struggle to take training performances on to the field and this was another case in point.

The ultimate target for this team is to win the home Euros in 2028 and the pressure will need handling in front of their own supporters if they are to do that. With that in mind, it's good to know that the FA are interested in hosting the finals of this Nations League competition next summer.

If England make it through next March's two-legged quarter-finals, they could do with some practice of playing high-stakes games at Wembley.

Who is really number one?

Asked last week on the day he announced his squad whether Jordan Pickford was still his number one goalkeeper, Tuchel was unequivocal.

'He is,' said Tuchel. 'But the competition is on there as well. Like for the outfield players. And James Trafford will get regular starts now, that's what we wanted. They shared the matches last time. There's an opportunity that we maybe do this again.'

Morgan Rogers impressed after opening the scoring inside the opening half-an-hour

Jordan Pickford starting against Croatia could lead to James Trafford playing against Spain

With all this in mind, it was expected that Trafford would start this game with Pickford getting the gloves for the one that really matters in Spain on Sunday. That wasn't the case, so we wait with interest to see what the England manager does in Madrid.

What nobody really wants is for a return to the situation we had in the 1980s when Ron Greenwood used to rotate between the late Ray Clemence and last night's guest of honour Peter Shilton.

England's back four is the one area of this team that can look unconvincing – they did again last night - and the last thing they need is not to know who their goalkeeper is from one match to the next. Tuchel is going to have to make a decision.

Branthwaite has work to do

Interesting that Tuchel chose to put Dan Burn into his team for this game, despite the Newcastle defender not being in the original squad.

With Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa both absent with injuries, Everton's Jarrod Branthwaite would have expected to play on the left of Jarell Quansah here. Instead, Burn leapfrogged him in the queue and maybe we should have paid more attention to something Tuchel said the day before the game.

'Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,' said Tuchel.

Jarrad Branthwaite clearly has a way to go before he's fully trusted to start by Thomas Tuchel

'You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe where they followed in a high press and to man-man. And of course he was with us at the World Cup so he is used a bit more to our style of play.'

That's all very well and logical but – that being the case – why was Branthwaite chosen ahead of Burn in the original group of 25 last Friday? Burn, as it happened, had a very good game last night.

Could Saka miss the train?

Tuchel talks always about the value of players being in camp. 'The train is leaving the station,' is one of the England manager's more memorable quotes of recent times. Players like Cole Palmer, for example, have learned to their cost that missing meet-ups with injuries can be costly.

Bukayo Saka is not in that category and has plenty of credit in the bank with the England manager. However, Tuchel's fondness for Morgan Rogers is well known and Saka's absence does give him a way of getting the Chelsea player into his team. Rogers may be a number ten at heart but he was effective once again here out on the right side.

The 24-year-old was one of England's better players on a muted night against Croatia and he deserved his first half goal. He gives England a more direct, athletic dimension on the opposite flank to the more balletic offerings of Anthony Gordon. Food for thought for Tuchel at least as Saka continues his own battle against persistent injuries.

Bukayo Saka's long-term place in England's team could be under threat from Morgan Rogers

United should have moved for Hall

Newcastle United were pretty much an open door in the summer as they sold players left right and centre. Gordon to Barcelona to make sure the club was the right side of the financial guidelines and then Sandro Tonali to Tottenham and Bruno Guimaraes to Arsenal simply because the players made it known they wanted to go.

Strange, then, that Manchester United didn't make a proper move for left-back Lewis Hall. Admittedly this wasn't the most difficult match in which he will have ever played, but Hall was impressive once again.

With Luke Shaw so injury prone, Hall pretty much has the left-back berth sewn up for England but it feels as though he now needs to make the next step in his club career. United retain a nominal interest but who knows what incoming manager Mauricio Pochettino may think? It's hard to work out why United didn't try harder to sign him last summer. He has subsequently signed a new contract at Newcastle, of course.

Sports.title: Paige Spiranac addresses speculation she was to blame for golf YouTuber's split from his fiancée
Sports.content:
Golf influencer Paige Spiranac is strongly denying rumors that she was at the center of a fellow content creator's recent breakup.

Barstool Sports' Internet Invitational saw Spiranac playing alongside Robby Berger - also known as Bob Does Sports - where the two shared some lighthearted moments.

Social media latched onto the playful banter between the two, with some suggesting that the bombshell was one of the reasons why Berger called off his engagement to his ex-fiancée, Narod.

In a post to X, Spiranac denied that she played any role in the couple's separation. She then deleted that post afterwards.

The only evidence of her denial posts came through from an account that made a joke about Spiranac and Berger, who then replied to her and said, 'Thank you Paige. I will destroy the rumors and those that try to spread it.'

The two content creators are frequent collaborators over the years, which has given a rise to such rumors.

I got absolutely smoked here by @RobbyBerger pic.twitter.com/0GTpUaVmy5 — Paige Spiranac (@PaigeSpiranac) November 13, 2026

Golf influencer Paige Spiranac has denied rumors she split up a content creator's engagement

Spiranac was caught in some candid moments with Robby Berger - also known as Bob Does Sports - during Barstool Sports' Internet Invitational golf tournament, which led to rumors that she may have had some influence in Berger breaking off his engagement earlier this year

The bombshell denied the allegations with a now-deleted post on X

At one point during the competition, Berger joked that one of their fellow competitors looked like 'he had tears in his eyes,' before adding, 'Imagine crying on a golf course.'

Whether intentional or not, it was a call back to last year's Internet Invitational where Spiranac broke down in sobs after being accused of illegally improving her lie.

It took Spiranac a few seconds to realize what Berger had said before whipping her head at him with a disapproving look. Berger then looked away while biting his bottom lip.

Berger announced that he had called off his engagement in August of this year on an episode of his podcast.

'Been a really really tough couple months, it really has... I have a lot of love for her, I have a lot of love for her family and all, and I think it makes it harder when you do have a lot of love - to nobody's fault of each other. It just, it wasn't meant to be,' he said over the summer.

'We split a couple months ago, you know, we were engaged and it didn't work out. It's been a really, really tough time. It wasn't meant to be and, looking forward to at least trying to move forward.'

Sports.title: Pat Cummins reveals his wife urged him to 'be honest' about Sandpapergate after Usman Khawaja's bombshell claims: 'People are hurting'
Sports.content:
Pat Cummins reveals his wife urged him to 'be honest' about Sandpapergate after Usman Khawaja's bombshell claims: 'People are hurting'

Pat Cummins has laughed off suggestions he was arguing with his wife, Rebecca, after they were photographed having an animated exchange outside their Sydney home, as Usman Khawaja's autobiography reignited the Sandpapergate saga.

In a lengthy Sydney press conference on Friday, Cummins addressed dozens of questions about the ball-tampering exposed during the third Test of the tour in Cape Town in 2018.

He described Usman Khawaja's claims that the whole Australian team knew about the plan as 'complete and utter nonsense', and accused Khawaja of being 'casual with lives and reputations'.

Cummins then addressed News Corp photographs of him and his wife in a heated discussion beside their car on Wednesday afternoon.

He was barefoot and alternated between pacing and leaning against the car, while Becky did much of the talking.

But on Friday, Cummins laughed off the interaction, and revealed his wife was actually upset with his former teammate.

'It's… very comical. Becky wears her heart on her sleeve. We weren't having a spat. Becky was very frustrated, animated and really not happy with Usman,' he said.

'She's always just said to be honest and tell the details and put your washing away.'

Pat Cummins has laughed off claims of a marital row after being photographed in an animated exchange with wife Rebecca outside their Sydney home

Cummins revealed his wife was actually furious with his former teammate, not her husband, as Usman Khawaja's allegations reignited the Sandpapergate saga

Mrs Cummins appeared to put the speculation to rest by sharing a sweet family photograph on her Instagram Story

Cummins added that his wife had witnessed all major events throughout his career.

'I've been with Becky since well before that tour, so she's seen everything. She leaves it all with me,' he said.

'So, she's just saying, like, show your emotion because there are a lot of people here hurting.'

He also expressed his frustration at being filmed during what he described as a private family moment.

'It's all a bit ridiculous, isn't it? Like, we're here talking about something that was dealt with eight and a half years ago [and] now I'm walking my daughter, one-year-old daughter in a nappy out the front, and I've got cameras chasing me and my family,' he said.

Hours after the couple were photographed having an animated discussion, Rebecca shared an affectionate family photo on her Instagram Story.

In the image, Rebecca rested her head against her husband as he held their daughter, Edith, whose face was hidden from view. She tagged Cummins and captioned the photo: 'My loves'.

The Australian cricket community erupted after Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, was released on Tuesday.

Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, released on Tuesday, alleges knowledge of the ball-tampering scandal extended beyond the three players Cricket Australia sanctioned over the incident

Cummins also expressed his frustration at being filmed during what he described as a private family moment

The book alleges knowledge of the ball-tampering scandal extended beyond Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft, the three players Cricket Australia sanctioned over the incident.

Bancroft was caught using sandpaper on the ball during the third Test in Cape Town in March 2018.

Smith and Warner were handed 12-month bans and stripped of their captaincy and vice-captaincy, respectively, while Bancroft received a nine-month suspension.

Khawaja's account has now placed renewed scrutiny on Australia's bowling attack, which included Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon.

'It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us,' he told the Sydney Morning Herald ahead of the book's release.

In a joint statement in 2021, the four bowlers maintained they had no knowledge that a foreign substance had been brought onto the field to alter the ball's condition during the Cape Town Test.

Khawaja, meanwhile, faced further questions about his account during an appearance on ABC's 7.30, including whether he was frustrated that the bowlers had not acknowledged knowing about the sandpaper.

'I'll say again, I've given my statement about what happened the game before. I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had,' he said.

Khawaja admitted he was unsure what the fallout from the revelations could mean for his friendship with Cummins

Khawaja has since cancelled several media appearances although he denied withdrawing from his book tour

'Sometimes I'm very specific on things, and sometimes I'm a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I'm trying to tell a story.'

When pressed further about the bowlers, Khawaja refused to elaborate.

'I'm not going to entertain that. I'm not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment,' he said.

He also admitted he was unsure what the fallout from the revelations could mean for his friendship with Cummins.

'I've told my truth, and I'd give him my reasons,' Khawaja said.

'Pat Cummins is a good friend of mine. Mitchell Starc, a lot of these guys, players in the team, Shaun Marsh, Mitch Marsh, are all very good friends of mine. I'm not here to go on a witch hunt.'

Khawaja has since cancelled several media appearances, including an interview with Seven News, although he denied withdrawing from his book tour.

Australian Cricketers' Association chief executive Todd Greenberg has said there would be 'absolutely no benefit' in reopening the investigation.

It has also been reported that CA chairman David Boon has backed Cummins and assured him his position as captain is secure.

Before the latest allegations emerged, Cummins insisted the team had already answered questions about the scandal repeatedly.

'It's obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times,' he said ahead of Australia's recent tour of South Africa.

'It was dealt with then. All I can say is, as a group, we've moved on.'

Cummins also revealed Khawaja had given him some warning about the contents of his book.

'He didn't go into too much detail... As always it was "no worries, you can tell your story, that's fine",' he said.

Sports.title: Dele Alli in line for enormous payday with ex-Tottenham star set for life
Sports.content:
Dele Alli in line for enormous payday with ex-Tottenham star set for life

As Mauricio Pochettino heads towards Manchester United, his former protege Dele Alli is set to make a fortune with his latest deal

View 3 Images Dele Alli was at Tottenham's home clash against Arsenal in February (Image: 2026 Marc Atkins)

Dele Alli is set to earn up to £8.3million in assets by closing his image rights company. The former England and Tottenham Hotspur golden boy was recently told by the tax man he owes £685,362 in corporation tax.

‌



‌



He is currently a free agent after being released by Serie A heavyweights Como last year, after only playing one match for Cesc Fabregas' side. It's now understood he will be winding up his company, Dele Alli Promotions, which is believed to have assets of up to £8.3m.

‌



A Declaration of Solvency was recently filed after the business was put into liquidation. While this may be a set-back for the ex-England international, who was part of the Three Lions side that reached the 2018 World Cup semi-final, it will also be an enormous payday.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

It's also not the only financial iron he has in the fire. Dele, as he prefers to be known as, has two other lucrative companies to his name which derive from previous investments.

He owns six rental properties, believed to be worth more than £1.5m, which are part of his business Future Homes Investments. In addition, he also boasts another company called Dele Investments, worth a purported £336,267.

‌



While his football career has experienced a freefall over the last three years, it's clear his other financial interests are more than enough for him to fall back on.

View 3 Images Alli only made one official appearance for Como (Image: 2025 Ciancaphoto Studio)

‌



In 2023, Dele opened up about the abusive childhood he experienced when he was of primary school age in a heartbreaking conversation with Gary Neville on The Overlap. The ex-midfielder revealed he was sexually abused when he was only six years old, before being sent to Nigeria to live with his father "to learn discipline".

‌



He also opened up on other awful experiences from his childhood after returning to the UK, including being hung off a bridge when he was 11 years old, as well as being made to sell drugs aged eight.

Juggling these traumas with a high-level football career also resulted in him becoming addicted to sleeping tablets which persisted throughout his career. Looking back, he said: "I got addicted to sleeping tablets and it’s probably a problem that not only I have. I think it’s something that’s going around more than people realise in football.

‌



View 3 Images Alli is still without a club (Image: 2026 Vince Mignott/MB Media)

"With our schedule you have a game, you have to be up early in the morning to train, you have all the adrenaline and stuff so sometimes to take a sleeping tablet and be ready for the next day is fine. But when your dopamine system and you’re as broken as I am it can obviously have the reverse effect, because it does work for the problems you want to deal with and that is the problem – it works until it doesn’t. I definitely abused them.

‌



"I was never really dealing with the problem which was growing and the traumas I had, the feelings I was holding on to; I tried to deal with it all by myself. My adopted family, my brother, there were times they would take me aside crying, asking me to just speak to them about what I was feeling, but I couldn’t do it.

"I lost myself for a few years, I was just turning everyone away, when I had the family that saved my life crying, asking me to tell them what’s wrong, and I just didn’t want to do it.”

Sports.title: Man Utd news LIVE: Mauricio Pochettino contract details leaked with announcement imminent
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino is set to be announced as the next manager of Manchester United

Mauricio Pochettino is set to be confirmed as manager of Manchester United after the club parted ways with Michael Carrick

The arrival of Mauricio Pochettino is set to be imminently announced by Manchester United. He will become the fourth permanent boss since Sir Jim Ratcliffe purchased his minority stake of the club in 2024.

Barring any dramatic developments in the eleventh hour, Pochettino will replace Michael Carrick, who was sacked only a matter of months after being promoted from interim manager to permanent head coach. United took a long time to make their decision on Carrick, but after not being convinced by other candidates such as Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe and Antonio Conte, they have decided Pochettino is their choice.

The Argentine still has two matches to fulfil as manager of the United States - a two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie against Haiti - but after that, he is expected to be in charge when United face Liverpool at Anfield after the international break.

Sports.title: Sacked Man Utd man labelled 'extremely arrogant' was the real target of Bruno Fernandes' anger
Sports.content:
Sacked Man Utd man labelled 'extremely arrogant' was the real target of Bruno Fernandes' anger

Bruno Fernandes broke ranks at Manchester United and one of the sources of his anger has departed the club

View 3 Images Assistant coach Steve Holland has left Manchester United alongside Michael Carrick (Image: Getty)

Steve Holland has been sacked by Manchester United along with manager Michael Carrick. But reports suggest the first-team coach was not as liked as his superior and even caused Bruno Fernandes' ire.

‌



‌



The Carrick era at Old Trafford is over. After just 174 days in the permanent job, which he earned by guiding United to third in the Premier League last term, the Englishman has been given the boot following a dismal start to the season.

‌



United sit 18th in the league, wallowing in the relegation zone, and have won a single top-flight game. Mauricio Pochettino will now be the man to step in and attempt to turn things around.

‌



It wasn't just Carrick who left the club on November 12, however. His coaching staff also waved goodbye, including former England assistant Holland. Whilst Carrick has received a club legend's farewell, Holland may not be as missed.

According to Roundtable, Holland became disliked during his stint at Old Trafford. He was said to be highly regarded when he first joined, but soon began clashing with players.

View 3 Images Holland was allegedly considered arrogant (Image: Getty)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

One source described him as "extremely arrogant" and not a popular figure. It is also understood that Fernandes's comments following a Champions League loss to Como last month were directed at Holland, not just Carrick.

‌



After United were defeated 4-1 by the Italian side, Fernandes gave an explosive post-match interview. He told TNT Sports: "It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball.

"But sometimes when you give too much of the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work."

‌



Questioned about the tactics, Fernandes then opened fire and said: "That's on the manager and on the staff to see it. It's not on me.

View 3 Images Fernandes was dropped following the post-Como comments (Image: Getty)

‌



"I just said, I think sometimes we have to be more brave on the pressure, trying to take a risk of getting that press very high and making them uncomfortable - as they did to us."

It now appears that the reportedly disliked Holland was the catalyst behind the club captain breaking ranks. Holland's fellow coach, Jonathan Woodgate, was said to have been considered too inexperienced by some staff as well.

Article continues below

However, not all of the cohort were judged in such a manner. Reports state that Travis Binnion was respected and goalkeeping coach Craig Mawson was well liked.

Both said farewell alongside Carrick, as did Jonny Evans, with Pochettino to bring in his own staff, including long-time sidekick Jesus Perez.

Anthony Joshua reveals Oleksandr Usyk advice for Tyson Fury fight

Anthony Joshua admits he has been getting some crucial tips by Oleksandr Usyk ahead of next month's all-British showdown with Tyson Fury

View Image Oleksandr Usyk with Anthony Joshua (Image: PA)

Anthony Joshua has been urged by Oleksandr Usyk to 'keep a cool head' in his fight with Tyson Fury.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury will finally go head-to-head on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium. 'AJ' comes into the December dust-up off the back of a second round KO victory over Kristian Prenga, while Fury forced Polish boxing veteran Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool.

‌



For Joshua's knockout win over Prenga - as well as his victory over Jake Paul - the British brawler had been trained by Usyk's team. 'AJ' and the two-time undisputed heavyweight champion are now good friends - just years after their two epic encounters in the ring.

‌



And ahead of next month's all-British showcase between Joshua and Fury, Usyk - who has beaten the 'Gypsy King' twice - has passed on some crucial advice to his close companion. "Usyk will tell me: 'keep a cool head, don't lose yourself in the back and forth,' and that's fair enough," said Joshua on the Mr. Verzace Podcast.

"But ultimately, as I go back to saying, a lot of people are going to tell me what they think is best, but only I can follow myself. If I want to talk, I want to talk, and that's just how I feel. Sports.title: Michael Carrick sacked news: Man Utd players break silence as Pochettino announcement due
Sports.content:
Manchester United have dismissed Michael Carrick after just 10 games of the Premier League season, with Mauricio Pochettino lined up to replace him at Old Trafford

Manchester United have finally dismissed manager Michael Carrick, with Mauricio Pochettino set to replace him.

The worst-kept secret in football is out, with Carrick’s fate sealed following a meeting of the Old Trafford hierarchy - Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox - in Monaco on Wednesday. Carrick arrived at Carrington on Thursday morning, where he was given the bad news, with the club confirming in a statement that they plan to confirm a permanent successor "as quickly as possible".

Barring an eleventh-hour twist, Pochettino will be that man. An agreement in principle has been reached for the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss, who is expected to take charge of two United States matches this week before joining the Red Devils in time for their Premier League trip to Liverpool.

Carrick's future was the source of constant speculation in recent weeks, despite only being made permanent manager during the summer. Under his guidance, the 13-time Premier League winners have put together their worst start in 40 years and find themselves in the relegation zone.

The 45-year-old leaves after securing just one win in 10 league matches since being given the reins permanently. That came all the way back in August against newly-promoted Ipswich Town, though all three promoted sides are now above United in the table.

The former United midfielder was given three games to save his job following a chastening defeats to Como and Bournemouth last month. But two miraculous comebacks in four days, which earned a win against Roma and a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, were not enough to keep him in a job.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

It is understood that Ratcliffe and the Glazers signed off on the recommendation from Wilcox and Berrada, that a change in the dugout was needed. Pochettino is the man they have chosen, with United making contact with USA Soccer to trigger their manager's £7.5million release clause.

We will have all the updates as they come on what promises to be yet another huge day in the recent history of Manchester United...

Sports.title: Two other managers 'interviewed better' than Mauricio Pochettino for Man Utd job
Sports.content:
Two other managers 'interviewed better' than Mauricio Pochettino for Man Utd job

Mauricio Pochettino is linked with taking up tenure at Manchester United as Michael Carrick's successor, but may not be the best man for the task at hand

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino interviewed for the Manchester United job in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino wasn't as convincing as Thomas Tuchel or Roberto De Zerbi when he interviewed for the vacant Manchester United job in 2024. It comes as a worrying revelation, considering the 54-year-old is heavily touted to land at Old Trafford as Michael Carrick's successor in the coming days.

‌



‌



The Red Devils made the decision to part ways with the Englishman on Thursday morning following a poor start to the new Premier League season. The club sit 18th in the English top flight's standings having won just one of their opening 10 fixtures.

‌



While a number of names have been linked with taking up tenure in his place, from Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, to Antonio Conte and Gareth Southgate, Pochettino has emerged as a leading favourite. Reports suggest that the club have reached an agreement in principle with Pochettino's camp, although they will have to pay a small fortune to bring him to the Theatre of Dreams.

‌



That's because Pochettino is under contract with the US national team until 2030, and his release clause is set at $10million (£7.4m). Add that to the severance package that Carrick will have commanded for the early termination of his contract, thought to be around £3m, and the Red Devils have once again will have wasted a large chunk of their war chest in hiring and firing managers.

Michael Carrick sacked LIVE: First Man Utd player breaks silence as Pochettino payments revealed READ MORE :

Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co will be insistent that they enlist the services of the best man for the job to avoid yet another short stint bearing limited return going forward. However, if recent history is anything to go off, then the ideal candidate may not be Pochettino.

‌



The Murphy-born coach is understood to have interviewed for the position in the summer of 2024, when officials were mulling over cutting ties with Erik ten Hag following a disappointing season which saw United finish eighth. While the club ultimately decided to renew their faith in the Dutchman, it is understood that Pochettino wasn't their first-choice in terms of a plan b in the event results didn't improve.

As per the I, insiders say that both Tuchel and De Zerbi gave a better account of themselves during the interview process. With Tuchel taking up tenure with England following Southgate's resigning, and De Zerbi taking the reins of Marseille, United ultimately opted to bring in Sporting CP's Ruben Amorim when things didn't work out as planned with Ten Hag in the October.

‌



View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel also interviewed for the Manchester United job in 2024 (Image: Getty Images)

‌



However, that turned out to be another wrong choice, with the Portuguese mastermind sent packing a little over a year later as a result of poor performances as a result of an incompatible gameplan with the players at hand.

Carrick stepped in on an interim basis, guiding United to a third-place Premier League finish, before receiving a two-year deal with the club this summer. But once again, time and patience has shown that the 45-year-old was the wrong appointment.

‌



Pochettino is now likely to get his chance at the Theatre of Dreams, albeit, with increased pressure to reverse fortunes instantly with an inherited group of players. United have proven that they aren't exactly keen on spending big in the January transfer window, and instead, look to do their business in the summer instead.

Whether those demands will suit Pochettino, who has proven that he can hang with the best teams in the Premier League via previous stints with Chelsea, Tottenham Hotspur and Brighton, remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland draw with Israel in second Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
