Sports.title: F1 2026 calendar update: Imola off the table, no plan B if Iran war escalates
Sports.content:
The Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix which will conclude Formula 1’s 2026 season are set to proceed as planned, provided there is no dramatic escalation of the Iran war.

The Middle Eastern conflict, which started in late February as the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran, has destabilised the region. The calendars of many motorsport championships have been impacted – not least F1’s, whose Saudi Arabian race was cancelled while Bahrain’s round was postponed and hosted in Malaysia.

F1 has been monitoring the situation closely, with a chilly Imola as an alternative season finale on the first weekend of December if Qatar and Abu Dhabi were unable to host their respective events.

Lusail did run its MotoGP round without major issues last weekend, though both Yamaha teams withdrew from the competition due to the geopolitical situation.

10 November was F1’s deadline to provide Imola with a final answer as to whether the Italian track would have to prepare for a grand prix in the next three weeks; it will not.

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Isack Hadjar, Racing Bulls Photo by: Zak Mauger / Motorsport Images

So the 2026 season will end with the planned Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi triple-header, with travel insurance and governments’ travel advice currently allowing it.

However, there’s a caveat: F1 is aware it cannot guarantee the situation won’t change by early December and insists it will prioritise safety if the conflict escalates.

Team bosses have been maintaining a straightforward stance on the matter – they trust F1 and the FIA to make the right calls.

“I trust them to take the best decision for all of us,” Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur commented in Mexico. “Me, personally, I want to race. It doesn't matter where, but I want to race. Now, I will go where they will tell us to go.”

“Stefano and Mohammed have been pretty clear about the situation that Formula 1 follows what the international guidelines are, whether there are travel restrictions, airlines not flying, any warnings in the region, the kind of feedback that local governments are making,” his Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff added in Friday’s press conference at Interlagos. “So not only the promoters, but what the local governments are making. And this is what you need to rely on, in my opinion, and I'm fully with that.

Toto Wolff, Mercedes Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

“I think that if riders stand up, who know nothing geopolitically about what's going on, but have an audience that listens, I think that is something that creates media value. But I would have done the same as MotoGP management has done. You want to ride or drive, go. If you don't want to, don't go. It's as simple as that, and everybody can take their personal decisions on that, and I respect that.

“Of course, you've got to be wary of what's happening in the next few days, a few weeks, and Stefano has his finger on the pulse to monitor that. If things were to get more dangerous and we would get that feedback, then he's going to be the first one, together with Mohammed, to protect the people that were meant to travel. So that's why I'm following their guidance.

“From what I'm hearing internally, it hasn't been raised. It hasn't been a topic. But also there, if someone feels they don't feel comfortable, he or she doesn't feel comfortable travelling, then it's something that I would always respect. And maybe that's an opportunity to give somebody else a chance. It wouldn't change anything for the relationship. I've always respected that some people didn't want to go to certain grands prix, and that's how I see it at the moment.”

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording

Sports.title: FIA reveals ADUO results in final review of 2026 F1 season
Sports.content:
The FIA has announced its final Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities (ADUO) results for the 2026 Formula 1 season, with no changes granted for any of the power unit manufacturers.

From this season, the FIA installed a mechanism in the F1 regulations which allowed power unit manufacturers the ability to make updates, if they fell behind the leading engine, in the form of tokens permitted under a performance scale.

After the first period in 2026, which ran from the Australian Grand Prix to the Canadian GP, it was announced that Red Bull Ford Powertrains emerged as the benchmark, while Mercedes’ internal combustion engine trails by between 2-4%, which gave the German manufacturer to one additional upgrade this year and one more next season.

Ferrari, Audi and Honda fell into the category of being more than 4% behind on ICE power, which grants them two upgrades during the current campaign and two more in 2027.

Red Bull Ford Powertrains asked for a review of the ADUO analysis, which delayed the official publication of the first results, as it disputed the results and being considered the manufacturer with the strongest engine.

As agreed before the start of the season by the teams, the FIA only measures the internal combustion engine, but once a manufacturer qualifies for ADUO, it is also allowed to modify electrical components such as the battery and MGU-K.

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Colin McMaster / LAT Images via Getty Images

So while Red Bull’s rivals have been able to install power unit upgrades across this season, the Milton Keynes-based effort has effectively faced an engine freeze.

In the third and final FIA analysis of ADUO – which took engine data from the Dutch GP up to and including the US GP – there has been no change and therefore no manufacturer will gain or lose its current concessions.

There was also no change in the second ADUO period over the summer.

“For the third period, the relative performance gaps to the leading ICE evolved, but these changes did not result in any additional homologations being granted to the Power Unit Manufacturers,” an FIA report stated.

Given the dispute over how ADUO is measured, the FIA is open to changes in the system in the future, subject to approval from the power unit manufacturers, while FIA single-seater director Nikolas Tombazis is confident the concept is working as desired.

“The FIA has undertaken extensive analysis as part of the review of ADUO this year. Based on the quality of the data and the robustness of the assessment process, we are confident in our findings and the conclusions reached,” Tombazis said.

Nikolas Tombazis, FIA Photo by: Kym Illman / Getty Images

“The first year of implementation has also reinforced our belief that the ADUO concept is the right one for Formula 1.

“However, it is important that the system continues to evolve to ensure it remains efficient, relevant and fit for purpose. To that end, we have been working closely with the power unit manufacturers and teams to explore refinements to the methodology that will support the continued effectiveness of ADUO in future seasons.”

The next ADUO period will start in 2027, covering the opening six races of the F1 season from the Bahrain GP to the Miami GP.

Sports.title: What's behind Piastri's split with Webber – and what it means for his F1 career
Sports.content:
On the Monday after the Formula 1 Brazilian Grand Prix, Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber announced in a joint statement that the latter and Ann Neal would no longer manage the 25-year-old McLaren driver. The timing may come as a surprise – now rather than at the end of the season – but the news itself had been on the cards for some time.

The clearest hint came from Piastri during pre-season testing in Bahrain. While this writer was mainly interested in his opinion of the 2026 cars – which immediately brought a telling smile to Piastri's face – an Australian colleague raised the subject of Webber's changing role.

Read Also: Formula 1 Piastri and Webber terminate management agreement

"There wasn't anything specific, we just made a decision for things to look a bit different," Piastri said on that unusually cold February evening in the Bahrain paddock. "Mark is still very much involved and I've been in contact with him a lot over the last few weeks. He just won't be trackside as much anymore. So that's really the extent of it. There was nothing specific that triggered it."

Although that last point is essentially true, it is clear that the 2025 season was intense on several fronts – including behind the scenes, at least from Webber’s perspective. That was naturally closely linked to the 'papaya rules' through which McLaren tried to treat both drivers as fairly as possible, but which also made life difficult for the team at certain moments, as Andrea Stella frankly admitted at the beginning of this year.

It is no secret that Webber was not always happy with how McLaren handled certain moments on track, nor with the explanation for Piastri's dip in form during the final quarter of the season, which ultimately cost him the world title. It is important to emphasise, however, that a manager's role is also to defend the interests of his own driver, even though there are multiple ways of doing so.

Webber naturally had the experiences from his own Red Bull years in mind and wanted to prevent Piastri from ever being labelled a number two driver in the F1 paddock. In a recent interview with Autosport, former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner even described this as a key part of Webber's mentality, a worldview that Horner believes he brought into the cockpit.

"I think probably the difficulty with Mark was, he motivated himself through adversity. He always drove better when he felt that the world was against him," Horner said. "He could see this talent emerging in Sebastian [Vettel], and he was using everything in his locker to try and destabilise that, or to cause any tension in a way that would then fall back in his favour. I think as a team we were learning how to handle these dynamics."

Watch: Christian Horner on Toto, Abu Dhabi 2021 and Life After Red Bull.

The differences between Red Bull back then and McLaren today are considerable, however. Red Bull was led at the time by Horner and Helmut Marko, two men who were certainly no strangers to the political side of F1, whereas McLaren is now much more engineering-led under Andrea Stella, who constantly emphasises the principles by which he wants to go racing – including fairness. This brings a different dynamic and also means that any attempts to avoid being pushed into a number two role are viewed in a completely different light.

It must be emphasised that McLaren has never formally asked Piastri to change his management, but Autosport understands that the driver himself, with some input from those around him, has formed his own view of what he needs going forward.

In any case, the decision had already been made at the beginning of this year for Webber to take a step back and operate primarily 'behind the scenes' rather than being in the spotlight during race weekends. With hindsight, that was a first step towards this split, which, according to the statement, has come about by mutual agreement. "Following our reduced trackside involvement this season, we have collectively agreed that now is an appropriate time to bring our management agreement to a close," Webber said.

Piastri's development and a new reality in the F1 driver market

Aside from all that, it must also be said that Piastri's situation is very different now from what it was at the beginning of his career. Consequently, what he needs from the people around him has changed as well. This applies in two areas: his experience as a driver and the current situation in the F1 driver market.

In his younger years, Piastri needed Webber's experience as a racing driver more than he does now. When the Australian made his F1 debut at the age of 21 – and was, as Toto Wolff tends to describe young drivers, still a "deer in the headlights" – it helped to have a trusted figure by his side who had already experienced it all. Someone outside the team who was concerned solely with his interests and could help him avoid potential pitfalls.

When Autosport spoke to Piastri in Barcelona during his debut season, that was precisely the added value he highlighted: "Mark’s advice was to not underestimate the challenge of F1 and how big of a step up it is, not just from the cars but from everything: the amount of people you need to interact with, the media commitments, and the sponsor commitments. It's all much higher than before. I think having him reminding me of that before the season started was nice, not to be shocked when I arrived. That's probably been the biggest thing.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren F1 Team, 2nd position, is congratulated by Mark Webber in Parc Ferme Photo by: Steven Tee / Motorsport Images

"But he's very helpful with small driving tips here and there as well, and sometimes thinking of questions for the engineers that don't even come to my head at the moment.

"He's still very sharp. He thinks like a racing driver still and is always trying to get the best out of me."

More than three years later, Piastri has experienced all of this himself and therefore needs that hands-on guidance as a driver less than he did during his rookie season. Logically, this means that a different type of management can now suffice, with different priorities in that respect as well.

Moreover, the situation in the driver market has changed. Piastri is committed to McLaren for the longer term, with a contract running until the end of 2028. Yes, an extraordinary amount has been said and written about Piastri's seat this summer, particularly in light of the Max Verstappen rumours, which have been blown considerably out of proportion by certain publications. In reality, however, the Dutchman indicated that he had come much closer to retiring from F1 than to moving to another team, meaning Piastri has not seriously been looking elsewhere either.

He did describe it as 'flattering' that his name was linked with Red Bull during the summer months, but the reality is that this route appears to be closed for the coming years. After all, Verstappen has extended his contract, meaning Red Bull – provided it gives him a competitive car – has its lead driver in place. And with talents such as Isack Hadjar, Arvid Lindblad and perhaps Nikola Tsolov in the longer term, Red Bull appears perfectly capable of filling its second seat from within its own talent pool.

Add to that the fact that Mercedes and Ferrari also still have long-term lead drivers in Kimi Antonelli and Charles Leclerc, and maintaining and further strengthening his relationship with McLaren seems far more important for Piastri than having contacts elsewhere, for example through Webber at Red Bull. These two factors may still make the timing surprising, but not so much the decision itself to end the partnership after Webber had already taken a step back.

Oscar Piastri, McLaren with Mark Webber Photo by: Getty Images

Finally, it must be said that Webber did play a key role in the early years of Piastri's career, one that should not be forgotten at a moment like this. Indeed, Piastri himself has not forgotten it either, as his quote in the joint statement demonstrates: "I'd like to thank Mark and Ann for all their support and advice over the years. Their guidance has been invaluable, particularly in navigating the beginning of my F1 career. I wish them all the best going forward."

The most important move, of course, was leaving Alpine for McLaren, including Piastri's now-famous tweet. That was a period in which Webber's 'us against the world' mentality, as Horner described it, proved particularly useful. The move also saved Piastri from the quicksand that Alpine was, especially at that time. It is a decision for which he remains grateful, but this phase of his career calls for something different, and that explains why the partnership between two of the four most recent Australian F1 drivers has come to an end.

Webber played an important role in getting Piastri to where he is today, and the current seventh-placed driver in the championship has not forgotten that. But he feels that something different is needed for the next phase of his career, ideally one of harmony within McLaren – and, given all of the above, that is understandable.

Sports.title: Spotlight: FIA pulls F1 reporter’s pass over column calling Leclerc a ‘sneaky b*****d’ | Brief
Sports.content:
The Daily Mail says the FIA has barred its Formula 1 reporter from attending the final three rounds of the world championship as a media representative.

It quotes a letter sent yestreday by FIA general manager Alberto Villareal regarding an article the newspaper published about Ferrari driver Charles Leclerc , whom its F1 correspondent Jonathan McEvoy called a “sneaky little b*****d”.

“The FIA considers that your article falls short of the standards of professionalism expected of media representatives accredited to cover the FIA Formula One World Championship,” said Villareal, quoted by the newspaper.

“Accordingly, the FIA has decided to exercise its discretion under the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Accreditation Guidelines to withdraw your media accreditation for the remainder of the 2026 season, with immediate effect.”

Three rounds of the season remain in the USA, Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

Earlier this year Max Verstappen ordered the removal of another journalist, Giles Richards of The Guardian, from a Red Bull press conference. Verstappen was unhappy Richards asked him three months earlier whether he regretted colliding with George Russell during last year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix.

Sports.title: Grosjean admits his single-seater career is likely over after ending IndyCar season 19th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Former Formula 1 driver Romain Grosjean, who survived a fireball crash six years ago in Bahrain, is preparing to call time on his single-seater racing career.

Grosjean raced in F1 between 2009 and 2020, then switched to IndyCar. He completed his fifth season in the series this year but the 40-year-old admits he is unlikely to return.

“The reality is, this is probably the end for me with single-seaters,” Grosjean told Racer.

Grosjean finished on the podium three times in his first season in IndyCar with Coyne, earning the attention of top team Andretti, who hired him for the 2022 season. The team replaced him after he finished 13th in the championship for two years running,

After spending one year at Juncos Hollinger, Grosjean lost his drive for 2025, but returned with Coyne this year. The season began promisingly when he reached the final round of qualifying in St Petersburg, but a string of finishes outside the top 10 followed.

The Coyne driver finished on the podium just once all year. He ended the season 19th in the standings ahead of just six other full-time drivers, including RLL’s Mick Schumacher, who replaced him at Haas in 2021.

Grosjean said it had been a “tough” season overall. “I had [a] few amazing moments. I got the chance to lead the Indy 500. I finished in the top 10. I ran [in] the top five most of the last 60 laps. Amazing! I got a podium in Markham, which was incredible with my ‘tractor.’

“But then we go to Milwaukee and Laguna Seca, and [at] Laguna Seca, I qualified dead last, almost. I know it’s one of my fastest tracks, so I’m like, ‘I don’t want that anymore.’ I’ve had enough of those moments where you just don’t have the tools to play.”

Grosjean was supposed to contest his final grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. However the burns he suffered in his Bahrain crash forced him out early. His former team Haas gave him the opportunity to test one of its cars at Mugello last year.

Sports.title: Court of Appeal to hear Audi’s case over Tsunoda decision on November 25th | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The International Court of Appeal has set a date to hear Audi’s appeal over the Italian Grand Prix stewards’ decision regarding Yuki Tsunoda.

Audi is challenging the decision not to penalise Tsunoda, who finished the race in 10th position, for triggering an extra formation lap before the start of the race.

The ICA will hear the case on November 25th at the FIA’s headquarters in Paris.

Tsunoda, who substituted for Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson at Monza, finished seven seconds ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto. Therefore the Audi driver could gain a point if Tsunoda is penalised.

Bortoleto previously said Audi’s case was “straightforward”.

F1’s sporting regulations state any driver who causes an extra formation lap must start the race from the pit lane and will receive a Stop-and-Go penalty if they fail to. As Tsunoda did not start from the pit lane, Audi believes he should receive a penalty.

The stewards ruled Tsunoda “was not the ’cause’ of the extra formation lap” and therefore did not have to start from the pit lane.

This is the second time this year the ICA has been asked to rule on a decision taken by the stewards at a grand prix. In September they reinstated two penalties which were originally issued to Pierre Gasly during the Monaco Grand Prix and later rescinded.

ICA hearing announcement

On 6th September 2026, at the end of the formation lap during the race restart following a red flag, the race director ordered an additional formation lap Following the race, the stewards investigated a potential breach of Article B5.9.4 of the 2026 FIA Formula 1 Sporting Regulations by Mr Yuki Tsunoda (driver of car number 22), which requires any driver who caused an extra formation lap to start from the end of the pit lane. Failure to do so, a Stop-and-Go penalty should be imposed on the driver. In decision number 69, the stewards decided to take no further action against Mr Yuki Tsunoda. On 9th September 2026, Audi Revolut F1 Team lodged an appeal against that decision, arguing that Mr Yuki Tsunoda had caused the extra formation lap and should therefore have received the prescribed Stop-and-Go penalty.

Sports.title: Racing Bulls keep Lawson and Lindblad as Tsolov gets Red Bull reserve role | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Racing Bulls has confirmed an unchanged driver line-up for the 2027 Formula 1 season.

Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad will continue to drive for the team next year.

The news ends speculation Red Bull’s second Formula 1 team would replace either of its drivers with Nikola Tsolov. The Red Bull junior driver lies second in the Formula 2 standings with four races remaining.

Shortly after Racing Bulls confirmed its driver line-up, Red Bull announced Tsolov as its reserve driver for 2027. Red Bull also announced Tsolov will be Racing Bulls’ reserve driver.

Racing Bulls is on course to score its best championship result under any of its identities, including its time competing as Minardi, before it was purchased by Red Bull at the end of 2005.

However Lawson’s future at the team came into doubt as Racing Bulls delayed its decision on its driver line-up for next year. Lawson made his F1 debut in 2023 and gained promotion to Red Bull in 2025 but the team dropped him after just two rounds. Lawson made a temporary return to Red Bull this year as a substitute for the injured Isack Hadjar.

During his time at Racing Bulls, Lawson has scored enough points to single-handedly put Racing Bulls fifth in the constructors’ championship. However he clashed with Red Bull driver Max Verstappen during a practice session in Mexico earlier this month, which his rival said was “not very smart behaviour” for a driver who was “fighting for [his] seat”. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies denied his team would have any say in its junior squad’s driver line-up.

Racing Bulls team principal Alan Permane said Lawson and his rookie team mate Lindblad form “the best driver line-up for us, bringing a strong combination of experience and ambition”.

“Together, we have a solid foundation to build on the progress made this year, continue pushing ourselves forward and take the next step towards achieving our ambitions in 2027.”

Tsolov said he hopes to make the step up to F1 after next year. “My ambition is clear: I want to become an F1 driver,” he said. “Having the opportunity to spend next year preparing for that next step is incredibly exciting.

“I’m confident that with the team’s support and experience, I’ll have the best possible preparation to make sure I’m fully ready to take the next step onto the F1 grid when the time comes.”

Mekies said Red Bull has been highly impressed by Tsolov. “Nikola is an exceptionally talented young driver, and we have been hugely impressed by his development and performances over the past few years,” he said.

“To fight for the championship in F3 and now challenge for the F2 title in his first full season says a great deal about his ability and determination. What has impressed us just as much is his maturity, his approach to racing and his willingness to keep learning and improving.

“We have enormous belief in Nikola’s potential and see him as a driver with a very exciting future in F1. This appointment reflects our confidence in him and our commitment to his continued development. Our focus in 2027 will be on giving him the experience, tools and support he needs to be ready to race in F1 next.”

Sports.title: Stats: Verstappen claims second place from lowest grid position since 1983 | 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
In 2024 Lando Norris’s championship hopes suffered a fatal blow when he failed to win from pole position at Interlagos.

Max Verstappen claimed an unlikely victory in a rain-hit race from 17th on the grid, putting him on course to retain his championship crown.

Norris has made amends since then, however, winning the next two grands prix at Interlagos from pole position. Both times he prevented Verstappen from completing another impressive back-to-front charge: the Red Bull driver finished second on Sunday from the penultimate place on the grid, just as he did 12 months earlier.

However as there are two more cars in the field this year, Verstappen’s charge to second place came from 21st position on the grid (he was actually the 20th car on the grid as Valtteri Bottas’s Cadillac was pushed into the pit lane). This is the lowest starting position anyone has taken second place from since the 1983 Long Beach Grand Prix, when Niki Lauda charged there from 23rd.

Lauda started one place behind his team mate John Watson, who led him home in a McLaren one-two, setting the record for the lowest grid position from which a grand prix has been won.

McLaren may not have managed a one-two last weekend but Norris took his 14th grand prix victory, giving him as many as a trio of multiple world champions: Jack Brabham, Graham Hill and Emerson Fittipaldi. This was also his 20th pole position, the latter giving him as many as Damon Hill and Valtteri Bottas.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Norris reached the podium for the 50th time in his career. Verstappen, meanwhile, took his eighth podium finish in a row, which is the longest streak any driver has managed this year.

Isack Hadjar equalled his best finish with another third place – this was his fourth. Although he briefly hit the front of the field after Norris pitted on lap 49 he did not officially lead a lap, as he pitted the next time by and Andrea Kimi Antonelli crossed the line in front.

Liam Lawson finished seventh for the second race in a row. He has now scored enough points for Racing Bulls to single-handedly put them fifth in the constructors’ championship.

Lewis Hamilton became the second driver in Formula 1 history to record his 400th grand prix start. He joins Fernando Alonso, who reached 400 two years ago:

For the second race in a row, Haas ran a new driver, but this time their rookie did not manage to bag a point. Rafael Camara made his debut in his home race, becoming the first driver to do so since Germany’s Markus Winkelhock in the 2007 European Grand Prix, held at the Nurburgring.

Camara raced with number 51 which last appeared in a grand prix at Abu Dhabi in 2020. It was also used on that occasion by another Brazilian driving for Haas: Pietro Fittipaldi.

Lance Stroll’s race ended in retirement yet again. That was the 14th time this year he has not been classified – failing to complete 90% of the race distance – equalling the all-time record which has been set on five other occasions by four drivers.

These are Andrea de Cesaris twice (in 1986 with Minardi and 1987 with Brabham), Piercarlo Ghinzani (in 1986 with Osella), Ivan Capelli (in 1989 with Leyton House) and Rubens Barrichello (in 1997 with Stewart).

It remains possible for Stroll to match or even exceed the record for most retirements in a season. De Cesaris set this in 1987 when he started but was not running at the end of all 16 rounds. In addition to his 14 non-classifications he ran out of fuel before completing the final lap at Spa (but was classified third) and spun out with four laps to go in the final race at Adelaide, taking eighth place.

George Russell has launched a karting academy to help unearth the next generation of new motorsport stars

The GR63 Academy will feature 25 racers next year. They will be chosen following a shoot-out involving 80 potential competitors at Silverstone. The competition is open to children aged eight to nine and the winner will receive a “fully funded karting season in 2028”.

20 years ago today Sebastien Bourdais won the 14th and final race of the 2006 Champ Car series. It was the final race for the Lola B2/00 chassis before it was replaced by a new designed built by Panoz.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford Flaunts Payment After Fans Call Him Broke
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford wants everyone to know his bank account is doing just fine without him stepping back into the ring. After some fans claimed the retired champ would eventually have to come back to boxing because he is running out of money, Crawford posted a video from a bank drive-through window to shut down that talk.

He held up a stack of checks topped with a bright yellow sticky note showing a handwritten figure of $111,353.60 before sending the deposit through, pointing out that the payout came from just a single stream of his income.

“I don’t know a lot of people that got a source of income like that… and that’s only 1 source of income,” Crawford said in the clip, which was shared by Source of Boxing on X.

Crawford walked away from the sport in December 2025 with a spotless 42-0 record right after defeating Canelo Álvarez for the undisputed super middleweight crown. Ending his career on its biggest victory naturally gave promoters an easy angle to pitch whenever comeback talk starts swirling. However, if Crawford is sitting around waiting for another $50 million payday like the massive haul he reportedly banked for the Canelo fight, he might as well forget about it.

The truth is that the first fight with Canelo was about as exciting as watching paint dry. Crawford fought a super cautious, safety-first style and showed zero interest in taking risks to make the bout entertaining.

The action dragged so badly that some fans in the stadium looked half asleep in their seats. Promoters are not lining up to hand out another mega-million check for a rematch when the original left the crowd nodding off.

If Crawford does not want to come back and volunteer for the rematch that Canelo and his trainer, Eddy Reynoso, called for after their win over Christian Mbilli, boxing will move right along without him. There are hungry go-getters like Willy Hutchinson and David Benavidez who would gladly step up to the plate to face Canelo for the final fight of his contract with Turki Alalshikh.

Sports.title: Pryor vs. Argüello: The Fight Behind the Black Bottle
Sports.content:
Aaron Pryor stopped Alexis Argüello in the 14th round at Miami’s Orange Bowl on November 12, 1982, ending his bid to become boxing’s first four-division world champion. Argüello landed one of his hardest right hands in the 13th. Sixty-six seconds into the next round, the unbeaten WBA junior welterweight champion had him helpless against the ropes.

Argüello entered as a 12-to-5 favorite despite moving up to challenge a champion who had stopped every man he’d defended against. At 30, the Nicaraguan had won world titles at featherweight, junior lightweight and lightweight. Pryor, 27, had taken his belt from Antonio Cervantes in 1980 and defended it five times. Argüello came to Miami chasing a fourth title. Pryor had his chance to beat one of the most accomplished fighters in the sport.

Pryor pressed from the opening bell, coming in fast and throwing several punches at a time. The taller Argüello stood his ground and looked for the straight right as Pryor crossed into range. When Argüello landed it cleanly, he could knock Pryor off his line of attack. He then had to get his feet set again before Pryor came back with another combination.

That made the early rounds difficult to score. Pryor could spend much of a round forcing the action, only for Argüello to land its hardest punch. Argüello also worked the body, where he found a target as Pryor leaned in to throw. “I never took harder shots to the body,” said Pryor afterward, as reported by The Washington Post.

A cut opened over Argüello’s left eye in the sixth. He continued to find Pryor with counters, and some of his best work came between the ninth and 11th rounds. Pryor kept coming forward, but every time he closed the distance he gave Argüello another chance to time him. A hard right in the 11th snapped Pryor’s head back. Argüello found him with another in the 13th, a shot heavy enough to make the final two rounds look dangerous for the champion.

Pryor was still ahead on two of the three cards after 13 rounds. Referee Stanley Christodoulou and judge Ove Ovesen both had him up 127–124. Ken Morita had Argüello ahead 127–125. The challenger had made the fight close enough that the last two rounds could decide it, and he had just shown he could still hurt Pryor with his best punch.

Pryor took the initiative as soon as the 14th began. A combination hurt Argüello and sent him back toward the ropes. Pryor followed him there and kept throwing, landing right hands as Argüello’s gloves dropped. The challenger was still on his feet when Christodoulou stepped between them at 1:06. Argüello slumped to the canvas after the stoppage. Pryor had made his sixth successful defense.

The black bottle controversy

“Give me the other bottle, the one I mixed,” said trainer Panama Lewis between the 13th and 14th rounds, as captured by HBO’s microphones. Pryor drank from the bottle. The recording caught Lewis asking for it immediately after Argüello’s big round, and viewers saw Pryor overwhelm him on the other side of that break. The bottle was never tested, and the Miami Boxing Commission collected no post-fight urine sample.

Lewis told The Washington Post that he had mixed Perrier and tap water to settle Pryor’s stomach. Bill Miller, Argüello’s manager, filed a protest with the WBA and the Miami Boxing Commission, alleging that Pryor had been given an illegal substance. Pryor denied wrongdoing. Before the rematch, he told United Press International he had been available for a urine test for two hours after the fight. The official result stood.

Lewis was banned from boxing in 1983 for tampering with Luis Resto’s gloves before his fight with Billy Collins Jr. Years later, Resto said in the documentary Assault in the Ring that Lewis had put crushed pills in his water. Resto was describing what happened in his own corner. The contents of Pryor’s bottle remain unknown.

Pryor wins the rematch in 10 rounds

Pryor and Argüello met again at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas on September 9, 1983. With Lewis out of his corner, Pryor dropped Argüello in the first and fourth rounds. All three judges had Pryor ahead when he knocked Argüello out in the 10th.

The Ring chose their first meeting as its Fight of the Decade for the 1980s. That night in Miami, Argüello came within two rounds of a decision in his bid for a fourth title. His right hand was still getting through in the 13th, and two judges still had Pryor ahead. The champion had spent the night making Argüello work whenever he wanted room to punch. In the 14th, Pryor finally drove him somewhere he couldn’t get it back.

Sports.title: Jhon Orobio Drops Hendri Cedeno Twice in Third-Round TKO
Sports.content:
Jhon Orobio dropped Hendri Cedeno in the first and third rounds and stopped him in the third on Thursday night in his first career main event at the Casino de Montréal. The unbeaten Colombian retained his WBA and WBC Continental Americas junior welterweight titles on the Eye of the Tiger card.

Orobio (20-0, 18 KOs) took control in the opening round, putting Cedeno on the canvas before the Dominican could settle into the scheduled 10-round fight. Cedeno (16-1, 12 KOs) got through the second, but Orobio kept him under pressure and dropped him again with a chopping right hand in the third.

Cedeno beat the count, and Orobio went straight back to work. He landed a left during the follow-up barrage and kept punching until referee Martin Forest stepped in. Cedeno had stayed on his feet after getting up, but he was still taking punches when Forest stopped it.

It was a step up on paper for the Montreal-based Orobio. Cedeno had knocked out 12 of his first 16 opponents and had won a regional WBO title, though he came in after more than 18 months out of the ring. The first-round knockdown put him on the defensive early, and he never had much time to use the power he brought into the fight.

Orobio had already stopped Antonio Moran, Jonathan Montrel and Yomar Álamo before taking his first headlining bout. The quick finish against Cedeno makes a case for matching him with an experienced junior welterweight who can make him work into the later rounds. Thursday was his 18th stoppage in 20 professional fights.

Erik Bazinyan stops Steven Butler in the 10th

Erik Bazinyan (33-1-1, 24 KOs) stopped longtime promotional stablemate Steven Butler (38-7-1, 32 KOs) 22 seconds into the 10th and final round of their super middleweight co-feature. Bazinyan was fighting for the first time since Jaime Munguia stopped him in September 2024. Butler took the fight on short notice after Lenar Perez withdrew with an injury, bringing together two fighters whose bout had already been postponed twice.

Bazinyan went to Butler’s body in the fourth and hurt him with a right hand late in the fifth. He switched to southpaw at times and found openings with both hands as the fight wore on. A left sent Butler down around the bell to end the ninth, but referee Junior Padullo ruled it was no knockdown.

Bazinyan hurt Butler with a right hand seconds into the 10th and followed with a flurry that forced him to take a knee. Butler got up before the count of 10, and Padullo waved it off. It was Butler’s second straight stoppage defeat following his July loss to Edgar Berlanga.

On the undercard, Avery Martin Duval stopped Damian Wrzesinski in the fourth round, and Wyatt Sanford took an eight-round unanimous decision over Gabriel Jimenez, winning 80-72 on all three cards.

Sports.title: Willy Hutchinson Won the WBC Belt. Why Fourth?
Sports.content:
Willy Hutchinson did everything required to claim the No. 1 spot in The Ring’s light heavyweight rankings, except get the actual ranking. Beating Joshua Buatsi for the vacant WBC title only moved him from seventh to fourth, leaving him stuck behind Callum Smith, Anthony Yarde, and Imam Khataev. I’d favor Hutchinson against all three, as he may already be the division’s best fighter behind champion Dmitry Bivol.

The Ring’s light heavyweight rankings

Champion: Dmitry Bivol

Callum Smith Anthony Yarde Imam Khataev Willy Hutchinson Najee Lopez Joshua Buatsi Radivoje Kalajdzic Lerrone Richards Albert Ramirez Umar Dzambekov

Putting Yarde at No. 2 makes the least sense. He is coming off a stoppage loss to David Benavidez, who exited the division to move up to cruiserweight. Yarde definitely has the power to trouble Hutchinson, assuming he can actually get inside to land it. Against Buatsi, Hutchinson forced the pace on his own terms, switched stances smoothly, and timed him on the way in. Yarde would likely spend most of the night chasing shadows, which puts him closer to the bottom of the top 10.

Smith holds the best argument of the trio since he already owns a victory over Buatsi. That win keeps him near the top, yet he has mostly been sitting around waiting for a shot at Bivol while Hutchinson went out and beat that exact same opponent for a world title. Smith belongs at second, clearing the path for Hutchinson to take the top spot.

Khataev is fine right where he is at third. His heavy hands and relentless forward pressure could easily carry him past Yarde, Smith, or Buatsi. I’d still pick Hutchinson in that matchup because his sharp footwork and sudden direction changes would force Khataev to reset his attacks every time he closed the distance. Khataev would need to cut off the ring far better than Buatsi managed to do.

The Ring made the right call leaving Artur Beterbiev off the list during his layoff. His resume will still be waiting for him whenever he decides to return. Hutchinson just delivered a fresh, championship-level performance, and it was more than enough to earn the No. 1 ranking.

Sports.title: Hearn Threatens to Sue WBA Over Jack Catterall Mandatory
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn says he’ll sue the WBA if it lets Teofimo Lopez keep his welterweight belt and fight Ryan Garcia ahead of mandatory challenger Jack Catterall. If the WBA holds Lopez to the order, he has a good reason to give up the belt. The power he showed against Rolly Romero in his welterweight debut gives him little reason to count on hurting Catterall.

“I would sue them immediately,” said Hearn on Inside the Ring when asked what he would do if the WBA ruled against him. Hearn promotes Catterall and argues the WBA had already promised his fighter a shot under a resolution that was in place before Lopez won the title.

Hearn has the WBA’s own written ruling to point to if it lets Teofimo Lopez fight Ryan Garcia and keep his welterweight belt. The WBA gave Jack Catterall a route to its top title with a 180-day deadline, then said Lopez inherited that obligation when he beat Rolly Romero. Hearn says he’ll sue if the WBA goes back on its decision.

The WBA allowed Romero one optional defense, which he used to fight Lopez. In its September order, the WBA expressly said Lopez took on Romero’s obligations when he won the title. The organization reaffirmed the mandatory on November 11 and gave the camps 10 days to agree on a fight date or propose another solution. An exception for Garcia would mean setting aside a specific commitment the WBA has now upheld twice.

The timing gives Hearn leverage. Mike Coppinger said on the show that Lopez’s team was trying to finalize a February 6 fight with Garcia. If the WBA cleared Lopez to bring its belt into that fight, Hearn could seek a court order blocking the WBA from sanctioning it as a unification while the dispute is heard. Even the prospect of that fight over the belt could complicate the promotion while the two sides are trying to close a deal.

Hearn expects Lopez to give up the title if the WBA holds him to the mandatory. It’s easy to see why. Lopez beat Romero in his welterweight debut, but his punches rarely discouraged him. If he can’t make Catterall respect his power, he could spend 12 rounds leading against a southpaw who can make him reach, catch him with the straight left, and get out before Lopez can follow up.

Lopez has the speed to win that fight. He’d still be risking the Garcia payday on his ability to win close rounds against a fighter who excels at making them close.

Catterall wants the Lopez fight. If Lopez gives up the belt to face Garcia for the WBC title, Hearn expects the WBA to elevate Catterall from its secondary champion and let him make a defense. Either outcome gives Catterall a way forward. The outcome Hearn is threatening to challenge is Lopez getting the bigger fight, keeping the belt, and leaving Catterall waiting again.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia’s Left Hook Could Derail Haney’s 154 Plans
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is already eyeing a run for all four belts up at 154 pounds. Before he can even think about junior middleweight, though, he has to clear out 147.

If Ryan Garcia is still holding the WBC welterweight strap when that undisputed opportunity rolls around, Haney will have to get past the exact guy who repeatedly caught him with short left hooks every time he reached in to clinch. That tactical hurdle is a way bigger problem than whoever ends up waiting for him at 154.

Eddie Hearn brought up the plan. He talked about Jaron “Boots” Ennis and Josh Kelly fighting, the winner going on to face Sebastian Fundora, and Haney moving up to challenge whoever comes out of that with all four belts.

“I told you that that’s what I wanted to do,” said Haney on Inside the Ring. He went a step further and said it was his idea. He still has Liam Paro to fight on December 19, and winning that unification would leave him two belts short at 147.

Haney quickly co-signed the timeline, noting he had already voiced that exact goal before taking things a step further by claiming the whole blueprint was his idea in the first place. Of course, he still has to get past Liam Paro on December 19. Even if he wins that unification bout, he will still be two belts shy of clearing out the welterweight division.

Looking back at the Brian Norman Jr. fight, it is easy to see why Haney feels confident he can control the rest of the weight class.

Ryan, on the other hand, made him pay dearly. Garcia made him pay for it. Every time Haney lunged in to grab hold, he left himself wide open for a split second before tying Ryan up. Garcia didn’t need to back up or make room to throw.

Haney was practically walking right into the punch, and once Devin got hurt and started reaching out just to survive, he kept making the exact same mistake. The commission eventually changed the official result to a no contest, but everyone saw how easily Garcia cracked him.

In a potential rematch, Haney definitely has the skills to outbox Garcia for long stretches behind his jab. The real test starts the moment Garcia closes the distance and forces Haney’s instinct to grab. Will Haney step away and make Garcia chase him? Can he tie up Ryan’s left arm before that hook comes flying in? Doing either of those things is easy enough when Haney is fresh and has his wits about him. The first fight showed what happens when he gets rocked and starts grabbing out of pure panic.

Garcia has plenty on his own plate right now, and that WBC belt could easily change hands before a second fight gets signed.

Still, Haney has made it clear he wants the rematch. If beating Garcia is the final step required to collect all four welterweight titles, Haney’s grand plan to conquer 154 might completely depend on what he does the next time he reaches in to tie Ryan up while that left hand is still loaded.

Sports.title: Josh Kelly Vows to Be ‘Bad for Business’ Against Boots
Sports.content:
Josh Kelly suspects promoter Eddie Hearn would rather see Jaron “Boots” Ennis win their February 27 unification fight in Atlanta. Kelly’s response to that reality is simple: he plans to be “bad for business that night.”

The subject came up during a joint appearance on Inside the Ring, where Devin Haney pressed Kelly on the politics of the matchup while Hearn sat right beside them. Thinking back to when Matchroom promoted both him and Regis Prograis, Haney recalled feeling that Hearn genuinely had his best interests at heart. He wanted to know if Kelly felt that same backing with Matchroom representing both corners.

“I know Eddie’s favorite probably Boots. He’s good for business in the U.S.,” Kelly said to Ring Magazine. “I’m going to be bad for business that night for the U.S.”

Hearn pointed to his long history with Kelly and claimed he hates matching two of his own fighters together because he can’t cheer for either side. He also insisted that Ennis and his father and trainer, Bozy, know how good Kelly is, even as talk about Boots becoming the pound-for-pound king has fans treating this like a showcase.

If Hearn does favor Ennis, it makes total sense. Ennis is a major, fan-friendly talent who closes the show, whereas Kelly’s recent run has been built on survival and generous scorecards. Kelly looked poor in his outing against Caoimhin Agyarko. Before that, he walked away with a questionable decision over IBF champion Bakhram Murtazaliev in a fight where he spent practically the entire night on his back foot.

Their shared history against David Avanesyan tells the whole story. Avanesyan stopped Kelly in six rounds; Ennis blew Avanesyan away in five.

Haney suggested on the show that a fighter who can change range, turn Ennis, and tie him up can force Boots to take his time and think his way into the fight. The problem is that Kelly’s game doesn’t center on breaking opponents down with smart boxing.

Lately, it has revolved around running around the ring and trying to steal rounds in the final ten seconds. Hearn can still steer the winner into a potential undisputed clash with Sebastian Fundora, and unless Kelly brings a completely different style to Atlanta, Matchroom’s U.S. business plans aren’t in much danger.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Won’t Touch Britain’s Harder-Hitting Shakur Stevenson
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is already trying to steer Devin Haney into an in-house unification trap with Jack Catterall, hoping the matchup will eventually set up an undisputed welterweight clash with Ryan Garcia.

For Hearn’s convenient blueprint to work, he is banking on Teofimo Lopez vacating his WBA title rather than fighting Catterall, his mandatory challenger. Sitting right beside Haney on Inside the Ring, Hearn laid out his preferred path: beat Liam Paro in December, face Catterall for the vacant WBA belt, and save Garcia for all four straps.

“Fight Liam Paro, fight Jack Catterall, who I believe will be the WBA world champion because Teo will vacate now,” Hearn said to Ring Magazine. “That’s been ordered. They’ve got 10 days to make a deal.”

Hearn’s In-House Matchmaking Hits a Wall

This is classic promotional maneuvering from Hearn, who has promoted Paro and represents Catterall. Trying to slip Catterall into a vacant title spot and feed him directly into a Haney unification bout keeps all the belts and business under the Matchroom umbrella, regardless of whether fans actually want to see it. The problem for Hearn is that the fight makes zero sense for Haney.

Haney is not going to take that kind of risk for a fraction of the money he would make fighting Garcia. Catterall is essentially Britain’s version of Shakur Stevenson, able to do everything Stevenson does in the ring while carrying more pop in his punches. Asking Haney to take on a slick, heavy-handed southpaw technician with virtually no commercial pull in the United States is a terrible business move when a massive rematch is within reach.

On paper, Lopez dropping the belt to chase Garcia opens the door for Catterall, who earned his mandatory spot by beating Shakhram Giyasov after Lopez inherited the obligation from his win over Rolly Romero. If Catterall picks up the vacant strap, he could bring a third title into the ring against Haney, assuming Haney gets past Paro first.

Haney defends his WBO belt against IBF titleholder Paro on December 19 at San Francisco’s Chase Center. Hearn naturally talked up Paro as underrated, pointing to his road win over Subriel Matias in Puerto Rico before picking Haney to unify. Hearn claimed Paro lacks the power to stop Haney or the skills to outbox him. Haney sounded even more dismissive, stating Paro looks the exact same in his recent fights as he did during their past sparring sessions.

Teofimo’s Choice Could Ruin Hearn’s Plans

Even if Haney gets through Paro, signing up for Catterall next means taking back-to-back southpaws who do nothing at the American box office while stalling the Garcia rematch. Hearn’s entire four-belt pitch also assumes Garcia holds onto his WBC title, which is far from guaranteed. Insider Mike Coppinger reported during the broadcast that Garcia and Lopez are trying to finalize a February 6 bout.

If Garcia and Lopez fight and Lopez wins, Lopez walks away with the WBC belt and instantly becomes the target Haney actually wants, leaving Catterall completely out in the cold. Haney made it clear he still wants to settle the score with Garcia alongside his goal of becoming a two-division undisputed champion.

Right now, Lopez holds all the leverage. Defending against Catterall lets him carry the WBA belt into a Garcia fight, while vacating clears his path to Garcia sooner. Hearn is clearly hoping Lopez drops the title so he can manufacture an in-house unification bout, but expecting Haney to willingly walk into an ambush against a sharper, harder-hitting version of Stevenson is pure wishful thinking.

Ghana News.title: Parliament scrap plans to hold 2027 Budget workshop outside parliamentary premises
Ghana News.content:
Parliament has abandoned plans to hold its post-budget workshop in the Volta Region, opting to organise the exercise at the Chamber of Parliament in Accra following opposition from the Minority, as preparations begin for a week of debate on the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy.

The decision brings an end to the proposed arrangement to move the workshop outside the parliamentary premises, with lawmakers now expected to undertake the exercise within the House over two days.

The change was announced by Majority Leader James Agalga during the presentation of the Business Statement, in which he outlined the revised arrangements for the workshop and the schedule for the budget debate.

According to Mr Agalga, the workshop will take place from Monday, November 16, to Tuesday, November 17, 2026, at the Chamber of Parliament, with proceedings beginning at 9 a.m. on each day.

"Honourable members are reminded that the post-budget workshop would be held from Monday 16th to Tuesday 17th November 2026 at the Chamber of Parliament at 9 a.m. each day." he announced.

He further informed the House that there would be no parliamentary sitting on Tuesday, November 17, to allow members to take part in the workshop.

"In view of the above, the House will not sit on Tuesday , November 17. Sitting will accordingly commence on Wednesday November 18," he added.

Mr Agalga urged MPs to take note of the revised arrangements and make themselves available for the exercise, which will precede the formal debate on the government's economic policy.

Budget debate to begin on November 18

Beyond the workshop, the Business Statement also outlined Parliament's programme for examining the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy.

The debate has been scheduled to begin on Wednesday, November 18, and continue until Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Mr Agalga explained that the Business Committee had programmed the exercise in accordance with Order 195(3) of Parliament's Standing Orders.

"The Business Committee has programmed the commentary on the Budget Statement and Economic Policy of the Government to commence on Wednesday 18th and end on Tuesday 24th November 2026," he told the House.

The Majority and Minority Leaders are expected to deliver the concluding contributions on Wednesday, November 25, bringing the scheduled commentary to a close.

The arrangement will allow members from both sides of the House to present their views on the government's budget proposals and economic policy direction for the 2027 fiscal year.

Presenting the Business Committee's recommendations, Majority Leader James Agalga told the House that the Majority Leader and Minority Leader would each be allocated 35 minutes to contribute to the debate, while other parliamentary leaders would have 20 minutes.

He said Ministers of State, chairpersons and ranking members of parliamentary committees would each be given 15 minutes, with vice-chairpersons and deputy ranking members allocated 10 minutes.

Mr Agalga further stated that other Members of Parliament would have seven minutes each to present their contributions.

He informed the House that the debate would run from November 18 to 24, 2026, with the Majority and Minority Leaders expected to conclude proceedings on November 25.

Ghana News.title: African countries urged to turn brain drain into brain circulation
Ghana News.content:
African countries have been urged to harness the expertise of their citizens in the diaspora to strengthen higher education, research and innovation on the continent.

The Technical Advisor to Ghana's Minister of Education, George K.T. Oduro, who made the call at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Carnegie African Diaspora Fellowship Programme (CADFP) Convocation, said African-born academics working abroad could play a significant role in developing universities on the continent if opportunities were created for them to share their knowledge and expertise with local institutions.

He added that the continent had for years grappled with brain drain, resulting in the loss of some of its finest academic talents to institutions in the Global North.

The three-day convocation, which opened on Tuesday in Accra is being organised by the Institute of International Education and the Association of African Universities.

It brought together fellowship alumni, university leaders, academics and programme stakeholders to celebrate the achievements of the initiative and discuss ways of sustaining academic partnerships between Africa and its diaspora.

Research priorities

Prof. Oduro further called for future fellowship engagements to be aligned with Africa's development priorities, including climate adaptation, renewable energy, public health, biomedical innovation, artificial intelligence, agriculture and food security.

He cautioned that the pursuit of global citizenship through higher education should not come at the expense of African identity and cultural values.

“True global citizens are not rootless wanderers; they are deeply rooted in their heritage, contributing to the world from a place of cultural confidence and identity,” he said.

He further called on African governments and private sector organisations to increase domestic investment in higher education research to complement philanthropic funding and ensure local ownership of academic partnerships.

Prof. Oduro also proposed three priority actions to institutionalise the collaborations, including embedding joint programmes into university curricula, increasing government and private sector support for research, and establishing durable academic networks linking African universities, research councils and diaspora academic associations.

Sustaining partnerships

The Head of Information Technology of the Association of African Universities (AAU), Dr Thomas Songu, said African universities needed to move beyond individual academic connections to build structured and sustainable institutional partnerships.

He said the value of the fellowship programme should not be measured only by the number of awards made or academic visits undertaken, but by the lasting institutional benefits arising from the engagements.

“The real value lies in the institutional capacity and strength of research collaboration to sustain academic programmes, improve innovations and develop future generations of scholars,” he said.

New initiative, Achievements

The Executive Vice-President of the Institute of International Education (IIE), Jonah Kokodyniak, said a new initiative, the African Diaspora Fellowship Initiatives (ADFI), was being launched to sustain and expand the achievements of the CADFP.

He said the independent not-for-profit organisation would build on the fellowship programme's achievements and provide opportunities for continued academic collaboration between African institutions, diaspora scholars and skilled professionals.

Mr Kokodyniak said the CADFP, established in 2013, had provided more than 750 fellowships and engaged more than 250 universities across the African continent.

He said Ghana had been one of the programme's major host countries, alongside Nigeria, Kenya and South Africa.

Ghana News.title: Minority says it has identified conflicting figures in the 2027 budget
Ghana News.content:
The Minority in Parliament has accused the government of presenting inconsistent figures in the 2027 budget, raising questions about the reliability and clarity of some of the financial information provided to Parliament.

The Ranking Member of Parliament’s Finance Committee, Dr Mohammed Amin Adam, said a review of the Budget Statement revealed different figures for key expenditure and economic indicators in various sections of the document.

He cited Ghana's gross international reserves at the end of September 2026, which were recorded as US$12.7 billion in one paragraph and US$12.1 billion in another.

He also pointed to varying allocations for the Big Push programme, which were listed as GH¢27.8 billion, GH¢28 billion and GH¢29.8 billion in different sections of the Budget.

The Minority further identified discrepancies in the capital expenditure figures, which were stated as GH¢98.4 billion, GH¢98.3 billion and GH¢100.4 billion across different parts of the document.

Dr Amin Adam also questioned the Budget's statement that it had identified five principal risks, saying only four were listed. He argued that the risks omitted included the Bank of Ghana's losses, COCOBOD's GH¢30.55 billion debt and arrears in the energy sector.

“The Budget's numbers do not add up. Where the numbers do not match, Ghanaians must ask which one is real,” he said.

Addressing the media at Parliament on Friday, November 13, following Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson's presentation of the 2027 Budget, Dr Amin Adam called for explanations to reconcile the differences.

He said the government must provide clear and consistent information to enable Parliament to properly scrutinise its expenditure plans, revenue projections and economic targets.

Ghana News.title: Accra Academy 95th anniversary gala to honour 40 recipients, raise funds for school projects
Ghana News.content:
n this photo ; Rodger Allotey (Chairman of the Anniversary Planning Committee), J. Kofi Amoa-Awuah (Old Boys President), AVM Mensah-Larkai (Old boy), and Emmanuel Bruce-Attah (Old boy)

Accra Academy will honour 40 individuals, groups and organisations at its 95th anniversary dinner, awards and fundraising gala on Saturday, November 14, 2026.

The event, scheduled for 7:00 p.m. at the Ridge Church Main Auditorium in Accra, will be held under the theme, “A Legacy of Pride, Purpose, and Achievements”.

A major part of the celebration will be a fundraising drive to support the construction of residential flats for school staff and the refurbishment of the K.G. Konuah Assembly Hall.

The school says the projects are intended to improve staff welfare and provide a more conducive environment for teachers living on campus.

The anniversary dinner will be chaired by Air Vice Marshal Joshua Lartei Mensah-Larkai, Chief of Staff at General Headquarters, Burma Camp. The Ga Mantse, His Royal Majesty King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, will attend as Special Guest of Honour.

Legal practitioner Bethel Agyeman Donkor, who specialises in aviation law and global commercial transactions, will deliver the keynote address.

His address will focus on the topic, “From Pride to Purpose: Safeguarding Accra Academy's Legacy and Shaping Its Future”.

The event is expected to bring together Old Boys, members of the Board of Governors, school management, corporate organisations and other guests.

The Board of Governors will confer the Founders’ Award on 37 recipients across the Silver, Gold and Platinum categories. Three additional special awards will also be presented, bringing the total number of award recipients to 40.

The awards recognise academic excellence, meritorious service, contributions to the development of the school and achievements in various fields.

This year's awards will also recognise some alumni groups under higher award categories in acknowledgement of their contributions to the Academy.

One of the groups to be recognised is Bleoo '93, which reconstructed the Alema Hall of Residence after it was destroyed in a fire six years ago.

Established during the school's 70th anniversary celebrations, the Founders’ Awards were initially intended to honour alumni and friends who had served Ghana with distinction and enhanced the Academy's reputation.

The awards have since expanded to recognise a wider range of achievements and contributions to the school.

The 95th Anniversary Planning Committee is appealing to Old Boys, corporate organisations, philanthropists and friends of the Academy to support the fundraising initiative.

The school says the projects form part of efforts to strengthen its facilities and improve conditions for staff as it prepares for its centenary in 2031.

The anniversary celebration is expected to mark both a reflection on the Academy's 95-year history and the beginning of a renewed effort to prepare the institution for its 100th anniversary.

Ghana News.title: Prof. Bokpin urges gov’t to increase infrastructure spending to drive economic growth
Ghana News.content:
A Professor of Finance and Economics at the University of Ghana Business School, Prof. Godfred Bokpin, has urged the government to reconsider its fiscal framework and increase investment in infrastructure, saying that inadequate public spending could undermine its ambition to achieve private sector-led economic growth.

He said although the government's efforts to control expenditure and improve value for money were necessary, the scale of Ghana's infrastructure deficit required a stronger public investment drive to create the conditions for businesses to thrive.

Speaking on Joy FM's Super Morning Show on Friday, November 13, during a discussion on the review of the 2027 Budget, Prof. Bokpin said the government's current fiscal strategy needed to reflect the country's development needs.

“I am happy to urge the government to take another look at the fiscal framework and the fiscal strategy because now that we have a commitment to a higher value-for-money drive and the rest of that, we need to scale up the level of infrastructure spending from the government,” he said.

“Without that, it is going to make private sector-led economic development literally impossible to achieve.”

Prof. Bokpin questioned whether the resources allocated to the government's key economic programmes were sufficient to bring about the structural transformation Ghana needed.

He pointed to the government's proposed investment of $10 billion across seven or eight pillars of the new economy over four years, arguing that the amount, when spread across the various sectors and the implementation period, would not be enough to deliver meaningful change.

“If you pick the new economy's seven pillars or eight over four years, the amount of money made available is $10 billion. If you divide that and see what is going into each pillar, you will realise that how much we are investing in each sector is not transformative,” he said.

While acknowledging concerns about wasteful public expenditure, the economist said the government must distinguish between unproductive spending and the infrastructure investment needed to support long-term economic growth.

He cited expenditure patterns in 2025 and 2026, saying that the returns on public spending should be assessed against the goods and services delivered to the economy.

Prof. Bokpin also referred to data from the Ghana Statistical Service's monthly GDP updates, which he said showed that nearly 70 per cent of the goods and services recorded came from the services sector, largely driven by information and communications technology (ICT).

In his view, the figures raised questions about the extent to which government investment was contributing to growth and whether sufficient resources were being directed towards infrastructure to support other productive sectors.

He said that the absence of adequate public investment could make it difficult to achieve economic growth that benefits different sectors and parts of the country.

“The level of investment that government needs to stimulate growth and make growth structurally and spatially inclusive is literally absent,” he said.

The professor also questioned the level of funding committed to the government's Big Push infrastructure programme, saying the amount spent so far appeared small compared with Ghana's annual infrastructure requirements.

He indicated that expenditure on the programme in 2025 was less than $1 billion, raising concerns about whether the government was investing enough to address the country's extensive infrastructure needs.

Prof. Bokpin said that Ghana would need to pursue a much higher growth trajectory to meet the expectations and aspirations of its citizens.

He said that the economy should be growing at a rate of at least 14 per cent over the next decade to achieve the level of development Ghanaians desire.

“This is a choice we have to make,” he said, stressing that the country must decide whether its fiscal priorities adequately reflect its development ambitions.

Prof. Bokpin further warned that Ghana's infrastructure deficit was already imposing high costs on economic activity and productivity.

He pointed to persistent traffic congestion on major roads, including the Accra-Kumasi road and the Dodowa-Adenta road, as examples of the challenges facing commuters and businesses.

He said the problem extended beyond major highways to inner-city roads, district-level roads and regional road networks, many of which require significant investment.

For him, the scale of the infrastructure deficit makes it difficult to justify severe restrictions on economic growth in the name of maintaining favourable debt indicators.

He cautioned that although debt sustainability was important, the government should not lose sight of the need to finance critical development projects.

“In that same year, you cannot celebrate an extreme debt-to-GDP ratio. The debt-to-GDP ratio we are looking at is 45 per cent within this space, and this will constrain our ability to respond to our developmental spending,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Somotex opens ultra-modern Electro Point showroom in Wa to boost access to home appliances
Ghana News.content:
Somotex Ghana Limited, in partnership with Jamang Enterprise, has opened a new electronics showroom, Electro Point, in Wa, the Upper West Regional capital, to expand access to household appliances and consumer electronics in the region.

The showroom, located opposite Fogu at the Old Military Station, is expected to provide residents with access to a range of appliances without having to travel to major commercial centres such as Tamale, Kumasi and Accra.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, Business Head of Somotex Ghana Limited, Shivesh Srivastava, said the investment formed part of the company's strategy to expand its retail presence across Ghana.

He said the expansion was underpinned by the company's 60-year history under the Mohinani Group, which has interests in several sectors, including manufacturing.

"Wa is a vibrant, beautiful, and rapidly growing city that truly deserves a premier retail destination like this," he said.

Mr Srivastava explained that although the showroom displayed a selection of products, the company's catalogue contained more than 400 items.

He added that some of the company's products, including air conditioners, televisions and gas cookers, were assembled locally, enabling it to offer competitive prices and after-sales support.

As part of the opening celebrations, Electro Point has brought forward its annual Black Friday promotions, offering discounts of up to 30% on selected products throughout November.

Jamang Enterprise highlights local partnership

Chief Executive Officer of Jamang Enterprise, Anala Bertrand Deyaaka, expressed appreciation to the chiefs and people of the Upper West Region for their support over the years.

He said the partnership with Somotex would enable the business to make established electronics brands, including Bhrum, Tamashi, Haier, Beko and Philips, more accessible to consumers in the region.

Mr Deyaaka said customers would also benefit from product authenticity, competitive pricing and after-sales services.

Representing traditional authorities at the ceremony, Biihee Naa, Naa Jaafar Natasung Pelpuo, welcomed the investment, citing its potential to create employment opportunities and stimulate economic activity.

He said the traditional authorities and the Tindamba were committed to supporting and protecting the business to ensure its long-term success.

Stanbic Bank offers financing options for customers

Branch Manager of Stanbic Bank in Wa, Mohammed Seidu, announced financing arrangements to help individuals and businesses purchase household appliances.

Under the partnership, Stanbic Bank account holders and walk-in customers can access personal loans, salary overdrafts and structured repayment plans to spread the cost of their purchases.

Mr Seidu said the financing arrangements were intended to make essential household appliances more affordable, particularly for civil servants and business owners.

He also highlighted the potential savings from modern inverter appliances, particularly air conditioners and refrigerators.

According to him, inverter technology can reduce electricity consumption by between 30% and 40%, depending on usage and other operating conditions.

He added that the bank was also offering asset financing for green technologies, including solar installation packages, to help customers manage electricity costs and power disruptions.

Somotex plans further expansion in Northern Ghana

Northern Regional Head of Somotex Ghana Limited, Kaushik Biswas, said the opening of Electro Point in Wa was part of the company's broader expansion plans in northern Ghana.

He described the showroom as a retail destination designed to give consumers access to quality electronics and household appliances.

Mr Biswas also announced plans to extend the company's presence to Bolgatanga as it seeks to reach more consumers across the northern part of the country.

The ceremony ended with an awards presentation coordinated by Mr Anafu, during which traditional leaders and other dignitaries, including the Digu Naa, received appreciation awards and high-definition televisions in recognition of their support.
