Earlier on Thursday, the EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, told the BBC's Newshour the presence of a European delegate showed the Kremlin "now realised that Europe is a big player".

Kallas also expressed doubts that there was Russian momentum towards a peace deal.

Taoiseach (Irish Prime Minister) MicheÃ¡l Martin told a host of European leaders gathered in Dublin on Thursday that he believed the security of the region had been "fundamentally reshaped" by Russia's war.

"Many member states [of the EU] feel an existential threat because of what has happened in Ukraine and the potential, if Ukraine was to fall, for further aggression on the European continent," he told reporters.

Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. Approximately one-fifth of Ukraine is now under Russian occupation and Kyiv has refused Putin's demand to give up areas of Ukraine's eastern Donbas that remain under its control.

Tensions between the US and Ukraine were on display on Thursday before Witkoff and Kushner's meeting with Zelensky.

Earlier, the Ukrainian leader said that the military was facing more "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones.

Starshield technology, which was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use, has played a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line.

World.title: North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
World.content:
State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.

More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.

"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.

This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (Â£4.7bn) from the company.

US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.

Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.

According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.

Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call â except that the audio would appear to malfunction.

A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.

Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.

The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".

"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.

"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

World.title: African Miss Universe beauty queens in limbo as US visa restrictions bite
World.content:
Miss Universe Zimbabwe Roseanna Hall and several other contestants from Africa could miss this year's competition in Puerto Rico as they race to secure a US visa.

Hall is due to represent Zimbabwe at the 75th edition of the Miss Universe pageant, with the winner set to be crowned on 24 November. But she has yet to obtain a visa to travel to the US territory.

"We have been back and forth, trying to get my visa approved," Hall said in a video posted on her Instagram page.

Hall is not the only African contestant to be affected by the restrictions. Zambia has withdrawn its representative, Pamela Mubanga, from the competition because of US travel restrictions.

Contestants began arriving in Puerto Rico on 8 November for registration, fittings and other pre-pageant activities, putting pressure on Hall, and others including the representative from South Sudan, to secure their visas.

"Officially, today is the day I was supposed to be leaving for Puerto Rico for the 75th edition of Miss Universe," Hall said.

Zimbabwe is among 19 countries subject to partial US travel restrictions introduced under the Presidential Proclamation 10998, which took effect on 1 January 2026.

The measures suspend the issuance of visitor, student and exchange visas, as well as immigrant visas, to nationals of the affected countries. They also impose restrictions on other categories of non-immigrant visas.

In a statement, the Miss Universe organization in Zambia said Mubanga's situation was a consequence of the travel restrictions rather than individual circumstances.

"Unlike situations where a contestant's visa is denied due to personal circumstances, documentation or organisational challenges, Mubanga's situation is linked to the United States' presidential travel restriction affecting Zambia and other African countries," the statement read.

Mubanga, 25, a registered nurse, was crowned Miss Universe Zambia on 8 October and was due to represent the country at the international pageant.

The statement said five other African countries faced similar difficulties, although it did not name them.

Hall said she shared their concerns, adding that she had spent the past few weeks in South Africa trying to secure her visa.

"I am not alone in this predicament. Some of my African sisters are facing the same predicament, and I know exactly what they are going through," she said.

Miss Universe South Sudan also expressed uncertainty about her participation, commenting on Hall's video: "It is 50/50 whether we will make it, Miss Universe."

In another video posted three days earlier, Hall said she was still hoping to make it to Puerto Rico.

She captioned the video: "The fight to get Zimbabwe to Puerto Rico continues,"

The pageant's final is scheduled to take place at the JosÃ© Miguel Agrelot Coliseum in San Juan.

World.title: Hegseth awards medal to war memorial guard who reprimanded him and group
World.content:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has awarded a medal to the guard who reprimanded his group at Arlington National Cemetery.

A video of a Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier before the guard told them to be quiet.

In a statement, the Pentagon later announced that Hegseth had given Specialist Thomas Iglesias a Joint Service Commendation Medal "for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier".

Photos shared on the defence secretary's X account showed him presenting the medal to Iglesias.

He was accompanied by others whom the Pentagon identified as members of the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, known as the Old Guard, which is responsible for holding vigil over the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

"We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots," the accompanying text on Hegseth's post reads.

In the video, the army sentinel on duty later identified as Iglesias can be seen stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."

World.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drone in Gulf of Finland
World.content:
Finnish officials have confirmed that a Russian warship was attacked in the Gulf of Finland on Wednesday, although little is known about the strike.

Ukraine's SBU security service said it targeted the ship Naro-Fominsk as part of a broader drone operation against Russia's Ust-Luga oil export depot on the Baltic coast.

The attack, thought to be the first time Ukrainian drones have attacked a Russian ship in an area of the Baltic Sea open to civilian maritime traffic, has raised questions about whether Ukraine could expand its strikes.

Helsinki has been one of Kyiv's closest European allies, and Finnish officials have described the incident as a direct result of Russia's continued full-scale war.

Finland's military has given few details of the incident, but it appears to have taken place in a narrow stretch some distance from the Finnish coast.

The country's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen was adamant that the situation in the Baltic Sea remained stable and safe and that there was no threat of any kind to marine traffic.

Defence officials are understood to have stressed to Kyiv that the Gulf is a relatively narrow waterway used by oil tankers and civilian vessels, and is also home to subsea data cables.

Ukraine's SBU described the Russian ship as a Buyan-M type small corvette that carried Kalibr and Oniks cruise missiles. There were also unconfirmed reports of Russian combat helicopters being destroyed.

Martin Herem, the defence minister of Estonia, which borders the Gulf, told public broadcaster ERR that the ship was hit at about 05:30 (03:30 GMT) on Wednesday but did not say how it was attacked: "We know that smoke came from the ship afterwards. The ship itself went back towards St Petersburg."

The extent of casualties or damage sustained by the Russian navy ship remains unclear, and Moscow rarely gives such details.

World.title: Election related risks and the future of Nigerian democracy, By Jibrin Ibrahim
World.content:
Yesterday, the National Institute for Legislative and Democratic Studies and the Kukah Centre organised a symposium on political communication, election security and the future of Nigerian democracy. It was chaired by Professor Attahiru Jega, the former INEC Chairman. The discussion centred around the often-deceptive nature of conversations between Nigerian politicians and voters. The political class is never shy of making elaborate promises of what they will deliver to constituents and when they win elections, never try to deliver on their promises.

Their attitude to voters remains to lie again and again. This has created a deep breakdown of trust between citizens and the political class. The radical advocate Aisha Yesufu in her intervention argued that the real weakness of Nigerian democracy is that the office of the citizen has not realised its worth and power. If and when it does, it can easily take over the power the Constitution gives it and elect a new governing class that works for it rather than for itself. I completely agree with this perspective.

Meanwhile, the political class is not the only institution failing the people. INEC has been unable to deliver the quality of elections Nigerians require and deserve. With the elections just over two months away, INEC has been unable to present the voters’ register Inspite of statutory conditions that have stipulated it should have been presented much earlier. Recent revelations about the interference with the voter’s register using AI and implicating INEC staff has been troubling. In addition, the have been other stories about staff in the FCT Minister’s office having access to the server with the voters’ list have also been very concerning. Nigerians are losing confidence our Election Management Body and that is worrying.

Concerns were also raised about reckless judicial interventions by judges that do not appear to be neutral arbiters. The scenario developing is one in which corrupt judicial officers appear to be replacing voters as the ones who determine electoral outcomes. Citizens need to mobilise to re-assert their control over their electoral mandate. This is required because the other challenge to the mandate comes from the political class which has been investing stolen money from the treasury in purchasing votes from citizens with insufficient political consciousness.

The larger concern is whether the entire country is headed towards a major political crisis that might compromise the elections. The concerted attempt by the regime in power to block the major opposition parties from contesting in the elections is on-going with potentially disastrous political consequences for the country. Opposition contestants have been banned from entering a state – Peter Obi in Benue, Atiku has been removed as a candidate and during the Osun Governors elections, Senator Folorunso asked his supporters to kill all ACCORD party organisers in his constituency and nothing happened to him.

This week, the National Peace Committee released its monitoring report where it said 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory recorded 109 breaches of the National Peace Accord over 10 weeks of monitoring between August 19 and October 27. Campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections commenced on August 19, while those for the governorship and State Assembly polls began on September 9. Against this backdrop, 19 political parties signed the National Peace Accord in Abuja on August 18, pledging to uphold 12 standards aimed at promoting peaceful and issue-based campaigns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Under the agreement, the parties and their candidates committed to rejecting violence, threats and intimidation.

Other commitments covered issue-based campaigns, the dissemination of truthful political information, responsible use of digital media, inclusive participation, respect for electoral and security institutions, rejection of the partisan misuse of public authority and civil communication among political actors.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The report identified: 33 incidents of political violence and thuggery; 29 cases of misinformation and disinformation; 19 cases of attacks on political activities and campaign assets; 15 cases of intimidation and threats; seven incidents of restrictions on freedom of expression and assembly and four inflammatory statements. On the geographical spread of the incidents, the report identified Kaduna, Edo, Cross River, Kogi and Borno among the states affected.

Highlighting some of the flashpoints, the NPC report cited the 8 September obstruction of the convoy of former Anambra State governor and Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, near Makurdi, Benue State. In Enugu State, the monitoring documented repeated armed disruptions of NDC and Peoples Democratic Party gatherings and party premises between September and October. The National Peace Committee also documented several incidents of political violence, including the disruption of PDP consultations by gunmen in Calabar South, Cross River State, on 2 October, and the reported shooting of an African Democratic Congress supporter during political engagements in Igueben, Edo State, four days later.

In Oyo State, the NPC said violence during a political procession in Ibadan between 14 and 17 October claimed one life, while an APC ward member was reportedly killed days later. It added that allegations linking a council official to the violence were denied. The National Peace Committee also raised concerns over the use of religious and family affiliations to influence political choices, citing an alleged appeal by an APC-affiliated lawmaker in Oyo State urging Muslim voters to reject Christian candidates.

One of the most worrying dimensions of the evolving crisis as stated by INEC is the frequent use by political leaders and the media of the slogan, ‘Rig and Die.’ The National Commissioner and Chairman of INEC’s Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, gave the warning on Saturday in Enugu at a forum organised for media practitioners ahead of the 2027 general election. Speaking on the theme, ‘Ethical and Professional Standards in Election Reporting Ahead of the 2027 General Election,’ he said, “Whatever the intention of its originators, and some insist it targets only those who rig, a slogan that links an electoral offence to death is dangerous.” He noted that election officials at polling units, rather than influential politicians, were often the most vulnerable to attacks arising from suspicions of electoral malpractice. The emergence of the phrase is an indication of the belief among many Nigerians that incumbency powers would be used to rig the 2027 elections. The government in power must do the needful to reassure Nigerians that it will not rig and that the elections would be free, fair and credible to ensure that major violence does not erupt.

A professor of Political Science and development consultant/expert, Jibrin Ibrahim is a Senior Fellow of the Centre for Democracy and Development, and Chair of the Editorial Board of PREMIUM TIMES.

World.title: Enugu govt sponsors five medical personnel on cardiac traineeship programme
World.content:
The Enugu State Government has sponsored five medical personnel for specialised cardiac care training at Babcock University Teaching Hospital, Ilishan-Remo, Ogun State, as part of efforts to strengthen healthcare delivery and build local capacity for advanced medical services.

The training, organised under the Trinitas Cardiac Traineeship Programme at the university and facilitated by the Office of the Special Adviser to the Governor on Health, will expose the fellows to advanced intensive care, high-dependency care, open-heart surgery and cardiothoracic surgery.

Speaking at a send-off ceremony for the five fellows in Enugu on Thursday, the Special Adviser to the Governor on Health, Dr Yomi Jaye, regretted that referrals of patients requiring cardiac surgery to Lagos, Abuja and overseas had continued to impose huge financial burdens on families and undermine public confidence in the local healthcare system.

He, however, said Governor Peter Mbah was determined to reverse the trend by ensuring that Enugu developed the capacity to provide quality healthcare services, including highly specialised and complex medical procedures.

“But Governor Peter Mbah has been clear that Enugu must be able to care for its own people, including the most complex cases. That is what health sovereignty means in practice. And for us, it is not a slogan. That is why we must continue to build capacity,” he stated.

Jaye disclosed that the beneficiaries comprised resident doctors, intensive care unit (ICU) nurses and a medical student.

He explained that while medical equipment could be procured and hospital buildings constructed within relatively short periods, developing the human expertise and teamwork required to operate a safe and effective cardiothoracic service demanded sustained investment in people.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Equipment can be bought in months. Buildings can rise in a year. But the ability to run a cardiothoracic service safely is built in people, and it is built in teams, as a heart operation is never one surgeon’s achievement. It belongs to the anaesthetist, the perfusionist, the theatre nurse, the intensivist and the ICU nurse,” he said.

According to him, the composition of the beneficiaries reflects the administration’s deliberate effort to develop a comprehensive team of medical professionals who would sustain the state’s cardiothoracic care capacity in the years ahead.

He noted that the programme had two distinctive features: providing the fellows with firsthand experience in the use of modern cardiothoracic and critical care equipment and exposing them to the expertise of visiting cardiothoracic specialists from overseas.

“Exposure of this kind shapes a clinician’s standards for life,” he added.

Jaye charged the beneficiaries to maximise the opportunity and transfer the knowledge and skills acquired to other medical personnel in the state.

He also appreciated Enugu Air, Cecilia Oyebola Foundation, Trinitas Healthcare Partners, Babcock University Teaching Hospital and the Enugu State Broadcasting Service, among other partners, for supporting the state’s healthcare capacity-building initiative.

Speaking on behalf of the beneficiaries, a resident doctor and Senior Registrar in the Department of Surgery at the Enugu State University Teaching Hospital, Park Lane, Enugu, Dr Nnaemeka Ugwuowo, expressed gratitude to the state government and its partners for the opportunity.

He assured that the team would make the most of the training and replicate the knowledge and skills acquired to strengthen medical practice and education in Enugu State.

“I want to say that we are not ignorant of the sacrifices and efforts put in place to make this happen. We want to say that we are grateful and, in reciprocity, the skills and knowledge we gain, we will extend to others so that we continue to ramp up medical education for the good people of Enugu State,” he stated.

In his remarks, a renowned gynaecologist and Chief Executive Officer of Enugu International Hospital, Prof Sam Agwu, commended Governor Mbah for what he described as massive investment in the state’s health sector.

He disclosed that the Enugu International Hospital, which is expected to be commissioned soon, would also specialise in cardiothoracic care and attract highly skilled medical professionals from across the world.

Agwu, who said his support for the administration was based on conviction rather than political considerations, described Mbah’s leadership as transformational, particularly in the health sector.

“I thank God for gifting this state the best governor I have seen in my lifetime. I have been out of this country for a very long time. So, I am not political, let it be known. I am in Nigeria and Enugu today because I am 100 per cent convinced of the transformational leadership that the Governor is bringing to this state, not just in the health sector, but also in every aspect of life in Enugu State and beyond,” he said.

He recalled that during his first interaction with Mbah, the governor had expressed his vision of ensuring that residents of Enugu North Senatorial District would no longer have to travel to Enugu metropolis to access quality medical care.

According to him, that vision informed the establishment of the State University of Medical and Applied Sciences (SUMAS) Teaching Hospital, which is already operational.

“The second stage was to bring advanced care to Enugu and the South-East, and today that vision is standing there as Enugu International Hospital, super-equipped to world-class level, and we are engaging super-duper experts at every level,” he stated.

Also speaking, the Chairman of the Nigeria Medical Association (NMA), Enugu State chapter, Dr Chima Edeoga, expressed delight at the administration’s efforts to position the state as a centre of excellence in healthcare delivery.

He said the investments being made by the Mbah administration would significantly strengthen the state’s healthcare ecosystem and contribute to the advancement of medical services across the country.

“I believe that by the time he has completed his eight years, the health ecosystem of Nigeria will understand what a governor who is determined to advance healthcare means,” he enthused.

In his remarks, the Commissioner for Health, Prof George Ugwu, represented by the Director of Public Health and Disease Control, Dr. Uche Okenwa, reaffirmed the administration’s commitment to sustained investment in the health sector.

He said the government’s interventions were aimed at positioning Enugu State as a leading destination for quality and specialised healthcare services in Africa.

World.title: Young Nigerians pledge to become responsible digital citizens in Lagos
World.content:
Students from 11 public schools in Lagos State have pledged to become responsible digital citizens, as part of an initiative aimed at protecting young people from cyberbullying, sexual exploitation and other forms of digital abuse.

The commitment was made on Thursday at the OPTS-AFF Be Safe Initiative held in Lagos. It was organised by the Oil Producers Trade Section (OPTS) of the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), in partnership with the Akin Fadeyi Foundation (AFF).

Participating schools included Community Senior High School, Alapere; Kosofe Senior College; Ojota Senior Secondary School; Immaculate Heart Comprehensive Senior High School; Comprehensive Senior High School, Alapere; and Menide Senior High School.

After the interactive sessions, the students signed a Be Safe pledge wall, committing to the declaration: “I pledge to be a responsible digital citizen.”

The initiative featured interactive sessions on digital safety, responsible online behaviour, protection of personal information, recognising online manipulation and abuse, and reporting mechanisms. Different advocacy dramas were also presented to reinforce the messages.

This comes amid growing concerns about children’s safety online in Nigeria. Findings from a Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) survey, presented in 2025, indicated that 90 per cent of Nigerian children had faced at least one form of cyber risk.

Speaking at the event, Akin Fadeyi, founder and executive director of the Akin Fadeyi Foundation, said the project is designed to encourage young Nigerians to make responsible choices when using digital devices.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Fadeyi said the Be Safe Initiative aims to equip young people with practical knowledge to recognise online risks, make informed decisions, and seek help when they experience digital abuse.

Exposure to online risk

Mr Fadeyi said the growing use of digital technology has created new risks, including cyberbullying, online harassment, sexual exploitation and the spread of false information.

He said the foundation believes that young people need to understand that their actions online could have consequences, including legal consequences.

He said the Be Safe Initiative is part of the foundation’s efforts to promote behavioural change among young Nigerians, encouraging them to uphold integrity, honour, and character.

He said the project also seeks to equip young people with information about the legal options available to them when they experience online abuse.

“When someone threatens you through a digital device, do not keep silent. You can report,” he said, urging young people facing threats such as sextortion not to give in to blackmail.

Need for monitoring

Toyin Taiwo-Ojo, a child safety advocate and legal practitioner, said children were increasingly exposed to online dangers because digital devices had become part of their everyday lives.

Mrs Taiwo-Ojo, who is also the general secretary of the Nigerian chapter of the African Women Lawyers Association, said parents sometimes give children phones and other electronic devices to keep them occupied or support their schoolwork without adequately considering the risks.

She advised parents to supervise their children’s online activities and, where possible, ensure that devices used by children below 16 years are monitored.

She also urged parents to teach children to recognise warning signs of online grooming, including strangers asking them to keep conversations secret or arrange physical meetings without their parents’ knowledge.

“Anybody who wants them to keep a conversation secret from their parents, or who wants to meet them physically without their parents being there, should be someone they are wary of,” she said.

Ms Taiwo-Ojo also cautioned students against sharing unverified information or participating in harmful online interactions, noting that even liking or sharing certain content could expose users to legal consequences.

She urged young people to consider whether a post was true, helpful, inspiring, necessary and kind before sharing it.

Digital boundaries

Sade Adeyemi, an associate professor of mental health education, remedial and reformatory counselling at the Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), also warned that young people could encounter misleading and harmful content while using the internet for learning, entertainment and social networking.

READ ALSO: AHF launches comic book to tackle menstrual stigma among Nigerian girls

She said children need to establish digital boundaries to protect their social and emotional well-being.

Ms Adeyemi encouraged students to adopt the principle of “THINK” before posting or sharing content online, asking themselves whether it was true, helpful, inspiring, necessary and kind.

Mr Fadeyi also urged parents to recognise that their conduct at home could influence their children’s behaviour more strongly than their instructions.

He said parents should model honesty, diligence and responsible behaviour, rather than “place excessive emphasis on money and material success.”

World.title: Akwa Ibom proposes N1.2trn 2027 budget, slashes 2026 estimate by 24%
World.content:
The Akwa Ibom State Government has proposed a N1.2 trillion budget for 2027, representing a 24 per cent reduction from the N1.584 trillion original estimate for 2026.

The proposal was approved by the State Executive Council at a meeting presided over by Governor Umo Eno at Government House, Uyo, on Wednesday.

Excerpts of the meeting signed by the Commissioner for Information, Aniekan Umanah, is posted on Facebook.

The council directed that the draft estimates be transmitted to the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly for consideration and approval.

The proposed budget is N384.3 billion below the original 2026 estimate.

However, after reviewing its 2026 budget downwards to N1.100 trillion through a supplementary appropriation, the government’s proposed 2027 spending is about 9 per cent higher than the revised figure.

Revenue shortfall prompts budget revision

The council also approved a 2026 supplementary budget of N1.100 trillion, down from the original N1.584 trillion estimate. The reduction of N483.8 billion represents about a 30.5 per cent cut.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The government said the review was necessary for the “realignment of Government expenditure and priorities in response to the shortfall in projected revenues against budget.”

The supplementary appropriation is expected to accommodate newly established ministries and agencies, including the Ministry of Aviation and Airport Development, the Akwa Ibom State Electricity Regulatory Commission and the Akwa Ibom State University of Education.

Other items include equity financing for Ibom Air, solar-powered water projects across the state’s 369 wards, the Ibom International Market in Ikot Ekpene, gully erosion control and equipment for the Command and Control Centre.

The council directed that the supplementary bill be forwarded to the House of Assembly for consideration and passage.

Projects receive council approval

The council ratified project memoranda covering additional works on the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly complex and the Ibom International Convention Centre in Uyo.

Other approved projects include the ARISE-GIFA solar-powered water scheme across the 369 wards; access roads and drainage works leading to the terminal building at Victor Attah International Airport; and a 5.66-kilometre flood-control project at Dakkada Luxury Estate, Airport Road, Uyo.

The council also approved plans for the corporate headquarters of the Akwa Ibom Broadcasting Corporation on Dominic Utuk Avenue, Uyo, erosion-control works at the Dakkada Skill Acquisition Centre in Ikot Ada Idem, Ibiono Ibom, and renovation and expansion works at the Ibibio Union Museum and Unity Park.

The memos also covered procurement and distribution of 2026 Christmas packages to residents across the state.

The council received reports on a review of state-owned investments aimed at improving their profitability. It also received plans for the state’s Christmas Unplugged programme.

The statement did not identify the investments examined, disclose their financial performance or outline measures being considered to improve returns.

World.title: Court orders INEC to publish Adebutu’s name as Ogun PDP governorship candidate within 24 hours
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Abuja has ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to publish the name of Ladi Adebutu as the Peoples Democratic Party’s (PDP) governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election within 24 hours.

Judge Peter Lifu gave the order on Friday in a judgement following a suit filed by Mr Adebutu and the PDP to challenge INEC’s exclusion of his name from the final list of candidates for the upcoming 6 February 2027 governorship election.

The judge held that INEC “acted beyond its statutory powers” by removing Mr Adebutu’s name from the list, adding that “the commission had no authority to disqualify a candidate duly nominated by a political party.”

He consequently declared the exclusion “unlawful, unconstitutional, null and void.”

The judge also declared that even if the party had violated the Electoral Act, INEC could not “unilaterally remove the name of a duly nominated candidate without an order from a court of competent jurisdiction.”

In resolving the issues raised by parties, Mr Lifu held that the power to nominate candidates for “elections rested solely with political parties.” He ruled that “Neither INEC nor any other authority could take over that responsibility.”

He explained that while INEC had the responsibility to publish candidates’ names, the publication was an administrative duty. He said it did not confer on the commission the power to nominate or disqualify candidates.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He noted that the PDP conducted its governorship primary on 24 May and that INEC, which monitored the exercise, did not raise any objection to the process at the time.

The judge faulted the commission for waiting more than four months before “belatedly publishing the final list on 10 October” without informing the plaintiffs of any intention to exclude their candidate.

He questioned INEC’s decision to raise the issue after the primary had been conducted and monitored, when it could have raised any concerns in its monitoring report.

Mr Lifu warned that allowing INEC to exercise such powers would amount to a “dangerous show of power”.

He said such authority could allow the commission to disqualify candidates only days before an election, adding that INEC did not possess absolute powers.

The judge also held that the membership register tendered before the court contained Mr Adebutu’s name against serial number 1536.

He said the evidence established that Mr Adebutu was a member of the PDP and that it was the political party, not INEC, that had the authority to determine its membership.

The judge questioned why INEC considered it its responsibility to determine who belonged to a political party, holding that the commission exceeded its powers by omitting Mr Adebutu’s name.

The dispute

The dispute followed the exclusion of Mr Adebutu and his running mate from the final list of candidates published by INEC for the 6 February 2027 Ogun State governorship election.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that INEC published the final list on 10 October, featuring 13 governorship candidates but excluding the PDP from the race.

INEC said its decision followed the PDP’s alleged failure to comply with the membership register requirements under the Electoral Act 2026.

Section 77(5)–(7) of the Act requires political parties to submit their membership registers to INEC within the stipulated period. The provisions also empower the commission to scrutinise the registers.

In September, the Supreme Court upheld the constitutionality of the provisions in a case involving the Zenith Labour Party and INEC. The ruling affirmed the requirement for political parties to submit their membership registers before conducting valid primaries.

Following the exclusion, the PDP and Mr Adebutu approached the Federal High Court in Abuja in October, asking it to compel INEC to recognise him as the party’s governorship candidate.

The plaintiffs challenged the commission’s decision, arguing that it violated their right to fair hearing and breached provisions of the Electoral Act. They asked the court to set aside the decision and direct INEC to publish Mr Adebutu’s name as the party’s governorship candidate within 24 hours of its order.

INEC opposed the suit, maintaining that Mr Adebutu’s name was missing from the PDP membership register submitted to the commission. It therefore urged the court to dismiss the suit for being incompetent.

Flash drive dispute

In his judgement on Friday, Mr Lifu considered the disagreement between the parties over the flash drive containing the PDP’s candidates’ list submitted to INEC.

In a counter-affidavit, Mustapha Mohammed, a chief programme analyst in INEC’s Information and Communication Technology Department, told the court that a search of the register produced the name of the party’s deputy governorship candidate, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, but not Mr Adebutu’s.

Mr Mohammed also disputed Mr Adebutu’s claim to membership serial number 1536, stating that the number belonged to another party member, Lugboso Sunday Seun.

He further alleged that the flash drive attached to the PDP’s court processes contained records different from those originally submitted to INEC. He said the commission received two flash drives alongside a hard copy of the membership register, but neither contained Mr Adebutu’s name.

PDP disputes INEC’s account

The PDP, however, disputed INEC’s account of the documents submitted to the commission.

Testifying for the plaintiffs, the party’s National Organising Secretary, Umar Bature, told the court that the PDP submitted its candidates’ list electronically through a flash drive, in line with Paragraph 4(3) of Part I of INEC’s Regulations and Guidelines for Political Parties 2026.

Mr Bature maintained that the flash drive contained the names of all the party’s candidates, including Mr Adebutu. He also disputed the flash drive presented by INEC, insisting that the device submitted by the party was silver in colour.

In resolving the issue, the judge noted that, under cross-examination, INEC’s witness, Mr Mohammed, admitted that he was not the person who received the flash drive.

The judge held that the failure to call the person who received the device “was fatal to INEC’s case.”

He also considered the plaintiffs’ evidence that they submitted the candidates’ list electronically in accordance with INEC’s guidelines. The judge held that the PDP complied with the regulations, noting that the commission’s acknowledgement letter did not establish that the party was required to submit a hard copy.

The court further considered evidence that the plaintiffs wrote to INEC after discovering the omission of Mr Adebutu’s name, but the commission still failed to upload his name.

On INEC’s preliminary objection, the judge referred to Order 7 of the Federal High Court Pre-Election Matters Rules 2026, which provides that pre-election matters must be commenced by originating summons.

He also held that the suit was duly filed and properly signed. The judge resolved the relevant issues in favour of the plaintiffs and held that their case was “meritorious.”

Consequently Mr Lifu ordered INEC to upload and publish Mr Adebutu’s name as the PDP’s governorship candidate for the 2027 Ogun State election within 24 hours of the order, but made “no order as to costs.”

Speaking to the Supreme Court’s decision on the membership register requirements under the Electoral Act, Mr Lifu clarified that his judgement did not challenge the Supreme Court’s authority or its ruling.

He held that INEC could not rely on the Supreme Court’s decision to exercise powers beyond those conferred on it by law.

World.title: COP31: Nigeria among 14 countries targeted for methane reduction support
World.content:
Nigeria is among 14 developing countries targeted for support under an international initiative to reduce methane and other climate-warming pollutants.

The initiative, known as the Super Pollutant Country Action Accelerator, provides technical assistance, dedicated national teams and support to develop investment-ready projects to help participating countries reduce emissions.

The announcement was made at the Leaders’ Level Methane and Other Non-CO₂ Greenhouse Gases Summit at the ongoing COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye.

Speaking on behalf of the Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC), UK Climate Minister Katie White announced an additional $25 million to expand the initiative to seven more countries: Côte d’Ivoire, Ethiopia, Fiji, Morocco, Pakistan, the Philippines and Uzbekistan.

The seven countries will join Brazil, Cambodia, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Mexico, Nigeria and South Africa, which were announced as the initiative’s first beneficiaries at COP30.

With the additional commitment, the initiative now has $50 million in announced funding and aims to support 30 developing countries by 2030.

The programme is designed to help participating countries translate their commitments to reduce methane and other super pollutants into practical action through technical assistance and the development of projects capable of attracting investment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Global funding for methane reduction

The announcement comes amid renewed international efforts to accelerate reductions in methane and other non-CO₂ greenhouse gases.

At the summit, philanthropies announced more than $480 million in new funding to support emissions reductions across the energy, agriculture and waste sectors, as well as action on black carbon, clean cooking, transport and cooling.

The funding adds to more than US$530 million already delivered by philanthropic organisations since the launch of the Global Methane Pledge in 2021.

The Leaders’ Level Methane and Other Non-CO₂ Greenhouse Gases Summit was co-hosted by Brazil, China and the United Kingdom, alongside the COP31 Presidency, and chaired by UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero, Ed Miliband

Participants included Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley, Australia’s Minister for Climate Change and Energy, Chris Bowen, China’s Minister of Ecology and Environment, Huang Runqiu, and senior representatives of international organisations.

Speaking at the summit, Fatih Birol, Executive Director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), said at least 75 per cent of methane emissions from fossil fuel operations could be reduced using existing technologies.

He added that more than 60 per cent of those reductions could be achieved at no net cost.

Mr Birol’s remarks highlighted the economic opportunities associated with reducing methane emissions, particularly through measures that prevent gas from being released or wasted during fossil fuel operations.

Also speaking, Ajay Banga, President of the World Bank Group, said the bank was supporting methane reduction programmes in 45 countries, three times the number committed to at COP28.

He said the programmes were on course to reduce 11 million tonnes of methane emissions and benefit more than 160 million people.

Mr Banga cited examples from Brazil, where small family dairy farms increased yields by 10 per cent while reducing emissions by six per cent in one year.

He also highlighted a $1 billion rice programme in India supporting more than 300,000 farmers.

Call for stronger action

Earlier, Ms Mottley called for stronger international cooperation to address methane emissions across fossil fuels, agriculture and waste management.

She said governments and international partners needed to provide financial support to farmers to enable them to adopt practices that reduce methane emissions.

“No one can reasonably expect farmers to bear the cost of adjustment for methane emissions, either in livestock farming or rice paddy farming,” she said.

She also called for countries to move beyond voluntary commitments towards stronger international cooperation and regulation.

Meanwhile, Simon Stiell, Executive Secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), called for stronger policies, increased investment and practical support to help countries implement their climate commitments.

He highlighted the CCAC’s Super Pollutant Country Action Accelerator as an initiative helping countries move from commitments to implementation.

Methane is a potent greenhouse gas that contributes significantly to global warming. Although it remains in the atmosphere for a shorter period than carbon dioxide, reducing its emissions can help slow the rate of warming in the near term.

The summit emphasised that cutting methane and other non-CO₂ greenhouse gases is an important part of efforts to limit global temperature rise, alongside sustained reductions in carbon dioxide emissions.

World.title: Alleged N21.2m Fraud: Court grants Felix Duke N10m bail
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on Thursday arraigned musician Felix “Felix Duke” Osagie before the Lagos State High Court in Ikeja over an alleged N21.2 million fraud.

In a statement posted on its social media platforms, the commission said Justice Ismail Ijelu presided over the arraignment.

It said the musician faces four counts of stealing, obtaining money by false pretence, retaining proceeds of crime, and giving false information.

The EFCC stated that the offences occurred between 2020 and April 2026.

According to the anti-graft agency, count one of the charges reads: “That you, Felix Duke Osagie, sometime in 2020, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, with a dishonest intent, stole and converted for your own use the sum of N21,250,000, property of one Mr Joseph Onuh Oguche, thereby committing an offence of stealing contrary to Section 280 and punishable under Section 287 of the Criminal Laws of Lagos 2015.

Another count reads: “That you, Felix Duke Osagie, on the 2nd April, 2026, in Lagos, within the jurisdiction of this Honourable Court, with intention to mislead, made a false statement to officers of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission in the course of investigation, of the existence a land you had authority to sell, which is situate at Ise in Ibeju- Lekki, Lagos, which to your knowledge is false, thereby committing an offence to wit, false information contrary to and punishable by Section 39 of the Economic and Financial Crime Commission Establishment Act, No.1 of 2004.”

Not guilty

The musician denied the charges when the court read them to him and pleaded not guilty.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

After the plea, the prosecution counsel, Abdulhamid Lamido Tukur, asked the court to fix a date for trial and order the defendant’s remand in a correctional facility.

However, the defence lawyer, Sunday Afolabi, drew the court’s attention to a bail application dated 4 November and filed the following day.

He explained that the application rested on an 18-paragraph affidavit sworn by the defendant’s wife.

Mr Afolabi consequently appealed to the court to grant his client bail on liberal conditions or on self-recognisance.

Prosecution opposes request

In response, Mr Tukur told the court that his team had filed a counter-affidavit dated 10 November in response.

Referring to paragraph six, he said the defendant had jumped bail since July 2026 and urged the court to take note of the claim.

He further disclosed that the prosecution would call four witnesses to testify during the trial.

Mr Tukur said: “We filed a 14-paragraph counter-affidavit, urging the court to reject the bail application. The defendant has jumped EFCC’s administrative bail since July. Also, the defendant has been carrying on with his fundamental rights enforcement suit in another court through his legal counsel.”

N10m bail

After hearing arguments from both the prosecution and defence, Justice Ijelu granted Duke bail of N10 million, with two sureties who must each provide the same amount.

The judge stipulated that one of the sureties must be a blood relative of the defendant.

He also directed both sureties to reside in Lagos, provide evidence of tax payments to the Lagos State Government over the past three years and demonstrate verifiable sources of income.

Justice Ijelu further ordered Duke to surrender his international passport to the court registrar and prohibited him from travelling outside Nigeria until the court concludes the case.

The judge adjourned the case until 16 December for the commencement of trial.

He also ordered that the defendant remain in a correctional facility until he fulfils his bail conditions.

Duke was known for classic songs like “Mr Goody Goody”, “Walare”, “Baba”, “Joanna”, “Cynthia”, “General”, among others.

World.title: Ebola: Swiss woman evacuated from Nigeria discharged after recovery
World.content:
The woman who tested positive for Ebola in Nigeria and was evacuated to Switzerland for treatment has been discharged from hospital after making a full recovery.

She was discharged from Geneva University Hospitals on Wednesday, after medical personnel confirmed her recovery, Reuters reported on Thursday, quoting a statement from the hospital.

“After the medical team confirmed her full recovery, the cantonal physician authorised the patient being treated for Ebola virus disease to leave the Geneva University Hospitals (HUG) on 11 November 2026,” the hospital said.

The Uganda-born woman and her husband, a Swiss diplomat, were evacuated from Nigeria to Switzerland on 26 October. Her evacuation was confirmed by the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate.

The patient had returned to Abuja from Uganda on 3 October. She developed symptoms days later and was admitted to a private health facility before the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) was notified. Laboratory tests confirmed the infection on 20 October.

Nigeria continues Ebola surveillance

The NCDC’s latest Ebola situation dashboard, updated on 12 November with data as of 11 November, lists one confirmed case, no deaths and seven negative cases.

It also shows that 62 contacts linked to the confirmed case have been identified. Of these, 52 have completed their mandatory 21-day follow-up, while 10 remain under monitoring.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The NCDC said its response includes contact tracing, investigation of reported alerts, laboratory testing, infection prevention and control measures, and surveillance at the country’s points of entry.

On 11 November, NCDC disclosed that Nigeria recorded no additional confirmed Ebola cases since the imported infection was confirmed.

The agency has urged healthcare workers to remain vigilant, ask patients about their travel and exposure histories, and promptly report suspected cases to public health authorities.

Regional outbreak continues

The situation in Nigeria is part of a wider outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease affecting parts of Africa.

In its latest situation update published on 6 November, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said the DRC had recorded 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths as of 3 November, across 67 health zones in eight provinces.

Kenya had recorded nine confirmed cases and two deaths, while Nigeria had reported one imported case. WHO said there had been no new confirmed cases in Kenya or Nigeria since its previous update.

World.title: 2027: We received phone call from Buhari’s grave to vote Atiku — Dalung
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

A former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, has claimed that supporters of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) received a phone call from the grave of former President Muhammadu Buhari, urging them to vote for the party’s presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the 2027 election.

Dalung, an ADC chieftain, made the remark on Thursday while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he also linked the alleged message to a recent visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to Atiku in Abuja.

“Last month you saw when the wife of the late president visited Atiku in Abuja. The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said.

Dalung argued that Atiku had inherited the political structures of both Buhari and former President Umaru Musa Yar’Adua, giving him a nationwide political network.

He also dismissed the possibility of President Bola Tinubu defeating Atiku in 2027, saying the ADC candidate would remain difficult to overcome even if the ruling party prevented the opposition from campaigning.

“I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, he cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” he said.

He alleged that President Tinubu is scared of 2027 election saying, “I have never seen a weak president in an election like Bola Ahmed Tinubu. If you drag anybody on the street and put him on a ballot at a contest with Tinubu, he will defeat him,” he said.

World.title: Tinubu’s govt using EFCC to blackmail governors into APC — Makinde alleges
World.content:
Gov Seyi Makinde

By Ayobami Okerinde

Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has accused the President Bola Tinubu-led administration of using the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to intimidate governors and pressure them into joining the ruling All Progressives Congress.

Makinde, who spoke during an interview on Arise News on Friday, alleged that opposition governors who refuse to defect to the APC risk being subjected to investigations and blackmail, warning that the development could undermine Nigeria’s multiparty democracy.

“What we’ve seen is, well, okay, I have the governors, they come to APC. If you don’t, you will be blackmailed,” Makinde said.

To illustrate his claim, he described a situation in which a contractor working for an opposition-controlled state could face scrutiny over government contracts and financial transactions.

“The EFCC will come down from that place. ‘Look, how much did they award this to you? Go and bring your account. Who have you been paying?’ That is the situation that we are facing today,” he said.

Makinde also alleged that the Federal Government tried to blackmail him over the Bodija explosion intervention funds, saying his administration had already compensated affected property owners before receiving federal assistance.

He said the state engaged the Nigerian Society of Engineers and valuers to assess the damage and determine payments to victims.

“We’ve spent the money. We got Nigerian Society of Engineers. We got valuers. You know, they went out there, had valuation of the properties, and then we gave money back to those people, and we did it before even getting anything from the federal,” he said.

He added that he released the state’s account of the transaction when the issue was raised and directed the Commissioner for Finance to channel the funds into projects.

Makinde did not provide evidence during the interview that the president or the APC had directed the EFCC to investigate opposition governors or their contractors.

World.title: Just in: Court orders INEC to publish Adebutu’s name as Ogun PDP gov candidate
World.content:
Ladi Adebutu

The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to, within 24 hours, publish Oladipupo Adebutu’s name as Peoples Democratic Party (PDP)’s candidate for the 2027 Ogun governorship election.

Justice Peter Lifu, in a judgment, held that INEC had no powers to unilaterally remove the name of a validly nominated candidate by a political party.

Justice Lifu held that the commission’s action was unconstitutional, unlawful and was of no effect.

Justice Lifu said that it is only the Federal High Court or the state’s high court that has the power to declare a candidate invalid and not the commission.

He held that INEC breached Adebutu’s right to fair hearing.

The judge, who dismissed the preliminary objection filed by INEC, declared that the suit was competent.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the PDP and Adebutu had, on Oct. 22, filed the suit following the removal of Adebutu’s name from the list of contestants of the governorship seat in Ogun.

The plaintiffs sued INEC as the sole defendant in the suit filed by their lawyer, Ahmed Raji, SAN.

The plaintiffs, who sought six questions for determination, prayed the court for 11 reliefs.

They sought an order setting aside the commission’s decision to omit, remove or refuse to publish Adebutu’s name in the final list of candidates published on Oct. 10 for denial of a fair hearing and violation of the provisions of Section 29 and Section 32 of the Electoral Act, 2026.

They also sought an order directing or compelling “the defendant to, within twenty-four (24) hours of the order/orders of this honourable court, include and/or publish the name of the 2nd plaintiff as the 1st plaintiff’s governorship candidate for Ogun State in the forthcoming 2027 General Election,” among other reliefs. (NAN)

World.title: 2027: INEC rules out inaccurate IReV uploads
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has built strict validation safeguards into its system to prevent inaccurate results or figures reflecting over-voting from being uploaded to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

Prof. Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, gave the assurance at the Chatham House, London, during a high-level dialogue convened in partnership with the Kimpact Development Initiative (KDI) under the theme “Nigeria’s 2027 Elections: Democratic Trajectory and Regional Stability Beyond the Ballot”.

Thus is contained in a statement issued by the Chief Press Secretary to the INEC chairman, Mr Adedayo Oketola, in a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja.’

Amupitan therefore urged Nigerians to trust his leadership to deliver free, fair and credible general elections in 2027.

He highlighted measurable operational improvements recorded in recent off-cycle polls and new technical safeguards designed to prevent a repeat of the 2023 election controversies.

On the trust deficit left by the 2023 presidential election, Amupitan acknowledged that the controversies surrounding that exercise severely dented public confidence in the electoral body.

“First, let me speak about what happened in 2023, which resulted in a significant trust deficit for INEC, damage so large that the commission has not yet fully recovered from it,” he said.

Amupitan, who assumed office in October 2025, noted that INEC had treated every subsequent election as a practical laboratory to identify operational weaknesses and strengthen accreditation, voting and result management.

Responding to a question on why Nigerians should trust his leadership ahead of 2027, he cited the successful conduct of recent off-cycle elections, including the Ekiti, Anambra and Osun governorship elections, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Area Council polls, and 16 legislative bye-elections.

“Nigerians must trust me because, number one, I have conducted off-cycle elections, and observers agree that the recent election in Osun marked a clear improvement.

“Every election is a lesson. The 2023 general election was a major lesson for Nigeria, and the Anambra election was another,” he said.

He noted that Anambra and Osun previously had histories of prolonged, inconclusive governorship contests, recalling that the 2021 Anambra governorship poll took roughly five days to conclude.

He, however, said targeted administrative reforms under his watch enabled results in both states to be declared the day after voting.

Highlighting insecurity, logistics and result management as INEC’s three top priorities for 2027, Amupitan revealed that the commission’s post-2023 audit traced the most acute result management failures to collation centres rather than polling units.

To eliminate discrepancies between polling unit figures and collation sheets, he explained that INEC’s new validation safeguards would block flawed data at the source.

“We found that the core problem of election result management and declaration in Nigeria is not even at the polling unit; it is at the collation centres.

“In 2023, there were instances of inaccurate results or results with over-voting being uploaded onto IReV. We have now devised a technical safeguard: if a result is not accurate at the polling unit, it will not go to IReV at all.

“The moment a result appears on IReV, citizens can trust what they see. By eliminating inconsistencies at the source, collation will become a transparent formality,” he explained.

Amupitan disclosed that while INEC considered introducing an entirely new electoral technology for 2027, it opted instead to upgrade and harden its existing infrastructure due to the tight operational timeline before the polls.

Addressing malfunctions of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) linked to extreme heat and poor storage conditions in 2023, he announced that INEC was constructing climate-controlled storage facilities across all states.

“Additionally, the commission has procured extra devices and reduced the maximum number of voters assigned per BVAS machine from 1,250 to 850, ensuring polling units exceeding 850 registered voters are deployed with multiple devices,” he added.

To test these upgrades ahead of the polls, Amupitan said INEC had fixed Nov. 28 for a nationwide mock accreditation and voting exercise across all states of the federation.

He said the exercise would simulate the presidential election and verify both accreditation and electronic result transmission.

On election financing, the chairman confirmed that while INEC had received a substantial portion of its 2027 election budget, it was awaiting the release of the outstanding balance.

He noted that the commission had received assurances that the funds, part of which were earmarked for the recruitment and welfare of ad hoc personnel, would be released before the end of November.

Addressing questions regarding his neutrality following social media allegations linking his phone number to a controversial X (formerly Twitter) account, Amupitan categorically denied ever operating an X account.

He noted that an independent forensic review had been obtained and the matter formally referred to the Department of State Services (DSS) and the Inspector-General of Police for investigation.

He also dismissed suggestions that his past legal representation in political disputes would compromise his impartiality, stressing that he acted strictly within his professional duties as a senior advocate of Nigeria prior to his appointment.

“My loyalty is solely to the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and the Electoral Act.

“Every constitutional institution, including the Presidency, the National Assembly and state governors, owes its primary loyalty to the Constitution and the rule of law,” he affirmed.

On concerns regarding alleged voter register anomalies, including claims of an 85 per cent surge in registrants in a ward in Ebonyi, he said that the commission had already investigated and resolved the complaint in line with statutory procedures.

He noted that the Electoral Act provided clear windows for public claims, objections and requests for certified true copies of the register.

Amupitan urged Nigerian youths to stay actively involved in the democratic process and guard against digital disinformation.

“This country belongs to young Nigerians, and they must not relent in working for the Nigeria they desire.

“Misinformation remains one of the greatest threats to our democracy. Citizens must verify information before acting or sharing and give our democracy the chance to succeed,” he said. (NAN)

World.title: Oriire: Tinubu never spoke to me over abducted pupils, teachers — Makinde
World.content:
By Ayobami Okerinde

Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has said President Bola Tinubu failed to contact him during the 56 days pupils and teachers abducted in the state remained in captivity, despite his efforts to reach the president.

Makinde said he expected Tinubu to call or show concern over the incident, which involved the abduction of schoolchildren and their teachers in Oriire Local Government Area of the state.

The governor made this known during an interview with Arise Television on Friday, while discussing his relationship with Tinubu, whom he supported in the 2023 presidential election.

“I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the president should be interested. Actually, I expected the president to call me,” he said.

Asked whether Tinubu eventually contacted him, Makinde replied, “He did not. No. Till tomorrow.”

The governor added that he also tried reaching the president through the State Chief of Protocol but received no response to his call.

Makinde maintained that he had never spoken directly with Tinubu, stressing that he was focused on governing Oyo State.

“I’m saying it again that till tomorrow I’ve not spoken directly with the President about anything. I’m just minding my own business, running Oyo State. And I’m not complaining,” he said.

The governor’s remarks come months after the abducted pupils and teachers regained their freedom following 56 days in captivity.

The victims were seized on May 15, 2026, when gunmen attacked schools in the area. The Nigerian Army announced their rescue on July 10 after a security operation involving multiple agencies.

World.title: Makinde scores Tinubu administration 34 per cent
World.content:
Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has scored President Bola Tinubu’s administration 34 per cent, saying the government has failed to secure the support of a majority of Nigerians.

Makinde gave the assessment during an interview with Arise Television, where he was asked to evaluate the administration’s performance in infrastructure, diplomacy and economic growth.

He likened the score to the percentage of Nigerians who supported Tinubu in the 2023 presidential election, arguing that the President needed to win over those who voted against him to build a national consensus.

“It’s just about the same percentage as the people that supported him in 2023, 34 per cent. You need the 66 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board. This is a national project,” he said.

The governor also criticised what he described as pressure on elected officials to join the ruling All Progressives Congress, alleging that some governors were compelled to defect.

“Look at what we’ve seen. You have the governors come to APC. If you don’t, you’ll be blackmailed,” he said.

Makinde, who is seeking the presidency in 2027 under the Action Peoples Party (APM), also addressed whether he would accept defeat if the election was free, fair and credible.

Responding to a question on whether he would concede defeat and retire to farming, the governor said he would accept the outcome if the electoral process met the required standards.

“There are a few things that must happen. If the process is free, fair, and credible, yes, I will,” he said.

However, when asked whether he would remain in the APM after the election, Makinde said his political future would depend on how Nigerians received his political agenda.

“I may evaluate my political future depending on how Nigerians, you know, see this agenda,” he added.

World.title: 5 smartphones with the best zoom cameras in 2026
World.content:
Smartphone cameras have become increasingly sophisticated in 2026, with manufacturers competing to deliver sharper photographs, improved low-light performance and, particularly, better zoom capabilities.

One of the biggest developments has been the introduction of more advanced periscope telephoto cameras, larger image sensors and optical zoom systems capable of capturing distant subjects without relying entirely on digital enlargement.

These improvements have made it possible to photograph wildlife, sporting events, concerts, buildings and other distant subjects with a level of detail that was previously difficult to achieve with a smartphone.

While several manufacturers advertise zoom capabilities of up to 100x or 120x, the actual quality of photographs at those magnifications varies considerably. Optical zoom, sensor size, optical image stabilisation and image processing are therefore more

important considerations than the maximum zoom figure alone.

Here are five smartphones with some of the best zoom camera systems available in 2026, based on their camera hardware and independent reviews.

1. Oppo Find X9 Ultra

The Oppo Find X9 Ultra stands out as one of the most capable zoom smartphones of 2026, particularly because it features two dedicated telephoto cameras rather than relying on a single zoom lens.

The smartphone comes with a 200-megapixel primary telephoto camera offering 3x optical zoom and a separate 50-megapixel periscope telephoto camera capable of 10x optical zoom.

The combination gives users greater flexibility when photographing subjects at different distances, from portraits and street photography to distant buildings, wildlife and performers at concerts.

Its 10x optical zoom is particularly important because it allows the camera to magnify distant subjects using its dedicated optical hardware rather than simply enlarging pixels digitally.

According to Digital Trends, the phone can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally. Its 200-megapixel telephoto camera also provides additional room for cropping images while retaining useful detail.

The publication highlights the phone’s impressive telephoto sharpness, autofocus performance and ability to capture distant subjects.

For people who regularly photograph sporting events, wildlife or concerts, the Find X9 Ultra is a particularly compelling option.

2. Huawei Pura 80 Ultra

The Huawei Pura 80 Ultra is another smartphone that deserves recognition for its unusual approach to long-range photography.

Its biggest attraction is a switchable dual-telephoto camera system that offers 3.7x and 9.4x optical zoom.

Unlike conventional smartphones that use separate telephoto sensors for different magnification levels, Huawei developed a system in which two telephoto lenses share a large 50-megapixel, 1/1.28-inch sensor.

A moving optical mechanism switches between the two lenses, allowing users to photograph subjects at different distances while maintaining the benefits of optical magnification.

The 9.4x telephoto camera has a 212mm equivalent focal length, making it particularly useful for photographing distant subjects.

Huawei also includes optical image stabilisation on both telephoto configurations, helping to reduce camera shake when taking photographs at high magnification.

According to DXOMARK’s camera assessment, the Pura 80 Ultra achieved outstanding telephoto performance, with impressive detail preservation, low noise and accurate colour reproduction.

Its digital zoom extends to 100x.

However, the phone comes with an important consideration for international buyers: Huawei devices do not offer native Google Mobile Services support, which may affect access to familiar Android applications.

3. Vivo X300 Ultra

Vivo has continued to push the boundaries of smartphone photography with the X300 Ultra, particularly through its advanced telephoto camera and optional external zoom accessories.

The smartphone features a 200-megapixel periscope telephoto camera with a 3.7x optical zoom capability, supported by optical image stabilisation.

Its large telephoto sensor helps preserve details when photographing distant subjects, making it suitable for wildlife photography, portraits and outdoor events.

However, one of its most interesting features is its compatibility with an optional telephoto extender.

According to Android Authority, Vivo offers a second-generation external telephoto lens that extends the camera’s reach to approximately 400mm equivalent, or around 17x magnification.

This accessory allows users to photograph subjects much farther away than they ordinarily could with a conventional smartphone camera.

DXOMARK also praised the X300 Ultra’s telephoto performance, highlighting its ability to preserve details across different zoom ranges, including at longer distances.

There are limitations, however. The external lens adds bulk, and image quality can deteriorate in challenging lighting conditions, particularly when AI processing becomes more aggressive.

Nevertheless, for photography enthusiasts who want to experiment with extreme-distance smartphone photography, the X300 Ultra is among the most interesting options in 2026.

4. Xiaomi 17 Ultra

The Xiaomi 17 Ultra takes a different approach to smartphone zoom photography by introducing a mechanically variable telephoto lens.

Rather than depending entirely on fixed optical zoom levels, the smartphone uses a 200-megapixel telephoto camera with a variable focal length covering approximately 75mm to 100mm, equivalent to 3.2x to 4.3x optical zoom.

This allows users to adjust their framing within that range without relying on digital cropping between fixed magnification levels.

The telephoto camera also features optical image stabilisation and a large 1/1.4-inch sensor, helping it capture detailed photographs in different lighting conditions.

Its Leica camera partnership further contributes to its photography capabilities, with colour profiles and processing options designed to give users greater creative control.

According to Digital Trends, the Xiaomi 17 Ultra can extend its zoom capabilities to 120x digitally, while its large telephoto sensor provides additional flexibility for cropping images.

The device also supports advanced video recording features, including 8K recording and 4K at up to 120 frames per second.

Although its native optical zoom range is shorter than that of the Oppo Find X9 Ultra and Huawei Pura 80 Ultra, its mechanically adjustable telephoto lens makes it an interesting choice for photographers who value flexibility and image quality.

5. Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Samsung remains a major competitor in smartphone zoom photography with the Galaxy S26 Ultra.

The device features a 200-megapixel primary camera alongside two dedicated telephoto cameras: a 10-megapixel camera with 3x optical zoom and a 50-megapixel periscope camera with 5x optical zoom.

The two telephoto cameras give users different magnification options for photographing subjects at varying distances.

Its 5x optical zoom is particularly useful for portraits, travel photography and capturing distant objects, while the 3x camera provides a shorter telephoto option for everyday photography.

Samsung also offers up to 10x optical-quality zoom and 100x Space Zoom, combining optical hardware with computational photography to extend its reach.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra benefits from optical image stabilisation and Samsung’s image-processing technology, which help improve sharpness and reduce camera shake when photographing distant subjects.

One of its biggest advantages over some of the other smartphones on this list is its established global retail and software ecosystem.

However, its 5x optical zoom means it does not offer the same native long-range reach as the Oppo Find X9 Ultra or Huawei Pura 80 Ultra.

Vanguard News

World.title: Disgruntled US tenant kills building manager, injures four, shoots self
World.content:
Law enforcement and emergency personnel respond near the scene of a shooting in Washington, DC, on November 12, 2026. One person was killed and four wounded in a shooting at and outside a fitness center in downtown Washington on Thursday, the interim police chief said. Jeffery Carroll told reporters that the suspect in the shooting had been found with a self-inflicted gunshot wound after barricading himself in his nearby apartment unit. (Photo by Ken Cedeno / AFP)

A disgruntled tenant shot dead his building manager and wounded four other people in an upscale neighborhood of Washington on Thursday before killing himself, police said amid a massive law enforcement response that shut down part of the city.

The shooting, which occurred about a mile north of the White House, sparked a massive police response in the nation’s capital with dozens of law enforcement vehicles racing to the scene and police helicopters hovering overhead.

Dramatic dispatch audio captured the initial callout for a shooting inside the gym just before 8 am (0100 GMT). Within minutes a breathless police officer could be heard telling the dispatcher “we have an active shooter” and requesting the SWAT team.

Jeffery Carroll, Washington’s interim police chief, told reporters that the gunman, identified as Matt Lambert, 55, had been involved in an ongoing dispute over maintenance with the condominium association for the building where he owned an apartment.

Lambert, an emergency medicine physician, fatally shot the building manager, James Stuart, 46, in a packed gym attached to the complex, located in the Logan Circle neighborhood. Lambert then barricaded himself in his seventh-floor unit, Carroll said.

He then opened fire from his balcony on people below, wounding four. One of the wounded was in critical condition while the others did not have life-threatening injuries.

The Washington Post reported that construction workers from a nearby jobsite were among the injured, citing a company executive.

Lambert fired at least twice at police through his apartment door and set the unit on fire before shooting himself, Carroll said. He was pronounced dead at the scene.

Photos and video quickly emerged on social media of police in tactical gear surrounding the building with rifles drawn as well as fire emerging from an exterior wall.

Carroll said Lambert had taken legal action against the homeowners association of the condominium complex where he lived over what he considered to be a lack of maintenance of the building.

An X feed reportedly linked to Lambert titled @OfMiceandMold is a litany of complaints about mold and water damage. The final post, described as a “manifesto,” is an engineering report detailing problems with his apartment.

Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser denounced what she described as a “senseless act of gun violence.”

The shooting occurred during the busy morning rush hour, snarling traffic as police closed off streets around the area and evacuated residents.

The Washington Sun quoted a member of the VIDA Fitness gym as saying that he was on a treadmill at the workout facility when the shooting began.

Michael Carney said he heard a “pop” and then saw someone on the gym floor who had been shot in the head.

“Everyone was kind of just hiding behind planters and stuff,” Carney told The Sun.

Late Thursday, church groups led Logan Circle neighbors in vigils and prayer near the site of the shooting.
