The local government has ruled the building uninhabitable from the fire damage, the Washington Post reported, and residents were asked to stay away.

The Logan Circle neighborhood is one of the most expensive in Washington and is known for chic restaurants and nightlife spots. It also sits a short distance from a heavy concentration of foreign embassies.

World.title: Makinde: Tinubu Breached 2023 National Unity Agreement, Failed to Call During Oyo Schoolchildren’s Kidnap
World.content:
Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde, has accused President Bola Tinubu of breaching a written agreement to establish a government of national unity after the 2023 presidential election, alleging that the President’s failure to honour the deal has damaged the trust between them and made future political cooperation difficult.

Makinde also criticised Tinubu for failing to contact him during the 56-day captivity of pupils and teachers abducted in Oyo State, despite his attempt to reach the President over the security crisis.

The governor made the disclosures during an exclusive interview with ARISE News anchor, Ojy Okpe, aired on Friday, where he spoke about his relationship with Tinubu, his political decisions ahead of the 2023 election and ongoing opposition consultations ahead of the 2027 general election.

Makinde, a member of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the build up to the 2023 election, said his decision to support Tinubu, then the presidential candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC), in the 2023 election was based on a written agreement that he expected would lead to the formation of a government of national unity.

However, he accused the President of reneging on the agreement after assuming office.

“I still have the agreement with us,” Makinde declared.

Explaining why the alleged breach had affected his relationship with Tinubu, the governor said: “I’ve had a certain experience with him, you know, where agreement was signed. And he didn’t keep to it.”

He challenged those questioning his political position to examine whether the arrangement that informed his support for Tinubu had produced the promised national unity government.

“Tell us if the agreement was fulfilled. That’s wrong. Tell us if, not in terms of something personal, what has Nigeria got out of this? Are we having a government of national unity right now?” he asked.

Makinde maintained that his support for Tinubu was not motivated by their shared Yoruba ethnic identity but by the expectation that the proposed arrangement would promote political inclusion and serve the broader interests of Nigeria.

The governor, however, did not reveal the full contents of the alleged agreement with Tinubu, including the identities of all its signatories and the specific commitments contained in the document.

The governor also spoke on what he described as another troubling experience in his dealings with the President, recounting how Tinubu failed to call him during the 56 days that schoolchildren and their teachers were held captive following their abduction in Oyo State.

According to Makinde, he attempted to secure an audience with the President during the crisis because he expected the Federal Government to show concern and interest in the plight of the victims.

“I tried to see the President when our students and our children and their teachers were kidnapped, because I thought if any part of Nigeria is going through such a challenge, the President should be interested. Actually, I expected the President to call me,” he said.

When asked directly whether Tinubu eventually contacted him during the ordeal, Makinde gave a blunt response.

“He did not. No. Till tomorrow,” the governor said.

Makinde’s account also adds another dimension to his allegations of a broken relationship with Tinubu, suggesting that his grievances extend beyond the alleged political agreement to what he considers a lack of presidential engagement during a critical moment for his state.

Makinde also accused the Tinubu administration of using the EFCC to intimidate opposition governors and compel them to defect to the APC.

He warned that the alleged practice was undermining multiparty democracy and weakening the opposition ahead of the next presidential election.

According to the governor, rather than concentrate on winning over Nigerians who did not support the APC in 2023, the ruling party was allegedly focused on attracting governors through coercion.

“What we’ve seen is, well, okay, I have the governors, they come to APC. If you don’t, you will be blackmailed,” Makinde said.

Illustrating what he described as the alleged mechanism of intimidation, the governor referred to a situation in which contractors working for opposition-controlled states could face EFCC scrutiny over government contracts and financial transactions.

“The EFCC will come down from that place. ‘Look, how much did they award this to you? Go and bring your account. Who have you been paying?’ That is the situation that we are facing today,” he said.

Makinde’s allegation suggests that the anti-graft agency is being deployed as a political instrument to pressure governors who refuse to join the ruling party.

However, he did not provide evidence during the interview establishing that Tinubu or the APC had directed the EFCC to conduct investigations for the purpose of forcing political defections.

The Oyo governor also gave the Tinubu administration a 34 per cent performance rating, arguing that the government had failed to secure sufficient national support for its policies and programmes.

Makinde gave the assessment when asked to rate the administration’s performance across major areas of governance.

“It’s just about the same percentage of the people that supported him in 2023. Thirty-four per cent,” he said.

He argued that the President’s challenge was not simply about implementing policies but also about winning the confidence of Nigerians who did not support him in the last presidential election.

“You need the 67 per cent of Nigerians that were against him in 2023 to be on board,” he said. “This is a massive number.”

Despite his criticism, Makinde acknowledged some areas where he believed the administration had made progress, particularly the push for state police and student financing.

On state police, an issue he has consistently advocated as part of efforts to decentralise security management, the governor credited Tinubu for advancing the proposal.

“The President has done well with the formation of the state police,” he said.

Asked whether he would consider working with Tinubu again ahead of the 2027 general election, the governor contrasted his experience with the President with his dealings with former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi.

“I’ve not had that issue with him before, with Atiku Abubakar, or H.E. Peter Obi,” he stated.

Makinde also advocated a broader opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 elections, insisting that any political alliance must prioritise Nigeria’s interests rather than the personal ambitions of political leaders.

Although he confirmed that consultations among opposition figures were ongoing, he did not announce a final agreement or disclose the political platform through which any proposed alliance would operate.

As of the time of this report, neither Tinubu nor the Presidency had publicly responded to Makinde’s allegations.

World.title: Gov Eno Send 2027 Draft Budget of N1.2trn  Assembly for Approval
World.content:
Okon Bassey in Uyo

Akwa Íbom State Governor, Umo Eno, has directed the transmission of approved draft of 2027 Recurrent and Capital budget of N1,200,000,000 to the State House of Assembly for legislative action.

The State Commissioner for Information, Aníekan Umanah, said in a statement yesterday that the draft budget of state was approved at the enlarged State Executive Council meeting on Wednesday.

The draft bill has a projected Recurrent Revenue of N1,062,000,000, projected Recurrent expenditure of N431:296,691,320; Projected Capital receipts and expenditure of N768,703,308,000

The Executive Council also considered a memo for the 2026 Supplementary budget of N1,100,460,835,290 which represents a downward review from the original figure of N1,584,271,856,630.

The council said the review became necessary for the realignment of Government expenditure and priorities in response to the shortfall in projected revenues against budget.

The governor said the supplementary appropriation is designed to provide for newly established Government institutions and Agencies such as the Ministry of Aviation and Airport Development, Akwa Ibom State Electricity Regulatory Commission, Senator Oluremi Tinubu Senior Citizens Centre and Akwa Ibom State University of Education.

Others include: Equity financing for Ibom Air, Solar Powered Water project in the 369 Wards, Provision for Ibom International Market, Ikot Ekpene, funding for Gully erosion, equipment for the Command and Control Centre, amongst others

Similarly, Council approved that the Supplementary budget bill be forwarded to the State House of Assembly for consideration and passage.

The Council received reports on the review of the state owned investments to optimize profitability, and planning for Christmas unplugged.

“FGPC Memos on various projects and programmes were ratifified, including

additional Works for the Construction/Rehabilitation of the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly Complex, Uyo

“Implementation of ARISE-GIFA Solar-Powered Water Projects Across the 369 Wards of Akwa Ibom State; additional Works for the Completion of Ibom International Convention Centre, Uyo.

“Procurement and Distribution of 2026 Christmas Packages to citizens in the 2272 villages of the State; construction of 1.814 km access roads to terminal building with 800 metered underground drain and side drain at Victor Attah International Airport.

Other ptojects considered were construction of 5.66km Flood Control Project at Dakkada Luxury Estate, Airport Road, Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

Also considered were the construction of the Corporate Headquarters of Ibom Broadcasting Corporation at Dominic Utuk Avenue, Uyo; reclamation and Channelization of Erosion Control at Dakkada Skill Acquisition Centre, Ikot Ada Idem, Ibiono Ibom LGA, Akwa Ibom State.

“Renovation of Ibibio Union Museum, Expansion of the of the Ibibio Union Museum, Driveway expansion and provision of other facilities at the Unity Park, Uyo.

At the meeting, the governor was presented with the international safety Leadership Award by Afrisafe International for institutionalising occupational safety in public work space.

World.title: Lai Mohammed: AI-Generated Fake News Could Undermine Democracy, Public Trust
World.content:
Ayodeji Ake

Former Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, has warned that the growing use of artificial intelligence(AI) to generate fake news, deepfakes and fabricated audio recordings could undermine democracy, public trust and national security.

He said the increasing sophistication of disinformation had made it easier to manipulate public opinion, distort political debates and circulate false narratives capable of triggering violence and social unrest.

Mohammed gave the warning recently while delivering the maiden public lecture of Caleb University, Imota, Lagos, titled, “Fake News, Disinformation and Artificial Intelligence: Defending Truth and Public Trust in the Digital Age.”

The former minister, who served between 2015 and 2023, said AI had fundamentally changed the information landscape by making it possible to produce convincing fake photographs, videos, voices and entire personalities at relatively little cost.

“The greater danger is that AI may create an environment in which people stop believing anything,” he said.

He warned that the emergence of deepfakes could make it increasingly difficult to establish the authenticity of digital evidence, particularly during elections and politically sensitive periods.

According to him, the problem could also encourage individuals confronted with genuine evidence to dismiss it as fabricated.

He described this as the ‘liar’s dividend’, explaining that people could exploit public awareness of AI-generated content to deny genuine recordings or evidence.

“This presents a profound challenge to journalism, law enforcement, the courts, elections and democratic accountability,” he said.

Reflecting on his experience in government, Mohammed recalled that the federal government launched the National Campaign Against Fake News and Misinformation in July 2018 after recognising the implications of false information for national security and social cohesion.

He said the initiative followed an extraordinary session of the National Council on Information held in Jos, Plateau State, in July 2017, which focused on fake news and hate speech.

Recalling his personal experience, the former minister disclosed that a false report alleging he had $1.2 billion in his bank account once created tension in his family.

He said his wife, having seen the report, suggested that she should be made a signatory to the purported account in preparation for any eventuality.

“I had to take time to explain that the report was entirely false, and that my ministry’s annual budget was only a fraction of the amount alleged,” he said.

Mohammed also cited the 2018 mob violence in India, reportedly triggered by false WhatsApp messages about child abductions, and a May 2026 incident in Ogun State where a TikTok content creator allegedly staged a fake bandit attack to attract followers.

He cautioned governments against using the fight against misinformation to suppress legitimate criticism.

“A democratic government must not demand that citizens believe everything it says. Its responsibility is to make accurate, timely and verifiable information available,” he said.

He urged journalists to strengthen fact-checking and verification, arguing that professional journalism remained indispensable in an information environment increasingly dominated by synthetic content.

“The more information we have, the more valuable professional verification becomes,” he added.

The former minister also called on universities to make media and information literacy a core component of education, stressing that students must learn to question sensational claims, examine original sources and verify information before sharing it.

He proposed stronger technological safeguards, responsible AI deployment, public education and protection of freedom of expression as essential measures against disinformation.

Earlier, the Vice-Chancellor of Caleb University, Prof. Olalekan Asikhia, said the university selected the theme because of the growing challenge of distinguishing authentic information from fabricated content.

He disclosed that Nigeria recorded 157.7 million active internet subscriptions in July 2026, compared with 140.3 million in August 2025.

Citing the Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2025, Asikhia said 84 per cent of Nigerian respondents expressed concern about distinguishing real information from fake content online.

He said the maiden public lecture was designed to strengthen public engagement with critical national issues and promote the university’s commitment to knowledge, integrity and service.

Mohammed, in his concluding remarks, urged Nigerians to take personal responsibility for the information they circulate.

“When you share a video without checking it, you become part of its distribution chain,” he said, adding that citizens must choose verification over virality and evidence over emotio

World.title: Imo East Senatorial Candidacy: Court Orders NDC to Submit Uche Nwole’s Name to INEC
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

Justice Mohammed Umar of the Federal High Court, Abuja, has ordered the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) to immediately forward the name of Uche Nwole to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its duly elected candidate for the Imo East senatorial district in the 2027 general election.

Justice Umar gave the order while delivering judgment in the suit brought against the NDC, INEC, and Hon. Onyeagucha Uchechukwu.

The court ordered the NDC to forward Nwole’s name without delay as the candidate who emerged from the party’s primary election, which was duly monitored by INEC and conducted in accordance with Sections 84(1) and (2) and Section 86 of the Electoral Act 2026.

It further directed INEC to immediately accept, enlist, and publish Nwole’s name on the final list of candidates for the Imo East senatorial seat.

In addition, the court issued a perpetual injunction restraining the NDC from nominating or submitting any other name for the position.

It also barred INEC from accepting, listing, or publishing any purported candidate from the NDC who allegedly emerged from a primary election that was never held or monitored by the commission, or any purported consensus candidate whose nomination breached Sections 87(1) and (3) of the Electoral Act 2026.

The court held that the NDC had duly conducted primary elections monitored by INEC for aspirants seeking the Imo East ticket. It further declared that, having conducted those primaries, the party could not lawfully nominate a consensus candidate for the seat.

The court also found that Nwole had fulfilled all statutory requirements to participate in the direct primary and to emerge as the party’s candidate.

World.title: Ogoni: Implement UNEP Report Before Oil Exploration, Community Tells FG, Shell
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Ogoni people of Rivers State have urged the federal government and Shell to fully implement the United Nations Environment Programme recommendations on the Ogoniland cleanup, insisting that oil exploration must not resume until environmental restoration and justice are achieved.

The people accused those handling the cleanup of paying lip service to remediation, saying the exercise falls short of the standards and emergency interventions prescribed in the UNEP report.

The position was reiterated during a remembrance programme organised by the Movement for the Survival of Ogoni People in Bori, Khana Local Government Area, in honour of late environmental rights campaigner, Ken Saro-Wiwa, and other heroes of the Ogoni struggle.

The event featured a panel discussion involving members of the international Justice for Nigeria Coalition and environmental and human rights activists from Nigeria and Europe.

MOSOP President, Lazarus Tamana, said Saro-Wiwa was executed for demanding environmental protection and the right of the Ogoni people to determine their future.

“He only raised issues of the destruction of the environment and for the people to be allowed to control their own affairs. We cannot allow them to die in vain,” Tamana said.

He also pledged to rebuild MOSOP, lamenting the internal divisions that had weakened the organisation.

Environmental rights activist, Sebastian Kpalap, questioned the integrity of the ongoing cleanup, accusing the implementing agency of disregarding critical UNEP recommendations, particularly the provision of emergency potable water to oil-contaminated communities.

“What they are doing is not remediation. What is happening is a negation of the UNEP report. What they are doing is just to tick the box. The cleaners must be sincere and use best practices,” he said.

Another discussant, Bayo Dornubari, warned against using political concessions, including the proposed creation of an Ogoni state, to secure the people’s consent for renewed oil exploration.

“Ogoni will not accept bribery in the name of state. They should not give us a state because they want to take our oil,” she declared.

The moderator, Arochukwu Paul Ogbonna, insisted that Shell must accept responsibility for decades of environmental devastation in the Niger Delta.

“Shell should clean where it sat and ate for the last 60 years,” he said.

Speaking for the Justice for Nigeria Coalition, Simon Taylor demanded an end to delays in the remediation process.

“Enough is enough. They have to do the remediation now,” he declared.

Similarly, coalition member, Olanrewaju Suraju, urged the Ogoni people to remain united, warning that the struggle for environmental justice was far from over.

“We have greater battles ahead that need our unity,” he said.

Another coalition member, Nick Hildyard, accused oil companies of prioritising profit over the welfare of host communities and the environment.

“They do not care about you or the animals or plants. They care about one thing. They care about money,” he said.

Italian activist, Antonio Recommon, pledged continued international solidarity, promising to sustain pressure on Shell to compensate for the environmental damage.

“We are bringing them (Shell) back to pay for the damage,” he said.

The speakers collectively demanded full implementation of the UNEP recommendations, environmental accountability, community participation and an end to oil exploration until the Ogoni people’s grievances are addressed.

They maintained that the sacrifices of Saro-Wiwa and other fallen heroes must translate into genuine environmental restoration, justice and sustainable development.

World.title: Abia 2027: PDP Kicks Off LG Campaigns in Obingwa
World.content:
Boniface Okoro in Umuahia

The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Abia State chapter, last Wednesday flagged off its local government-based campaigns for the 2027 general election with a pledge to protect every vote cast for the party.

The governorship candidate of the party, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, gave the assurance while addressing a large crowd at Obingwa, where the statewide tour began.

The campaign will go through all 17 local government areas of the state in rallies and sensitisation programmes aimed at mobilising the Abia electorate ahead of the 2027 general election.

Anosike was responding to concerns raised by party faithful over vote protection.“Do your part first. Vote for PDP and leave the rest for me,” he said.

On the governorship contest, he added: “Vote for me first. I have the capacity, and our votes will be protected. I came fully prepared for this project.”

He said he entered the race out of a desire to improve the welfare of the people, lamenting the hardship and high cost of living in the state.

If elected, he promised to turn the state around through welfare programmes that would boost agriculture and farming, expand access to education, create skills and job opportunities for youths, and provide soft loans for women, artisans and youth entrepreneurs.

Anosike said the cost of living had skyrocketed since the PDP lost power in 2023, describing 2027 as a restoration journey.

“We are coming to take over the government of Abia State. People are suffering. If it was not about the welfare of the people, I will not be in this race. Women and youths will be at the centre of the next government,” he said.

The state party Chairman and deputy governorship candidate, Elder Amah Abraham, thanked the people for standing with the party since it exited power, describing Obingwa as the political capital of Abia State PDP. He promised them adequate reward if the party wins.

The Abia South senatorial candidate, Chinyere Onuoha; the candidate for Obingwa/Osisioma/Ugwunagbo federal constituency, Soloman Akpulonu; the Obingwa East state constituency candidate, Chimaroke Nwogu, and his Obingwa West counterpart, Enyinnaya Apollos, assured the party leaders thatthe Obingwa bloc vote for PDP is intact, and promised the people good laws, development, and welfare.

The Chairman of the Abia State PDP Campaign Council, Empire Kanu; the Director-General, Chief Obinna Nwachukwu; Abia South Zonal Chairman, Nze Boniface Ahuruonye; the Deputy Director-General, Abia South, Eze Nwanganga, and the Director of the Campaign Council in Aba South, Lady Chikodiri Nwankodo, described Anosike as the candidate to beat in the 2027 governorship contest, predicting that his emergence will launch Abia State into a new era of development and growth.

Obingwa stakeholders, including Chief Rowland Nwakanma, reassured the party leadership of their unwavering commitment to PDP’s victory in 2027.

The carnival-like event also featured goodwill messages from pro-groups, women and youth groups, who pledged support for PDP victory.

Earlier, the Abia South Youth Development Forum adopted Anosike as its sole governorship candidate for the 2027 contest during a reception at the Mgboko Council headquarters.

The President of the group, Chief Uche Okezie, said the adoption would pave the way for Anosike’s victory in the zone during the election, explaining that the forum will deliver 24,000-strong votes to the PDP flag bearer.

World.title: UNICEF, GAC Partnership Strengthens Health Governance, Others in Bauchi
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The partnership between Global Affairs Canada (GAC) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) in Bauchi State has recorded significant progress in strengthening gender-responsive health governance, improving healthcare delivery and empowering women and communities in the state.

The Chief of Field Office, UNICEF Nigeria, Bauchi Field Office, Dr. Nuzhat Rafique, disclosed this yesterday during a two-day visit by a delegation from Global Affairs Canada to Bauchi State, where the team assessed development interventions and their impact on the state’s healthcare sector.

Rafique, who was represented by Dr. Abdulrahman Ibrahim Ado, said Canada’s investment through the partnership was producing tangible results, particularly in addressing challenges affecting children, adolescents, and women.

She explained that the collaboration was strengthening healthcare systems, promoting gender equality, empowering girls and women, building resilient communities and improving health outcomes for children and young people.

According to her, one of the major achievements of the partnership is the promotion of gender equality and women’s participation in health-related decision-making.

She said the programme had mobilised and engaged 6,460 women through Mama2Mama support groups, positioning them as community advocates for improved healthcare practices.

She added that the intervention had contributed to an 18.6 per cent increase in women’s participation in decisions relating to contraceptive use, antenatal care and institutional delivery, including skilled birth attendance.

On strengthening governance and leadership in health and nutrition, Rafique disclosed that sustained engagement and advocacy with government institutions had helped mobilise hundreds of millions of naira in funding from local and state governments for nutrition commodities in 2025.

She described the development as an important step towards increasing domestic financing, strengthening government ownership and ensuring the sustainability of nutrition interventions.

The UNICEF official further revealed that 398 health workers had been trained in Essential Newborn Care, the management of Postpartum Haemorrhage (PPH), Health Logistics Management Information Systems (HLMIS), and the District Health Information Software 2 (DHIS2).

She said the training was aimed at improving the quality of healthcare services, strengthening the management of medical commodities and enhancing the use of routine health data for evidence-based decision-making.

On child nutrition, she disclosed that the project supported Vitamin A supplementation during the first half of 2026, reaching 1,626,825 children aged between six and 23 months with two doses.

According to her, the intervention is contributing to the prevention of vitamin A deficiency and strengthening child survival efforts across the state.

Rafique also highlighted the programme’s interventions in adolescent and young people’s health, saying it supported the operationalisation of 102 Adolescent and Young People’s Health Clubs across 11 MAMI local government areas.

She said the initiative reached 208,920 adolescents and young people in 2025 with integrated information and services covering sexual and reproductive health, HIV prevention and nutrition.

She added that 1,058 women and adolescent girls had benefited from practical skills development in reusable sanitary pad production, an intervention designed to improve menstrual health and hygiene knowledge while encouraging healthy practices.

Other priorities, she said, included promoting equitable access to essential health and nutrition services, reducing home deliveries and the number of unimmunised and zero-dose children, as well as expanding high-impact interventions for children under five, adolescents, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.

She further identified gender equality and women’s empowerment, increased domestic resource mobilisation for health, nutrition, education and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) as key areas of the partnership.

On sanitation, she said UNICEF was supporting efforts to improve hygiene practices, promote sanitation facilities and help Bauchi attain Open Defecation Free (ODF) status through the implementation of the Clean Nigeria Campaign.

In his remarks, the Bauchi State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Sani Muhammad Dambam, appreciated the Global Affairs Canada delegation for the visit, and expressed the state’s readiness to consider recommendations that would emerge from the assessment of the healthcare sector.

Dambam expressed satisfaction with the contributions of development partners to the growth of the state’s health sector, noting that the Bauchi State Government had continued to prioritise healthcare delivery.

He assured the delegation of thestate’se willingness to welcome constructive recommendations and strengthen collaboration with development partners to address existing challenges and improve healthcare services for residents.

Access Pensions MD Joins Industry Leaders to Launch PenCom’s Initiatives

Nume Ekeghe

Access Pensions has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting initiatives that strengthen Nigeria’s pension industry and improve retirement outcomes for Nigerians, following its participation in the Presidential Pension Security Initiatives launch held recently in Abuja.

The event, organised by the National Pension Commission (PenCom), featured the presentation of the Presidential Pension Legacy Award to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in recognition of his administration’s interventions in the pension industry. The award was presented on behalf of the pension industry by the Director-General of PenCom, Omolola Oloworaran, and the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Access Pensions, Sa’adu A. Jijji. The ceremony was also attended by the Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Access Holdings, Innocent Ike.

The event also witnessed the unveiling of two key initiatives by PenCom aimed at strengthening retirement security and improving retirees’ welfare: the Minimum Pension Guarantee, which establishes a minimum monthly pension of N52,500 for eligible retirees under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), and PenCare, a healthcare initiative designed to provide low-income retirees with access to essential medical services at no cost.

President Tinubu, who was represented at the event by the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, was recognised by the industry for his administration’s efforts to address longstanding pension obligations, expand coverage to the informal sector and strengthen the framework for sustainable retirement benefits.

Speaking at the event, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Access Pensions, Sa’adu A. Jijji, expressed appreciation to the president for his commitment to repositioning the pension industry, noting that the appointment of the current leadership of PenCom had brought renewed direction and positive changes to the sector.

Jijji particularly acknowledged the appointment of the Director-General of PenCom, Ms Omolola Oloworaran, describing her leadership as a reflection of the impact that young professionals and women could make when entrusted with critical responsibilities.

He said: “We are truly grateful to Mr President, first, for appointing the current leadership of the National Pension Commission, and particularly for appointing the Director-General of the Commission.

“We have seen what appointing a young person can do for an industry, and what appointing a woman can bring to an industry. When you have a young woman leading the industry, you can see the difference and the positive changes taking place.

“So, thank you very much, sir, for all the initiatives that have been implemented and for the support we have continued to receive. We are truly grateful.”

His remarks underscored the importance of regulatory leadership and sustained collaboration between pension operators and the Commission in strengthening an industry that plays a critical role in Nigeria’s long-term savings and retirement security architecture.

For Access Pensions, the ongoing reforms represent an important opportunity to deepen public confidence in the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), particularly at a time when the industry is seeking to expand participation, improve retirement outcomes and address concerns around the adequacy of pension benefits.

Earlier, the DG of PenCom, Oloworaran, said the decision to honour President Tinubu was a collective recognition by the pension industry of his administration’s interventions, which she noted had helped address some of the challenges that previously undermined confidence in the system.

According to her, the award was presented on behalf of Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs), Pension Fund Custodians (PFCs), Closed Pension Fund Administrators and PenCom.

“The pension industry, comprising Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs), Pension Fund Custodians (PFCs), Closed Pension Fund Administrators and, of course, the National Pension Commission (PenCom), is pleased to present the Presidential Pension Legacy Award to Mr President in recognition of his lasting interventions in the industry,” she said.

Oloworaran noted that the administration’s efforts to clear outstanding pension obligations and extend the benefits of the pension system to previously underserved segments of the population had helped rebuild trust in the industry.

“As I said earlier, this President has changed the pension industry landscape in this country forever by ensuring that dignity is restored to Nigerians, putting measures in place to ensure that the informal sector is not left out, and restoring confidence in the industry by clearing outstanding obligations that had caused people to begin to doubt the system,” she stated.

She further explained that the recognition went beyond the immediate interventions of the administration, reflecting the industry’s appreciation of policies intended to strengthen retirement security for future generations.

“The industry is happy once again to present the Presidential Pension Legacy Award to Mr President today in recognition of his historic leadership in transforming Nigeria’s pension system, restoring dignity to retirees, and securing the future of generations of Nigerians.

“Mr President, thank you for transforming the pension industry and securing the future of generations,” Oloworaran added.

The ceremony also provided an opportunity for the Federal Government to reaffirm its commitment to improving the welfare of retirees through the introduction of the PenCare Health initiative and the Minimum Pension Guarantee (MPG).

World.title: UNN Declares Three Days Mourning as Four Students Lose Their Lives in House Party
World.content:
Emmanuel Ugwu-Nwogo in Enugu

The management of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) has declared three days of mourning on the campus after confirming the deaths of four students at an off-campus house party while celebrating their graduation.

The Vice-Chancellor of UNN, Prof. Simon Ortuanya, confirmed the deaths while addressing journalists yesterday over the tragic incident that reportedly happened on November 11, 2026.

Contrary to earlier reports that had put the death toll at seven, the VC clarified that four students of the university died out of the 10 who were involved in the party.

He said that the students organised the ill-fated party to celebrate one of their friends who finished his final year examination.

“Unfortunately, four of them died after consuming substances suspected to be alcohol and drugs. The remaining six students are currently at various stages of recuperation in a hospital,” the VC said.

While declaring three days of mourning for the deceased students, Prof. Ortuanya said that “within these three days, all social and academic activities will be suspended in the university.”

The UNN VC had earlier in the day suspended a town-hall meeting scheduled between the university community and the Governor of Enugu State, following the gloomy cloud of mourning that descended on the campus.

He described the tragic loss of the students as “a death too many” and extended his heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of the deceased students.

“The management, staff and the students of the University of Nigeria share in their grief at this difficult moment and pray for the repose of the souls of the departed,” he said in a somber tone.

Prof. Ortuanya also clarified that the students involved in the incident cut across different departments, contrary to the widely speculated reports that they were from the Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences.

However, he reiterated the ban on all forms of sign-out celebrations in the university, urging students to desist from indulging in activities that will endanger their lives.

He said that the university “is cooperating with security agencies to unravel the actual cause of the death of the students.”

Sign-out parties have become a common practice among students who usually organise the event to celebrate the successful completion of the academic programme of one or more students.

The celebrants may come from one department or be drawn from several departments, and because of indulgences by students, tragedy could become the aftermath.

Meanwhile, the Enugu State Police Command said it has launched investigation into the “sudden and unnatural deaths” of the four UNN students.

A statement issued by the Police Public Relations Officer(PPRO), SP Daniel Ndukwe, identified the victims as two males and two females students “who took ill during an alleged academic sign-out celebration at Hilltop lodge, Nsukka, on November 11, 2026.”

He said that the victims “reportedly took ill after allegedly consuming alcoholic beverages at the gathering. Six other students were also rushed to the hospital for treatment, while the four victims were confirmed dead on arrival.”

According to the police spokesman, “alcoholic beverages were recovered from the scene, and the remains of the deceased have been deposited in a mortuary for autopsy.”

“The Command is investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident to establish the cause of the deaths. Further updates will be communicated as the investigation progresses,” he added.

World.title: Bafana Bafana v Kenya: Benni McCarthy on ‘David v Goliath’ clash
World.content:
Kenya head coach Benni McCarthy has dubbed Friday’s Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifier against Bafana Bafana as a ‘David vs Goliath’ encounter.

This encounter is scheduled to take place at Orlando Amstel Arena on the night.

Kick-off is at 18:00.



Now, speaking to the media, McCarthy said he always seem to be a ‘David’ and never a ‘Goliath’ in this kind of games.

In short, McCarthy regards his team as the underdogs while admitting that Bafana Bafana are strong favourites.

And indeed, Bafana Bafana are strong favourites having already won their opening two AFCON qualifiers.

Mosimane’s charges beat Guinea 2-1 in their opening match before hammering Eritrea 5-0 in their second Group D encounter.

BAFANA BAFANA VS KENYA: BENNI MCCARTHY SAYS HE’S ALWAYS ‘david’

“Coach Pitso has always had the upper hand because he has always been at places that had the infrastructures and the best of everything,” McCarthy told reporters.

“And for me, you know, as a young coach, I always just tried to give my best and stay true to myself.



“Go out there and try and play the best way that I can, that can make it difficult for whoever you’re up against, and sometimes we were fortunate.

“And on other occasions, we weren’t as fortunate. So, today is another one of those cases. It’s David versus Goliath, and unfortunately, I seem to always be David, I’m never Goliath,” added McCarthy.

World.title: The historic town where crime could peak this year
World.content:
Many South African towns are being plagued by crime.

But Ladysmith is unique in that crime in the area has risen 30.1% since 2019.

Last year, crime in the town overtook its 2013 peak after 4 consecutive years of rising crime.



Crime has increased every year since 2020 in this farming town

During the COVID-19 pandemic, when crime in many South African towns declined, crime in Ladysmith only decreased 8.7% from its previous all-time low in 2018.

Then in 2021, crime started rising again.

Crime has been rising ever since and peaked during the 2025-2026 period, which ended in March this year.

What’s worse: in the first quarter of this year, between April and June, crime rose 3.6%.

If this trend continues, crime in Ladysmith will surpass last year’s record.

In the uThukela District Municipality, Ladysmith recorded the most crime, nearly three times as much as the second police precinct: Estcourt.



Ladysmith still managed this position despite crime in Estcourt rising 45.1% in the first quarter.

Drug-related crime in the area is up 28.7%, while arrests for driving under the influence of alcohol and drugs are up by 491%.

Ladysmith is also part of a scary pattern affecting South Africa’s farming and historical towns: drug crime increases and so do other crimes.

Will unemployment make things worse?

Those in authority rarely want to admit the connection between unemployment and crime.

Yet crime is most persistent in areas with a large unemployed population.

Ladysmith, part of the Alfred Duma Local Municipality, meets this standard.

According to data from the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA), the Alfred Duma Local Municipality recorded 64 898 beneficiaries receiving the Social Relief of Distress (SRD) grant.

The grant is limited to people receiving less than R670 a month.

Ladysmith, as part of the Alfred Duma Local Municipality, had the fifth-highest number of beneficiaries in KwaZulu-Natal.

According to National Treasury, unemployment in the municipality stood at 34% in 2022, higher than the national unemployment rate at the time.

World.title: Asanele Velebayi ‘proud’ after netting first Kaizer Chiefs goal
World.content:
Asanele Velebayi opened his goal account for Kaizer Chiefs with the winning strike in the Carling Knockout Cup quarter-finals. Image: Kaizer Chiefs

Asanele Velebayi opened his goal account for Kaizer Chiefs with the winning strike in the Carling Knockout Cup quarter-finals.

The speedy winger scored the decisive goal in Kaizer Chiefs’ 2-1 quarter-final victory over Siwelele FC at the new Peter Mokaba Stadium in Polokwane last Sunday.

It was a significant contribution from the 23-year-old, who was introduced as a substitute in the 75th minute and needed just nine minutes to make his mark.



Dominated the encounter

The Glamor Boys had dominated much of the encounter, but found themselves trailing before Wandile Duba converted a penalty on the stroke of half-time to restore parity.

Mduduzi Shabalala had earlier missed an opportunity from the penalty spot.

With the match finely balanced, Velebayi eventually provided the breakthrough in the 84th minute.

A defensive mistake from Siwelele allowed Kaizer Chiefs striker Flavio Da Silva to win possession in a dangerous area.

Velebayi immediately found space on the right side of the penalty area, received the pass and calmly fired home.

The goal secured Kaizer Chiefs’ place in the last four and gave the winger a memorable personal milestone.



Velebayi wants more goals for Kaizer Chiefs

Reflecting on the victory, Velebayi admitted that Kaizer Chiefs could have settled the contest much earlier.

“It was a game of transition,” he said.

“There were a lot of turnovers in possession. In truth, we should have wrapped up the game by half-time, and we are working hard to be more clinical in front of goal.”

The former Cape Town Spurs player, who turns 24 in December, said scoring his first Kaizer Chiefs goal was particularly special because it proved decisive.

“Scoring my first goal means a lot, especially that it was a goal that won the match and takes us into the next round,” he said.

Velebayi also made it clear that he wants to contribute more regularly as the season progresses.

“I aim to help the team by improving my all-round game and scoring more goals when I get the chance.”

Kaizer chiefs face massive Sundowns test

Kaizer Chiefs now have Mamelodi Sundowns standing between them and a place in the Carling Knockout Cup final.

The semi-final represents another opportunity for Amakhosi to move closer to ending their long wait for major silverware.

Should they overcome Mamelodi Sundowns, Kaizer Chiefs will face either Stellenbosch FC or Orlando Pirates in the final.

The dates and kick-off times for the semi-finals have yet to be confirmed as at the time of publishing, but are expected to take place over the weekend of 21/22 November.

The final is set for Saturday, 12 December 2026.

For Velebayi, his first goal could be the start of an important contribution to Kaizer Chiefs’ pursuit of cup success this season.

World.title: WEATHER: 36°C heatwave gives way to weekend rain in Gauteng
World.content:
After experiencing its second heatwave of the 2026/27 summer season, Gauteng residents can finally breathe a sigh of relief, with temperatures expected to drop this weekend as rain makes a return to the province.

The heatwave follows recent severe weather that brought heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and localised flooding to parts of Gauteng last week.

Over the past three days, temperatures have climbed as high as 36°C, with Wednesday to Friday bringing little to no rainfall.



According to Gauteng Weather, Pretoria recorded a high of 36°C on Thursday, while Johannesburg reached 34°C.

On Friday, the capital is expected to reach a maximum of 35°C, following a minimum of 21°C, with no rain forecast. Johannesburg is also expected to experience similar weather conditions as the heatwave comes to an end.

Gauteng residents can expect rain this weekend

Although temperatures will remain relatively high in Pretoria on Saturday, afternoon showers are expected to bring some relief after three days of intense heat.



By Sunday, temperatures in the capital are expected to drop to a maximum of 28°C, with showers forecast for most of the day.

In Johannesburg, thundershowers are expected on Sunday afternoon, with temperatures dropping to a maximum of 26°C.

Looking ahead to next week, no rain is currently predicted for Gauteng, but temperatures are expected to remain in the mid-to-high 20s, offering residents some relief from the recent heatwave.



In Limpopo, rain is expected on Sunday; however, no rainfall is predicted in the North West province with temperatures reaching 33°C.

World.title: South Africa’s most beautiful beaches that tourists overlook
World.content:
South Africa is blessed with thousands of kilometres of coastline, offering everything from bustling beachfront promenades to secluded stretches of white sand and turquoise water.

Yet, when it comes to planning a summer holiday, many travellers tend to gravitate towards the same familiar destinations, including Camps Bay, Umhlanga, Ballito and Plettenberg Bay.

While these popular beaches have plenty to offer, there are several lesser-known coastal spots around the country that are just as deserving of attention.



From remote beaches along the Wild Coast to subtropical shores in KwaZulu-Natal, these destinations offer beautiful scenery and a chance to experience a different side of South Africa’s coastline.

Here are some of the country’s most beautiful beaches that deserve more attention.

1. Mabibi Beach, KwaZulu-Natal

Located along KwaZulu-Natal’s northern coastline, Mabibi is one of the province’s more secluded coastal destinations.

Situated within the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, the beach is surrounded by indigenous coastal forest and impressive dunes, with clear Indian Ocean water providing a striking contrast to the greenery.

Unlike the busier beaches further south, Mabibi offers a more remote experience, making it particularly appealing to travellers who want to spend time away from crowded beachfronts.

The surrounding area is also known for its marine life and turtle nesting activity, although visitors should be mindful of conservation rules and seasonal restrictions.



Access generally requires planning, and visitors should check road conditions and accommodation availability before travelling.

2. Mbotyi Beach, Eastern Cape

The Wild Coast is home to some of South Africa’s most dramatic coastal scenery, and Mbotyi is one of its standout destinations.

Situated near Lusikisiki in the Eastern Cape, Mbotyi is known for its long sandy beach, rolling green hills and surrounding forests.

The area offers a very different experience from the country’s more developed coastal resorts, with a landscape that feels relatively untouched.

Visitors can explore the surrounding coastline, enjoy long beach walks and discover some of the region’s waterfalls.

It is worth remembering that the Wild Coast is not always the easiest place to reach. Travellers should research their route and accommodation arrangements before setting off.

3. Hamburg Beach, Eastern Cape

Hamburg is a small coastal settlement at the mouth of the Keiskamma River, approximately 90km from East London.

It is a particularly appealing destination for those looking for a quieter seaside escape, with a pristine beach and river setting that feels far removed from the country’s major holiday resorts.

South African Tourism highlights the area for its beach, river and outdoor activities, including canoe trails, hiking and fishing.

Its relatively low-key atmosphere is part of its appeal, particularly for visitors who prefer exploring smaller coastal communities rather than spending their holidays in busy resort towns.

4. Strandfontein, Western Cape

Not to be confused with the beach of the same name near Cape Town, Strandfontein is a small coastal village on the West Coast.

The destination is particularly beautiful for its sweeping coastline and dramatic ocean views.

It is a good option for travellers wanting to explore beyond the more familiar West Coast destinations.

5. Gonubie Beach, Eastern Cape

Just outside East London, Gonubie offers a combination of beautiful sandy beaches, coastal scenery and a relaxed seaside atmosphere.

The beach is particularly attractive because of its river mouth and surrounding natural landscape.

Visitors can enjoy walks along the shoreline, explore the boardwalk and spend time enjoying the views over the Indian Ocean.

Although it is a popular destination for residents, it tends to receive less national attention than some of South Africa’s better-known coastal resorts.

6. Zinkwazi Beach, KwaZulu-Natal

Located along the KwaZulu-Natal North Coast, Zinkwazi is a small seaside village known for its beach and lagoon.

The area offers a quieter alternative to larger coastal destinations such as Ballito and Umhlanga.

Its lagoon provides opportunities for birdwatching and other water-based activities, while the beach is popular with visitors looking for a relaxed coastal getaway.

The surrounding greenery and laid-back village atmosphere make it an appealing summer destination.

7. Blythedale Beach, KwaZulu-Natal

Blythedale Beach is another North Coast destination that often gets overshadowed by its more established neighbours.

Situated between Ballito and the Tugela River area, it offers a long sandy coastline and a more relaxed holiday atmosphere.

It is particularly appealing to visitors who want to enjoy the KwaZulu-Natal coastline without necessarily staying in one of the province’s busiest resort towns.

8. Mzamba Beach, Eastern Cape

Near the KwaZulu-Natal border, Mzamba Beach is a striking coastal destination known for its sandstone formations and natural scenery.

The beach is particularly interesting for visitors who enjoy exploring geological features and unusual coastal landscapes.

Its location near the Wild Coast also makes it an appealing stop for travellers exploring the northern Eastern Cape coastline.

9. Noetzie Beach, Western Cape

Just outside Knysna, Noetzie Beach is one of the most distinctive coastal spots along the Garden Route.

The beach is famous for its unusual stone castles overlooking the shoreline, creating a setting that feels almost like something from a storybook.

Surrounded by forest and cliffs, it offers a beautiful contrast to the busier beaches in the area. Visitors should be prepared for the walk down to the beach and check local access arrangements before visiting.

10. Kosi Bay, KwaZulu-Natal

For travellers who want something that feels a little more tropical, Kosi Bay is difficult to overlook.

Located close to the Mozambique border, the area is known for its interconnected lakes, estuaries, mangrove forests and beautiful coastal scenery.

The combination of warm water, white sand and lush vegetation makes it one of KwaZulu-Natal’s most distinctive coastal destinations.

It is also part of the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Kosi Bay is not necessarily a quick beach stop, and visitors should plan their journey carefully, particularly when travelling to more remote areas.

A different kind of South African beach holiday

South Africa’s coastline has far more to offer than its best-known holiday destinations.

For travellers willing to venture a little further, places such as Mabibi, Mbotyi and Hamburg offer a chance to experience some of the country’s most beautiful coastal scenery without following the usual holiday crowds.

However, less-developed beaches do not always have lifeguards, public facilities or easy road access. Visitors should check local swimming conditions, safety information and access arrangements before travelling.

World.title: SASSA approves 22 000 old age grants in 3 months
World.content:
The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) is coming out in support of pensioners, recent data would suggest.

In 90 days, the agency approved 22 060 Old Age grant applications.

Most pensioners approved within one week after applying

SASSA isn’t wasting time getting pensioners their grant money. According to the most recent data, the agency approved 22 244 applications by the end of September.



Of these, 22 060 were approved within 90 days; the remaining 184 took longer.

19 959 of these applications were approved within the first 7 days.

The agency also approved 93 031 Child Support Grant (CSG) applications and 34 221 Disability Grant (DG) applications.



However, the grant applications look less impressive when you consider that the agency received 64 409 Older Persons Grant applications in the period when it only approved 22 244 applications.

This means only 34% of applications had been approved by the end of September.

Approved applicants will receive between R2 400 and R2 420 a month in assistance, depending on their age.



By the end of September, the agency recorded 2 495 new Old Age Grant beneficiaries, meaning most of the more than 22 000 approvals were simply reapplications.

Getting an Old Age Grant

About 76% of South Africans over 60 receive an Old Age Grant.

And in these tough economic times, many more pensioners, some of whom are still working, are applying.



To apply for the grant, applicants can visit the SASSA online services portal.

There, create an account by selecting LOGIN and clicking “register new account.”

Follow the prompts and enter all your details.

SASSA will generate a list of supporting documents you need to provide.



Before applying, ensure you’re eligible.

An unmarried applicant must receive less than R9 350 a month and have less than R1 584 000 in assets.

Married applicants must have a joint income below R18 700 a month and own less than R3 168 000 in assets.

World.title: Can France stop the Springboks’ maul at Stade de France?
World.content:
France need to contain the power of the Springboks' driving maul. Image: France Rugby, Springboks (X).

The Springboks’ maul remains one of the most important pieces of their arsenal.

South Africa are making full use of their power and the new World Rugby guidelines.

Can an injury-stricken France defuse the driving maul in their Nations Championship clash on Friday?



How the Springboks mauled Italy in Turin

South Africa thrashed Italy in Round 4 on Saturday, leading 45-0 at the halftime break.

A major component of their ruthless attack was the driving maul.

As cited by South Africa Rugby, this set piece was the platform for four tries against the hosts.



The match ended in a thumping 66-7 win for the Springboks, who are chasing the inaugural Nations Championship title.

When Italy did stop the rolling maul, Morne van den Berg breached the defensive line instead, according to KickOff.

This may be a warning sign for France ahead of the game at Stade de France today (13 November).



Effectively, Coach Rassie Erasmus’ tactical brilliance means closing one door just opens another.

World Rugby changeS the game for mauls

In June, World Rugby published a Law Application Guideline on the driving maul.

This was in response to concerns about the difficulty of refereeing, managing, and even explaining the set piece.



The rugby body said it aimed to ‘clear up those messy situations when the contest for possession/space has been won’.

In essence, the maul has become a contest of timing and momentum, instead of the previous free-for-all.

Rassie seems to have immediately latched onto the new guidelines to make the driving maul even more potent.



As cited by Planet Rugby, he said the maul could be a strength for all teams:

“So well done to World Rugby. When it was seven- or eight-man mauls, in the past you could stop it with the four going around and dragging the maul back. Then there was no space for the backs to attack, but now you have to commit to the maul and the vacuum is open.” Your #Springboks team to face France in Paris tomorrow night 🇿🇦#ForeverGreenForeverGold pic.twitter.com/dFe6jG7pYE  November 12, 2026

Can France contain the Springboks’ maul?

French coach Fabien Galthié is already aware that South Africa’s top set piece is delivering results.

The last time the two giants met, the Springboks’ maul played a crucial role in their 32-17 win over France.

With few options for stopping it, Les Bleus were penalised repeatedly for dragging the maul down illegally.



The Springboks’ XV remains focused on power, and the driving maul is sure to be used as a primary weapon.

France, meanwhile, head into the contest with a team depleted by injuries.

As reported by SuperSport, Les Bleus have recalled several veterans, including experienced hooker Julien Marchand.



RugbyPass lists Emmanuel Meafou, Thibaud Flament, Demba Bamba, Marko Gazotti, Oscar Jegou, and Anthony Jelonch on the forwards injury list.

Galthié has also switched Antoine Dupont to flyhalf to cover for injuries among the back line.

Romain Ntamack dislocated his shoulder in the 54-17 win over Fiji on 7 November.



For France, finding an answer to the Springboks’ maul remains the big question.

World.title: Wins by religious Democrats break Republican grip on faith in politics
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Wins by a string of openly religious Democratic candidates in last week's midterm elections have broken the Republican stranglehold on integrating faith and politics, a change that could reshape America's political landscape for years to come.

For decades, Democratic Party candidates have been reluctant to talk about faith and done little to actively reach out to religious voters, who favored Republicans, viewed as the party of traditional family values.

But this year, that pattern was shattered as Methodist megachurch pastor Adam Hamilton in Kansas and Presbyterian seminarian James Talarico in Texas won in deeply conservative states that hadn't elected a Democratic senator in decades.

Using the Bible to call for decency in politics and oppose the violent crackdown on undocumented immigrants, they were among six clergy or pastors-in-training winning seats as Democrats, helping them recapture Congress and deal a heavy blow to President Donald Trump's party.

In Michigan, voters provided another kind of religious breakthrough by electing Democrat Abdul El-Sayed as the first Muslim senator.

"Democrats have long been the party of policies and programs rather than faith and values," but they "finally cracked the code," said Andrew Koneschusky, head of public relations firm Beltway Advisors in Washington and a former Democratic aide.

World.title: Bollywood bolsters security as underworld fears return
World.content:
MUMBAI - It sounds like a Bollywood thriller, but a spate of shootings and extortion threats targeting Mumbai's stars has sent the industry scrambling for bodyguards, reviving memories of the underworld's grip on cinema in the 1990s.

From gunshots to cash demands, the incidents have unsettled the Indian industry, decades after police crackdowns weakened the criminal gangs once deeply embedded in the multi-billion-dollar business.

Police have linked the latest violence to the gang of Lawrence Bishnoi, a convicted Indian gangster accused by US prosecutors of directing a global criminal network from behind bars.

"Stars are moving around with bodyguards on either side," actor and security agency owner Ronit Roy said.

"There has been a sharp increase in demand... Requests have expanded beyond just lead actors, to include family members and children."

Author S. Hussain Zaidi, a former investigative journalist, said opportunistic criminals were exploiting the notoriety of established gangsters.

"Some desperadoes are opening fire in the air to scare the industry and spread fear," Zaidi told AFP.

"And they have succeeded -- as people have started believing that the mafia-dominated 1990s era is back."

The latest incidents include gunfire targeting actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai in October, and an alleged $600,000 extortion demand against actor Tusshar Kapoor.

Police have arrested 13 people under organised crime laws in connection with the October shooting, alleging it was intended to extort money, establish gang dominance and spread fear.

Police said there had also been surveillance of other prominent figures.

They have named Anil Pandit, an alleged Bishnoi gang member, as wanted in connection with the shooting.

- Darkest periods -

Anxiety reverberating across the industry has spilt into public view.

Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan recently greeted fans from behind a bulletproof enclosure outside his Mumbai home during his customary Sunday appearance, while security was beefed up around actor Shah Rukh Khan's home for his birthday.

But Zaidi said the major gangsters of the 1990s were now dead, imprisoned or inactive.

"The only gangster we hear of these days is Lawrence Bishnoi and even he is in jail, so there is no way that any local Mumbai-based gangster has control over the city," he said.

The late 1990s and early 2000s were among Bollywood's darkest periods, when criminal syndicates used threats, extortion and violence to influence film financing, casting and distribution.

They included Dawood Ibrahim, a UN-sanctioned fugitive accused of involvement in the 1993 Mumbai bombings that killed 257 people, and his former lieutenant turned rival Chhota Rajan, who is behind bars in India.

Producers were pressured to pay protection money, surrender business interests and bow to gangsters' demands.

The underworld's influence waned as police intensified operations, strengthened by laws passed in 1999 targeting organised crime, while the growth of corporate financing further reduced gangsters' influence over the film business.

- 'We will kill you' -

Rajiv Rai, director of the hit thriller "Gupt", received extortion demands and threatening calls in the late 1990s before eventually leaving India for Britain.

"I was the victim in the 1990s, the world knows," he told AFP.

Watching the latest incidents unfold, Rai said the motives were harder to decipher.

Bishnoi's gang has been linked to threats against Salman Khan, reportedly over allegations that the Bollywood star had hunted blackbuck antelopes in 1998.

The animals are revered by the Bishnoi community, a Hindu sect whose faith places strong emphasis on wildlife protection.

Indian authorities have also accused gang members of opening fire outside Khan's Mumbai home and of involvement in the killing of Baba Siddique, a prominent politician with close ties to the film industry, in 2024.

After the October shooting targeting Shroff, a social media post and audio message attributed to a Bishnoi gang associate reportedly claimed responsibility, citing the actor's closeness to Khan.

"In the 1990s, we knew their agenda... ransom money," Rai said.

"Now they are calling and saying if you are Salman's friend, we will kill you... now what kind of agenda is this?"

Ahmed Ali, a crime journalist, said he believed that "many of these seem to be prank calls, to cash in on the situation that Bishnoi has created".

Producer Boney Kapoor, who was targeted by underworld figures over a dispute involving overseas distribution rights for his 1997 Salman Khan film "Judwaa", believes the latest wave of violence will be "short-lived".

"I don't feel that kind of fear," he said. "But one has to be cautious; these shootings can't be ignored."

World.title: Record-breaking Kane fires England into Nations League knockouts
World.content:
LONDON - Harry Kane celebrated his record-breaking 126th England cap with a goal from the penalty spot as England beat Croatia 2-1 on Thursday to book a place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

Slaven Bilic's team were determined to avoid another embarrassment after their 7-0 mauling by England in Rijeka last month and looked much more solid from the kick-off at Wembley.

But goals from Morgan Rogers and captain Kane kept England second in Group A3 behind Spain, confirming their place in the Nations League last eight in March.

Thomas Tuchel's men have a chance to avenge their 3-2 defeat against the world champions in their Nations League opener when they travel to Madrid for Sunday's clash.

Spain beat the Czech Republic 2-0 in Prague on Thursday.

"After the first game when we lost here against them (Spain), we knew we left a bit out there," Kane told ITV.

"We knew we could've done a bit better. We said to ourselves 'let's win every game until the next one and see what happens'. It's the perfect opportunity now on Sunday to try and prove ourselves."

England and Croatia struggled to get out of second gear in the opening stages of their match in London.

Elliot Anderson fired over in the 16th minute and Croatia's Josip Misic flashed a shot wide midway through the first half.

Chelsea forward Rogers broke the deadlock in the 24th minute in slightly fortuitous fashion, following a neat move by the home side.

Kane floated a ball to Jude Bellingham on the right of the penalty area and the Real Madrid man cushioned the ball first time across the area towards Rogers.

World.title: LIVE | JMPD corruption under the spotlight at Madlanga
World.content:
PRETORIA - The Madlanga Commission will listen to testimony pertaining to criminality and corruption at the Johannesburg Metropolitan Police Department (JMPD).

The first witness on Friday will be the Hawks' Warrant Officer Phuti Eric Mashala.

On Thursday the Commission heard evidence on the country's crime intelligence.

Acting Coordinator of the National Intelligence Coordinating Committee, Dr Ntandazo Sifolo, revealed worrying information about the state of some law enforcement agencies.

Sifolo highlighted concerns about the integrity of the Independent Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC), the Inspector-General of Intelligence and the Independent Police Investigative Directorate (IPID).

He also raised concerns about vacant positions with the State Security Agency.

World.title: John Mathane steps down from Athletics South Africa leadership
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Athletics South Africa (ASA) Deputy President John Mathane has left the federation, stepping down from his leadership positions.

He has resigned as Deputy President, a member of the ASA Board and Acting President.

His departure brings an end to his involvement in the federation's leadership structures.

Mathane served in various capacities at the federation, including as Acting President during a period of transition.

He was elevated to the position following the suspension of James Moloi, who was found to have used the federation's corporate credit card at bottle stores and to fund international trips for girlfriends.

Jean Vester has since been appointed interim acting head of the beleaguered federation.

ASA is set to convene a two-day board meeting this weekend to deliberate on its governance roadmap.

Discussions are expected to focus on the proposed constitutional reform process and preparations for elections to appoint a new board.

World.title: 'Inside Gaza': Reporting a war when it hits home
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - How do journalists report on a war when they become victims of the violence, and when their proximity to the conflict is used to paint them as unreliable witnesses?

That's the issue explored in "Inside Gaza," a new documentary that follows journalists from global news agency AFP who were trapped in the territory as Israel exacted a fearsome revenge for Hamas's October 7 attack.

Director Hélène Lam Trong brings these news industry veterans in front of the camera, showing how they balance the difficult task of reporting on the massive military response with their own survival, as it destroys their city, killing family, friends and colleagues.

"Most international correspondents... cover a war or a news event and then return home to safety," freelance journalist and documentary filmmaker Lam Trong told AFP in Los Angeles, where the film was shown as part of The American French Film Festival.

"Palestinian journalists could not do that. They were trapped alongside the civilian population of Gaza, with no way out; as the days passed, they themselves became victims of the war."

- Questioned -

The Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, killed more than 1,200 people, the vast majority of them civilians. Armed men also took more than 200 people hostage.
