World.title: Leo XIV to 52,000 young people in Lima: “Be passionate about everything worthwhile”
World.content:
Leo XIV to 52,000 young people in Lima: “Be passionate about everything worthwhile”

13th Friday, November 2026 - 02:58 UTC Full article

Photo: REUTERS/Yara Nardi

Pope Leo XIV met some 52,000 young people at Lima’s National Stadium on Thursday, according to El País, in the last event of his stay in the Peruvian capital before travelling to Chiclayo, the diocese he led as bishop. “Someone told me that Peru needs hope. You are the sign of hope,” he told them, to applause.

The young people came from the coast, the highlands and the jungle, many with parish groups and others on their own, and alongside Peruvian flags there were also Venezuelan and Chilean ones. The Pope entered the stadium track in the popemobile at around six in the evening, as the stands displayed signs asking for his blessing. The vigil included testimonies, a theatrical performance in which Peruvian saints came to the rescue of young people in crisis, music and scissor dancers, an Andean ritual.

At around half past seven, Leo XIV spoke with a message of comfort and encouragement. “Dear young people, when you suffer, turn to Jesus. Do not be afraid to speak to him sincerely. He knows our tears,” he said. “Be passionate about everything worthwhile. Cultivate your talents. Discover the richness of your culture. Do not settle for living according to what others expect of you.” He ended with an invitation to those who believe they are beyond redemption: “It is not too late to begin again.”

The Archbishop of Lima, Cardinal Carlos Castillo, recalled during the event Inti Sotelo and Bryan Pintado, the two young men of around twenty who were shot dead during the November 2020 protests. “In the recent history we have lived through in our country, young people often took to the streets to protest and in some cases several were shot. There are two martyrs: Inti and Bryan,” he said. Castillo said that after the crackdown many young people found in dance a form of expression that eventually reached the parishes. The testimonies included that of a young woman who lost a dozen relatives and of a nun who suffered abuse by a member of the Church.

Leo XIV, 71, who is recovering from lung cancer surgery, celebrates Mass on Friday at the Pampas de Pimentel, near Chiclayo, where nearly a million faithful are expected. On Saturday he will visit Cajamarca and Zaña, and on Sunday Cusco and Pucallpa, before returning to Rome on Monday, November 16.

World.title: British veteran returns to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took in 1982
World.content:
British veteran returns to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took in 1982

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 22:01 UTC Full article

Aged 18, Andy Gatrick found two wounded Argentine soldiers, later captured, at Mount Harriet in June 1982 and kept one’s helmet, which bore a name: Hector. Photo: Mick Dawson

A former Royal Marine has travelled to Argentina to return to an Argentine veteran the helmet he took during the Battle of Mount Harriet in the 1982 Falklands War, in a reunion filmed for a documentary, BBC Sussex reported.

Andy Gatrick, who was 18 at the time of the war, came across two injured Argentine soldiers during the Battle of Mount Harriet, fought on June 11 and 12, 1982. Both were captured by the Marines. Gatrick kept the helmet of one of them, which bore a name: Hector. Now 63, he managed to track him down and on October 23 flew to Gualeguaychú, in Entre Ríos province, to return it in person to Héctor Pereyra.

“I put my weapon down and as I bent down to put the strap over my shoulders, I saw movement and a cloth which looked like a white handkerchief. My eyes adjusted and there was two Argentinians, I didn’t know they were badly injured. I dived to the floor, weapon up. There was lots of shouting and swearing, bedlam,” Gatrick, from Bolton in northern England, said in footage sent to the BBC.

He was joined by another Royal Marine veteran, Mick Dawson, 62, who filmed the meeting for a documentary called Hector’s Helmet. According to Dawson, the British kit was poor and the Marines fought in berets, while the Argentines had American helmets, so Gatrick “borrowed” Pereyra’s. “In a very emotional day, he handed the helmet back in person to the guy he could have just as easily killed that night,” Dawson told BBC Radio Sussex. The two veterans “embraced like long lost brothers”, he said.

Dawson interviewed Pereyra about the moment when, wounded, he saw Gatrick emerge from the darkness. “He said, ‘I knew this man had the power of life or death over me and he chose life’,” Dawson recounted. “He then showed me a picture of his nine grandchildren and four children that wouldn’t have existed if Andy made a different decision that night. It was just the most amazing thing to witness.”

Dawson hopes to release the documentary next year. The 74-day war in 1982 left 907 dead: 649 Argentine military personnel, 255 British personnel and three civilian islanders.

World.title: Lula to visit Madrid on Monday to meet Sánchez, two weeks before Spain’s election
World.content:
Lula to visit Madrid on Monday to meet Sánchez, two weeks before Spain’s election

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 18:02 UTC Full article

The visit will also include a political event at which Lula will expressly back the Socialist candidate, and Sánchez’s team had spent two weeks trying to arrange it

Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will visit Madrid on Monday, November 16, to meet Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, less than two weeks before the snap general election on November 29, in which Sánchez is seeking re-election. It will be Lula’s first visit to Spain since he won Brazil’s election on October 25.

According to the Spanish government’s official statement, the two will hold a bilateral meeting at the Moncloa Palace to discuss relations between the two countries and coordination of initiatives such as Democracy Always and the Global Alliance against Hunger and Poverty. Lula will stop in Madrid on his way back from the UN climate summit, COP31, in Antalya, Turkey, and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila, where he will also make a state visit to the Philippines.

According to the Spanish press, the visit will also include a political event at which Lula will expressly back the Socialist candidate, and Sánchez’s team had spent two weeks trying to arrange it. Sánchez has presented Lula’s re-election and the Democratic victory in the US midterms as proof that the advance of the radical right can be halted.

CNN Brasil reported that Lula will be accompanied by congressman André Janones, the architect of the digital strategy that helped his electoral comeback. The Spanish government and the Socialist Party insist that Janones is not advising Sánchez’s campaign and there are no plans for him to do so.

Polls show a slight recovery for the Socialists, so far insufficient to govern. A survey by 40dB for El País and Cadena SER shows the Socialist Party up almost two points, but the People’s Party and Vox would together win a comfortable absolute majority of more than 190 seats; 176 are needed to govern. The state-run Centre for Sociological Research shows a stronger Socialist recovery.

Neither Lula nor Sánchez attended the Ibero-American Summit held in Madrid last week. According to El País, Lula needed to rest and recover his voice after the campaign. Sánchez spoke by phone on Thursday with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum about bilateral relations and the outcome of the summit.

World.title: Paraguay’s banking superintendent arrested in the Ueno Bank investigation
World.content:
Paraguay’s banking superintendent arrested in the Ueno Bank investigation

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 11:20 UTC Full article

Insfrán was named in a criminal complaint expanded by opposition lawmakers last week, alongside the economy minister and other officials

Paraguay’s Superintendent of Banks, Holger Insfrán, was arrested on Thursday as part of the investigation into the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has already led to the pre-trial detention of former President Santiago Peña and former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, according to prosecution sources cited by the EFE news agency. The charges against him have not been disclosed.

The Superintendency of Banks, part of the Central Bank, is responsible for supervising and regulating Paraguay’s financial institutions, including Ueno. Insfrán was named in a criminal complaint expanded by opposition lawmakers last week, alongside the economy minister and other officials.

According to prosecutors, Ueno received large amounts of public funds during Peña’s term, including from five pension funds, while granting allegedly irregular loans to companies owned by its owners, the Vázquez Group. The bank had 2.94 million customers.

Peña, removed by the Senate on November 6, is charged with alleged breach of trust, as instigator, and self-serving administration, as perpetrator, and could face a maximum sentence of 15 years, according to prosecutors. He says he is innocent. Carvallo, who headed the finance company from which the bank emerged before Peña appointed him to lead the Central Bank in 2023, is accused of breach of trust, producing false public documents and self-serving administration.

The Central Bank said on Wednesday that 100% of customers covered by the state guarantee have received an advance of up to 40 minimum wages, about 121.8 million guaraníes or roughly US$19,600, under the emergency law passed by Congress. It has until Monday to complete repayments up to the guarantee ceiling of 75 minimum wages, about 228.3 million guaraníes or roughly US$36,600.

World.title: Leo XIV arrives in Peru, his “homeland”, defending international law and reconciliation
World.content:
Leo XIV arrives in Peru, his “homeland”, defending international law and reconciliation

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 10:59 UTC Full article

Leo XIV will remain in Peru until Monday, November 16. On Friday he will celebrate Mass in Pimentel, near Chiclayo, the diocese he led from 2015 to 2023

Pope Leo XIV arrived in Lima on Wednesday, the final stage of his South American tour, and in his first speech in Peru, the country where he lived for some twenty years and whose nationality he holds, called for diplomacy that “respects international law” in the face of wars and for the country’s past events “to be dealt with justice and sensitivity”.

President Keiko Fujimori received him at the foot of the plane, and thousands of people greeted him along the route from the airport. After meeting him at the Government Palace, the Pope addressed the authorities. “Today I understand how much of this land remains with me and how much of my own history also belongs to you,” he said, referring to a country he regards as his homeland.

In the first international reference of his tour, Leo XIV said, without naming any country, that “the wars and tensions afflicting so many peoples demand patient diplomacy that keeps dialogue open, respects international law and seeks agreements that protect the life and dignity of people”. “Every nation has legitimate aspirations, but none can consider the fate of others alien to it,” he added, encouraging Peru to keep contributing to regional and international cooperation.

The Pope also referred to the country’s recent past. “Peru too has gone through difficult moments that have tested coexistence among its people. The events of the past deserve to be dealt with justice and sensitivity, leaving room for harmony to grow,” he said, adding that “democratic life means recognising that no one can be treated as a problem, but as a person with dignity”. Fujimori, who spoke before him, said “Peru needs to reconcile” and that “no country can live as a prisoner of its wounds”.

The Pope spoke alongside the daughter of Alberto Fujimori, the former president convicted of human rights violations, pardoned in 2017 and who died in 2024. According to El País, in 2017 the then Bishop of Chiclayo Robert Prevost criticised the former leader for apologising only in a “generic” way. On the eve of the visit, victims of state violence during the armed conflict of the 1980s and 1990s and of the crackdown on the 2022 and 2023 protests, in which at least some fifty people died, sent a letter alleging that “some people, from within the Church” are preventing their stories from reaching the pontiff. Former President Dina Boluarte, under whose government those deaths occurred, attended the speech.

Leo XIV will remain in Peru until Monday, November 16. On Friday he will celebrate Mass in Pimentel, near Chiclayo, the diocese he led from 2015 to 2023, where nearly a million faithful are expected; on Saturday he will visit Cajamarca and Zaña, and on Sunday, Cusco and Pucallpa, before returning to Rome.

World.title: Law of the sea tribunal to rule on November 28 on Argentina’s bid to halt Sea Lion
World.content:
Law of the sea tribunal to rule on November 28 on Argentina’s bid to halt Sea Lion

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 10:58 UTC Full article

Because the United Kingdom chose the International Court of Justice and Argentina the Hamburg tribunal, the merits of the case will be decided by an arbitral tribunal

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will announce on Saturday, November 28, its decision on Argentina’s request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, after two days of hearings concluded in Hamburg on Wednesday. Argentina presented final requests that were more specific than its initial ones, and the United Kingdom asked the tribunal to reject them all.

According to the tribunal’s statement, the reading of the order is tentatively set for noon on November 28. The date is later than some experts had anticipated, who had put the decision around November 13.

In its final submissions, signed by Argentina’s agent, Ambassador Mario Oyarzábal, Argentina asks that, pending the constitution of the arbitral tribunal that will rule on the merits, the United Kingdom take all necessary measures to ensure that no new drilling for exploitation and no installation of production infrastructure takes place in the North Falklands Basin, referred to in the Argentine filing as the North Malvinas Basin, in connection with Sea Lion. It also asks that the UK refrain from using information obtained during exploration to the detriment of Argentina’s rights, cease preventing Argentina from complying with its obligation to protect the marine environment of the disputed areas, and refrain from measures that might aggravate the dispute, in particular the granting of new exploitation authorisations. In its October request, Argentina had asked more broadly that the start or continuation of exploitation be prevented.

The United Kingdom, in a filing signed by its agent, Sally Langrish, asked the tribunal to “reject all the requests” by Argentina. Attorney General Ellie Reeves, who led the delegation, argued that the tribunal has no jurisdiction over sovereignty issues and warned that blocking the project would “kill” it, with “devastating” consequences for the islanders, who would lose billions of pounds in revenue. “In reality, what Argentina opposes is the Falkland Islands government licensing hydrocarbon activities for the economic benefit of the Falkland islanders,” she told the judges, according to coverage of the hearing.

For Argentina, jurist Marcelo Kohen said the United Kingdom cannot behave like a 17th-century colonial power treating vast expanses of the ocean as its own, according to The Guardian. Argentina also argued that London cannot invoke the sovereignty dispute to escape the tribunal’s jurisdiction while exploiting the resources “as if the dispute had already been resolved in its favour”.

Because the United Kingdom chose the International Court of Justice and Argentina the Hamburg tribunal, the merits of the case will be decided by an arbitral tribunal. Hamburg can only order provisional measures if it finds that tribunal would have prima facie jurisdiction, that there is urgency and that the right invoked is plausible. Sea Lion, operated by Israel’s Navitas Petroleum and Britain’s Rockhopper Exploration, is expected to begin drilling in January 2027.

The hearing took place while Princess Anne is visiting the islands and ahead of the debate on Argentina’s sovereignty defence bill in the Chamber of Deputies, scheduled for Thursday.

World.title: British Antarctic Survey begins a season featuring the largest-ever penguin census
World.content:
British Antarctic Survey begins a season featuring the largest-ever penguin census

12th Thursday, November 2026 - 10:51 UTC Full article

The season began with the departure from the UK of the polar icebreaker RRS Sir David Attenborough, which is running on hydrotreated vegetable oil, a biofuel

The British Antarctic Survey (BAS), the UK’s national operator in Antarctica, began its 2026/27 research season in late October, including the largest penguin census ever carried out on the continent, with flights from the British Rothera station and from Chile’s Marsh station on King George Island.

The season began with the departure from the UK of the polar icebreaker RRS Sir David Attenborough, which is running on hydrotreated vegetable oil, a biofuel, as part of the organisation’s efforts to reduce emissions, and with the arrival of its aircraft at Rothera. Dozens of scientists and support staff will be spread across the five British stations.

The census will use an aerial camera system aboard a Twin Otter aircraft, successfully trialled last season, to count around 200 colonies of Adélie, chinstrap and gentoo penguins on the Antarctic Peninsula and the South Shetland, Elephant Island and South Orkney groups. The data will help scientists understand population changes and the potential impact of krill fishing, and will feed into the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

New projects also include the first drone-based monitoring system for the body condition and demography of humpback whales, whose populations are recovering after the end of commercial whaling. A multinational study will investigate why the flow of warm water to the Amundsen Sea, a major driver of ice loss in West Antarctica, varies, with the help of the autonomous submarine Autosub Long Range. Other teams will study the compacted snow layer that protects ice shelves from melting and, with NASA and the California Institute of Technology, deploy an instrument beneath the Filchner-Ronne Ice Shelf.

At King Edward Point station in South Georgia, the groundfish survey will mark 40 years since it began in 1987, one of the longest records in the Southern Ocean and key to studying the effects of ocean warming on fish and the wider ecosystem.

“Collaboration is at the heart of Antarctic science,” said BAS Director Professor Dame Jane Francis, highlighting the participation of researchers from Chile, the Netherlands, the United States and Australia, as well as the value of long-term monitoring programmes.

World.title: Milei in tears as he bids farewell to Leo XIV at Ezeiza, closing the Pope’s Argentina visit
World.content:
Milei in tears as he bids farewell to Leo XIV at Ezeiza, closing the Pope’s Argentina visit

11th Wednesday, November 2026 - 19:49 UTC Full article

The day had begun at the Devoto prison in Buenos Aires, where the Pope listened to some 70 inmates

President Javier Milei was moved to tears during Pope Leo XIV’s farewell at Ezeiza airport, at the end of a four-day visit, the first by a pontiff to Argentina in 39 years. The Pope left for Peru, the second leg of his South American tour, after celebrating his last Mass at the Basilica of Luján.

Milei, accompanied by his sister and presidential chief of staff, Karina Milei, and Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno, greeted the Pope and the bishops present and walked him to the steps of the plane, an Aerolíneas Argentinas Airbus A330. While the aircraft was still waiting to depart, the three embraced, as behind a fence a group of children waved small Vatican flags. The plane began taxiing at 2.14 p.m.

Javier Milei in tears, absolutely balling his eyes out, thanking Pope Leo XIV for his visit, as he asks the Pope repeatedly to pray for him. This has been an incredibly well organised trip. Everyone involved should rightly be praised. Argentina you won. https://t.co/1vAO8wZqXp — Catholic Sat (@CatholicSat) November 11, 2026

Earlier, in Luján, the Pope bade farewell to the faithful. “Thank you for receiving me with such affection. Thank you, Argentina, for receiving me with open arms. Farewell, my dear Argentina!” he said. Official figures reported by Argentine media put the crowd at the Mass at more than three million people, which have not been independently verified. At the start, he placed a Golden Rose, the highest honour the Vatican grants to Marian shrines, at the feet of the image of the Virgin. According to Infobae, he said in his farewell message that the country “now has two Popes, one born here and one by adoption”.

The day had begun at the Devoto prison in Buenos Aires, where the Pope listened to some 70 inmates. “I hope to take away the message that a new life is possible,” he said, according to the news site MDZ.

The visit began on Sunday with a speech to the authorities, with Milei present, in which the Pope said that “the economy must be at the service of the person”. On Monday he celebrated Mass in Palermo, with some 2.5 million people according to the authorities, and on Tuesday another in Córdoba, with some 650,000, according to El País. The visit was preceded by tensions between the government and the Catholic hierarchy over austerity policies. Milei, who harshly criticised Pope Francis in the past, described him on Sunday as “the most important Argentine in history”.

The Pope arrives in Lima tonight, where President Keiko Fujimori will receive him at the Government Palace. Between November 13 and 16 he will visit Chiclayo, Cusco and Pucallpa, among other places, and he will return to Rome on the 16th.

World.title: Mexico agrees to buy 11 Black Hawk helicopters from the United States for US $1.07 billion
World.content:
Mexico is moving to acquire 11 UH-60M Black Hawk helicopters from the United States, in a deal valued at an estimated US $1.075 billion.

The purchase will modernize Mexico’s helicopter fleet by expanding its existing Black Hawk fleet, which the U.S. sees as being in its own best interest.

“This proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of an ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in North America,” the State Department said in a statement.

“In addition, the procurement will reinforce U.S.-Mexico bilateral relations and strengthen Mexico’s capability to provide in-country airlift support for its forces engaged in counter-drug operations,” it added.

Although the State Department has authorized the potential sale, the transaction is not yet finalized. But Mexico’s Defense Minister Ricardo Trevilla Trejo said that the purchase process is underway and that the aircraft units are expected to arrive in 2028 and 2029.

The State Department said the principal contractor will be Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin Company, located in Stratford, CT.

According to Trevilla, the aircraft would support tasks under the DN-III-E Plan for rescue work in weather emergencies, as well as firefighting efforts, troop transport, and air ambulance operations.

Sheinbaum emphasized the need to acquire more aircraft for rescue work, recalling that last year “the country saw the most significant air bridge ever established” in response to the emergency caused by heavy rains in five states.

During that crisis, helicopters had to be called in from other regions, leading the president to suggest that the Navy and Defense Ministries buy more aircraft.

But the aircraft is designed for military use, and the purchase included weaponry, military equipment, training and logistical support.

The potential transaction comes amid increased bilateral Mexico-U.S. coordination against organized crime. U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson has described the cooperation as “historic,” highlighting their efforts to dismantle drug and arms trafficking networks.

With reports from El Economista, and Defensa.com

World.title: Sheinbaum meets with OpenAI’s Greg Brockman to discuss AI’s potential in Mexican healthcare
World.content:
President Claudia Sheinbaum met on Wednesday with Greg Brockman, president and co-founder of OpenAI, the San Francisco-based company that created ChatGPT.

“At the National Palace, we welcomed OpenAI’s president and co-founder Greg Brockman and his team,” Sheinbaum wrote on social media.

En Palacio Nacional, recibimos al presidente y cofundador de OpenAI, Greg Brockman, y a su equipo; conversamos sobre las diversas aplicaciones de la inteligencia artificial, particularmente en el sector Salud. Coincidimos en que esta tecnología puede generar beneficios en atención médica. — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 12, 2026

“We discussed the various applications of artificial intelligence, particularly in the healthcare sector. We agreed that this technology can bring benefits to healthcare,” she wrote.

Sheinbaum’s meeting with Brockman came a few weeks after the federal government announced the establishment of an Advisory Council for the Digital Transformation of the Health Sector, which is aimed at improving the control, storage and distribution of medications.

Members of the council will use digital tools and artificial intelligence (AI) to detect medication shortages — a long-running problem in Mexico — track warehouse inventory and expedite delivery to public hospitals and health centers.

There was no indication from Sheinbaum that OpenAI is going to collaborate withe the council in any way.

However, it is clear that the federal government is seeking to use AI as a means to improve healthcare in Mexico.

At her Thursday morning press conference, Sheinbaum told reporters that her government is interested in collaborating with China on “different issues,” one of which is “smart hospitals.”

“We’re very interested in the smart hospitals they have in China,” she said ahead of her trip to Shenzhen to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Leaders’ Meeting.

“… [We want to] implement this model in our country,” Sheinbaum said.

A smart hospital is a healthcare facility that uses a range of technology, including AI, to automate certain tasks and improve patient care.

The president is not the only Mexican official to have met with an OpenAI executive. Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard met OpenAI CEO Sam Altman in the United States in early September. Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO of chipmaker Nvidia on Thursday, and Tom Brown, co-founder of the AI company Anthropic, also met Ebrard at a G20 meeting in North Carolina.

According to the Economy Ministry, Ebrard said at the time that “Mexico must develop its capabilities in AI, given that the impact AI will have on the economy is as disruptive as the impact the advent of electricity once had on manufacturing.”

World.title: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico as a new migrant caravan heads north in Chiapas
World.content:
Listen to this article

U.S. President Donald Trump threatened on Thursday to double tariffs on Mexican goods if Mexico doesn’t stop migrants traveling through the country en route to the United States.

His threat in an early morning post to Truth Social came two days after a caravan of more than 1,000 migrants began walking north from Tapachula, a city in the southern state of Chiapas near the border with Guatemala.

https://t.co/D8zHTd06Tk — Rapid Response 47 (@RapidResponse47) November 12, 2026

“Here we go again!” Trump wrote at the start of his post.

“With the perceived loss by the Republicans in the Midterms – I WAS NOT ON THE BALLOT – the INVASION of our Country is taking place again. Huge CARAVANS are forming and beginning their illegal march through Mexico. Many of the people in these Caravans are those that various countries don’t want – ‘Send them to America,’ they say – But they will not be accepted!,” he wrote before making his threat.

“MEXICO MUST STOP THEM, NOW, and if they do not do so, the Tariffs on Mexico will be IMMEDIATELY DOUBLED,” Trump wrote.

“MEXICO, THE GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, THE VERY LIBERAL NEW GOVERNOR OF TEXAS, OUR GREAT BORDER PATROL, & ICE, HAVE BEEN SO INFORMED. There will be no leniency!”

Among the U.S. tariffs Trump could conceivably double are those that currently apply to Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles. In ongoing trade talks with the U.S., Mexico is attempting to negotiate a reduction of the Section 232 duties, which were imposed last year.

Trump’s latest tariff threat — one of various he has directed at Mexico over the years — came after his administration’s border czar, Tom Homan, told Fox News that Mexico “needs to put troops on their southern border and northern border” to stop migrant caravans.

“It’s against the law in Mexico to transit that country if you’re from another country without a transit visa. So they’re breaking Mexico’s law … [and Mexico] needs to step up,” he said in an interview on Wednesday.

Referring to last week’s U.S. midterm results, Homan also said:

“Congress may be more blue, Texas may be more blue, but the White House is red, bright red. And again President Trump created the most secure border in history. These caravans can come to the border all they want. They’re not going to be released into the United States. They’re going to be turned around or prosecuted and turned around because we will charge them with a crime so they can sit in jail, serve their sentence before they’re deported. But we’re not giving one inch on this border.”

For his part, U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin shared Trump’s Truth Social post to his X account.

“This illegal migrant caravan will NOT be allowed to enter our country. Full stop,” he wrote above it.

Sheinbaum: No migrant caravan has reached the northern border in Trump’s second term

Asked about Trump’s tariff threat at her Thursday morning press conference, Sheinbaum said that “no migrant caravan has reached the northern border” since Trump began his second term in January 2025.

U.S. authorities’ encounters with migrants have significantly declined during Trump’s second term, indicating that unauthorized border-crossing attempts have fallen. The White House said late last month that “illegal crossings” were at an “all-time low” thanks to Trump’s border policies.

On Thursday morning, Sheinbaum said there are currently two migrant caravans traveling through Mexico.

“One caravan is in Arriaga, Chiapas. It formed with around 500 or … 600 people and fewer than 100 remain,” she said.

Mexico is committed to orderly migration, with dignity for migrants. As President Sheinbaum said today, no migrant caravan has reached Mexico’s northern border. Mexico makes clear to migrants that there is no path into the United States and offers them a safe return home. The great majority choose to return. The results are visible at the border: a historic 97% reduction in encounters, reaching their lowest level since 1959. That reflects Mexico’s work every day alongside our U.S. counterparts, and that cooperation will continue. — Roberto Lazzeri (@robertolazzeri) November 12, 2026

“How do we… [reduce the size of the caravan]? We tell the people in the caravan that it’s very difficult to get to the United States, that if their goal is to get to the United States, they won’t be able to achieve it,” Sheinbaum said.

“We seek a way for them to safely return to their countries. If someone wants to stay in Mexico under certain conditions in a certain place they can. But the vast majority return to their countries of origin once they find out they won’t be able to cross Mexico’s border with the United States,” she said.

Sheinbaum said that the government wouldn’t use force against migrants traveling through the country, as has occurred in the past.

W Radio reported on Thursday that a caravan of around 1,500 migrants was in Huixtla, a town around 40 kilometers north of Tapachula. It reported that 80% of the caravan’s members are from Honduras, while the remainder are from Nicaragua, Guatemala and El Salvador. W Radio reported that the migrants in Arriaga, located in northern Chiapas near the state’s border with Oaxaca, are waiting for the larger caravan to arrive in order to join it and continue traveling toward the Mexico-U.S. border.

The caravan of 1,500 migrants left Tapachula on Tuesday and includes many families, according to Reuters. The news agency reported that many migrants in the caravan “saw new reason for optimism” about their chances of entering the United States “after last week’s US elections.”

“… The migrants, mostly from Central America, hope the political shift could open pathways for them to live and work in the United States,” Reuters reported.

“There might be a light at the end of the tunnel, a way for us to ​get in,” said César Sandoval, a 47-year-old Nicaraguan man who was deported from the United States earlier this year.

“We believe the Democrats will help us… with God’s help,” he told Reuters in Tapachula.

Reuters reported that the caravan is first aiming to get to Mexico City “to seek assistance from the Mexican federal government and protection from being detained while traveling toward the U.S. border.”

The news agency noted that the journey to the capital is likely to take at least several weeks, reporting also that the migrants were carrying water “in the hot temperatures typical of southern Mexico.”

With reports from Reuters, W Radio and Reforma

World.title: Inside the Mexico City auction of Canadian trafficker Ryan Wedding’s US $40 million motorcycle collection
World.content:
A collection of luxury motorcycles formerly owned by Canadian drug lord Ryan Wedding is expected to put close to 60 million pesos (US $3.2 million) into Mexico’s Treasury by end-of-day Thursday.

The government raked in more than half of that total during the first day of a two-day auction at which 62 high-end and competitive motorcycles — valued at approximately US $40 million — were up for sale by the Institute to Return Stolen Goods to the Public (Indep).

About 100 collectors and specialty companies were on hand to participate on Wednesday when 30 bikes were on the block, with one U.S. company sweeping up nine motorcycles for 17 million pesos (US $913,000)

Wednesday’s collection from the sale of the first 30 lots exceeded 30 million pesos (US $1.6 million), according to Indep.

More than 600 lots of movable goods were up for sale during this week’s proceedings, although the motorcycles were the headline attraction.

Wedding’s motorcycles were seized last December after authorities raided four properties in Mexico City and México state linked to the former Olympic athlete known as The King of Cocaine.

Among the first items made available to bidders was a Ducati Desmosedici GP15 motorcycle, a prototype with which the Italian manufacturer competed in the premier class of the MotoGP World Championship in 2015. The opening bid was US $112,000.

The collection includes Ducati models used by renowned racers such as Valentino Rossi, Jorge Lorenzo and Marc Márquez. Some pieces are racing prototypes and historic examples from MotoGP and Superbike.

There are also classic Kawasaki, MV Agusta and Yamaha models manufactured in the 1950s.

Bids reached record highs compared to starting prices, and the most sought-after item was a 2006 Ducati Desmosedici GP7, which started at 2.5 million pesos (US $134,000) and reached 4.5 million pesos (US $242,000).

Wedding, who was arrested in Mexico in January, is in a U.S. federal prison in Los Angeles awaiting trial on charges of murder and leading a transnational cocaine trafficking network linked to the Sinaloa Cartel.

The resources obtained from the sale of the seized assets will be allocated to the Office of the Presidency, and will be used to finance social justice projects, including actions benefiting the widows of the 2006 Pasta de Conchos mine disaster and communities of the Indigenous Raramuri and Amuzgo peoples.

The auction also included aircraft, boats, jewelry, electric vehicles, personal cars and armored vehicles.

With reports from El País, Aristegui Noticias and Radio Fórmula

World.title: Energy equipment manufacturer WEG will build a $250 million plant in Hidalgo, creating over 2,000 jobs
World.content:
The Brazilian company WEG is set to invest US $250 million in Mexico to build a new industrial plant in the state of Hidalgo, where it will manufacture electrical equipment to strengthen energy infrastructure and data centers.

WEG, whose Mexico headquarters are in Huehuetoca, México state, will also work to develop technologies related to artificial intelligence at the new plant.

The announcement was made by Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard during President Claudia Sheinbaum’s Thursday morning news conference.

The project, the latest component of Sheinbaum’s national economic and sustainable development strategy known as Plan México, is slated for development between 2027-2030 and is expected to create 2,000 direct and 4,000 indirect jobs.

Ebrard emphasized WEG’s importance in Mexico’s industrial sector, noting that it is one of the world’s leading companies in the manufacture of generators, alternators and transformers, all essential equipment for expanding production capacity.

Calling it “a sign of confidence and certainty for the country,” Ebrard said that “everything that involves economic growth depends on the type of equipment” WEG manufactures.

Sheinbaum described the investment as historic, especially as it means critical equipment will now be produced in Mexico, instead of being imported.

“The investment being made in transmission and distribution, substations and transformers … is between two and three times the investment made in previous administrations,” Sheinbaum said.

Also in attendance, WEG Global Vice President Daniel Godinho said the investment highlighted a “new stage of growth” for WEG in Mexico, explaining that the expansion of digitalization requires electrical networks capable of supplying power to servers, cooling systems and processing equipment

“Technology needs energy and energy needs industry,” he said, adding that behind every data center there is an integrated infrastructure consisting of generators, transformers, electric motors, distribution systems and automation solutions.

Godinho also thanked the government of Hidalgo for making this process possible for WEG, which has been in Mexico for more than 25 years and invested more than US $400 million during the past four years.

WEG employs 6,000 people in Mexico and its national infrastructure includes four industrial parks and 15 industrial buildings, as well as a commercial network featuring 500 distributors.

With reports from El Universal, El Economista and Excelsior

World.title: MND LOCAL BCS: Baja 1000 revs up for action in Los Cabos as an epic year for cruise ship visits nears the finish line
World.content:
The first-ever SCORE Baja 1000 to start and finish in Los Cabos — and to be run entirely within the state of Baja California Sur — is only days away. So excitement is building.

But anxiety is also growing among some business owners in San José del Cabo, who worry about what traffic could mean for their bottom line during times when vehicles aren’t off-road but on city streets.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Luke McMillin (@lukemcmillin83)

Traffic worries and the build-up to the 2026 Baja 1000

The race is scheduled to begin and end on Avenida Centenario in San José del Cabo on Nov. 13-14; the thoroughfare that borders the city’s historic downtown district and is a key access point for downtown commerce.

Business owners in this district have already gotten a sneak peek at what the race might mean for local traffic … and they didn’t like what they saw. When Avenida Centenario was closed for street cleaning in the days leading up to the race, two hours of gridlock ensued, affecting traffic downtown and on the Transpeninsular Highway, and leading to predictable dips in sales for local shopkeepers.

“The entire Centro Histórico area is, in a sense, held hostage (by the race), which directly impacts the local economy,” local business owner and civic activist Blanca Pedrín Torres told El Sudcaliforniano. “While it’s true that the Baja 1000 generates significant economic activity — perhaps benefiting the hotel industry — the Historic Center is not made up solely of hotels.”

Of course, as Pedrín notes, the race does generate substantial economic benefits — an estimated US $35 million statewide — and San José del Cabo is the primary beneficiary; even if not all business owners benefit equally.

In Cabo San Lucas, for instance, which is not on the race map at all, a special “block party” exhibition of 10 race cars, trucks and buggies was scheduled for Tuesday, Nov. 10, presumably so that downtown business owners there could see at least some economic boost. It worked, as an estimated 10,000 people attended.

A record-setting year for cruise ship visits continues

Cabo San Lucas, despite its relatively low profile for the Baja 1000, remains the primary economic engine for the region’s tourism economy, and in a down year for tourism (international air arrivals are down 8.4% through September, total air traffic by 5.6%), the Land’s End city has provided the lone bright spot with its thriving cruise port.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Princess Cruises (@princesscruises)

Last year, Cabo San Lucas welcomed over 1 million cruise ship passengers for the first time in its history (1,057,758 passengers from 285 cruise ships, to be exact), establishing itself as the second-most popular cruise port on Mexico’s Pacific Coast (behind only Ensenada, which welcomed over 1.3 million, and just ahead of Puerto Vallarta, which narrowly topped the million mark).

To say that Cabo San Lucas is going to smash that record this year is a bit of an understatement. Through August, it had received 956,964 cruisers aboard 244 ships, and was pacing towards upwards of 1.4 million passengers for the year.

It’s a remarkable rise. Cruise passenger numbers increased by 46.7% from 2024 to 2025, and this year, at least so far, they’ve climbed by another 50.7%, with the results of two traditionally robust months (November and December) yet to be tallied.

World Wide Technology Championship winner puts golf world on notice

In my recent preview of Los Cabos’ PGA Tour event, the World Wide Technology Championship, I noted that this year’s field featured an electrifying young player. I should have said three of them.

While press attention has understandably been lavished on Jackson Koivun, the 21-year-old who set an NCAA record for scoring average while winning two national championships at Auburn and won his first PGA event just 24 days after turning pro in June, he’s not the only young player who’s putting the tour on notice.

Ben James, who also turned pro in June and is only 23, cruised out to a four-shot lead after three rounds on the Tiger Woods-designed El Cardonal course at Diamante, just north of Cabo San Lucas. However, the leaderboard tightened up considerably on the final day, with several players making charges, including 19-year-old phenom Blades Brown and Álvaro Ortiz, the Guadalajara-born player who emerged as the crowd favorite.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by PGA Tour (@pgatour)

Brown becomes youngest winner on tour since 1931

Brown, vying to become the youngest PGA Tour winner in 95 years, fired a final-round 63. But James eagled the dramatic par-5 18th to force a playoff for the winner’s share of US $1,080,000 and a two-year tour exemption.

Youth was going to be served regardless of the outcome, but in the end it was Brown who won the battle of future stars, becoming the youngest PGA Tour event winner since 18-year-old Charles “Chuck” Kocsis in 1931 with a birdie on the second playoff hole.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Sheinbaum to address APEC business leaders in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🎤 Sheinbaum to address business leaders at APEC in China: Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard said the president will be in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 19, making an appearance as the main speaker at an APEC Business Advisory Council event. She and Chinese President Xi Jinping will be the only world leaders to address the event’s plenary session, according to Ebrard. She will also hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam, Ebrard said.

Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard said the president will be in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 19, making an appearance as the main speaker at an APEC Business Advisory Council event. She and Chinese President Xi Jinping will be the only world leaders to address the event’s plenary session, according to Ebrard. She will also hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam, Ebrard said. 🚫 No Trump meeting in China: Sheinbaum said she won’t hold a bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump during the trip, but will “probably” meet him at the G20 Leaders’ Summit at Mar-a-Lago in Florida in December. “We will seek [a bilateral meeting] if the opportunity arises,” she said.

Sheinbaum said she won’t hold a bilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump during the trip, but will “probably” meet him at the G20 Leaders’ Summit at Mar-a-Lago in Florida in December. “We will seek [a bilateral meeting] if the opportunity arises,” she said. 📈 Plan México pitch to investors: Sheinbaum said she will tell APEC businesspeople about Plan México and how they can invest in Mexico.

Sheinbaum said she will tell APEC businesspeople about Plan México and how they can invest in Mexico. 🤝 Xi meeting “shouldn’t be a problem” for U.S. trade talks: Sheinbaum said her meeting with Xi should not affect negotiations with the United States, and that communication on trade between the two countries is constant. The bilateral trade talks follow the Trump administration’s July decision not to renew the USMCA for an additional 16 years.

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Sheinbaum’s agenda in China next week was a key focus of today’s mañanera.

Sheinbaum will attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting in the southeastern Chinese city of Shenzhen next Wednesday and Thursday.

She announced last week that she will also attend a bilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

On Thursday morning, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard provided an overview of Sheinbaum’s agenda in China.

He and other cabinet ministers, including Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Velasco, will accompany the president on her trip to China, her first to Asia since she was sworn in on Oct. 1, 2024.

The focus on Sheinbaum’s upcoming trip at today’s mañanera served as a reminder that Mexico has taken a more prominent place on the international stage under her leadership than it occupied during Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s presidency. AMLO only took seven international trips during his six-year term, a number matched by Sheinbaum before she reached the two-year milestone of her presidency.

In addition to attending the APEC meeting in China next week, Sheinbaum will also travel to Florida next month to attend the G20 Leaders’ Summit. At today’s mañanera, she said that her first formal face-to-face meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump could take place at the latter event.

Ebrard outlines Sheinbaum’s agenda in China

Ebrard told reporters that Sheinbaum will have official activities scheduled in Shenzhen from Nov. 17 to 19.

He noted that Shenzhen is considered the technology capital of China.

“That’s why they proposed holding [the APEC meeting] there,” Ebrard said.

He announced that Sheinbaum will be the main speaker at an APEC Business Advisory Council event to be held in Shenzhen next week. Ebrard said that the council is made up of “more than 1,000 businesspeople from the 21 [APEC] countries.”

“We think that this is the most important [business] forum for … the Asia-Pacific [region] and our president is going to play a very important role,” he said.

“She will be one of the few heads of state that will address the group in the plenary session,” Ebrard said.

In fact, just Sheinbaum and Xi will address the session attended by all members of the APEC Business Advisory Council, he said.

Ebrard also announced that Sheinbaum will hold bilateral meetings with the leaders of various APEC countries, including those of China, Canada, Australia and Vietnam. He said that other APEC countries have requested bilateral meetings with Mexico, and that it is “very likely” they will take place. Ebrard said that leaders of APEC countries have significant interest in “talking to the president and Mexico.”

He said that Sheinbaum will also participate in the APEC Leaders’ Meeting. Ebrard noted that the theme of this year’s meeting is “Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together.”

He subsequently told reporters that 52% of foreign direct investment in Mexico comes from APEC countries. Ebrard also noted that Mexico will host the APEC Leaders’ Meeting in 2028.

No meeting with Trump in China

Later in the press conference, Sheinbaum told reporters that she won’t hold a bilateral meeting with Trump during her visit to China next week.

She said she would “probably” meet with the U.S. president during the G20 Leaders’ Summit at the Mar-A-Lago Club in Florida in December.

“We will seek … [a bilateral meeting] if the opportunity arises,” Sheinbaum said.

She emphasized that there is constant communication between Mexico and the United States on trade issues.

Sheinbaum said last week that she was interested in meeting with Trump in China.

Sheinbaum says she will speak about Plan México at business event

Sheinbaum told reporters that she will speak about Plan México — the federal government’s ambitious economic plan — at the APEC Business Advisory Council event.

“We’re going to talk about Plan México, about what we’ve done, about what our country’s economic model means,” she said.

Sheinbaum said she will also speak to businesspeople about how they can invest in Mexico.

Among the goals of Plan México are to attract more foreign investment to Mexico and to increase the use of national content in products made in Mexico’s large manufacturing sector.

“The objective of Plan Mexico is to produce more in Mexico and import less,” Sheinbaum told reporters.

Sheinbaum says her meeting with Xi won’t affect trade negotiations with US

Sheinbaum told reporters that there is no reason why her meeting with Xi should affect Mexico’s trade negotiations with the United States.

“That we’re going to have a meeting with the president of China shouldn’t be a problem in the trade agreement negotiations with the United States,” she said.

Mexico and the United States have been seeking to resolve a range of trade differences after the Trump administration announced in July that it had decided against renewing the USMCA free trade pact for an additional 16 years to 2042.

The United States’ concerns include its large trade deficit with Mexico, Mexico’s trade relationship with China and Mexico’s energy sector rules. Mexico is seeking a reduction, if not the elimination, of U.S. tariffs on Mexican steel, aluminum and vehicles.

World.title: US Jobless Claims Reach 200,000 in November
World.content:
Rio Times Markets · United States

Key Facts The figure New US jobless claims were 200,000 in the week ended 7 November 2026, seasonally adjusted.

Versus forecast Analysts expected 195,000, and the prior week was 191,000, so claims rose by 9,000.

The trend The four-week average held at 195,250, the same as the week before.

Why it matters Weekly claims are an early gauge of layoffs in the world’s largest economy.

What ends it A reading below 195,000 next week would show the rise was a blip.

New US claims for jobless benefits rose to 200,000 in the week ended 7 November 2026, above forecasts, though the four-week average did not move.

What Changed

New US claims for unemployment insurance, the weekly count of people applying for jobless benefits, were 200,000 in the week ended 7 November 2026. That was 9,000 more than the 191,000 of the previous week and 5,000 above the 195,000 consensus (average analyst forecast) on the RT economic calendar, our feed of official release dates and forecasts.

The figure is seasonally adjusted, which removes regular calendar patterns such as holiday hiring. The US Department of Labor, the federal employment agency, publishes it weekly, normally on Thursdays.

Where It Sits in the Trend

The Department of Labor series, as carried by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis’s FRED database, shows weekly claims of 198,000, 200,000, 195,000, 195,000 and 191,000 for the five weeks before this one. The new reading matches the 200,000 of the week ended 10 October and is higher than the other four weeks in that span.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on North America Email address Follow

The four-week average, which smooths out weekly noise, stayed at 195,250. That means one higher week has not yet changed the underlying picture.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico” Get the brief

Why It Moved

The release does not state a cause, so the reason for the rise is not confirmed. Weekly claims are noisy and can change by several thousand from one week to the next.

A single week above forecast is therefore a prompt to watch the next release, not a signal of a turning point.

What It Means for Readers Abroad

At this level, there is no sign of a wave of layoffs in the data released. For Latin America and Africa, US employment matters because it feeds into American consumer spending and the dollar.

A sustained climb well above 200,000 would be an early warning of slower US growth, which investors in emerging markets watch closely. This reading alone does not show that.

What Would End the Rise

A second week at or above 200,000 would suggest layoffs are edging up. A reading back near the 191,000 of the prior week would suggest the latest figure was a blip.

The next weekly report, normally due on Thursday, 19 November 2026, covers the week ended 14 November. A four-week average moving above 200,000 would be a clearer sign of change than any single week.

What Is Not Known Yet

It is not known which states or industries accounted for the rise, because the figures released here do not show that detail. The data also does not show whether people who lost jobs have found new ones.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Americans filed new jobless claims in early November 2026?

There were 200,000 in the week ended 7 November, seasonally adjusted. That was 9,000 more than the previous week and 5,000 above the forecast.

What is the four-week average?

It averages the last four weekly readings to smooth out noise. It stayed at 195,250 in this release.

Why do jobless claims matter outside the United States?

They are an early read on US layoffs. Investors in Latin America and Africa watch them because US growth and the dollar affect emerging markets.

What would show whether layoffs are rising?

A second week at or above 200,000, or a four-week average above 200,000, would suggest so. A fall below 195,000 would point to a blip.

World.title: Argentina October Inflation Rises to 2.2%
World.content:
Rio Times Markets · Argentina

Key Facts The figure Argentina’s consumer prices rose 2.2% in October 2026 from September, and 33.1% from a year earlier.

Versus forecast Analysts expected 1.9% on the month and 32.7% on the year, so both readings came in higher.

The trend Monthly inflation sped up from 1.9% in September, while the yearly rate eased from 33.4%.

Why the two differ October 2025 saw a 2.3% monthly rise, so the 2.2% of October 2026 pulled the yearly rate down slightly.

What ends it A November monthly reading below 1.9% would show October was a one-month jump.

Argentina’s monthly inflation sped up to 2.2% in October 2026, above forecasts, even as the yearly rate slipped to 33.1%.

That is faster than the 1.9% recorded in September and 0.3 percentage points above the 1.9% consensus (average analyst forecast) on the RT economic calendar, our feed of official release dates and forecasts.

Where It Sits in the Trend

Monthly inflation moved the wrong way in October: from 1.9% to 2.2%, a rise of 0.3 points in one month. The RT calendar holds only the September reading for comparison.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on INDEC (Argentina) Email address Follow

The yearly rate moved the other way, from 33.4% to 33.1%. Both can be true at once, because the yearly figure drops the oldest month in its window and adds the newest.

Why the Two Numbers Differ

INDEC reported a 2.3% monthly rise for October 2025. When that month left the 12-month window and October 2026 at 2.2% entered, the yearly rate eased slightly, even though prices accelerated from September.

INDEC’s breakdown, as quoted in Argentine press, shows housing, water, electricity and gas rose 4.2%, the largest of any division. Core inflation, which strips out volatile items, was 1.5%, so the pickup came from items outside the core.

What It Means for Readers Abroad

A monthly rate of 2.2% would add up to roughly 30% over a full year if it were repeated every month, so the pace is still fast. For visitors, importers and investors, it means local prices keep rising fast.

The miss against forecast shows analysts had expected a calmer month. One reading is not a trend, but it makes the path of falling inflation harder to read in the short term.

What Would Confirm or End the Pickup

A November monthly reading at or above 2.2% would confirm that price pressure is building again. A reading back below the 1.9% of September would suggest October was a one-off.

The next yearly reading will drop November 2025 from the window, so it depends on both November 2026 prices and that earlier base.

What Is Not Known Yet

It is not known whether utility increases will keep pushing prices up in November. It is also unclear whether the pace will last beyond one month.

How much did prices rise in Argentina in October 2026?

Consumer prices rose 2.2% from September and 33.1% from October 2025. Analysts had expected 1.9% and 32.7%.

Why did the yearly rate fall if monthly inflation rose?

The yearly rate drops the oldest month and adds the newest. October 2025 had risen 2.3%, slightly more than the 2.2% of October 2026, so the yearly rate eased.

Who publishes Argentina’s inflation figure?

INDEC, the national statistics institute, publishes it monthly. The RT economic calendar tracks the release date and analyst forecasts.

What would show whether inflation is picking up again?

A November reading at or above 2.2% would suggest so. A figure below 1.9% would point to a one-off.

Latin America feels like a continent holding its breath over money: governments are paying to keep prices calm, and households are not yet convinced.

São Paulo, Brazil’s financial centre. File photo.

The Continent’s Mood Today

On 12 November, the region’s front pages were about the cost of calm. Brazil’s Senate passed a savings package, Chile cut diesel prices, and Argentina learned that inflation is stubborn.

Underneath sits an old memory of prices running away. Governments from Santiago to Mexico City are spending political capital to avoid a repeat.

Brazil – Relief, With the Bill Still to Come

The Senate approved the base text of the fiscal adjustment bill of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by 45 votes to 31. The government says the package will improve the 2027 budget balance, and four amendment votes are set for Tuesday 17 November before it moves to the lower house.

The bill is known as PLP 299/2026. It still needs the lower house, where the government will need another majority.

Mexico – Two Warnings in One Week

On Thursday 12 November, President Donald Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans marching north. More than 1,000 mostly Central American migrants left Tapachula, in southern Mexico, on 10 November.

The threat comes days after Mexican forces arrested ‘R2’, an alleged cell leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), in Zapopan on 8 November. For ordinary Mexicans, both stories touch daily life: trade, jobs and safety.

Chile – Paying for Peace on the Roads

The government agreed on Thursday 12 November to cut diesel by 142 pesos a litre (about US$0.14) and to freeze diesel prices against increases until March 2027, aiming to end a truckers’ strike. A motorists’ group, No + TAG, says its own protest against highway tolls will continue.

Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz puts the cost at about US$500 million over 2026 and 2027. Chileans remember the 2019 unrest and the trucker blockades, so many see this as a price worth paying.

Argentina – The Last Mile Is the Hardest

INDEC, Argentina’s national statistics office, reported October inflation of 2.2%, above the roughly 1.8% that economists expected. The monthly rate has stopped falling, and the weariness is easy to hear.

Argentines have been told for two years that the worst is over. A stalled monthly rate feels like a promise slowly breaking.

Colombia – Profits Up, Rubble Still Down

Davivienda, one of Colombia’s largest banks, reported a 38% rise in profit. Miner Mineros also hit a record profit.

Not every company shared the cheer, though, as cement maker Argos saw profit fall 29%.

Peru – A Budget Vote and a Cooling Mood

Congress set the 2027 budget vote for 20 November. Prosecutors are asking for double their budget, which shows how much institutions are fighting for money.

A poll found 53% disapprove of Fujimori. The pattern is familiar in Lima, where political approval has often collapsed within months.

The Shared Mood

From Brasília to Santiago, the feeling is the same: governments are buying calm and families are checking the price. Nobody wants to be the first to relax.

Hope exists, in rising bank profits and the Buen Fin sales weekend that starts today in Mexico. Patience is the scarce resource, and it is being spent faster than the budgets.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the mood in Latin America today?

Cautious and cost-conscious. Brazil’s Senate backed a fiscal package, Chile cut diesel prices to end a strike, and Argentina’s inflation stalled at 2.2%.

What did Brazil’s Senate approve?

It approved the base text of Lula’s fiscal adjustment by 45 votes to 31. Amendment votes are set for Tuesday 17 November, then it goes to the lower house.

What did Chile agree with truckers?

Diesel falls 142 pesos a litre (about US$0.14) under a deal announced on 12 November, and prices are frozen against increases until March 2027. The government expects Congress to vote on Tuesday 17 November.

01 The bond market flinches, and shares follow

Wall Street is giving back a little after Wednesday’s rally. The S&P 500 sits at 7,592 (-0.35%), the Dow at 52,297 (-0.36%) and the Nasdaq at 25,366 (-0.39%).

The falls are small, but the mood is nervous. The VIX, Wall Street’s fear gauge, is at 18.7 (+6.92%) as investors pay more for protection after a week of violent swings.

The cause is the bond market. The US 10-year Treasury yield is 5.134% (+2.68%), and a yield that high makes future company profits worth less today.

Gold has lost its shine as a result. The spot price is $3,881/oz (-2.46%), another hard fall this week, because the metal pays no interest while Treasuries now pay over 5%.

The dollar adds to the pressure. The dollar index is at 103.146 (+0.23%), which makes gold and other dollar-priced assets dearer for buyers elsewhere.

02 A hot jobs market and a hawkish Fed

The labour market is why the Fed cannot relax. October payrolls rose 165,000 against a forecast of 65,000, and unemployment fell to 4.1%.

Traders have since begun to bet on a Fed rate rise rather than a cut. That sharp turn explains why the 10-year yield has pushed above 5%.

Weekly jobless claims rose to 200,000 in the week to 7 November against 195,000 expected, and continuing claims fell to 1.697 million in the week to 31 October, according to the US Labor Department’s series. Producer prices are the next test.

The US PPI arrives at 13:30 Lisbon (08:30 New York), with forecasts of 0.4% on the month after 1.3% last time, and 6.6% on the year after 6.3%. Core PPI, which strips out food, energy and trade, is forecast at 0.3% after 0.7%.

A figure above forecast would harden the case for a rate rise. Fed officials then take the stage.

Collins speaks at 14:10 Lisbon and Bowman at 15:50, with Jefferson just after midnight.

03 Brazil feels the squeeze from Washington

Brazil received a friendlier inflation print than the US did. Official October IPCA, reported by the statistics agency IBGE on Thursday, rose 0.14% on the month, after 0.82% in September.

The annual rate is what counts for policy. It edged up to 4.63% from 4.58% in September, still above the 4.5% upper limit of the central bank’s tolerance band.

Brazil’s central bank held the Selic at 13.75% on 4 November, ending five straight cuts, according to its own statement. With the US 10-year above 5% and the dollar index at 103.146, a pause is the comfortable option.

The real is the shock absorber. When US yields rise, investors demand more to hold Brazilian assets, and the currency usually weakens, which feeds back into import prices.

Brazil’s own data follow today. Retail sales are due at 12:00 Lisbon (09:00 Brasília) and business confidence at 14:00, forecast at 46.5 against 46.2.

Colombia reports retail sales and industrial production at 15:00 Lisbon (10:00 Bogotá). Forecasts are 8.7% and -0.8%, against 7.3% and -3.7% before.

Oil is a second pressure point for Latin America’s exporters. The US Energy Information Administration (eia.gov/petroleum/supply/weekly) reports commercial crude stocks at 414.4 million barrels for the week to 6 November, up 4.7 million.

Gasoline stocks rose 1.8 million barrels to 210.8 million, and distillates rose 4.1 million to 103.3 million. Builds like these weigh on crude.

In Europe, the UK economy grew 0.7% in the third quarter, matching forecasts and beating the 0.5% before. The goods trade gap widened sharply to £22.29 billion (about US$29.5 billion) from £19.61 billion (about US$25.9 billion), which tempers the good news.

The three-month average growth rate was 0.7%, up from 0.6%. Japan sold five-year bonds at 2.186%, below the 2.379% of the previous auction.

In China, total social financing is forecast at 1,420 against 3,550 before, a drop that would signal weak credit demand.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why are US Treasury yields above 5%?

Strong October payrolls of 165,000, against a forecast of 65,000, pushed traders to bet on a Fed rate rise. The 10-year yield is now 5.134%.

Why is gold falling?

Gold pays no interest, so higher Treasury yields and a firmer dollar make it less attractive. Spot gold is $3,881/oz, down 2.46%.

What does the US producer price index show?

It measures the prices firms receive for goods and services, and often leads consumer inflation. Today’s forecast is 0.4% on the month and 6.6% on the year.

How does this affect Brazil?

Higher US yields and a stronger dollar pressure the real and limit how far the Selic can fall. October inflation of 4.63% over 12 months is still above the central bank’s 4.5% tolerance limit, and the Fed still sets the backdrop.

Where did the oil figures come from?

They come from the US Energy Information Administration’s weekly report at eia.gov. Commercial crude stocks rose 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million.
