World.title: Toll rebels being barred
World.content:
The Caymanas toll plaza where motorists enter and exit the Edward Seaga Highway. (Photo: Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited)

Unruly motorists have pushed the operators of the Edward Seaga Highway (or T3 leg of Highway 2000) to develop a blacklist system that flags vehicles linked to toll road violations and restrict them from accessing the motorway.

According to the Jamaica North South Highway Company Limited (JNSHCL), developer and operator of the 66.13-kilometre road which has six toll plazas and one local head office operating on a 24/7 basis, the violations include tailgating through the barrier, forcing the barrier, and stealing or swapping toll cards to avoid payment. Verbal abuse or violent threats against staff will also result in blacklisting. Blacklisted vehicles are prohibited from entering the highway and once identified will be turned away.

According to the operators, those responsible will bear full legal responsibility under applicable law for any resulting harm, disruption or consequences to the highway and the travelling public.

Trudy-Ann Williams, deputy commercial and compliance manager for the JNSHCL, told the

Jamaica Observer that a pilot of the feature was conducted last month and full roll-out is slated for the end of this month.

“We had security on the ground, personnel from the Jamaica Constabulary who were willing to assist us once we were able to identify these motorists, to escort them from the toll lane

— if it is that they became boisterous

— or just simply to provide further information to them about the reason they were placed on the blacklist,” Williams told the Observer.

She said the operators have developed a working list based on past violations committed by operators of private and public passenger vehicles.

“The numbers fluctuate. Right now I think we have over 50 licence plates; it’s not an extensive list and the list is updated as time goes by, as we do more research, so the list will change if a motorist comes forward and clears themselves; they will be removed and the list updated,” she told the Observer.

Williams said an individual who, for example, was blacklisted because they did not pay the toll can clear themselves by coming forward to pay the relevant sum.

Explaining how the debarring feature works, Williams said, “Once a motorist who is on the blacklist approaches the toll lane, their licence plate will be detected by our new QR code system and an alert will go off, meaning an alarm, and they will be barred and not allowed to enter the highway. Once they are discovered we will alert the motorist that they are on the blacklist and that they should remove themselves from the toll lane,” Williams said.

“There is a flashing light, there is an alarm and the barrier will not open,” she said, adding that motorists who wish to be clear about their status can contact JNSHCL through its general office or customer service lines (1-876-803-5075 or 1-888-429-5674), respectively.

“We also will make a list available through our website where they can search to confirm whether or not they are on the blacklist. However, their full details will not be available on the website because we do not want to disclose sensitive details to just about anyone who has access, so they will still have to call to clarify the reason they are blacklisted,” Williams outlined.

She also emphasised that individuals who are involved in altercations with toll booth staff are only blacklisted after thorough investigations.

“There are different reasons why motorists might become blacklisted; it might not only be for toll evasion, even through toll evasion is the number one reason. If we have persons who have violated or abused the toll in any way, including being overly rude or violent toward our staff, they can also be placed on the blacklist. There are not a lot of those persons; however, we would just like persons to bear in mind that we are non-tolerant of our staff members being abused in any way,” she pointed out.

“If it is that someone thinks it was unfair of us to have blacklisted them for that reason, we would have ensured that we did our due diligence before adding them to that list, which includes gathering relevant evidence… for any of those violations. We have evidence, and that is how we determine if the vehicle will be blacklisted. We are not taking it lightly or trying to just build a list on a whim; it is all evidence-based,” Williams said.

In the meantime, she said in addition to the blacklist feature, the JNSHCL is introducing a new way to access the toll road via the QR code or cardless system, effectively phasing out the use of toll cards.

“Persons will be able to access the toll road without taking a toll card and, instead, will use their cellphone to scan a QR code. The cellphone, if it has data or even if it doesn’t have data, we will provide free Wi-Fi at our toll plazas; they can connect or use their data, scan the QR code app or feature on their phone, and that will generate a journey code. Once that information is captured, then they are allowed access to the motorway and then when they get to the exit the information, in most cases, will automatically populate. If it is, that it is not automatically populated, then they can show the QR code on their phone or scan another at the exit. The payment is normal, you can pay via cash or debit card,” Williams explained.

“For persons who are not so familiar or tech-savvy, we are trying to ensure that we do some more public education campaigns. We will have persons at the entrance who can show them how to access the feature and to give further instructions. We will ensure that this happens for a period of at least 10 days once the feature has been launched,” she assured.

Toll evasion in Jamaica is a criminal offence under the Toll Roads Act, resulting in fines up to $10,000 or 30 days’ imprisonment per count for non-payment. Authorities, including TransJamaican Highway

— concessionaires for the tolled motorway running between Portmore and Kingston, and Kingston and Manchester

— use surveillance and police enforcement to target offenders, especially those tailgating or using stolen tags, which can lead to higher penalties.

World.title: Bell in hot water
World.content:
BELL... the Integrity Commission found that he attended deliberations on his wife’s application to the municipal corporation without withdrawing or recusing himself from the Commercial Services Committee

Councillor Ian Bell (People’s National Party, Beecher Town Division) is facing a two-month expulsion from the St Ann Municipal Corporation, removal from two key committees, and a formal reprimand following an Integrity Commission investigation which found that he failed to withdraw from discussions concerning his wife’s application for space at the Ocho Rios Transportation Centre.

St Ann’s Bay Mayor Michael Belnavis announced the proposed disciplinary measures during Thursday’s monthly council meeting, saying a notice of motion for Bell’s expulsion would be brought before the council later that day.

Belnavis said the corporation would also seek Bell’s immediate removal from the Commercial Services Committee, which considers applications and matters relating to the corporation’s commercial activities, and the Planning Committee.

According to the mayor, the proposed two-month expulsion is being pursued under section 44(1) of the Local Governance Act, 2016, on the grounds that Bell brought the corporation into disrepute.

The measures follow an investigation into the circumstances surrounding an application made by Bell’s wife, businesswoman Shirlyn Campbell-Bell, to rent a section of the transportation centre to operate a gaming lounge.

The Integrity Commission found that Bell, who was a member of the Commercial Services Committee, attended deliberations on his wife’s application without withdrawing or recusing himself. The commission said this breached the conflict-of-interest standards expected of elected officials under the Ministry of Local Government and Community Development’s Councillor’s Handbook.

The Integrity Commission recommended that Bell be formally reprimanded for failing to withdraw from the committee’s consideration of the application, despite his personal interest in the matter and his knowledge of the proper procedure.

“The purpose is to protect the integrity of the committee and ensure that its membership can carry out its responsibilities without any unresolved concern regarding this matter. In addition, mandatory refresher training will be required for all members of council. That training must strengthen members’ understanding of the conflicts of interest, disclosure, recusal, ethnic decision-making, statutory obligations and good governance,” Belnavis announced on Thursday.

“We must ensure that members understand not only the procedures but their personal responsibility to uphold them. We cannot allow uncertainty, silence or conflicting interpretations of procedures to compromise the work of this corporation,” he added.

He also noted that the corporation will introduce stricter procedures requiring councillors to formally declare conflicts of interest, with every departure from and return to committee meetings duly recorded in the minutes.

“Conflicts must be declared in writing. Every withdrawal and return must be recorded in the minutes. The clerk to the committee must provide guidance whenever conflict arises and the presiding chair must confirm that the matter can properly proceed before discussion or decision-making begins,” he said.

The Integrity Commission report traced the matter to March 31, 2023, when Campbell-Bell applied to rent space at the transportation centre to place a 40-foot container for a gaming lounge.

The investigation found that the application was delivered to the corporation by Bell rather than being submitted through its Registry Department, as required under the established procedure. It also found that Campbell-Bell’s married name was omitted from the application.

Although the corporation sent her correspondence in May 2023 indicating that the request had been approved, the commission found that the required approval process had not been completed.

The report also found that the structure was built without the necessary building and planning permits, in breach of the Building Act, 2018. It said there was no evidence of a lease agreement between Campbell-Bell and the corporation, or that the application had been referred to the Ministry of Local Government for the minister’s approval.

The commission further found that the gaming lounge had operated since 2023 without paying user fees to the corporation, and that the corporation had made no attempt to collect those fees.

The investigation also examined whether Bell had declared his relationship with the applicant. While six councillors told investigators that he had disclosed that Campbell-Bell was his wife, they could not identify the specific meeting at which this was done. The commission said it was therefore unable to definitively conclude that he had made the declaration.

However, it found that Bell remained present when the application was considered and that the evidence suggested he did not recuse himself from the meeting.

Belnavis said the corporation would now examine the status of the building and take the necessary steps through the relevant legal and technical processes.

“The Integrity Commission’s report indicates that the required building plans were not submitted to the relevant agencies before construction commenced. The existence of the structure does not, in itself, constitute lawful approval,” he said.

The mayor said the corporation would also consider the requirements of section 49 of the Local Government Act, which deals with the sale or lease of land vested in a municipal corporation and requires ministerial approval.

The Integrity Commission recommended that the corporation assess and recover all outstanding fees relating to the business and enforce the relevant laws and policies concerning Campbell-Bell’s occupation of the property.

It also recommended that the corporation strengthen its conflict of interest procedures and consider disciplinary action against Bell, including a formal reprimand.

Belnavis said the measures were intended to ensure that the commission’s findings led to changes in how the corporation manages its commercial properties and conducts its affairs.

World.title: Complex Ricki’s Loving You embraces healing
World.content:
Complex Ricki.

Recording artiste Complex Ricki is encouraging listeners to embrace healing and second chances in love with her latest single, Loving You, released on November 6 through VPAL Music, the distribution arm of VP Records.

The track explores the emotional journey of moving beyond past disappointments, rediscovering one’s worth and finding the courage to pursue meaningful relationships.

For Complex Ricki, the song represents a celebration of personal growth and the possibilities that come with allowing oneself to love again.

“Loving You is about healing, embracing second chances, and finding happiness again. I want people to know that no matter what they’ve been through, they deserve genuine love,” she shared.

Through reflective lyrics, the entertainer addresses the importance of emotional maturity, commitment, and self-discovery, while highlighting the reassurance that comes with finding a relationship built on mutual understanding.

Rather than allowing previous experiences to dictate her outlook on romance, Complex Ricki uses the single to promote a renewed sense of confidence and optimism.

The song also touches on the importance of recognising one’s value and refusing to settle for relationships that do not contribute positively to personal development.

Beyond its romantic message, Loving You encourages listeners to acknowledge their individual progress and remain receptive to new experiences, even after navigating difficult circumstances.

The release adds to Complex Ricki’s growing musical catalogue as she continues to use relatable themes and personal experiences to connect with audiences.

With Loving You, the singer hopes to resonate with individuals who have experienced heartbreak but remain hopeful about finding genuine affection and happiness.

The single is available on all major digital streaming platforms through VPAL Music.

World.title: Everything Fresh eyes bigger slice of Bahamas
World.content:
GRANT...demand is exciting; we have concluded negotiations with RIU and increased volumes on that side in Jamaica

EVERYTHING Fresh Group Limited is eyeing further expansion in The Bahamas, targeting mom-and-pop shops and smaller retailers as it seeks to build its presence beyond the hotel sector. The food distributor, which entered the market in 2018, currently serves close to 50 customers and is pursuing proposals that could significantly improve the profitability of its Bahamian operation.

In an interview with the Jamaica Observer following the company’s annual general meeting at the AC Hotel on Wednesday, General Manager Nicola Maitland said some of the proposals were awaiting approval.

“If we get the approval, within as early as two years we can be very profitable,” she said.

The company is targeting 10 per cent growth in The Bahamas operation by the end of its 2026 financial year. While pursuing growth overseas, Everything Fresh is also adjusting its Jamaican operation following Hurricane Melissa in 2025, which disrupted hotel operations and affected its traditional business model.

Maitland acknowledged that the company had not returned to its pre-hurricane position, particularly as it continues to address outstanding receivables from hotel customers.

“We’re not where we used to be, but we are working with the hotel privately regarding the receivables; however, we are not held fast on a strategy; we are taking multiple options,” she said.

One of those measures has been to increase the company’s exposure to the retail market locally. Although Everything Fresh previously supplied supermarkets and other retailers, it has since increased its presence in that market as it seeks to diversify its customer base and reduce its dependence on hotel business.

“We always supplied retail; however, we have increased our footprint, and we continue to bring in more SKUs based on the demands,” Maitland said.

The company is also introducing products aimed at consumers seeking more affordable alternatives, as it targets the down trend market. This includes a new margarine line, which was introduced in October. To support the expansion of its customer base, Everything Fresh is investing in its distribution infrastructure, including improvements to its Bog Walk facility in St Catherine. The warehouse serves as a central distribution hub for its hotel business and is being expanded to accommodate additional storage and freezer capacity. The company is also increasing its delivery fleet, with additional trucks expected to come on stream in 2027 and 2028.

“We have a lot more trucks coming in for 2027/2028 so we can deliver more products and reduce our delivery times to our customers,” Group Chief Financial Officer Errol Grant said during the AGM.

The investments are expected to improve the company’s ability to service hotel chains while supporting its growing retail distribution network. Alongside the capital expenditure, the company is investing in brand marketing and staff development, while reviewing its operating costs to improve efficiency.

“We look at every line item, and we see where it must add value to remain in our books,” Grant said.

Despite the disruption caused by Hurricane Melissa, Everything Fresh is anticipating improved business as hotel properties resume operations and demand strengthens ahead of the winter tourism season.

“Demand is exciting; we have concluded negotiations with RIU and increased volumes on that side in Jamaica,” Grant said.

He noted that some hotels that had been operating below capacity following the hurricane were gradually returning to normal operations, providing scope for increased business in the final quarter of 2026 and into 2027.

For its 2025 financial year, Everything Fresh reported revenue of $4.17 billion, an increase of $489.97 million, or 13.3 per cent, compared with the previous year. Jamaica accounted for the largest share of the increase, contributing $428.3 million, or approximately 87.4 per cent, to group revenue growth. Revenue from the Jamaican operation rose 14.8 per cent to $3.33 billion, up from $2.9 billion in 2024. The Bahamian operation contributed the remaining $61.7 million, representing approximately 12.6 per cent of the group’s revenue increase. Revenue from the territory rose eight per cent to $840 million, compared with approximately $770 million in the previous year.

Everything Fresh distributes meat, dairy products and fresh produce to customers across its markets.

World.title: BROADER SCOPE
World.content:
Arnett Gardens goalkeeper Alesha Robinson (left) and Sara Needham of Los Perfectos vie for the ball during the Jamaica Women’s Premier League first-leg semi-final match at UWI Mona Bowl on May 16, 2026. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

Despite the imminent introduction of relegation and promotion in the Jamaica Women’s Premier League (JWPL), Professional Women’s Football Jamaica Limited (PWFJL) Chairperson Christina Hudson believes the move will significantly raise the standard of the competition and strengthen women’s football locally.

The JWPL has operated without a promotion and relegation system since 2008, instead using a league and play-off format. However, the limited number of clubs with active women’s teams has resulted in changes to the competition, with clubs entering or withdrawing depending on their circumstances.

That is expected to change with the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) planning to introduce a National Women’s Tier Two competition next year which would see the return of a second division in women’s football for the first time in nearly two decades, since the former Women’s ‘A’ League.

The Jamaica Observer has learnt that the plan has been in development for several months, with a host of teams expressing interest in joining the competition and ultimately earning promotion to the JWPL. An early 2027 start date has been proposed and would end before the completion of the 2026/2027 JWPL season.

A reliable source told the Observer that Waterhouse FC, three-time JWPL champions who did not return to the competition in 2023 following the COVID-19 pandemic, Montego Bay United and Tru-Juice FC are among six or seven clubs expected to participate in the Tier Two competition. All three clubs also field teams in the men’s Jamaica Premier League.

The Observer has learnt that a club from St Ann, separate from Mount Pleasant Football Academy, is also interested in joining the competition.

When contacted, JFF President Michael Ricketts didn’t confirm the exact details but told the

Observer that the federation is leaning towards a 2027 start date following further consultations with relevant stakeholders.

“It depends on how serious these teams are and even a shortened version would serve the programme well, so definitely we’ll be looking at that and we’ll make an announcement in that regard soon,” he said.

“We will need to look at those teams that would have given an indication that they want to play football and once you meet with them and they are serious, then we could very well have this Tier 2 but we are super excited.”

Hudson believes the planned introduction of the Tier Two reflects the growth of the JWPL, which has been managed by the PWFJL for the past two seasons.

“I think that this is super exciting [and] I think that shows the power of what we have been doing,” she told the Observer.

“So for the very first time this season, the top two winners of the Tier Two will be promoted to the Jamaican Women’s Premier League and the bottom two of the Jamaican Women’s Premier League will be relegated to Tier Two.”

Although relegation could present a challenge for clubs in the revamped JWPL, Hudson believes the introduction of the system will raise the competitiveness and commercial appeal of women’s football.

“I think it can only benefit the quality of the football that we’re seeing. All of the benefits that the Jamaican Women’s Premier League gives or builds out in each season for our clubs is something that is renewed season to season,” she said. “So the clubs get to benefit from being a part of the league for that season and then a new club that comes along will also benefit in their new season, so I don’t think that there’s any downside to the relegation and promotion system.”

“People have been saying that the bottom half of our league is not overly competitive. So now that clubs have this goal that if you’re not making it in the top, you might lose your spot. I think it’s definitely going to push teams at the bottom half of the table to want to improve the quality of the football that they’re playing so that can only help us because obviously the more exciting football and the better quality football that we’re seeing on the pitch, the more people will want to come out and watch the games.”

The JWPL is set to kick off next month with 12 teams including Frazsiers Whip who will be looking to defend their title for a fourth straight year.

World.title: Madden on point to victory
World.content:
The tight and complex course took its toll on competitors such as Cleve Ottey. (Photo: Rory Daley)

Zidan Madden once again claimed the top spot at the fourth round of the Point 2 Point Time Attack dexterity series, which took place at Overton Plaza, Montego Bay, St James, on Sunday, November 1.

Having missed the previous round, and with a pending flight later in the day threatening his participation, Madden completed his two-lap championship run, leaving a time that turned out to be unbeatable through the rest of the event.

His 2:08.56 lap time saw many attempts at being bested, only to fall to errors as the complexity of the course caught out many of the rivals. Each driver contesting the championship run left the crowd on edge, and when Cleve Ottey received a Did Not Finish, victory was assured for the by-then missing Madden.

The win added another 20 points to his championship score, giving him the lead in the series.

Second went to Marc-Dayne Graham, who came the closest with a 2:12.53 lap time.

Completing the podium positions was Maurice Whittingham. Jaden Wright finished fourth, and Kingstonian Daren Givans continued to be a challenge for the more powerful Montegonian drivers as he took his Toyota Corolla to fifth overall.

World.title: Iberostar to hire 400 workers for JOIA Rose Hall reopening
World.content:
JOIA Rose Hall, formerly known as Iberostar Grand Rose Hall, is undergoing a comprehensive renovation involving all 295 suites.

IBEROSTAR Hotels & Resorts is looking to hire approximately 400 workers as it prepares to reopen its renovated adults-only JOIA Rose Hall resort in Montego Bay on December 1, 2026.

The property, formerly known as Iberostar Grand Rose Hall, is undergoing a comprehensive renovation involving all 295 suites, its restaurants, arrival lobby, swimming pools, oceanfront terraces and the introduction of fresh dining concepts.

Thomas van Balveren, general manager of JOIA Rose Hall, told the Jamaica Observer that the transformation represents more than an upgrade to the property’s physical facilities but an opportunity to introduce a new level of all-inclusive luxury to the English-speaking Caribbean.

“We are opening our doors to travellers who seek substance behind luxury, including cultured couples, wellness seekers, and high-end incentive groups who appreciate understated elegance, warm and attentive closeness, and a stay that honours the destination they are visiting,” he said.

According to van Balveren, the company recently held a job fair where several candidates were interviewed across the island to support the resort’s reopening.

“We are hiring around 400 people this year to support JOIA Rose Hall by Iberostar, which represents an incredible opportunity for local talent. We recently held a job fair where we interviewed several candidates from across the island for roles in front desk, guest services, housekeeping, and food and beverage. It is a genuine privilege to welcome so many passionate Jamaican professionals into our team as we prepare to reopen,” he added.

He said the December reopening is particularly important as the resort seeks to capitalise on the start of the winter tourist season, when visitors from key markets, including the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, travel to Jamaica to escape colder temperatures.

“Our timeline is focused on having our physical transformation completed by December 1, 2026, paving the way to welcome our first guests. The momentum on the ground is palpable. We are renewing all 295 suites, reimagining our culinary spaces, and sculpting our oceanfront pools and gardens to craft an experience that is elevated in every detail,” van Balveren said.

He said while work takes place at JOIA, its sister properties, Iberostar Selection Rose Hall Suites and Iberostar Waves Rose Hall Beach continue operating seamlessly, ensuring that its presence in Montego Bay remains vibrant and uninterrupted throughout the transformation.

Meanwhile, van Balveren said the resort’s sustainability efforts will also be guided by Iberostar’s Wave of Change movement, which focuses on environmental protection and creating positive social benefits in the communities where the hotel group operates.

“It is about caring for the people and ecosystems around us, ensuring that our presence directly benefits the local community while protecting the natural beauty that makes this island so special,” he added.

Jareth Vermeulen, destination stewardship representative for Iberostar Hotels & Resorts in Jamaica and Aruba, said the company is also prioritising green spaces as part of the renovation, with an emphasis on incorporating native vegetation into the resort’s landscape.

“We have a GPR, which is a green plot ratio, and that is a three-to-one ratio where every part of cement, our building that we have, we want to have a green space, and that is one for guest experience having luscious gardens, but also only native vegetation is good not only for the guest experience, but also for the sustainability and the nature part of things,” he said.

Vermeulen was speaking to the BusinessWeek recently during the Iberostar Sustainability Learning Exchange in Punta Cana, Dominican Republic.

He said his work in Jamaica will focus on strengthening partnerships across the tourism industry to advance environmental sustainability, particularly in responsible seafood sourcing and waste management.

“My focus is going to be on Blue Foods. So creating an alliance with different hotels to work together creating a roadmap for Blue Foods so responsible fisheries or responsible seafood moving away from reef fish, going more into pelagic, or diversifying what we see as Blue Foods in Jamaica,” he said.

He said Iberostar was seeking to establish an alliance involving other hotel operators, including Sandals, and the Jamaica Hotel and Tourist Association (JHTA), to develop a roadmap for sustainable seafood sourcing.

Waste management was another priority identified by Vermeulen who noted that there is an opportunity to expand the work of local waste management companies and explore initiatives such as waste-to-energy.

“There are very good waste managers in Jamaica. Jamaica Recycles is one of them, and we work with a couple of farms. So we see that there is the moment now they’ve been doing good work, they’ve been validated. So they are doing really responsible and sustainable work and now maybe it’s the moment to upscale that.

So going from one or two trucks to maybe 10 trucks, maybe one day going to waste to energy, things that we saw during this learning and change. These are all things happening in the Dominican Republic but I see Jamaica as the same,” he added.

Looking ahead, Van Balveren said the resort hopes to contribute to Jamaica’s efforts to attract more high-value visitors by offering a luxury experience centred on gastronomy, wellness, personalised service and connections to local culture.

“We also look forward to welcoming the StarAgents Awards LATAM in 2027, which will bring influential travel advisors and industry professionals to the property. It will be a valuable opportunity to introduce JOIA Rose Hall to an important audience and showcase Jamaica as a destination for sophisticated, culturally rich luxury travel,” he added.

World.title: Keep spending tight…
World.content:
The IMF has told Jamaica that revenue mobilisation and restraint in current spending growth are critical to preserve fiscal space for priority investment and return public debt to a sustained downward path.

THE International Monetary Fund (IMF) has applauded the Jamaican Government for its “strong policy frameworks and sustained reforms” which “have underpinned its resilience in the aftermath of Hurricane Melissa”.

The category 5 system left severe damage in sections of the island after its rampage on October 28, 2025.

But the IMF has warned that addressing supply-side constraints is essential to raising Jamaica’s potential growth and enhancing the country’s resilience and has urged the Dr Andrew Holness-led Administration to ensure it contains non-priority recurrent spending.

Holness has already announced a pause on several government expenditure items, including non-essential travel, parties, and retreats at resorts, with the IMF agreeing that this should remain a priority.

“Revenue mobilisation and restraint in current spending growth are critical to preserve fiscal space for priority investment and return public debt to a sustained downward path. The authorities’ efforts to broaden the tax revenue base and strengthen administration are welcomed, along with the intention to develop a mechanism to anchor medium-term public wage growth in a manner consistent with the fiscal framework,” the IMF said on Wednesday as it released its ‘Jamaica: Staff Concluding Statement of its 2026 Article IV Mission’.

According to the IMF, its team, led by W Raphael Lam, held meetings in Kingston with Jamaican authorities, representatives of the private sector, civil society, and development partners during October 27-November 4 to conduct the 2026 Article IV consultation.

In his mission statement, Lam said the Jamaican authorities’ effective disaster risk financing framework, together with the strength of the country’s fiscal, monetary, and financial sector frameworks, have supported an appropriate policy response to cushion the severe impact of Melissa while preserving market access on favourable terms.

“The priority now is to advance reconstruction while preserving macroeconomic stability and deepening reforms, considering the more challenging external environment,” said Lam, who noted that economic activity is recovering gradually in Jamaica.

“Following a contraction of 1.2 per cent in fiscal year (FY)2025/26, growth is projected to recover moderately to 1.3 per cent in FY2026/27, with output returning to its pre-hurricane level by mid-2027, supported by reconstruction efforts and a recovery in tourism.

“Headline inflation, largely driven by higher energy and food prices, has risen above the Bank of Jamaica’s target band of 4-6 per cent, yet is projected to return within the target band by mid-2027 as supply pressures ease,” added Lam.

He pointed out that Jamaica’s risks to the growth outlook are tilted to the downside, while inflation risks remain on the upside.

“Higher energy and food prices from prolonged conflict in the Middle East and drought conditions from El Niño, and a further tightening in global financial conditions, could weigh on growth and intensify inflationary pressures. On the domestic front, delays in both reconstruction and restoration of tourism capacity would also weaken the recovery.”

Lam said the Jamaican Government correctly eased the fiscal stance in response to Hurricane Melissa, although accelerating reconstruction efforts remain essential.

“The multi-layered disaster risk financing provided rapid liquidity, including through IMF’s Rapid Financing Instrument. The Government appropriately activated the fiscal rule’s escape clause to support vulnerable households and hurricane-related reconstruction efforts. Revenue mobilisation efforts to broaden the tax base and strengthen administration are welcome,” said Lam.

“However, efforts are needed to accelerate reconstruction and build back better by closing long-standing infrastructure gaps and strengthening resilience to future natural disasters. The establishment of a new National Reconstruction and Resilience Authority (NaRRA) provides an opportunity to do so, although work should continue in enhancing procurement, contract management, public investment management, and interagency coordination to address implementation bottlenecks.

“Meanwhile, containing non-priority recurrent spending remains essential, including by ensuring that the current fuel price smoothing mechanism continues to operate symmetrically to ensure cost recovery over time,” Lam added.

He pointed out that preserving debt sustainability should remain a priority for the Jamaican Government, with fiscal efforts shifted towards rebuilding buffers.

The IMF official applauded the Bank of Jamaica for its September policy rate hike which, it said, was appropriate, given above-target inflation and persistent commodity-price pressures.

“Monetary policy should remain focused on anchoring inflation expectations and limiting second-round effects, particularly as fiscal policy supports reconstruction efforts. Alongside an active monetary policy response to inflation risks, greater exchange rate flexibility would strengthen Jamaica’s capacity to absorb external shocks, including those coming from less favourable terms of trade.

“Over time, scaling back foreign exchange interventions would allow the exchange rate to play a greater buffering role and support foreign exchange market development,” Lam added.

He argued that Jamaica’s financial system remains resilient, but continued vigilance and reforms are needed.

“Continued close monitoring of credit and market risks, insurers’ financial positions, and vulnerabilities stemming from financial groups’ interconnectedness remains essential,” said Lam.

“In addition, cyber security risks require increased attention, building on the sector-wide cyber intelligence sharing hub.”

He called for the strengthening of the country’s energy security and electricity infrastructure, including by accelerating the transition towards renewable energy sources, which would reduce Jamaica’s exposure to imported fuel prices.

“Progress should continue in reducing crime, streamlining the regulatory burden for businesses, improving education outcomes and workforce skills, and addressing broader infrastructure bottlenecks. Continued implementation of reforms to strengthen climate resilience will help Jamaica better withstand future shocks,” declared the IMF official.

World.title: L’objectif de 1,5° de réchauffement est mort, mais personne ne veut l’enterrer
World.content:
L'ONU a déclaré le mois dernier que, même si les pays réduisaient drastiquement dès maintenant leurs émissions responsables du réchauffement climatique, le meilleur scénario possible serait une hausse des températures mondiales de 1,8°. S’ils déploient également à grande échelle des technologies de capture du carbone pour assainir l’atmosphère, il serait théoriquement possible de revenir à 1,5°, même si ce seuil a été dépassé.

En réalité, les émissions de gaz à effet de serre continuent d’augmenter et les technologies de capture du carbone nécessaires pour inverser cette tendance n’ont pas encore fait leurs preuves à grande échelle.

Le risque de la “pente glissante”

L’ambition globale des plans nationaux de lutte contre le changement climatique, déjà insuffisante avant l’annonce de l’ONU, est encore plus faible que ce qui avait été prévu l’année dernière. Les pays qui comptaient parmi les plus fervents défenseurs de l’objectif de 1,5° relâchent leurs efforts pour y parvenir.

Mais dans le même temps, de nombreux pays (ainsi que des climatologues) craignent que le fait d’abandonner publiquement le discours sur l’objectif de 1,5° n’ouvre la voie à un affaiblissement encore plus marqué des ambitions mondiales. Mettre en avant d’autres objectifs possibles, tels que celui de 1,8° évoqué par l’ONU, reviendrait à s’engager sur une “pente glissante”, a averti un négociateur climat européen.

Johan Rockström prend la parole lors d'un événement à Berlin le 9 mai 2025. | Sebastian Reuter/Getty Images pour Billie Eilish et Support+Feed présentent : OVERHEATED Berlin

“Je ne soutiens pas le message politique visant à maintenir l’objectif de 1,5°, mais d’un autre côté, je ne veux pas y renoncer”, a expliqué Johan Rockström, éminent climatologue et directeur de l’Institut de recherche sur les impacts climatiques de Potsdam.

“Les responsables politiques, lorsqu’ils tiennent ce discours, pensent peut-être naïvement que nous sommes encore, d’une manière ou d’une autre, engagés dans ce parcours linéaire et progressif qui peut tout simplement nous mener vers la sécurité, ce qui n’est pas le cas”, a ajouté le scientifique.

World.title: Spain’s Sánchez laments potential for ‘planetary annihilation’
World.content:
It “was not an act of hostility toward an ally. Nor was it an expression of neutrality or sympathy for the Iranian regime,” Sánchez wrote. Instead, the decision was “a judgement that getting involved would enable escalation.”

Sánchez added that “to keep its commitment to peace, Spain had to be willing to say no, even when doing so carried a political cost.”

“Had more countries done the same, the wars in Gaza and Iran would have been far harder and costlier to wage,” the prime minister speculated, holding up the Spanish government he has led since 2018 as an example to be followed.

The Socialist also criticized the war-readiness strategy the European Union has recently endorsed, noting that “even centrist leaders are embracing the language of war preparedness.”

“Although they do not intend to start a war, their words feed a dangerous militaristic mindset,” the prime minister added.

Sánchez grounded his opposition to war in decades of Spanish civil society activism against armed conflict, flagging the ¡No a la guerra! (“No to war!”) protests in Spain from when the conservative government of José María Aznar backed the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

World.title: European citizens overwhelmingly back creation of an EU army, survey finds
World.content:
The findings come as European governments debate how to strengthen their military capabilities amid Russia’s continued aggression and growing uncertainty over the United States’ commitment to European security.

GLOBSEC surveyed respondents in 14 countries across the transatlantic space, including 11 EU member states, Ukraine, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The enthusiasm for European military capabilities did not appear to be a rebuke of NATO. Some 77% of respondents in the NATO countries surveyed said they would vote to remain members, while 78% of respondents in the EU countries surveyed supported developing the bloc’s own defense capabilities alongside the alliance.

There was also strong support for the most direct form of contribution to national defense: a draft. Among respondents in countries without compulsory military service, 64% favored its reintroduction, according to the report, with the highest numbers found in Czechia, France, Germany and Slovakia.

German exception

Attitudes toward Washington revealed a growing transatlantic divide. More than one-third of respondents across the European countries surveyed now consider the United States a security threat. Around half of respondents in Germany, France and Britain held that view, compared with roughly one-third in Central and Eastern Europe.

Germany was the only country surveyed where a majority regarded Washington as a security threat.

World.title: Comment l’influenceuse complotiste Candace Owens a fait de l’infox sur Brigitte Macron un phénomène mondial
World.content:
Owens ne découvre pas le sujet : elle en a déjà parlé sur sa chaîne YouTube, qui abrite l’un des podcasts les plus regardés au monde, et a été frappée par l’engouement de son public pour cette histoire, racontera Xavier Poussard dans un entretien à POLITICO. Elle est maintenant prête à passer à la vitesse supérieure.

Le duo est aussi improbable que complémentaire. Poussard — alors guère à l’aise face aux caméras, avec un look d’intellectuel tempéré par d’épaisses lunettes à monture plastique — a couché sur le papier tous les détails de la théorie dans un style dense, donnant parfois le vertige. Owens, rompue à l’exercice médiatique et massivement suivie sur YouTube, a, quant à elle, la communauté et le savoir-faire nécessaires pour donner à l’histoire une dimension mondiale. C’est elle, relate Xavier Poussard, qui a suggéré de s’inspirer de Becoming, le best-seller de Michelle Obama, pour le titre et l’identité visuelle du projet.

A peine trois semaines après son arrivée, l’auteur français publie donc Becoming Brigitte (Devenir Brigitte, en français), un livre auto-édité “présenté” par Candace Owens. Au même moment, l’influenceuse diffuse une série de huit vidéos sur sa chaîne YouTube, qui dépassent aujourd’hui les 30 millions de vues. Interrogé par POLITICO, Xavier Poussard a refusé de dévoiler le nombre précis de ventes, précisant cependant que le livre s’est écoulé entre 50 000 et 100 000 exemplaires— un chiffre qu’il n’avait jusqu’ici jamais rendu public.

L’histoire en question a pourtant un problème de taille : elle est mensongère. Brigitte Macron ainsi que son mari, le président de la République française, décident de porter l’affaire en justice. Dans une plainte de 250 pages déposée dans l’Etat du Delaware, ils accusent Candace Owens d’avoir propagé des récits “extravagants, diffamatoires et farfelus” doublés de “mensonges dévastateurs, portant sur des faits [facilement] vérifiables,à l’égard des Macron”.

Les poursuites intentées en juillet 2025, très médiatisées, ont marqué une nouvelle étape dans la lutte que mène le couple présidentiel contre cette théorie du complot qui a vu le jour dans l’ombre en France, en 2018, avant de gagner une plus vaste audience outre-Atlantique via des relais médiatiques d’extrême droite.

L’histoire de la plainte contre Owens et celle des procédures en France met au jour le cheminement d’une théorie conspirationniste à succès, des tréfonds de l’internet français à des chaînes YouTube à l’audience planétaire. Elle raconte aussi les limites du pouvoir à l’ère des réseaux sociaux, où même les personnes parmi les plus puissantes au monde peinent à endiguer la propagation d’une fake news, où l’audience devient profit et le marché de l’attention une manne pour les théories les plus extrêmes.

World.title: Who is Britain’s ‘perfect’ immigrant?
World.content:
Shabana Mahmood is the latest home secretary to try to reform Britain’s complex immigration policy.

Her latest proposals on so-called ‘indefinite leave to remain’ are designed to assess migrants based on the extent of their contribution to the country — by taking account of their skills, salary and what kind of job they are able to fill.

As MPs in the Commons consider Mahmood’s plans, this week on Westminster Insider host Sascha O’Sullivan tries to find out who Britain really sees as its ‘perfect’ immigrant, reflecting on the very different perspectives of the Home Office, voters and economists.

Sascha is joined by Madeleine Sumption, director of the Migration Observatory at Oxford University and interim chair of the Migration Advisor Committee, which advises the Home Office.

Keralan-born Labour MP Sojan Joseph tells Sascha his story of coming to the UK to work as a care worker, and reflects on how he tried to navigate British society amid its various and often contradictory demands for the ‘perfect’ immigrant.

World.title: 5 things to watch at the Dublin EU leaders’ summit
World.content:
Formal talks begin at 9:45 a.m. followed by lunch around 1 p.m. and a press conference provisionally scheduled for 4:15 p.m.

Here are the five issues that really matter — and what to watch for.

1. AI: Can Europe compete at the frontier?

Leaders will debate how Europe can build its own AI capacity, from computing power and cloud infrastructure to chips and models. European Council President António Costa framed the discussion around sovereignty, asking leaders to consider “how Europe can become a leading and sovereign player” across the AI value chain.

The central question is whether Europe should build frontier models to rival U.S. and Chinese developers, or focus on applications built on those models. Finland’s Petteri Orpo and Estonia’s Kristen Michal have argued that Europe “can compete at the frontier” and must aim beyond merely adopting AI.

The obstacle, however, is money. Leaders will discuss how to fund the computing capacity needed to turn European research into products. They will also hear from the CEO of French AI company Mistral, Arthur Mensch, who has railed against abandoning the frontier, and AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton about global rules for the technology. The EU’s position is that its AI Act already provides a regulatory framework.

What to watch: Whether leaders back frontier AI development — and commit money to it.

World.title: Dissident leader wants Europe to consider Belarus in broader Ukraine peace deal
World.content:
Belarus has been a steadfast ally of the Kremlin, which also came to Lukashenko’s aid in August 2020 after a popular uprising threatened to unseat the longtime authoritarian ruler after he rigged an election against Tsikhanouskaya, who then fled the country. Now living in exile in Lithuania, she was handed a 15-year jail term after being convicted in absentia for treason.

The dissident leader criticized what she viewed as a lackadaisical approach to Belarus from Europe’s leaders, particularly before the 2020 election. “For us it looked like Europe just closed eyes, like ‘Lukashenko, you are son of the bitch, but you’re our son of the bitch. We know how to work with you, so okay. We are okay with this.’”

Asked if she blamed former German Chancellor Angela Merkel for the chain of events that led to the invasion of Ukraine, particularly the German leader’s role in the 2014 and 2015 Minsk agreements, which failed to deter Putin from further aggression, Tsikhanouskaya demurred.

“It’s not because of Angela Merkel that the war started against Ukraine,” she said. “It was because Russia was emboldened. I cannot judge politicians who have to make difficult decisions in difficult times. Maybe at that moment she was supported by German people … the policy of appeasement of Putin not only came from the side of Germany but from other [European] countries [and] brought us to the situation we are in.”

However, she accused Europe more broadly of turning a blind eye to the repression of the regime in Minsk. “For 30 years, Lukashenko was playing seesaw between Russia and Europe,” she said, seeking cheap oil and gas from Russia in winter and courting European investment for the rest of the year.

Tsikhanouskaya was attending the Freedom and Security Women Summit in Germany’s parliament during Berlin Freedom Week, which marks the anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall and supports pro-democracy dissident movements.

You can hear the full interview here.

World.title: How to win friends and throw people: Judo’s big impact on politics
World.content:
The five-time Olympic gold medal-winning judoka — that’s someone who does judo, not a number puzzle — announced his candidacy by saying: “France doesn’t need a professional politician who recites talking points and spends all day bickering. It needs common sense, firmness, justice and a government that sets things right.”

As anyone who has ever tried to rewire a house or perform their own dentistry knows, many tasks very much do require a specialist. Politics is usually, though not always, one of them, and therefore Riner may be underestimating the challenge ahead. That said, he is a national hero and has already received an endorsement of sorts from President Emmanuel Macron — although that might not be great news for Riner, as Macron is about as popular in France as putting extra butter on a croissant or working 40 hours a week.

Most of the current crop of candidates have years of experience in political debates behind them, whether that’s far-right leader Marine Le Pen, far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon or any of the 430 centrist ex-prime ministers who want to replace Macron. To level the playing field for Riner, surely it’s only fair to hold a judo competition to see who makes it to the second round — my money would be on Le Pen to beat Riner in the runoff with a Hane-goshi, that’s a springing hip throw that uses the right side of the body.

But what if Riner wins? Could he be the answer to the question “who speaks for Europe when it comes to Russia”? Judo is, after all, Russian President Vladimir Putin’s favorite sport — well, second favorite after “bombing Kyiv.”

Judo is also fairly popular among politicians. Staying in France, David Douillet was a two-time Olympic champion who became a member of parliament and even sports minister. His predecessor as minister was karate champion Chantal Jouanno,, and the president while both were in government was Nicolas Sarkozy, who is reportedly a brown belt in judo — although for security reasons, they do make you remove your belt, no matter the color, when you go to prison.

Outside France, Pierre Trudeau, the former prime minister of Canada, and ex-Japanese Prime Minister Yoshihiko Noda were serious judokas too.

World.title: European diesel prices stay high as global oil supply overtakes demand, IEA says
World.content:
European diesel prices remained 77% above pre-war levels even as recovering Gulf exports pushed global oil supplies above demand for the first time since the Iran war began, the International Energy Agency said on Friday.

 

Prices have fallen sharply in recent weeks, with North Sea Dated crude falling 32% from an early October peak of $136 a barrel to about $93 by the time the IEA wrote its report. European diesel prices fell 11% over the same period, to nearly $180 a barrel.

The IEA said diesel shortages remained the market’s “overriding concern”. Attacks on Russian energy infrastructure continued to disrupt the country’s diesel exports, adding to supply losses in the Middle East. The agency said releasing emergency diesel stocks faster over the coming months would help cover the shortfall while refinery output recovers.

Despite continued attacks on tankers, Gulf oil exports excluding Oman reached 18.4 million barrels per day in October, still 26% below pre-war levels, the Paris-based agency said in its monthly report. Crude led the recovery, while Gulf exports of refined products and liquefied petroleum gas remained at roughly half their pre-war levels.

"The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran," the IEA said.

Global oil supply rose by 3 million barrels per day in September and a further 2.3 million in October, reaching 105.4 million barrels per day. The IEA expects global oil supplies to exceed demand in the fourth quarter but warned that continued attacks on shipping could disrupt the recovery.

Global oil demand is forecast to fall by 2.7 million barrels per day this year, to 102.3 million, as high fuel prices and disruptions to Gulf exports weigh on consumption. The IEA expects demand to recover in 2027, though it sees only a small rise in road fuel use as more drivers switch to electric cars and vehicles become more fuel-efficient.

World.title: China to encourage investment in Turkish renewable energy with $15bn solar and wind deal
World.content:
Türkiye signed a preliminary agreement with China on Thursday (12 November) aimed at attracting around $15 billion (€13.5bn) in investment in solar and wind projects, its energy minister said.

 

The agreement was signed at the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya. It covers plans for solar and wind farms with a combined generating capacity of seven gigawatts, alongside energy storage and improvements to the electricity grid.

Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said the cooperation would also involve sharing technology to support the production of wind-turbine equipment in Türkiye.

The announcement gave no timetable for the projects or details of how they would be financed.

China to encourage investment in Turkish renewable energy

The signing followed talks between Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Chinese Vice President Han Zheng at the summit on 11 November.

Han said Beijing was ready to encourage more Chinese companies to invest in Türkiye and identified renewable energy as an area for closer cooperation, according to Chinese state news agency Xinhua.

Türkiye had around 43.8 gigawatts of solar and wind power capacity at the end of September, accounting for just over a third of its total electricity generating capacity, according to its energy ministry.

The government wants to increase solar and wind capacity to 175 gigawatts by 2040 under its new national energy strategy. The plan aims to shift more of the country’s energy use from oil and gas to electricity.

Speaking at the summit on 10 November, Bayraktar estimated that Türkiye would need around $300 billion (€270bn) in investment for its energy transition by 2040. He said attracting that money would require international partnerships and predictable conditions for investors.

World.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Club Kid' - Sex, drugs & sudden parenthood
World.content:
Brooklyn, 2016. Peter (Jordan Firstman) and his merry partygoing mates are off to the club with only two questions on their minds.

 

"What is the year's best album?"

The answer seems to be a toss-up between Beyoncé's 'Lemonade' and Frank Ocean's 'Blonde'. (Even if we all know that Danny Brown's 'Atrocity Exhibition' is the clear winner, but that's by the by.)

"What do we want?"

The answer is, empathically, drugs. And they want them now.

The club they're heading to won't be Peter's only stop of the night. He's the life of the party on New York's gay club scene, as he's launching events with his friend and business partner Sophie (Cara Delevigne). His task as a club promoter is to make sure everyone has a good time - which means overseeing that the drugs are freeflowing. If he happens to indulge along the way, even better.

Despite having "never touched a vagina in (his) life", he ends up having an LSD-fanned threesome, which includes Leonora (Paris Petitjean), a British "innit, babes?" tourist.

There goes that gay gold star.

“A decade-ish later,” Peter is still hitting the clubs. He's older but not wiser. He's still selling drugs and can't seem to go out without getting fucked up. He's also dealing with both an increasingly pissed off Sophie and Nicky (Eldar Isgandarov), a neurotic twink from Azerbaijan who is an "aspiring queer philosopher" with a marked aversion to paying rent.

On the same day that Sophie fires Peter for being "literally a fucking child" comes a knock at the door. It's Edison (Kirby Howell-Baptiste), another "innit, babes?". And she's not alone. The fast-talking Brit has come to New York with Arlo (Reggie Absolom), Peter's 9-year-old biological son from that 10-year-old drug-fuelled dalliance.

They came over from London because Edison's friend Leonora died by suicide and Arlo's stepfather is a bad egg. Edison has the birth certificate to prove the paternity, needs a quick coke hit to calm her jitters, totally gets it if Peter doesn't want to be a dad, and she'll totes take Arlo back to the UK, but first she has to run a few errands and she'll be right back to pick up the tyke, promise babes.

Spoiler: She's off for good and heads back to London before you can say "fuck this comedown".

Whether he's ready for it or not, it's growing up time for Peter.

Club Kid A24

Firstman’s feature debut finds him not only on triple duty – scriptwriting, directing and acting - but telling a familiar story of stunted adulthood and accidental parenthood.

From Chaplin's The Kid to Mike Mills' C'mon C'mon via Big Daddy, Instructions Not Included and 2023's underseen Scrapper, the story of a manchild meeting his child and dealing with newfound father figure status is hardly new. However, what Club Kid lacks in storytelling originality it makes up for in intoxicating mood and a heartfelt devotion to its characters.

Firstman may be sticking to the established coming-of-age formula but he has a clear appreciation for the city and nightlife he is depicting, as well as an evident understanding and empathy for the New York queer community. He makes the scene feel simultaneously vibrant and believably bittersweet, envelopping the viewer in a world that has many facettes. This is felt the most when it's clear the party's over for Peter, even if he can't quite bring himself to realise the lights have gone up. The euphoria feels genuine, as does the inevitable comedown from the casual sex and ketamine bumps on the dancefloor. To Club Kid 's great strength, you can feel the draw emanating from the hedonistic party lifestyle in the same way you sense how the exhilaration is only a temporary release from daily troubles and deep-seated vulnerabilities.

As Peter tells Arlo in an affecting moment: "I basically don’t have any self-esteem."

Club Kid A24

Central to the film's many charms is the blooming bond between Peter and Arlo. Firstman nails the unlikely father act and shrewdly underplays the torment at the heart of letting go of a treasured part of yourself.

His efforts are rewarded by Absolom. A first-time actor, the young Brit is a revelation here and makes the double-act work wonders. Playing Arlo as a believably precarious scamp with an affinity for Cocteau Twins and DJing, Absolom manages to hint at nascent trauma hiding behind his angelic features in an impressively naturalistic way.

The pair's excellent on screen dynamic is bolstered by Firstman's script, which neatly balances dry humour with warmth. Whether it's some throwaway acerbic zingers or an inappropriate "I Heart Björk And Barebacking” t-shirt, the laughs never overpower the sweetness.

Granted, Nicky's volatile roommate shenanigans cartoonishly clash with the overall tone, and some sentimental moments are occasionally threatened by a few plot shortcuts that undermine real-world realism. Still, cheap melodrama is avoided, and the final shot does bring Club Kid to an honest end.

Sadly, it falls short of tearjerker status. Not by much, mind you, but unlike Charlotte Wells' Aftersun, it doesn't achieve the same level of emotional resonance at the heart of a nuanced story between a young father and his child. Maybe some predictable third act developments are to blame here; but there's no denying that its heart is always in the right place.

All in all, this sincere tale of self-discovery and loving queer familial dynamics is a very promising debut from Firstman, who manages to convey that it's never too late to find a new trajectory in life.

Oh, and it's never too early to introduce those wee urchins in your life to Cocteau Twins and Björk. The definition (and pitfalls) of barebacking will have to wait.

Club Kid is out in cinemas now.

World.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Huang and US Commerce Secretary Lutnick summoned to testify before Congress
World.content:
Tech billionaire Jensen Huang and US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick have been summoned to testify before US lawmakers over the unfolding Nvidia scandal.

 

Huang resigned as CEO of the chipmaker on Thursday after recent reports revealed details of two extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Congress is now calling for more clarity on the situation and what the Trump administration may have known about it.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive U.S. technology," Republican Sen. Tim Scott wrote in a post on social media.

"I am requesting that NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee," he added. "The American people deserve answers."

Scott, the chairman of the Senate Banking Committee, warned Huang that the committee was prepared to subpoena him should he fail to appear voluntarily.

Huang has also been summoned to appear before the House Committees on Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China.

The three committees sent a letter to Huang on Thursday calling him to a "closed-door, transcribed interview" on 1 December.

"Failure to cooperate with this request will result in the House Foreign Affairs Committee issuing a subpoena to compel your testimony in a format of the committee's choosing," the chairmen wrote.

They gave him until 8pm EST on Friday to accept the request.

Huang's decision to exit Nvidia 33 years after founding the company came as reports emerged that he had had a relationship with an executive at the firm. He had already been facing scrutiny over reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a suspected spy. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has since taken over as interim CEO.

The New York Times reported in October that US intelligence officials had previously determined that a senior Chinese executive at a Singapore-based data centre known as Megaspeed had been delivering information to Beijing.

The exec, named as Alice Huang or Huang Le, was reportedly being monitored over possibly steering AI chips to China and had developed a close relationship with the former Nvidia chief.

China has pushed back at the spy plot allegations, calling them "purely unsubstantiated."

Mao Ning, a spokesperson for China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said on Thursday that the US should "should stop fabricating the 'Chinese spy' narratives as a pretext for imposing technology restrictions."

"China and the US maintain close communication on heads-of-state interactions," she continued, adding that Beijing was ready to work with Washington to "jointly build a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity."

World.title: How a new ‘green energy corridor’ from the Caspian Sea could help Eastern Europe kick fossil fuels
World.content:
Azerbaijan has put 'Green Energy Corridors' at the top of its agenda at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya.

 

The goal is to physically integrate renewable grids across multiple countries and establish a direct electricity transit route from the Caspian Sea to European markets.

The country has formed a new alliance with Türkiye, Georgia and Bulgaria, who all signed the multi-state Strategic Partnership Agreement in Clean Energy.

Moving beyond broad climate pledges, discussions at the Azerbaijan Pavilion highlighted the proposed green energy routes and strategic Azerbaijan-Türkiye energy interconnection as critical drivers of cross-border infrastructure.

By linking the South Caucasus and Eastern Europe, the four nations intend to diversify transmission routes and ensure long-term regional energy security.

Azerbaijan, Turkey, Georgia and Bulgaria have signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement in Clean Energy at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya The Ministry of Energy of the Republic of Azerbaijan, November 2026

Forging the Green Energy Corridor

Formalised on the sidelines of the Antalya climate talks, the agreement turns years of conceptual planning into binding infrastructure commitments.

The core objective is to develop a high-capacity transmission network that exports wind and solar energy generated in the Caspian basin directly to Eastern and Central Europe.

Azerbaijan's Energy Minister Parviz Shahbazov, Türkiye's Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Alparslan Bayraktar, Georgia's Vice Prime Minister, Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development Mariam Kvrivishvili, and Bulgaria's Minister of Energy Iva Petrova signed the document on 10 November 2026.

To achieve their goals, the four nations are establishing a synchronised grid framework that bypasses traditional logistical bottlenecks.

The infrastructure will rely on expanding existing overland high-voltage lines through the South Caucasus and Türkiye.

A crucial component of the project involves the parallel enhancement of fibre-optic communications along the transit route, ensuring secure, uninterrupted transmission and modern grid management.

The initiative aims to transform Azerbaijan into an interregional electricity hub.

Azerbaijan, Turkey, Georgia and Bulgaria have signed a Strategic Partnership Agreement in Clean Energy at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya The Ministry of Energy of the Republic of Azerbaijan, November 2026

Driving EU supply diversification

For European markets, Bulgaria’s formal involvement as a signatory is critical.

The partnership directly addresses Eastern Europe's urgent macroeconomic mandate to diversify energy imports and reduce historical reliance on legacy fossil fuel corridors.

Integrating the South Caucasus power network directly with Bulgaria establishes a vital new energy artery into the broader European Union grid.

Establishing a dedicated Green Energy Corridor will provide European consumer markets with a stable, alternative supply of decarbonised electricity.

Distributing the immense financial and technical burdens of grid modernisation across four distinct national economies will create a highly structured environment.

Multilateral alignment lowers logistical risks for international investors, private equity firms, and development banks expected to fund the upcoming construction phases.

Accelerating bilateral grid diplomacy

Throughout the COP31 summit, the Azerbaijan Pavilion functioned as a central hub for detailing the logistical and financial scope of these cross-border projects.

Presentations highlighted the 'Corridor of Dialogue' concept, framing the strategic Azerbaijan-Türkiye energy interconnection as the foundational backbone for the wider four-nation initiative.

Massive investments in domestic renewable generation, particularly onshore and offshore wind projects in the Caspian Sea, will require robust, export-oriented infrastructure to be economically viable.

Aside from the principal signing, the Azerbaijani Ministry of Energy conducted a rapid series of parallel diplomatic engagements to solidify the broader grid agenda.

Related Health gets just a small fraction of climate finance as COP31 warns of growing crisis

Minister Shahbazov held intensive bilateral meetings with international renewable giants including Vestas, ACWA Power and NKT to discuss the parallel development of power generation, energy storage and cross-border grids.

Framing the Antalya pact as a continuation of Baku's historical energy strategy, Shahbazov stated that the ministry is actively turning previous COP grid agendas into concrete projects physically connecting producer nations with consumer markets.

World.title: Darth Vader's lightsaber breaks Star Wars auction record by selling for nearly €4.5 million
World.content:
The iconic lightsaber used by Darth Vader in Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back (1980) and Star Wars: Episode VI - Return of the Jedi (1983) has broken records in a US auction held by Heritage Auctions.

 

The lightsaber, which was used in the climactic duel in Cloud City where Vader tells Luke Skywalker “I am your father,” was originally expected to sell for over $1 million. It ended up going for $4.875 million (approx. €4.4m) at the Ultimate Star Wars Auction.

The lightsaber used by Darth Vader in the film The Empire Strikes Back Heritage Auctions via AP

The sale marks not only a world auction record for any Star Wars collectible, according to Heritage Auctions, but also a new auction record for a screen-used Star Wars prop.

Indeed, the final sum shoots past the $3.75m mark established in July and last year's $3.6m auction sale.

Brian Chanes, the senior director of Hollywood and entertainment at Heritage Auctions, said the Darth Vader saber - which was one of 27 lightsaber props up for sale - was “like the Holy Grail” to a Star Wars collector.

Elsewhere, 2027 marks the 50th anniversary of the first Star Wars film, Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope (1977). To celebrate the milestone, the iconic sci-fi adventure has been dubbed into the Welsh language – Cymraeg – for the very first time.

World.title: Ukraine: Russian drone attacks hit Kyiv hospital, leave two dead in Odesa
World.content:
In the capital's Shevchenkivskyi district, a strike sparked a fire at a medical facility and partially destroyed its second floor, Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported. Hospital staff evacuated 30 people, while emergency crews rescued another seven. Footage released by the emergency service shows patients being helped to safety, including people using wheelchairs and crutches, as firefighters work to extinguish the blaze. Other images reveal damaged windows, smoke rising from the building and rescue workers moving through hospital corridors. The fire had been extinguished.

 

In the southern port city of Odesa, a separate Russian drone attack killed two people and injured five others, according to Serhii Lysak, head of the city's military administration. A private house and several vehicles were also damaged in the strikes, while nighttime footage shows firefighters tackling a blaze at the scene.

The attacks affected two major Ukrainian cities, with emergency services responding to fires, damaged buildings and casualties. In Kyiv, the evacuation of patients highlighted the disruption caused when medical facilities are struck, particularly for people with reduced mobility. The incidents come as Russia continues its aerial attacks on Ukraine more than four years after launching its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

World.title: ‘Monstrous injustice’: King Charles condemns slavery as UK agrees to talks
World.content:
In this episode of Spotlight on Africa, we talked to scholars from the continent and the Caribbean about slavery reparations – a key topic discussed at this year’s Commonwealth Heads of Government meeting in Antigua and Barbuda.

Advertising

The Commonwealth is a 56-nation group of mostly former British colonies, 21 of them in Africa. King Charles III remains head of state in 15 of them, including the UK.

Its biennial Heads of Government Meeting took place from 1 to 4 November 2026 in Antigua and Barbuda.

In a final communiqué issued on Wednesday, the group said the time had come for “meaningful, truthful and respectful conversation towards forging a common future based on equity”.

Timetable of talks

While no timetable for talks was announced, the group welcomed the United Kingdom’s willingness to engage “in a structured, time-bound, inclusive and good-faith dialogue with affected parties addressing the transatlantic trafficking of enslaved Africans and its historical harms”.

In his opening speech, King Charles III, who is politically neutral, called the slave trade “a monstrous injustice” that filled him with “profound personal sorrow”, but stopped short of a formal apology.

UN backs resolution calling slave trade ‘gravest crime against humanity’

For his part, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was open to saying sorry but ruled out paying the financial reparations demanded by some Caribbean countries.

Britain’s Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also said it was “not feasible” for the country to pay reparations for slavery, but that “there are things we can work on co-operatively”.

According to reports, Britain could issue a formal apology next year, during its G20 presidency.

Britain played a pivotal role in the slave trade, which saw between 10 and 15 million enslaved Africans taken to the Americas over four centuries.

The country abolished the slave trade in 1807 and slavery throughout the British Empire in 1833. It paid financial compensation, but to plantation owners rather than to the enslaved people themselves.

UN resolution

In March this year, the United Nations adopted a resolution recognising the transatlantic slave trade and the enslavement of Africans as the “gravest crime against humanity”, in a motion spearheaded by Ghana.

Ghana backs Jamaica’s petition to push UK for slavery reparations

For many countries, the time has come for formal apologies and concrete plans for slavery reparations.

To find out how these issues are being tackled on the African continent and in the Caribbean, RFI spoke to a panel of four guests:

Edem Adotey: professor at the Institute of African Studies in Accra, Ghana,

Joel Kibazo: Commonwealth spokesperson,

Matiangai Sirleaf: professor at the University of Maryland Francis King Carey School of Law in the United States,

Verene A. Shepherd: Jamaican historian and one of three vice-chairs of the Caricom Reparations Commission.

This episode was mixed by Nicolas Doreau.
