World.title: Iraq to close Mandali border crossing with Iran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has announced the temporary closure of the Mandali border crossing with Iran, as Baghdad is under increased US pressure to limit trade channels with Tehran amid the continuing US-Iran dispute.

The crossing, in Iraq’s eastern Diyala region, is set to shut on Friday, November 13, for maintenance and technology improvements.

Iraq’s Border Ports Authority said that the work is meant to enhance operations ahead of the rainy season but did not say when the crossing will reopen.

The decision came after Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein announced that Washington had urged the closing of practically all border crossings with Iran, leaving just two open.

Hussein admitted that such limitations might have a considerable impact on Iraq’s economy, considering the extensive commerce between the two nations.

The statement comes after another incident involving Iranian aviation, in which Iraqi officials denied permission for an airplane carrying Iran’s national football team to land at Basra International Airport on November 10.

The plane returned to Iran, and the players continued their trek to Iraq by road.

The denial reportedly stemmed from US restrictions on Iranian airlines.

Baghdad has also increased its inspection of border operations and smuggling networks, as it faces pressure to put Iran-backed armed organizations under state control.

Groups like Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba continue to wield considerable power in Iraq, hampering the government’s attempts to keep the nation out of the larger regional struggle.

At the same time, Iraq reopened the Sheeb border crossing with Iran in Maysan province on November 10, after many weeks of shutdown for security and technological upgrades.

The reopening reveals that Baghdad has not implemented a complete blockade of its border with Iran.

The events reflect Iraq’s increasingly strained relationship with Washington and Tehran, as the government works to bolster national security, comply with international sanctions, and safeguard its economic interests.

As the US-Iran war continues, Baghdad is under increasing pressure to display stronger control over its borders, airspace, and armed groups while preserving vital commerce with its eastern neighbor.

World.title: Spinneys opens second Iraq branch at Baghdad’s Iraq Gate Residential Complex
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Spinneys, an international grocery chain, has launched its second branch in Baghdad, increasing its presence in Iraq with a new location at the Iraq Gate Residential Complex in the Mansour area.

The 700-square-meter grocery serves inhabitants of the complex, which has around 4,800 residential homes.

The supermarket is intended to serve as a neighborhood shopping attraction, selling groceries, fresh organic produce, bakery goods, dairy, deli items, and common home necessities.

The new facility also provides grocery delivery services, enabling consumers to have their purchases delivered straight to their homes.

The launch follows Spinneys’ introduction into the Iraqi market and is part of the company’s ambition to grow its supermarket network in Baghdad and across the nation.

Spinneys opened its first Iraqi branch at Iraq Mall in Baghdad earlier in 2026. The flagship supermarket covers more than 7,000 square metres, making it considerably larger than the new residential-focused location.

Spinneys’ activities in Iraq are overseen by Gray Mackenzie Retail Lebanon (GMRL), a retail firm founded in 1996 that manages the Spinneys supermarket brand in Lebanon and has expanded into the Iraqi market.

The Iraq Gate location features a smaller residential-focused supermarket concept, intended to enable quick shopping for residents inside the development rather than operating as a huge independent retail attraction.

The launch is another step in Spinneys’ development in Iraq, as multinational supermarket operators increase their presence in Baghdad’s retail sector.

World.title: Silicon Valley insiders nervously eye Nvidia scandal fallout
World.content:
San Francisco – Hours after Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia, shocked tech insiders at a conference in San Francisco saw his departure as troubling for the business but were uncertain over how heavy the impact would be.

Many were still processing the spectacular departure of the rockstar CEO, who came to embody the global boom for AI chips but fell from grace after revelations of multiple extramarital affairs, one reportedly with a Chinese spy.

“It’s a blow to I think everything and pretty much every player in (the) space, except direct competitors,” Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi said in onstage remarks.

“The culture of the company is a lot… the personality of the CEO that is there for a long time,” Ghodsi said.

A lot now “depends on who the next CEO is,” he added.

Nvidia’s board has appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to replace Huang on an interim basis, but it remains unclear who will take over in the long term.

Investors had begun taking a dimmer view of the company even before news of the scandal broke.

Nvidia’s shares have lost 13 percent of their value since Monday, and are down more than 26 percent over the past month.

One venture capitalist told AFP that the fallout from Huang’s infidelities was accelerating a correction that had already been underway.

– Show must go on –

Others were more sanguine about the industry’s prospects.

“We’re very sad to see Jensen go,” Asher Spector, the founder of an artificial intelligence startup called Flapping Airplanes, said onstage at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit.

“That said, Nvidia has been a great partner,” Spector said, adding: “We’re very optimistic.”

A lighthearted note came from an arcade game in the style of “Mortal Kombat”, which pitted tech CEOs like Huang, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and even disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes against each other.

Other major tech companies, including Microsoft, Uber and Apple, have survived and even thrived after the departure of era-defining executives.

Still, some attendees noted that Huang’s downfall might leave competing AI chip designers circling for a chance to grab a piece of Nvidia’s market share.

“It was kind of unimaginable to us that there would be a world where Nvidia wouldn’t be the biggest player a few years from now,” Robert Wachen, the co-founder of AI computing startup Etched, said.

“But now you see there’s probably a pretty big opening” for other players in the sector, Wachen said.

– Open-model guru –

Huang’s exit has particularly rattled the open software community.

The former Nvidia chief advocated for an ecosystem that includes so-called open models, which users can download and customize to varying degrees.

That differs from leading model developers like OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, and Anthropic, which crafts Claude, both of which push for closed models.

Huang was “the leader of the pack” for open models and his departure does “create a lot of uncertainty,” Igor Babuschkin, the CEO of a startup called River AI, said.

He also led Nvidia to provide billions in financing commitments to other companies, notably a more than $100 billion data center for OpenAI, which sparked concerns about circular dealmaking and a growing tech bubble.

“Will circular deals face greater scrutiny and a reality check? Very likely,” Hivemind Capital partner Emmanuel Vallod told AFP via email.

“But does that mean the music is about to stop? I very much doubt it.”

World.title: Iraq orders only national flag at government buildings amid crackdown on militias
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is said to have instructed ministries, government agencies, and public institutions to show only the Iraqi national flag, with other flags prohibited from flying at official sites.

The decision comes as Baghdad steps up attempts to reinforce state authority and limit the influence of armed factions, especially those with strong links to Iran.

Iran-backed militias, such as Kataib Hezbollah and Harakat Hezbollah al-Nujaba, have maintained a visible presence in Iraq, with their flags and insignia seen at public meetings, roadblocks, and other armed group sites.

The alleged limitation would highlight the contrast between Iraqi state institutions and political or military groups, stressing that government buildings should represent the nation rather than specific factions.

Since entering office in May 2026, Al-Zaidi has progressively opposed militia authority, pushing for firearms to be solely controlled by the state and warning that armed organizations who refuse to comply might face legal penalties.

The government has also taken action against alleged militia-related business interests, including the cancelation of contracts at Mosul International Airport.

The moves have heightened tensions with Kataib Hezbollah and other Iran-aligned militias who oppose Baghdad’s disarmament initiatives.

The restrictions come amid ongoing regional instability in the aftermath of the US-Iran war earlier this year, which has exposed Iraq to assaults and raised pressure on the government to prevent armed groups from pulling the nation into the fight.

For Baghdad, limiting flags at official buildings would be a symbolic step toward bolstering national sovereignty. The greater question is whether the administration can transform such efforts into effective control of armed groups and their weaponry.

World.title: Iraq offers condolences to UAE after Fujairah road accident kills 14
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has sent its condolences to the United Arab Emirates after a tragic traffic accident in Fujairah that killed 14 people and wounded 30 others.

Iraq’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs released a statement on November 12 expressing sorrow to the UAE government, its people, and the families of those killed, confirming Baghdad’s support for the nation in the aftermath of the tragedy.

According to the UAE’s Emirates News Agency (WAM), the accident happened soon before midnight on November 11 on Sheik Khalifa bin Zayed Road, near Fujairah’s entrance.

Fujairah Police reported that a truck driver lost control and struck another car before flipping and colliding with many automobiles stuck in sluggish traffic.

A fire then broke out, spreading to surrounding automobiles.

According to UAE media outlets, the collision included 23 cars, five of which were trucks, and was one of the country’s bloodiest in recent years.

Emergency responders, including police, ambulance personnel, and Civil Defense teams, were sent to put out the fire, rescue casualties, and take the wounded to hospitals.

Fujairah Police stated that 15 wounded individuals had been released from the hospital, while another 15 were still receiving medical attention.

Authorities reportedly indicated that the dead were Emirati and international nationals, with DNA tests underway to identify some of those slain.

World.title: Microsoft battling to fix global Outlook outage
World.content:
Washington – Microsoft said on Thursday that efforts to repair a major outage of Outlook were not going as expected and the firm was seeking alternative solutions as users around the world were left without its crucial services.

The hours-long disruption, which Microsoft attributed to “elevated load” on its infrastructure, has hit email as well as products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.

The impact of the outage has been felt globally, with users ranging from companies to governments reporting that they were unable to communicate via Outlook.

“We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they’re not taking as expected,” Microsoft said on X.

“We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity,” the tech giant added, without saying when service was expected to be fully restored.

The disruption went global within an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.

A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.

One of the impacted countries was New Zealand, where the foreign ministry sent a notice saying its “ability to receive emails has been affected by the global Microsoft outage. This also impacts all New Zealand Embassies, Consulates and Representative Offices around the world.”

Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports “in the Americas,” but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected “Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.”

Microsoft 365 is the company’s cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.

“We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors,” the company wrote on X.

“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” it added.

Downdetector, which tracks online outages, showed a sharp decline around 0450 GMT in users’ reports of disruptions in Washington and Hong Kong.

Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.

As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.

In one update shortly after 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT), Microsoft said it was “observing limited recovery” as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.

“As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect,” the company added.

World.title: SpaceX Starship test to attempt first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
World.content:
Houston – Elon Musk’s SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking “catch” of the spaceship following a day in orbit.

A successful capture of the Starship upper stage would mark a significant milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable spacecraft that can drastically reduce mission costs and make frequent travel possible.

“If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket,” SpaceX said.

For the 15th Starship test flight Friday, SpaceX aims to recover both stages of the massive 124-meter (407-foot) launch vehicle.

The company has caught the booster, dubbed Super Heavy, on three previous occasions, with the first stage descending vertically back to the launch site shortly after blastoff and nestling into mechanical “chopstick” arms.

It will now attempt to do the same with the spaceship. Some versions of the vessel are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while others will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars.

A spacecraft that can be fully reused is the “Holy Grail” of the space industry, said Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

“No one’s really been able to do that so far,” he said. “People have been trying to do that since the (NASA) space shuttle. But the space shuttle ended up being kind of a compromise because a lot of the vehicle wasn’t reusable.”

Reusing the Starship spacecraft would require the vessel to withstand the extreme heat of reentering Earth’s atmosphere and then return to service without extensive refurbishment.

– Refueling challenge –

Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which are regularly employed to launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station.

The Starship project, however, has been plagued by years-long delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges — even as NASA is counting on the spaceship to serve as a lunar lander for its Artemis program.

Other technical challenges include transferring fuel to Starship in orbit — a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars.

Following SpaceX’s high-profile stock market debut in June, the company carried out the first orbital flight of Starship in September, though the mission was cut short due to an engine issue.

It is also investing heavily in additional launch sites for its mega-rocket in Louisiana and Florida.

– Complex capture –

Friday’s launch is scheduled to take place at SpaceX’s “Starbase” in southern Texas at 4:45 pm (2245 GMT).

Following liftoff and the mid-air separation of the two stages, SpaceX plans to bring Super Heavy back to Earth six and a half minutes later, catching it at the launch site on the Gulf of Mexico coastline.

The spaceship will continue to reach Earth’s orbit, where it will deploy 26 satellites into Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation that has become a major revenue stream for SpaceX.

It will then circle the planet 14 times, before returning 22 hours later and — SpaceX hopes — descending safely into the chopstick arms.

This capture attempt is more complex than that of the booster, as the spaceship will be descending much faster and from a much greater altitude.

SpaceX has said it would proceed with these maneuvers only if conditions are optimal, and in the past has made last-minute changes to test flights under Musk’s “fail fast” strategy of learning through crashes, explosions and other mishaps.

As of late Thursday, the US Federal Aviation Administration had not yet given its final approval for the test flight.

World.title: Cunningham scores 52 as Pistons win double-OT thriller against Wizards
World.content:
Washington – Cade Cunningham racked up 52 points as the Detroit Pistons edged a double-overtime thriller 144-140 against Washington on Thursday.

The Wizards twice extended the game with clutch scores in the dying seconds, but could not repeat the trick a third time as the Pistons held their nerve to claim an epic road win.

Cunningham became the first player in NBA history to score 50 points and add 10 assists with zero turnovers, while Ausar Thompson had a triple-double with 17 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds.

The Wizards had three starters scoring 30-plus points — Trae Young, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr — but it was not enough to prevent Washington’s sixth defeat in a row.

In a back-and-forth game featuring 20 lead changes, Detroit started slow but built a double-digit lead early in the second half.

It was slowly whittled down by Washington, but the Pistons were clinging on to their lead when Cunningham was fouled at 119-118 with less than two seconds remaining.

Cunningham sank both free throws, but Trae Young made a nerveless trey right at the buzzer to force overtime.

The Wizards raced 128-121 up, but Cunningham would not quit.

He made a three-pointer with 30 seconds left to level the score, then set up Dunacan Robinson for what appeared to be another. A video replay ruled Robinson’s toe was on the line, and Detroit had only a two-point lead.

That proved crucial, as Young set up this year’s top draft pick AJ Dybantsa, who forced a second overtime period with a pull-up jump shot.

Cunningham made a fadeaway shot for a four-point lead with 25 seconds left, and this time the Wizards could not conjure a third comeback.

Young missed two three-point efforts, with Washington settling for two free throws, but were unable to score in their final possession.

Elsewhere, Tyrese Maxey powered Philadelphia to its latest comeback victory, scoring 27 points as the Sixers shrugged off a slow start and the absence of LeBron James to beat the Toronto Raptors 123-112.

Maxey added eight assists, linking up seamlessly with Joel Embiid, who briefly left the court early with a knee injury but returned to add 20 points.

The Sixers had trailed by 17 points in the first quarter, immediately following Embiid’s absence, but rallied for their fifth double-digit comeback this season.

“We’ll take it. I mean, extreme professional win by us. We stayed with it. Didn’t start out great, but it was a good win,” said Maxey.

“We played together the last seven years, so I kind of know where he’s going to be, he knows where I’m going to be at, and it’s good for us,” he said, of his partnership with 2023 MVP Embiid.

Veteran James, who turns 42 next month, was ruled out of Thursday’s clash to manage a lower back issue.

That meant extra work fell on the Sixers’ bench, who managed 39 points led by Anfernee Simons’ 17.

Philadelphia moves to 10-3, just half a game back from the 10-2 Boston Celtics atop the Eastern Conference.

World.title: 'Potential to disturb public peace': Centre refuses RTI on 'Any Kuki Tribes' deletion proposal
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has refused to disclose details of a reported Manipur government proposal to delete the nomenclature "Any Kuki Tribes" from the state's Scheduled Tribes (ST) list, citing concerns that sharing the information could aggravate inter-community tensions in the violence-hit state, PTI reported.The Central Information Commission (CIC), while hearing an RTI appeal, upheld the ministry of tribal affairs' decision to withhold the information, saying the public interest in disclosing internal deliberations did not outweigh the potential risks to public order.The RTI application was filed by an applicant Micheal Haokip, who referred to a Manipur government letter that he claimed concerned a proposal to remove "Any Kuki Tribes" from the state's ST list and replace "Any Mizo (Lushai) Tribe" with "Mizo".Haokip had sought confirmation of whether the ministry received the proposal, along with its date of receipt and official file number. He also sought details of the action taken, whether it had been forwarded to the Registrar General of India (RGI) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST) for concurrence, and copies of relevant communications and file notings.In its reply dated June 24, 2025, the ministry said it was the nodal authority for processing claims relating to the inclusion, exclusion or modification of communities in the ST list under Article 342 of the Constitution.It said proposals recommended and justified by the concerned state government or Union Territory administration could be processed further, subject to concurrence from the RGI and NCST, before being considered for legislative amendment.The ministry argued that disclosing information during the examination and consultation process could exert "undue pressure and influence" on authorities and allow vested interests to interfere with independent decision-making.It also cited instances where disclosure of information relating to the notification of a community had allegedly led to violence."Such disclosure of information will have the potential to disturb public peace, tranquillity and encourage enmity between the communities," the CPIO said.During the CIC hearing, the ministry reiterated that the matter was sensitive given the ethnic violence and prevailing law-and-order concerns in Manipur. It apprehended that premature disclosure of internal proposals, communications and deliberative records could aggravate inter-community tensions, exert pressure on authorities and potentially disturb public order.Haokip argued that the ministry's response was vague and failed to explain how basic administrative details, such as the date of receipt, file number and names of officials handling the matter, could be treated as information held in a fiduciary capacity.He also contended that the public-order concerns cited by the ministry were general and speculative.The CIC, however, said it was not persuaded that the public interest in disclosing substantive internal deliberations and communications outweighed the potential harm identified by the ministry.It also examined whether non-sensitive portions of the records could be disclosed after redaction under Section 10 of the RTI Act but rejected even the limited relief of providing redacted copies of the proposal and related action-taken notings.

The opposition party alleged that households were struggling to manage their budgets as food prices and the cost of everyday necessities continued to climb.

"Under the Modi government, inflation is no longer just a witchâit has now become an uninvited guest, devouring every householdâs budget. World.title: Manipur 2023 violence probe commission gets 7th extension, report due by May 20, 2027
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The commission set up to investigate the ethnic violence that broke out in Manipur in May 2023 received its seventh extension on Friday, with the Centre directing it to submit its report by May 20, 2027, according to a government order.

The commission was initially given a deadline of November 2023 to submit its findings under a notification issued in September that year.

Its terms of reference included investigating the causes and spread of the violence that broke out in Manipur on May 3, 2023, targeting members of different communities, and examining the sequence of events that led to the unrest.

It was also asked to assess whether there had been any lapses or negligence on the part of officials or other individuals, and whether the administrative steps taken to prevent and contain the violence were adequate.

World.title: 'Hopeful they will come': India on inviting Pakistan to SCO Civilisational Forum in Delhi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India has invited

to the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi from November 20 to 22, with Union culture minister

saying he remained hopeful that Islamabad would participate.

"I should be hopeful that they will come," Shekhawat said at a press conference while discussing the invitations sent to participating countries.

will attend the inauguration of the forum on November 20, Shekhawat said.

According to the minister, India sent invitations to 25 countries, including SCO member states, and 15 have confirmed their participation so far. China, Iran and Kazakhstan are among the countries that have confirmed their presence.



The forum will be held at Purana Qila in Delhi and is intended to strengthen cultural understanding and people-to-people ties among SCO member states.

Shekhawat said the grouping should serve as more than a geopolitical platform and also provide a space for countries to discuss their shared civilisational heritage.

Unesco sites, shared heritage on agenda

The minister said discussions at the forum would include multinational nominations for Unesco sites.





The initiative is also expected to promote cultural cooperation and a better understanding of the region's shared heritage.

The proposal for the civilisational dialogue forum was put forward by PM Modi during his visit to Tianjin for the SCO summit last year. The initiative was aimed at fostering closer people-to-people connections and cultural understanding within the grouping.

India's invitation to Pakistan comes despite strained bilateral ties.

Pakistan's minister for national heritage and culture, Aurangzeb Khan Khichi, was invited to the meeting.

The SCO has continued to provide a platform for engagement between the two countries even in the absence of substantive bilateral talks.

World.title: Indonesian woman with alleged Chinese links caught at Sonauli border after failing to speak Hindi
World.content:
Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs; NGO links under investigation

LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly.Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.

World.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims

Tamil Nadu Social Justice Minister Vanni Arasu, who is the Minister in-charge for Kallakurichi, on Friday (November 13, 2026) hailed the District Collector J.E. When journalists asked the Minister about claims that ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) MLA C. Arul Vignesh had sent an objectionable text message to the Collector, Mr. Arasu, who belongs to the VCK, an ally of the TVK, said he was yet to inquire into the matter.

‘Collector Padmaja an honest, impartial officer’

World.title: New panel to study Plus One seat shortage in Keralam
World.content:
A new committee will study the shortage of Plus One higher secondary seats in Keralam, Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen has said.

The committee will examine Plus One seat shortage in each education district and address the issue at the education level itself, the Minister said at a press conference recently. The panel, he said, would give its recommendations ahead of the Plus One admission process next year.

Previous panel

The previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) government too had in 2023 appointed a committee to study higher secondary batch reorganisation. The committee led by former higher secondary director V. Karthikeyan Nair submitted its report in 2024. Its recommendations included fixing the maximum number of students in a class at 50 and sanctioning of around 200 new batches to solve the seat shortage in the Malabar region. However, the LDF government neither acted on the findings of the report nor made it public.

Mr. Samsudheen said it was a fact that there was shortage of Plus One seats in Malabar region, with the maximum shortage of around 20,000 seats in Malappuram, followed by Palakkad, Kozhikode and Kasaragod districts, as per General Education department figures.

In other Malabar districts, there was shortage in some regions, such as urban areas of Kannur and Wayanad. At the same time, some seats in interior areas in these districts were vacant, he said.

Mr. Samsudheen also indicated that vacant seats that existed in parts of various districts could not be taken back as it could lead to local-level issues.

Besides marginal increase, the United Democratic Front (UDF) government had sanctioned a total of 120 additional temporary batches in Malabar this year on the basis of an analysis after the main phase of admissions was completed this year, he said.

Most of the vacant seats, the Minister said, were in the unaided sector. These could not be conflated with government and aided sectors, as many children were reluctant to take admission to unaided schools owing to the high fee there.

Significantly, the Karthikeyan Nair committee had recommended that 50-odd batches with 20-25 students each in higher secondary schools in districts such as Thiruvananthapuram, Kottayam, Pathanamthitta, and Alappuzha be shifted to Malappuram.

World.title: Silver Beach in Cuddalore gets coveted Blue Flag tag
World.content:
Silver Beach in Cuddalore district has received the coveted ‘Blue Flag’ certification from the Denmark-based Foundation for Environment Education (FEE), marking a significant milestone in the district’s efforts to strengthen coastal environmental protection and promote sustainable tourism. The certificate was received on November 12, 2026.

Blue Flag eco-label recognises beaches that comply with stringent criteria relating to environmental management, bathing water quality, cleanliness, safety, sanitation, environmental education, and visitor facilities.

Silver Beach is one of three beaches in Tamil Nadu to receive the new certification for 2026-27. The other two are Kameswaram Beach in Nagapattinam district and Ariyaman Beach in Ramanathapuram district. Kovalam Beach in Chengalpattu district has retained the certification for the sixth consecutive year.

The development of Silver Beach was undertaken by the Cuddalore Municipal Corporation under the Tamil Nadu Coastal Restoration Mission. The works were implemented under the guidance of District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar with the coordination of Corporation Commissioner S. Kishankumar.

Infrastructure and visitor facilities

The beach extends over one kilometre, of which a 500-metre stretch has been earmarked for Blue Flag activities. It receives an average of 2,500 visitors a day, with the number rising to an estimated 3,500 during peak periods.

According to Mr. Kumar: “The infrastructure improvements include separate restroom blocks for men and women, changing rooms with shower facilities, a dedicated toilet for persons with disabilities, a greywater treatment plant, solar power infrastructure, a first-aid station, a CCTV monitoring facility, information display boards, and a beach layout map. Bamboo-based facilities, including seating benches, sit-outs, recliner chairs, litter bins, protective enclosures, and accessible ramps, have also been provided to improve visitor convenience.”

Scientific monitoring of water quality

According to S. Manivel, Green Fellow, Department of Environment and Climate Change: “Water quality monitoring is a key component of the Blue Flag requirements. Five sampling points have been identified, including one in the designated swimming zone. Samples are analysed by the National Centre for Sustainable Coastal Management (NCSCM), Chennai.”

He added that the Blue Flag application records compliance with prescribed microbiological parameters, including Escherichia coli and intestinal enterococci, as well as physical and chemical parameters such as pH and oil content. A sampling calendar has also been established, and updated bathing water quality information is displayed on public information boards.

The beach is cleaned twice daily by six sanitation workers, supported by a mechanised beach-cleaning machine. Separate collection facilities are provided for biodegradable and non-biodegradable waste, including food waste, plastic, and glass. The collected waste is transported to the Corporation’s Micro Composting Centre (MCC) and Material Recovery Facility (MRF) for further processing.

A designated safe bathing zone has been established based on a Safety Risk Assessment conducted by NCSCM in 2025. The area is demarcated using a flag system and information boards.

Interdepartmental coordination

A Beach Management Committee has been constituted under the chairmanship of the District Collector, with the Corporation Commissioner as Vice-Chairperson. Representatives from the Forest Department, Police Department, Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, Fisheries Department, Tourism Department, Department of Environment and Climate Change, and other agencies are members.

“The international recognition is expected to strengthen Cuddalore’s profile as a coastal tourism destination while encouraging continued efforts in environmental monitoring, scientific waste management, coastal vegetation protection, and public participation. The certification marks an important step in the district’s efforts to align beach management with internationally recognised environmental and safety standards,” Mr. Manivel added.

World.title: HYDRAA launches Fox Sagar Lake development; plans STP for preventing sewage, industrial effluents

List of works at Fox Sagar lake

HYDRAA Commissioner A.V. Ranganath performed the ground-breaking ceremony and said the lake would be comprehensively developed within a year. The works would include removal of encroachments and accumulated silt, treatment of polluted water and strengthening of the lake bund and its inlet and outlet systems.

Fox Sagar lake polluted by sewage and industrial chemical waste

Mr. Ranganath said the lake, which had been polluted by sewage and industrial chemical waste, had accumulated silt of nearly five metres depth, preventing water from percolating into the ground. The restoration aimed to increase its storage capacity from the existing 1,000 million litres to 4,000 million litres.

Water samples from the lake and groundwater in the surrounding areas would be tested by the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) before and after the restoration works. A sewage treatment plant would be established to prevent untreated sewage and industrial effluents from entering the lake. Measures would also be taken to allow rainwater into the lake and strengthen flood management arrangements.

Built in 1897 during the Nizam’s rule, Fox Sagar supplied water for irrigation and drinking purposes to Secunderabad. Storm water channels connected it to Hussain Sagar, while a stone pump house on the bund was used for drinking water supply. HYDRAA would seek the assistance of European experts to restore the damaged heritage pump house, Mr. Ranganath said. A ring bund would also be developed around the lake.

‘Most of the encroachments overs 150 acres removed’

The lake is spread over nearly 500 acres, of which about 150 acres had been identified as encroachments. Most of these had already been removed, he said. However, houses that existed before the formation of HYDRAA on July 19, 2024, would not be demolished. Those losing plots or land in approved layouts would be eligible for Transferable Development Rights (TDR) as per rules.

A 10-metre buffer zone would be considered to protect the main bund and surrounding areas. Measures concerning temples and other structures below the bund would be taken keeping flood risks in view, he said, adding that the works were aimed at environmental protection, public safety and development of water resources.

The agency said it aimed to complete the works required to store water before the next monsoon and undertake the overall development of the lake within a year.

World.title: Who is Jensen Huang and how the timeline of spy scandal unfolded
World.content:
Jensen Huang resigned as Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), bringing an end to his 33-year stint at the helm of the artificial intelligence giant he co-founded, following revelations of his extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China.

Nvidia and Mr. Huang, are also facing a proposed class-action lawsuit that accuses them of misleading shareholders by failing to disclose Mr. Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang, who has been linked to Chinese intelligence.

The complaint, filed in a U.S. federal court in San Jose, California, on November 9, 2026, alleges that Nvidia and Mr. Huang concealed the relationship and the national security concerns surrounding it. Shareholders contend that the alleged omission exposed the company to reputational and business risks.

Who is Jensen Huang?

Sixty-three-year-old Taiwan-born Mr. Huang has led U.S. chipmaker Nvidia for more than three decades, transforming it into what is arguably the world’s most influential technology company. He is now at the centre of a controversy stemming from his alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based firm Megaspeed and an alleged Chinese spy.

Mr. Huang was born on February 17, 1963, in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher. In 1968, his family moved to Thailand before relocating to the United States amid the Vietnam War, according to Graphics News. He graduated in electrical engineering from Oregon State University and later obtained a master’s degree from Stanford University, according to his Linkedin profile.

Jensen Huang timeline (according to Graphics News)

February 17, 1963: Jensen Huang is born in Taiwan, the second son of a chemical engineer and a schoolteacher.

1968: His family moves to Thailand before relocating to the United States during the Vietnam War.

1970s: He spends part of his childhood at a boarding school in Kentucky before moving to Oregon, where he develops an interest in computing.

1984: Graduates with a degree in electrical engineering from Oregon State University.

1984-1992: Completes a master’s degree at Stanford University.

1993: Co-founds Nvidia with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. He becomes chief executive officer as the company enters the computer gaming market with an initial capital of $40,000.

1999: Nvidia goes public. The launch of the GeForce 256, promoted as the world’s first GPU, establishes the company as a major force in the technology industry.

2006: Under Mr. Huang’s leadership, Nvidia introduces CUDA technology, enabling graphics processors to handle complex computing tasks beyond gaming and helping lay the groundwork for the AI revolution.

2022: The launch of ChatGPT triggers a sharp rise in demand for advanced AI processors.

2024: The boom in generative AI drives Nvidia’s rapid expansion, with Mr. Huang’s net worth surpassing $100 billion.

Spy scandal timeline

2024-2025: Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are reportedly seen together at several industry events in Taipei.

2026: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio sends a memo warning Trump administration officials about the Nvidia chief executive’s relationship with Alice Huang.

October 29, 2026: The New York Times reports that U.S. authorities investigated Alice Huang over suspicions that she passed intelligence to Beijing and helped circumvent U.S. restrictions on advanced AI chips.

November 5, 2026: Senior U.S. lawmakers seek a closed-door briefing from Jensen Huang over potential national security concerns.

November 8, 2026: Mr. Huang admits he was “unfaithful” to his wife. Nvidia announces an independent investigation into the espionage allegations.

November 9, 2026: Nvidia shares fall by more than 4%. U.S. President Donald Trump says the FBI is investigating the controversy involving Mr. Huang and Alice Huang.

November 12, 2026: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia.

The Jensen-Alice saga

Mr. Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife but did not disclose details about the alleged relationship with Ms. Alice Huang. The Nvidia chief executive said he was “deeply sorry” for the affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did,” he said in a statement posted on Nvidia’s website.

The New York Times reported that Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen allegedly recruited by Beijing to gather intelligence on Mr. Huang.

Mr. Huang also sent a message to Nvidia employees on November 8, 2026, acknowledging the affair and apologising to both his family and company staff. While expressing regret for his actions, he did not address allegations that Alice Huang was a suspected spy.

The Times reported last month that U.S. intelligence agencies had concluded that Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and chip buyer, and alleged that she was providing information directly to Beijing.

Nvidia announced a probe into the matter on November 8, 2026. Independent directors have engaged external legal counsel to examine the circumstances surrounding the relationship. Nvidia’s board said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised, and that Mr. Huang would remain in charge while cooperating with the investigation.

Who is Alice Huang?

Ms. Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who was allegedly recruited by Beijing to collect intelligence on the Nvidia chief executive, according to The New York Times, which first reported that Mr. Huang was the target of an alleged espionage operation.

Few public details are available about Ms. Huang, also known as Huang Le. She reportedly held a senior position at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed International.

Despite sharing the same surname, Ms. Alice Huang is not related to the 63-year-old Nvidia chief executive.

An online search revealed a brief profile of Alice Huang, including her photograph, on a Chinese fund database. The profile listed previous roles at HSBC and as a reporter for Chinese media organisations CCTV and Hunan TV. However, AFP said it could not independently verify the contents of the profile or determine who created it, though it had contacted the organisations mentioned.

Singapore firm under scrutiny

Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based cloud computing company, has come under scrutiny following the allegations.

According to its website, Megaspeed is an Nvidia cloud partner in the Asia-Pacific region and a core business partner in Nvidia’s cloud computing ecosystem. The Times reported that Megaspeed purchased more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years.

Washington has restricted exports of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China, citing national security concerns. The measures are also seen as part of broader efforts to maintain a technological advantage in the field of artificial intelligence.

The New York Times reported that the U.S. government has been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over concerns that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to China.

An AFP report quoting a 2025 Bloomberg News report said that Singaporean authorities were investigating Megaspeed over allegations that Nvidia chips had been smuggled into China. AFP reported that Megaspeed rejected the claims in December that year, saying Bloomberg’s reporting “contains misleading information and incorrect insinuations, including suggestions that we may have been involved in illegal chip transfers”.

The allegations involving Ms. Alice Huang, combined with concerns surrounding the movement of advanced chips, have fuelled speculation about Megaspeed’s possible role in the transfer of restricted technology to China.

Importance of Nvidia chips

Nvidia designs advanced processors originally developed to render 3D graphics in video games. Known as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), these chips can process enormous amounts of data and are widely used to train and run artificial intelligence systems.

The launch of ChatGPT in 2022 highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence and triggered a surge in investment, with governments and technology companies racing to develop the technology further.

Washington has banned exports of Nvidia’s most advanced Blackwell and Rubin GPUs to China, citing national security concerns and the potential military applications of advanced AI.

Scandal to access AI chips?

Access to Nvidia’s GPUs has become increasingly difficult for Chinese companies since 2022 as the United States tightened controls on advanced semiconductor exports. The policy is also intended to help leading U.S. AI firms maintain their global advantage.

A major step came in October 2022, when the U.S. Commerce Department prohibited sales of Nvidia’s A100 and H100 chips to China. Nvidia subsequently developed modified versions, the A800 and H800, for the Chinese market.

Washington later imposed restrictions on the A800 and H800 as well, prompting Nvidia to develop the H20 chip to comply with revised thresholds. Each new restriction was followed by an alternative product, which in turn prompted further regulatory measures.

The Trump administration introduced licensing requirements for H20 sales in April 2025 before easing the restrictions a few months later. Nvidia and AMD subsequently agreed to provide 15% of their China-related revenue to the U.S. government, an arrangement that has drawn scrutiny within the United States.

China rejects allegations

Meanwhile, China has dismissed all allegations. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on November 9, 2026, that “the so-called Chinese spy allegation is unsubstantiated. It is nothing but smears against China”.

State-run Global Times said, “Whenever China-U.S. relations begin to improve, there are often those firing shots from the shadows.”

China had earlier denied a New York Times report that stated Mr. Huang had developed a close relationship with Ms. Alice Huang, who operated a company accused of helping move advanced chips into China and was allegedly acting on behalf of Beijing.

FBI probe

The controversy has also drawn scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over the distribution of advanced artificial intelligence chips and the possibility that restricted technology may have reached China through third countries.

Democratic members of the House Foreign Affairs Committee have sought answers from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding the administration’s export policies, while Republican lawmakers have requested a closed-door briefing with Mr. Huang.

U.S. President Donald Trump said on November 9, 2026, that the FBI was investigating Mr. Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese government agent, but added that he did not believe the Nvidia chief executive had reason for concern.

“I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he’ll be in good shape,” Mr. Trump said at a White House briefing.

“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right, how you’re doing,” Mr. Trump said. “He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy.”

World.title: Telangana approves 2,000 affordable houses for auto-rickshaw workers in & around Hyderabad
World.content:
Telangana government approved a proposal for taking up an affordable housing scheme exclusively for auto-rickshaw workers, in four areas in and around Hyderabad, on the lines of affordable flats at Indiramma Housing towers in Core Urban Region Economy (CURE).

Permission was given for construction of a total of 2,000 Economically Weaker Section (EWS) houses, with 500 each in Bandlaguda (LIG Colony) in Nagole; Gandamguda; Petbasheerbad and Jalpally or Laxmiguda. The societies would be titled ‘Auto Nagar Colony’, as per a government order (G.O.) issued on Friday (November 13, 2026).

Location Number of EWS flats Bandlaguda (LIG Colony) 500 Gandamguda 500 Petbasheerbad 500 Jalpally or Laxmiguda 500

The State Housing Board was cleared to adopt the same guidelines, beneficiary eligibility criteria, financial assistance, reservation provisions, selection and allotment procedures and other conditions applicable to Indiramma Indlu, with a specific condition that the beneficiaries shall be auto-rickshaw workers.

The Board would take up the scheme with an indicative project cost of ₹22 crore. It was directed to submit necessary detailed project reports and finance proposals after verification of land availability, site suitability and technical feasibility.

World.title: Not 'Amrit Kaal', but 'mehengaai ka bhuchaal': Congress takes dig at Modi government
World.content:
The Congress on Friday (November 13, 2026) took a swipe at the Modi government over rising prices of essential commodities and said this was not an 'Amrit Kaal' but 'mehengaai ka bhuchaal' (earthquake of inflation).

Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh shared media reports on X claiming that people were grappling with rising inflation and a sharp increase in the prices of food and beverages.

In a post in Hindi, Mr. Ramesh said, "Under the Modi government, inflation is no longer just a 'daayan'; it has now become an uninvited guest, devouring every household's budget."

From the kitchen to every other daily necessity, prices have spiralled out of control, he claimed.

"The Modi government's misguided policies have broken the backs of ordinary people. Inflation has been rising for the past 12 years, and its real impact is far greater than government statistics suggest," Mr. Ramesh said.

"But this year, even those figures have been rising every month. Retail inflation has reached a two-year high of 6.09%. What is surprising is that inflation has risen in 11 of the 12 consumption categories, yet the arrogant 'pravachan mantri' has remained silent about his government's performance," he said,

"Food inflation has reached 8.94%. Onions have become 116% more expensive, garlic 60%, and ginger 48%. Inflation is running rampant across everything, from flour, oil, ghee, milk and lentils to soap. Besides raising prices, companies are considering reducing product quantities," Mr. Ramesh said.

Now there are also fears of interest rate hikes, which would make both borrowing and living even more expensive for ordinary people, he said.

"This is not an Amrit Kaal; it is 'mehengaai ka bhuchaal' ( earthquake of inflation)," Mr. Ramesh said.

The Congress on Thursday (November 12, 2026) launched an attack on the Modi government over rising prices of essential commodities, saying households are struggling with mounting expenses and demanding effective measures to control inflation.

World.title: PM Shehbaz hopes Pakistan will become world's 6th largest economy 'earlier than 2050'
World.content:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday expressed hope that Pakistan could become the world’s sixth-largest economy “earlier than 2050”.

The premier made the remarks while addressing the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 (PMIF26) in Islamabad, where delegations, exhibitors and attendees have arrived from across the world to attend the event.

As the two-day event opened on Thursday, Pakistan showcased its vast mineral resources, ranging from coal and salt to gold and critical minerals, to attract international investment, promising predictable, investor-friendly policies, institutional support and security.

PM Shehbaz recalled a Goldman Sachs assessment, which had projected Pakistan to become the sixth-largest economy in the world by 2075 and said: “I would like to make a small amendment here — instead of 2075, it will be earlier than 2050.”

Earlier in the day, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik addressed the forum and stated that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were increasingly focused on minerals that were of strategic importance to global investors.

In continuation of the pitch, Malik told the investors that Pakistan’s exploration efforts were being complemented with “modern geochemical and geophysical surveys, exploratory drilling, and upgrading of our geoscience advanced research laboratories with sophisticated analytical technologies”.

Here, he particularly mentioned the exploration of copper and gold in Chagai and western Balochistan to lithium, tin and tungsten in Gilgit-Baltistan and antimony and base metals in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

He said Pakistan had been exporting raw ore and importing the finished products to meet its requirements for a long time.

“We are now advancing copper smelting to capture more of the value chain from the mine to the finished metal,” he added.

The minister said Pakistan was also strengthening the scientific foundation of its mineral sector through the Geological Survey of Pakistan.

“The government’s accelerated geological mapping programme, including detailed surveys at a scale of 1:50,000, is helping identify mineral prospects across the country.”

The minister further said that through international technical cooperation, including the UK Pakistan Geoscience Capacity Building Programme, “we are strengthening expertise in digital mapping, airborne surveys and mineral assessment”.

“We are also digitising decades of geological information to give investors greater access to reliable data, reduce exploration uncertainty, and enable informed investment decisions,” he continued.

The petroleum minister highlighted that discovering a mineral deposit was only the initial stage and a commercially viable mine required, electricity water, roads, railways and access to international markets.

“That is why infrastructure development is aligned with our mineral ambitions,” he explained. In this context, he described the planned upgrade of the Rohri-Nokundi railway corridor, connectivity to Port Qasim and the development of supporting infrastructure around Reko Diq as “important steps” towards connecting Pakistan’s mineral-rich regions with the global markets around the world.

He said, “Our objective is very clear: to build not just individual mines, but an integrated, competitive and sustainable mineral industry.

“Where it is commercially and technically viable, we want investment to support processing, refining, downstream industry, technology transfer and integration into the global value chains.

“We want this industry to build Pakistani capability as it grows through technical skills, vocational training, engineering services, a stronger base for Pakistani suppliers and real career opportunities for young people, including women entering the sector for the first time.”

But, he contended, not of this would hold together without the communities in our producing regions. “Projects that earn the trust of the communities around them are, in our experience, the projects that actually get built and sustain.”

World.title: IHC suspends local government elections in Islamabad
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Friday suspended the upcoming local government elections in the federal capital, putting the Election Commission of Pakistan’s (ECP) latest election schedule on hold until the next hearing.

Last week, a writ petition was filed by Chaudhry Amjad Ali, who had challenged the ECP’s short order and the subsequent election schedule, both dated Oct 21, 2026, for holding local government elections in the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT).

He argued that the polls, scheduled for Dec 20, could not be held until the legal status of the existing constituency delimitation was conclusively determined.

A single-member bench comprising Justice Umair Majeed Malik granted the interim relief while hearing the writ petition on Friday.

“Operation of the impugned order dated Oct 21, 2026, and the impugned election schedule dated Oct 21, 2026, as revised by the Election Commission, shall remain suspended until the next date of hearing,” the court order read.

The court also issued notices to the respondents, directing them to submit their reports and para-wise comments before the next hearing, scheduled for Nov 26, 2026.

Advocate Barrister Qazi Adil Aziz appeared for the petitioner, along with Malik Talha and Muhammad Yaseen Iqbal.

They argued that under Articles 140-A(2), 218(3) and 219(d) of the Constitution, the ECP was “duty-bound to hold local government elections honestly, justly, fairly and in accordance with the law”.

The counsel contended that the election programme had become legally compromised due to legislative changes between the original Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Act, 2015 (LG Act 2015), and the subsequent Islamabad Capital Territory Local Government Ordinance, 2026 (LG Ordinance 2026).

According to the petition, the LG Act 2015 provided for one Metropolitan Corporation and 125 Union Councils, each divided into nine wards. The delimitation process for this structure began in December 2024, and an election programme was issued on Dec 26, 2025, but was subsequently withdrawn.

Meanwhile, the LG Ordinance 2026 altered the capital’s local government structure by introducing three Town Corporations, changing the process for constituting and delimiting Union Councils, removing the nine-ward structure and providing for delimitation on the basis of census blocks. Consequently, the number of Union Councils increased from 125 to 130.

The counsel submitted that the ECP subsequently issued revised delimitation timelines on Aug 25, 2026, and completed the process with the publication of the final list of 130 Union Councils on Oct 14, 2026.

However, after a single 120-day extension, the LG Ordinance 2026 ceased to have effect under Article 89 of the Constitution, resulting in the revival of the original LG Act 2015. At this point, the counsel argued, the ECP suddenly issued the impugned order and election schedule to conduct polls under the original LG Act 2015.

The petitioner’s counsel contended that the impugned order did not address the delimitation of the 125 Union Councils, their nine wards or the Metropolitan Corporation under the revived law. They argued that the delimitation carried out under the amended law could not serve as the basis for elections under the revived LG Act 2015.

They therefore maintained that fresh delimitation and preparation of electoral rolls in accordance with the LG Act 2015 and the Elections Act, 2017, were necessary before the elections could lawfully be held.

The counsel further argued that holding elections without completing the required delimitation would violate Article 218(3) of the Constitution and the electoral framework under the LG Act 2015 and the Elections Act, besides resulting in unnecessary expenditure of public funds.

After hearing the initial arguments, the court observed that the points raised required consideration and suspended the operation of the ECP’s order and election schedule until the next hearing, scheduled for Nov 26.

On Thursday, Chief Election Commissioner CEC Sikandar Sultan Raja accused the federal government of trying to sabotage the local government elections in Islamabad.

The local government elections in Islamabad have faced numerous delays and postponements since the term of the last local government expired in February 2021.

The ECP has issued multiple schedules, only to cancel them later for various reasons, including legislative changes and court orders.

The delimitation of constituencies and union councils was carried out six times, while the election schedule was issued four times.

The ECP had decided that, since the local government law enacted in 2015 was still in force, elections would be held under the Act. This meant polls would be held in 50 constituencies, after which the mayor and deputy mayors would be elected.

After the completion of various stages of the electoral process, it had decided that polling would be held on Dec 20. The ECP had reserved four days, from December 21 to 24, for the consolidation of results.

World.title: Babar Azam fails again with Pakistan 151-5 in first Sri Lanka Test
World.content:
Babar Azam’s century drought continued as Sri Lanka pushed hard for victory over Pakistan in the weather-hit first Test in Rawalpindi on Friday.

The tourists took four wickets in bad light in the morning as Pakistan reached 151-5 at lunch on the fifth and final day, leading by 139 runs with five wickets in hand.

At the break Saud Shakeel was unbeaten on 23 and Ghazi Ghori seven not out after a 20-minute break due to bad light halted Sri Lanka’s push for a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

Babar fell to a leg-side trap, handing the short square-leg fielder a simple catch off fast bowler Milan Rathnayaka for 34, making it a 42nd innings without a Test century.

Salman Ali Agha too fell in the same manner off Rathnayaka for 13, leaving Pakistan struggling on 125-5.

Earlier, Sri Lanka struck with the first ball of the day when Lahiru Kumara dismissed Azan Awais for 22 at Pakistan’s overnight total of 57.

Next over Asitha Fernando made it 57-3 with Mohammad Taha caught behind for 24.

Sri Lanka could have had Azam on 22 but Kamindu Mendis spilled a simple chance off Fernando as the Pakistan skipper failed to get an advantage.

Babar hit six fours and added 50 for the fourth wicket with Saud before playing a loose shot.

Fernando has taken 2-20 and Rathnayaka 2-32.

World.title: Islamabad to become country's first fully cashless city by year-end
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The government has decided to make the federal capital the country’s first fully cashless city, setting Dec 31 as the deadline for the transition.

The decision was taken at an important meeting on the Cashless Capital project chaired by State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudry, in Islamabad on Friday, according to an official statement by the Ministry of Interior on X.

Speaking on the occasion, Chaudhry said consultation and suggestions from all stakeholders were important for the success of the project, the statement said.

“The implementation of the project is under way at a fast pace on the special instructions of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi,” Chaudhry was quoted as saying.

Naqvi had promised the prime minister that Islamabad would be made Pakistan’s first cashless city and the world’s first cashless capital, the state minister added.

“After Nov 30, no cash payment will be accepted in any department of the Islamabad Capital Territory administration and the Capital Development Authority (CDA),” Chaudhry stated.

“The target is to bring all merchants in Islamabad into the cashless system by Dec 31,” he said.

He said the cashless system would improve financial transparency, tax monitoring and the transaction system, adding that 26,000 merchants in Islamabad had already been connected to the digital payments system.

“Digital payment facilities will be provided at every level, from street vendors to major business centres,” the state minister affirmed.

“All relevant institutions will work together to make Islamabad a modern digital city.”

According to the statement, CDA Chairman Sohail Ashraf, representatives of the banking sector and other senior officials attended the meeting.

Representatives of the banking sector appreciated the government’s Cashless Islamabad initiative and assured full cooperation for its success, it added.

The prime minister has repeatedly emphasised the need to implement digital transaction systems across the country, insisting that it is vital to bring transparency to the economy.

In a meeting last week, PM Shehbaz also directed authorities to prepare a “clear roadmap and time-bound targets” for establishing a 100 per cent digital payments system in the country.

“Promoting a cashless economy is one of the government’s top priorities, with its positive results already beginning to emerge,” PM Shehbaz said.

He was also apprised that the work on the digitisation of payments in all federal and provincial government institutions was progressing rapidly, and payments in “most institutions” would be fully digitised by December 2026.

World.title: Copper, gold deposits identified at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district: mining company
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Mining company National Resources Limited (NRL) on Friday announced that it had identified copper and gold deposits at eight sites in Balochistan’s Chagai district, following nearly 25,000 metres of drilling that yielded encouraging results.

The company is now moving towards its first estimate of the area’s mineral resources.

One of the drill holes revealed a 295-metre stretch of mineral deposits containing 0.43 per cent copper and 0.13 grams of gold per tonne. Within this, a 132-metre section showed a higher copper concentration of 0.83pc, National Resources Limited Chairman Muhammad Ali Tabba told the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026.

The discoveries cover an area of 5.6 square kilometres in Darigwan, adjoining the company’s earlier discovery at the Tang Kaur copper-gold site. Tabba said further exploration at the exploration licence EL214 was expected to help establish the size of the mineral deposits, subject to the completion of exploration work and a formal assessment of the resources.

A joint venture between Fatima Fertilisers, Liberty Mills and Lucky Cement Ltd, NRL holds five exploration licences in Balochistan. These comprise two copper-gold projects, one lead-zinc project and two antimony projects, with exploration work under way.

NRL plans to begin environmental, hydrogeological, metallurgical and geotechnical studies in 2027, with the aim of completing a bankable feasibility study by the end of the decade.

Tabba reaffirmed NRL’s previously announced commitment of $100 million to mineral exploration in Pakistan and invited domestic and international investors and service providers to explore emerging opportunities.

Although preliminary resource estimates have been prepared by an independent consultant, the company is withholding their release pending compliance with international reporting requirements. NRL is working towards completing its maiden mineral resource estimate in line with international standards.

The company has also partnered with the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS) to develop a predictive artificial intelligence model aimed at accelerating exploration, using geological modelling and data gathered through its drilling programme.

“Our ambition is to build a world-class mineral exploration platform and contribute to an integrated mineral value chain, spanning discovery, mining, processing and further value addition,” Tabba said.

He said the programme was helping develop local expertise, with Baloch geologists working alongside international consultants and Pakistani contractors carrying out inclined drilling.

The company’s technical workforce is almost entirely local, supporting its ambition to build domestic expertise that could also contribute to international exploration projects.

Alongside its exploration programme, NRL is supporting education and community development through the newly established Chagai Foundation. Tabba urged industrialists, investors and corporate partners to contribute to its vision of “Enabling Balochistan”.

“The people of Balochistan must share in the opportunities created by their mineral wealth,” he said.

World.title: Short-term inflation clocks in at 11.21pc
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose to 11.21 per cent year-on-year in the week ending on Nov 12, driven largely by perishable food products, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics (PBS) on Friday.

The index, comprising 51 items, whose prices are collected from 50 markets in 17 cities, is calculated weekly to track changes in the prices of essential commodities and services.

The data showed that of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, the prices of 19 commodities (37.25pc) increased, while those of 9 items (17.65pc) declined. Meanwhile, the prices of 23 items (45.10pc) remained unchanged from the previous week.

Short-term inflation has remained in the double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely on the back of persistent increases in petroleum and diesel prices. However, the oil prices have been slowly declining for the past three consecutive days.

The impact of this decline will be visible in the next review. However, the unprecedented increase in the LPG price caused short-term inflation to rise.

The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly declined by 0.46pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items.

The surge in energy costs is not only fuelling inflationary pressures, but also indirectly boosting sales tax collections through higher prices of goods and services.

This is an example of cost-push inflation, in which rising energy costs lead to increases in food prices. As a result, households are facing mounting pressure from higher consumer prices.

The items that recorded the highest price increases over the previous week included tomatoes (12.06pc), eggs (5.98pc), potatoes (2.42pc), garlic (1.76pc), chicken (1.32pc), firewood (1.10pc), wheat flour (0.94pc), pulse masoor (0.64pc), beef (0.47pc), and LPG (0.30pc).

The items that recorded week-on-week price declines included petrol (7.42pc), diesel (6.10pc), onions (1.70pc), bananas (1.03pc), gur (0.59pc), sugar (0.43pc), powdered milk (0.36pc), pulse moong (0.32pc) and pulse gram (0.08pc).

On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included LPG (111.35pc), tomatoes (78.94pc), electricity for Q1 (52.38pc), wheat flour (36.14pc), diesel (30.77pc), petrol (26.23pc), onions (19.67pc), chilies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.67pc), bread plain (12.35pc), beef (11.30pc) and chicken (10.98pc).

In contrast, potato prices fell by 36.41pc, followed by sugar (24.54pc), eggs (23.29pc), salt powder (12.51pc), pulse masoor (7.21pc), pulse moong (6.83pc), gur (6.63pc) and bananas (3.35pc).

Last week, short-term inflation rose to 12.31pc year-on-year driven largely by LPG and perishable food products.

World.title: Delhi overtakes Lahore as world's most polluted major city as air quality deteriorates
World.content:
India’s capital, Delhi, overtook Lahore to become the world’s most polluted city on Friday, with air quality reaching hazardous levels and visibility dropping as smog blanketed the city of 20 million people.

Earlier, Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) stood at 334, categorised as “hazardous”, making it the most polluted major city globally, according to Swiss air quality monitoring group IQAir, which measures pollution levels based on the concentration of pollutants. An AQI reading of up to 50 is considered good, indicating little or no health risk.

India’s official Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), meanwhile, recorded a higher AQI of 403 in Delhi and classified the air quality as “severe”.

The difference between the Swiss and Indian readings is due to the different AQI scales and methodologies used to calculate and classify air pollution levels.

According to IQAir’s hourly readings, Delhi’s AQI had dropped to 208 by 11am PKT. At the time, Lahore was ranked seventh among the world’s most polluted major cities, with an AQI of 155.

In Delhi, cars and motorcycles emerged from dense smog, which also appeared to obscure street lights on the city’s main roads, videos from news agency ANI showed.

Pollution is a seasonal problem in many parts of northern Pakistan and India, as the cold, heavy air of winter traps vehicle emissions, construction dust and smoke from agricultural burning.

Friday’s readings marked a drop in Lahore’s pollution levels after the city had ranked as the most polluted major city in the world for several days in a row.

Earlier this week, Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration was eight times the World Health Organisation’s (WHO) guideline value, according to a report by the Pakistan Air Quality Initiative (PAQI).

The report, released on Tuesday, said the number of likely crop-residue fires in Punjab, Pakistan, remained almost unchanged from the corresponding period last year.

Lahore’s average PM2.5 concentration stood at 126 micrograms per cubic metre during the period, exceeding the 24-hour National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) on all 40 days for which valid data were available. The average was 11pc lower than in the corresponding period in 2025.

Satellite instruments detected 18,825 fires across Punjab, Pakistan, 89 per cent of which were classified as likely crop-residue burning. The highest daily count was recorded on Nov 1, with 1,102 detections.

The 24-hour National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) were exceeded on all 40 days for which valid data were available. The average concentration was 11pc lower than during the corresponding period in 2025.

However, the report cautioned that the association did not establish the precise contribution of crop-residue burning to urban pollution, as stagnant weather conditions and reduced atmospheric dispersion also contributed to the accumulation of pollutants.

EPA intensifies action

After Lahore’s air quality improved on Friday, Punjab Environment Protection Agency (EPA) spokesperson Sajjad Bashir outlined actions that he said had been intensified against major sources of pollution.

He said authorities had intensified action against polluting industries and brick kilns, agricultural residue burning, smoky vehicles and open burning of waste.

The spokesperson said comparative data for the period between Jan 1 and Nov 10 this year showed a “substantial increase” in inspections, regulatory action and financial penalties against polluting industries and brick kilns compared to the corresponding period last year.

Brick kiln inspections increased from 37,838 in 2025 to 80,594 during this period while authorities demolished 1,372 kilns during the current year against 1,223 last year. Moreover, 864 kilns were sealed for violations this year. Financial penalties, meanwhile, increased to Rs163.35 million compared to Rs156.05m in 2025, he added.

Industrial inspections rose from 38,098 in 2025 to 47,643 in 2026 for the period between Jan 1 and Nov 10 while 1,419 industrial units were sealed and fines totalling Rs216.98m were imposed, more than double the Rs101.41m imposed during the corresponding period in 2025.

The department also instensified action against prohibited plastic material, with confiscations rising to 438,159 kilogrammes from 378,630kg last year.

Fines imposed in cases involving prohibited plastic materials also increased to Rs34.21m from approximately Rs7.63m in 2025, according to the comparative figures.
