World.title: ‘Sisters, Stand Up!’ A Bar’s Urinals for Women Make a Splash in China
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019249/‘Sisters, Stand Up!’ A Bar’s Urinals for Women Make a Splash in China
World.content:
“Sisters, stand up!” reads a slogan written in pink on the mirror above three pink-and-white urinals. Alongside each sits a stack of disposable paper funnels, waiting for those willing to heed the call.

The scene, reportedly captured in the women’s restroom of a bar in China’s eastern city of Wuxi, began circulating online last week, sparking debate and prompting a related hashtag to garner over 54 million views on microblogging platform Weibo as of Tuesday.

“I stood there in disbelief for two minutes, thinking I’d walked into the wrong restroom,” one user wrote on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote, attaching photos of the urinals. “I kept checking until a cleaner confirmed it was indeed the women’s restroom.”

The user, a Wuxi resident in her 30s surnamed Shi, told domestic media she was unsure how to use the urinals as there were no instructions nearby. She said she eventually opted for a traditional squat toilet in the same restroom instead because she worried about making a mess or soiling her clothes.

“I’d actually love to try this,” one commenter wrote. “In winter, it’s a hassle to squat with all those thick, long layers on, especially when you’re also carrying a bag.”

“Better yet, let the brothers sit down,” read another comment, which received nearly 1,400 likes.

On Tuesday, a woman surnamed Tang, who runs Gungun Folk Theater, the bar where the urinals were reportedly installed, told domestic media that they were intended for women who find it difficult to squat, including those wearing long dresses or with limited mobility. “We just wanted to make things easier and give women another option,” she said.

Studies suggest that standing to urinate may be easier for pregnant women and those with knee osteoarthritis, while standing, crouching, and sitting have been found to make no significant difference to bladder emptying in healthy women.

Standing urinals are increasingly common worldwide at music festivals to save space and reduce restroom queues, and at outdoor activities where toilets are scarce.

In China, efforts to introduce standing urinals for women reportedly date back to 2004. At that time, Ye Ganlin, a retired senior engineer, spent 10,000 yuan ($1,400) developing a portable standing urinal for all genders, and offered free disposable funnels to female users. She said the idea grew out of her own experience with a spinal condition that made squatting increasingly difficult as she aged.

Her toilet was tested in busy public areas of neighboring cities Xi’an and Xianyang, in the northwestern Shaanxi province, and reportedly drew around 200 users a day. However, women were in the minority, Ye said.

In 2010, Shaanxi Normal University, also in Xi’an, installed six standing urinals for women, an initiative championed by professor Qu Yajun to conserve water. Female students welcomed the idea but said it would take practice to get used to the fixtures.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: Urinals installed in a women’s restroom at a bar in Wuxi, Jiangsu province, October 2026. From Weibo)

World.title: Collage: Robots, Health and New Tech at China Expo
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019251/Collage: Robots, Health and New Tech at China Expo
World.content:
SHANGHAI — The ninth China International Import Expo ran from Nov. 5 to 10, with 4,142 overseas exhibitors from 162 countries, regions and international organizations.

More than 480 exhibits made global, Asian or Chinese debuts. Qualcomm brought a 6G terminal prototype out of the lab. Medtronic’s China-developed Kanghui orthopedic surgical robot had its world premiere. And a rare type of durian tree fruit, the Malaysian white durian, made its global debut.

Robots at the expo could be found working hotel front desks, taking photos for visitors, and running booth demos on their own — visibly more advanced than in past years. In place of the mechanical arm designed to play ping-pong featured last year, at this year’s expo, a company debuted an entire humanoid robot playing the sport. At the forum held alongside the expo, Xiong Jijun, Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology, said humanoid robots must be upgraded from performing simple actions to being “able to think and work.”

Sixth Tone photographers spent the week in the halls, capturing the new products, technologies and services on display.

(Header image: CIIE attendees play table tennis against a robotic opponent, Shanghai, Nov. 9, 2026. All photos by Wu Huiyuan/Sixth Tone)

World.id: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019240/From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
World.title: From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
World.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019240/From 6G to Aerospace, New Tech Takes the Stage at CIIE
World.content:
The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) closed in Shanghai on Tuesday after showcasing cutting-edge technologies in artificial intelligence, commercial aerospace, and innovative drugs.

The six-day event drew exhibitors from a record 162 countries, regions, and international organizations. A total of 4,142 overseas companies took part — also a record high — with more than 480 representative products making their global, Asian, or China debut.

U.S. wireless chipmaker Qualcomm exhibited the world’s first 6G terminal prototype — the first time the device has been shown publicly outside the lab. The prototype has been used in joint tests with China Mobile, China’s largest telecom operator, and Chinese telecom equipment manufacturer ZTE. The prototype will provide the foundation for 6G chips and support the technology’s commercial rollout.

The event featured an expanded medical devices and health care exhibition area, acting as the stage for the China debut of pharmaceutical giant AstraZeneca’s new hypertension medication baxdrostat. The oral medication works by inhibiting the enzyme aldosterone synthase, which helps synthesize the blood pressure-regulating hormone aldosterone, and was approved in the U.S. in May.

German optical giant Zeiss also made its global debut of its new non-spherical lens PT Lunana, designed for myopia correction. Novartis, a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical company, showcased ianalumab, a drug used for treating the autoimmune illness Sjögren’s disease — also a China debut.

American electric vehicle company Tesla presented its Cybercab autonomous vehicle. Lacking a steering wheel or pedals, the vehicle relies on cameras and AI to drive. Hexagon — a global digital reality and metrology tech company — also displayed its industrial humanoid robot AEON.

Aerospace technology was also present, including the Zhuque-3 rocket developed by Chinese commercial aerospace company LandSpace. The rocket’s reusable booster, which uses liquid oxygen and methane as fuel, can land vertically, first achieved by the company in August.

Beyond showcasing new tech, the expo held its first exhibition area for 100 long-established, reputable international brands — from Canadian shoe companies to Spanish wineries — as well as hosted a trade and investment “matchmaking” conference, where companies and buyers met to sign cooperation agreements. The latter conference attracted more than 600 exhibitors and over 2,000 buyers from 59 countries and regions.

The deals reached at this year’s expo are projected to be worth a total of $85.45 billion over the coming year, up 2.3% from last year and a record high.

Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

(Header image: A view of the China International Import Expo in Shanghai, Nov. 6, 2026. Wu Huiyuan/Sixth Tone)

World.title: Philippines, UAE go after Filipino visa scammers
World.content:
ASSURANCE. Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac tells Filipino household service workers during a get-together in Dubai on November 7, 2026, that there are legal services and funds available to them.

The Philippines and UAE are collaborating to pursue visa scammers who duped hundreds of OFWs. The two countries also roll out new digital recruitment systems.

DUBAI, UAE – The Philippines’ Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) is working with the United Arab Emirates’ Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MOHRE) to go after the Filipinos who allegedly victimized fellow Filipinos seeking freelance visas.

“We have coordination with the host government in running after the scammers, protecting victimized visa scams as well as cooperation with respect to addressing and finding those who prey upon OFWs,” DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac told overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) in Dubai on November 7.

Cacdac was in Dubai until November 8 for the fourth Serbisyo Caravan of government agencies to provide one-stop services for OFWs, and for the Salamat Kabayan early Christmas celebration for household service workers.

Rappler earlier reported that two Filipinos — Junie Sorsano, a prominent Dubai-based content creator for over a decade, and Ryan Ronel Baco — allegedly duped some 400 overseas Filipino workers of AED 3.6 million (around P62 million) in visa facilitation.

The victims were mostly domestic helpers, caregivers, and retail sales staff, who sought freelance visas to legally pursue independent, self-sponsored employment.

Cacdac said he had raised the issue during a meeting with MOHRE head Dr. Abdulrahman Abdulmannan Al Awar.

“We have stronger cooperation now,” Cacdac said, noting this was his fourth meeting with Al Awar this year.

“If the alleged visa scammers have already fled UAE and are hiding in the Philippines, we will also talk to the DOJ, to Secretary [Fredderick] Vida about this matter and determine what charges can be filed against them,” he added.

He highlighted that victims can access MWO’s legal services and action fund.

“Rest assured, we have the legal services of our legal retainer that will help victims and in coordination with MOHRE on this issue. We may also tap the action fund on this,” the DMW secretary said.

He urged OFWs to consult the MWO to avoid scams.

Digitalized

Cacdac also signed an agreement with DataFlow Group to pilot the Digital Recruitment and Employer Accreditation Management (DREAM) System, an online platform allowing UAE employers, principals, and recruitment agencies to submit documents and pay fees digitally.

Designed to cut processing time and costs, the system complements MWO Dubai’s Online Employment Contract Verification System (OECVS), which has verified over 100,000 contracts since July 2025.

“Our 20 to 30 people at MWO will not anymore be sitting behind desks doing clerical or documentation work because these can now be done through the digitalized system, which means more of our people will be out there talking to the Filipino community, going to places where the Filipinos usually congregate visit hospitals, visit prisons to deploy legal services,” Cacdac explained.

Abu Dhabi Dialogue

Cacdac also discussed the upcoming Manila meeting of the Abu Dhabi Dialogue (ADD), which the Philippines will chair in 2027.

Established in 2008 as a voluntary consultative forum and currently chaired by Oman, ADD member states include the UAE, Philippines, Afghanistan, Bahrain, Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Kuwait, Malaysia, Nepal, Pakistan, and Qatar.

The 9th edition (2026–2027) will focus on Artificial Intelligence and digitalization.

Cacdac also visited Pinas Cargo, a logistics firm shipping care boxes to the Philippines, meeting with founder and CEO Marlyn Castro. (READ: Dubai OFWs pay it forward with scholarships for Filipinos back home) – Rappler.com

World.title: FACT CHECK: Old Remulla video misused to falsely claim Dela Rosa has no ICC warrant
World.content:
A January 2026 interview clip released months before the ICC unsealed the warrant recirculated on social media and was falsely presented as a current update on Dela Rosa’s arrest

Claim: Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said there is no arrest warrant against Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa.

Rating: FALSE

Why we fact-checked this: A reel posted on November 6 by the Facebook page “Pobre Nga Uyamot” shows an interview clip of Remulla with the overlaid text, “Klaro walang warrant (Clearly no warrant).”

Additional overlaid text read: “Walang kaso si Bato sa Pinas! Pag lumaban, mamatay pulis order sa taas ma-blame! High risk! Law of the land pa rin.”

(Bato has no case in the Philippines! If he fights back, police will die and whoever gave the order will be blamed! High risk! The law of the land still applies.)

In the clip, Remulla says: “Si Bato, ano hahanapin namin? ‘Di ba, alam naming nasa Davao siya. Pero wala naman kaming warrant of arrest. Wala. So bakit namin hahanapin? Ba’t namin aarestuhin? Kung gusto niya, siya [ang] mag-citizen’s arrest.”

(Why will we search for Bato? We know he’s in Davao, but we don’t have an arrest warrant. None. So why would we search for him? Why would we arrest him? If he wants to, let him make a citizen’s arrest.)

As of writing, the video has 2.5 million views, 15,000 reactions, 2,300 comments, and 3,400 shares.

The facts: The clip is old and was misleadingly presented as a current update on Dela Rosa’s status as a subject of an International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant.

The clip was from Remulla’s January 27, 2026 interview on ANC, during which he addressed former senator Antonio Trillanes IV’s suggestion to search for Dela Rosa, who at the time had not been attending Senate sessions amid rumors of an ICC warrant against him.

Remulla then made the remark shown in the Facebook reel, adding that he would personally go to Davao to fetch Dela Rosa. He also suggested that Trillanes could carry out a citizen’s arrest if such a warrant existed.

At the time Remulla said this, the ICC warrant had not been made public. The ICC’s records show it was issued as secret on November 6, 2025, and unsealed only on May 11, 2026, several months after the interview from which the clip was taken.

Dela Rosa is accused of murder for crimes against humanity involving at least 32 killings between July 2016 and April 2018 under the bloody drug war of former president Rodrigo Duterte.

What happened after January: In May, the Supreme Court denied Dela Rosa’s request for a temporary restraining order seeking to block the ICC warrant. Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida then said a valid ICC arrest warrant exists and is now enforceable, allowing the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) and the Philippine National Police (PNP) to effect the senator’s arrest.

Dela Rosa went into hiding shortly after the warrant was issued and is now the subject of a P50-million bounty. (READ: Bato dela Rosa’s escape: Timeline, analyses, opinions from experts)

Manhunt for Dela Rosa: On October 23, Remulla described Dela Rosa as “armed and dangerous.” He also warned that an attempt to arrest the senator by force could result in a “bloodbath.”

Dela Rosa’s camp continues to dispute how the warrant can be enforced. His lawyers argue that no local court has issued an arrest warrant and that the bounty cannot replace domestic judicial procedures that they said were necessary before the senator could be arrested.

Authorities have received at least 500 tips about Dela Rosa’s whereabouts, PNP chief General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said on November 9. The NBI has said it hopes to arrest the senator before the year ends. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com

Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024.

Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

World.title: TIMELINE: Jensen Huang’s fall from Nvidia grace
World.content:
JENSEN HUANG. Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang speaks with the media ahead of a meeting with the Senate Banking Committee on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., USA, December 3, 2025.

The resignation of Jensen Huang from Nvidia comes after a scandal still unfolding, with its aftereffects rocking both the tech industry and geopolitics.

The discovery of his extramarital affairs — with businesswoman and alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang (no relation) and two Nvidia employees — have threatened to upend the business amid US-China tensions and a race for AI dominance. Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation into reports Huang was targeted in a foreign intelligence operation.

Huang is an ally and adviser to US President Donald Trump on matters of artificial intelligence, which feeds into American aspirations for AI leadership.

As a private-sector leader, Huang wielded influence as to where Nvidia processors could go, and the fallout from this scandal brings up the debate over whether the US should allow advanced AI chips to be sold to China.

Below is a timeline of key points leading up to Jensen Huang’s fall:

JENSEN AND ALICE. A photo shows NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang with a woman confirmed by a Reuters source to be Alice Huang in Taipei, Taiwan released on June 7, 2024. Obtained by Reuters

June 7, 2024: The first known photo of Jensen Huang and Alice Huang of Singapore-based Megaspeed is seen. The two are seated together at Computex Taipei.

January 2025: US President Donald Trump meets Jensen Huang for the first time. This meeting is held at the White House.

EATING OUT. A screengrab from CTI video footage obtained November 9, 2026 shows a woman identified by Reuters as Alice Huang after comparison with a photograph obtained separately, attending a dinner with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (in black) at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan May 22, 2025. CTI via REUTERS TV

May 22, 2025: Jensen Huang and Alice Huang are seen leaving a restaurant together in Taipei.

December 8, 2025: Trump said the US would allow Nvidia to export its H200 processors, its second-best AI chips, to China.

Spring of 2026: Secretary of State Marco Rubio ​oversees drafting of classified memo warning senior Trump administration officials that Jensen Huang was in a close relationship with Alice Huang, according to a November New York Times report.

March 25, 2026: Trump appoints Jensen Huang to his President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology.

May 2026: Jensen Huang joins a US delegation of Trump’s that was visiting China to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trump aimed to urge Beijing to open up to US business.

September 14: Jensen Huang takes a phone call from Donald Trump during a ​live taping of the annual All-In summit. The two speak against proposals to slow AI development and discuss US leadership in AI.

September 24: Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, attend a White House state dinner hosted by Trump during the state visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to the US.

October 8: Trump awards Jensen Huang the National Medal of Science, the United States’ highest honor for scientists and engineers, alongside other tech industry ​leaders. The same day Trump gave the award, the president disclosed buying up to $1.6 million and selling up to $1 million in Nvidia stock during the summer of ​2026.

October 29: The New York Times (NYT) reports that Jensen Huang and Alice Huang had a “close relationship.” The report added US intelligence officials were concerned Alice Huang was acting on behalf of Chinese intelligence. Nvidia meanwhile says the relationship was not “unusual.”

November 5: Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives seek a closed-door briefing on November 18 from Jensen Huang on the allegations detailed in the NYT report.

November 8: Jensen Huang tells Nvidia employees he was unfaithful to his wife, without giving specifics. Nvidia’s board launches an independent investigation into reports the CEO was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.

November 9: Nvidia and Jensen Huang are sued in a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang’s ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

November 10: Jensen Huang’s affair facilitated the shipment of at least $7.5 billion ​worth of the company’s chips to Chinese firms, The Information reported. Meanwhile, Republican US Senator Kevin Cramer calls for Jensen Huang’s resignation, and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer calls on Congress to pass the AI Overwatch Act, which would give Congress power over advanced chip exports.

November 11: The ⁠CEO also ​had an extramarital affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reported to ​him, according to a NYT report. The Nvidia board meets to decide on Jensen Huang’s ouster.

November 12: Nvidia announces Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO. Colette Kress, executive vice president and CFO of Nvidia, was appointed interim CEO while the board begins a search for a permanent replacement. A separate report found sources that said Jensen Huang had a second affair with a different, unnamed Nvidia employee.

– with reports from Reuters/Rappler.com

World.title: Huang exit, US scrutiny imperil $3 billion in Chinese AI projects reliant on Nvidia
World.content:
NVIDIA AND CHINA. The Nvidia logo and Chinese flag are seen in this illustration taken August 27, 2025.

The projects reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing's access to the technology powering the global AI boom

BEIJING, China – Nvidia has said US export controls have effectively shut it out of China’s AI data-center market, but a Reuters review has identified more than $3 billion in Chinese computing projects built around the American chipmaker’s restricted processors.

The projects, stretching from China’s wealthy coastal technology hubs to remote western provinces, reveal the scale of continuing demand for Nvidia hardware even as Washington seeks to curb Beijing’s access to the technology powering the global artificial-intelligence boom.

The Reuters review examined more than 150 Chinese procurement notices, investment plans, construction contracts and corporate disclosures, identifying projects and equipment agreements with a combined reported value exceeding 23 billion yuan ($3.2 billion).

The findings paint a detailed picture of how deeply Nvidia technology remains embedded in China’s AI expansion. They reveal the company’s technology reaches well beyond China’s largest tech firms, into local government-backed ventures, universities and regional computing centres.

The estimate includes planned investments and signed contracts as well as completed installations. It covers buildings, power systems and other infrastructure, and does not reflect spending on Nvidia chips alone.

China’s commerce ministry and Nvidia did not immedietely respond to Reuters request for comment.

The findings come a day after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive amid a scandal over his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of intelligence ties to Beijing.

Huang, a vocal advocate of easing export restrictions, said last year Nvidia’s market share in China had fallen from 95% to zero. The company has also excluded China data-center computing revenue from its forecasts, citing regulatory uncertainty.

That does not mean Chinese demand has disappeared. While Nvidia’s statements address its own ability to compete and sell directly in China, the documents Reuters reviewed show Chinese customers continuing to plan purchases and, in some cases, operating restricted processors.

Sunny Cheung, an analyst at the Washington-based Jamestown Foundation, said Reuters’ findings reinforce his own view on enforcement: “Washington must stop focusing solely on who buys the chips on the surface and start examining who ultimately uses the computing power—and for what purpose.”

Billions in the pipeline

Across China, developers and institutions are advancing billions of dollars in AI data-centre projects designed around restricted Nvidia H100, H200, and H800 processors. These range from massive regional computing hubs to retrofitted commercial sites — such as a facility in northwestern Gansu province that was expected to install thousands of Nvidia chips before year-end, though it remains unclear if those processors ever arrived.

While some facilities are already operational or under construction, operators are exposed to potential delays, supply disruptions, or costly redesigns around domestic chips as export controls tighten.

Huang’s departure could deepen these vulnerabilities by weakening Nvidia’s lobbying leverage as US lawmakers press for tighter controls.

Washington’s dilemma

Washington began restricting Nvidia’s advanced AI processors in 2022 and subsequently tightened controls on modified chips developed for China, including the H800.

In January, the Trump administration moved to review H200 export licences for eligible Chinese customers individually, subject to conditions.

Nvidia’s August filing said it was effectively excluded from China’s data-center computing market. But an IDC report cited by Reuters in October estimated Nvidia still accounted for 34% of Chinese AI-accelerator shipments in the first half of 2026.

The figures measure different things and do not establish how the restricted hardware identified in the Reuters investigation reached Chinese users.

The scrutiny has intensified since Huang’s resignation on Thursday, following allegations involving Alice Huang, a former executive associated with Singapore-based Nvidia cloud partner Megaspeed.

Megaspeed has denied illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China. Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation, saying it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security were compromised. There has been no public finding that Jensen Huang violated export-control laws.

The Chinese projects identified by Reuters have not been linked to Megaspeed or the allegations involving Huang. – Rappler.com

World.title: DILG is latest government agency to report data leak
World.content:
The Department of the Interior and Local Government is assessing what kinds of information have been potentially compromised

MANILA, Philippines – The Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) on Wednesday, November 10, announced that it received reports of a data breach involving its Local Government Unit Support System-Barangay Information Management System (LGUSS-BIMS).

The system tracks resident profiles; manages issuances, such as ordinances, resolutions, certificates; disaster preparedness plans; gender and development plans and budgets; and reports for national agencies.

In an advisory, the department said that the potential data breach contains Records of Barangay Inhabitants (RBI). These records include household demographics, such as the residents’ names, civil status, occupation, address, contact details, and classifications (person with disability, overseas Filipino worker, or solo parent).

The DILG has also coordinated with the National Privacy Commission (NPC) and initiated precautionary measures to protect data and strengthen its security system. It has also begun its investigation and will take appropriate action based on findings.

Users have received an email from the DILG about the breach, advising them to report any suspicious activity observed related to the misuse of personal information.

Recent data leaks, breaches

Several government agencies and institutions have recently reported data breaches.

St. Luke’s Medical Center revealed unauthorized access to its mobile application, which is managed by a third-party service provider. The incident includes personal information of patients and employees.

According to an email forwarded to Rappler, the compromised pieces of information include the name, hospital patient number, birth date, civil status, gender, address, email, contact number, dependents, citizenship, and nationality.

Ten other government agencies reported leaks, according to the NPC:

Presidential Commission on Good Government

Department of Information and Communications Technology

Department of Labor and Employment, through its Bureau of Local Employment

Bureau of Internal Revenue

Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation

Department of Justice, through its Office for Alternative Dispute Resolution

Securities and Exchange Commission

Philippine Coast Guard

Department of Trade and Industry

Department of Science and Technology-Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology

Under the Data Privacy Act of 2012, government agencies or institutions that hold personal information should immediately inform the NPC and the affected individuals if their personal information has been compromised. They are also held accountable for the information they hold, including records processed by third parties. – Rappler.com

World.title: Cebu experts urge gov’t to comply with WHO air quality standards
World.content:
NETWORK. Health professionals, scientists, and environmental advocates launch the Cebu Clean Air Network (Cebu CAN) at the University of the Philippines Cebu on November 13, 2026, calling for stronger measures to address air pollution and protect public health.

Experts from UP Cebu, in collaboration with Clean Air Asia, are set to deploy new sensor technology to support air quality monitoring in the province

CEBU, Philippines – Environmentalists and health and science experts launched the Cebu Clean Air Network (Cebu CAN) on Friday, November 13, to urge the government to take immediate action towards meeting the World Health Organization (WHO) Global Air Quality Guidelines.

Francis Joseph dela Cruz, Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities (ICSC) Partnerships and Advocacy advisor and AktivAsia Co-founder, told Rappler in an interview that the network specifically chose Cebu for the launch due to developments in the province’s struggle for clean air.

“Cebu is a major economic center and it’s here that we find evidence of air pollution. We know where it’s coming from because research showed that 70% of it comes from mobile sources, which means transport and the rest, stationary — coal plants,” Dela Cruz said.

In April, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources–Environmental Management Bureau in Central Visayas (DENR-EMB 7) reported “very unhealthy” levels of air quality index (AQI) due to a lack of wind movement and accumulation of vehicle and industrial air pollutants.

“Data from the Talisay City Station confirms a significant and concerning rise in fine particulate matter (PM2.5),” said a DENR-EMB air quality advisory in April.

Cebu also experienced strong haze due to volcanic activity from the Kanlaon Volcano in July and forest fires from Indonesia in September.

The WHO air quality guidelines set an average annual limit of no more than 5 micrograms per cubic meter for concentrations of PM2.5 or particulate matter smaller than 2.5 micrometers — these are particulate matter small enough to travel deep into the lungs and even enter the blood stream.

According to Cebu CAN, the country’s current annual guidelines for PM2.5, set in 2020, remain five times higher than the limit recommended by the WHO.

Dela Cruz explained that the impact of unhealthy air quality can be seen in disrupted economic activity and hampered use of public resources.

“If you have an unhealthy citizenry, then the money that they earn, rather than go to what they need, goes to medication and if they cannot work, it gives them more problems. If they go to a public health center, the center will have to allocate more resources for patients,” the clean air advocate said.

According to a 2021 study by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air and the ICSC, air pollution costs the country an estimated P4.5 trillion a year in economic costs.

PLEDGE. Cebu CAN member organizations Clean Air Asia, the UP Cebu Center for Environmental Informatics, 350 Pilipinas, CAP-Cebu Chapter, Health Alliance for Climate and Clean Air Philippines, Philippine Movement for Climate Justice, AktivAsia, Health Care Without Harm, Greenpeace Cebu, and Amnesty International joined the signing for the Cebu Clean Air Network Pledge on November 13, 2026.

Acting on air quality

For Jonnifer Sinogaya, center head of the University of the Philippines in Cebu Center for Environmental Informatics, there’s a need to address gaps in the reliability of the monitoring of the province’s air quality index.

“During the haze, there was only one source of data, which was from the station in Talisay City so if there is now a network, more stations to deploy, you can get more reliable data and that will supplement those from the DENR-EMB,” Sinogaya said.

With the launch of the Cebu CAN, the University of the Philippines Cebu (UP Cebu), in a memorandum of agreement with Clean Air Asia, is set to deploy new air quality sensors in the province.

Apart from data gathering, Dela Cruz shared that local governance could also take part in improving Cebu’s air quality by reviewing the province’s reliance on energy sources like coal that emit harmful pollutants.

At present, Cebu contributes a majority of the energy from coal in the Visayas grid. The Cebu island sub-grid consists of coal (82.03%), diesel (12.94%), solar (4.93%), and hydroelectric (0.1%) power plants.

The province is also host to the coal-fired power plants that have been on forced and unplanned outages in recent months.

Dela Cruz suggested that the electrification of transport packaged with a transition to the use of renewable energy would provide the province an advantage in addressing gaps in its energy and air quality demands.

“So that’s the first step, looking at how you can transform modes of mobility and transportation. If we can afford it, switching to electric vehicles will address mobile sources of pollution,” the clean air advocate said. – Rappler.com

World.title: Customs chief takes BCDA helm amid controversial Pax Silica
World.content:
BOC. Bureau of Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno speaks before the start of the bidding of seven luxury vehicles confiscated from the Discaya family, on November 20, 2025.

The change comes as BCDA prepares long-term arrangements for Camp John Hay’s key facilities and as the Marcos administration readies the Pax Silica framework deal with the US

BAGUIO CITY, Philippines – A leadership shake-up is putting a new man in charge of two major government development projects, including Camp John Hay in Baguio and the controversial US-backed Pax Silica initiative at New Clark City, Tarlac.

Bureau of Customs Commissioner Ariel Nepomuceno has been appointed president and chief executive officer of the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA), replacing Joshua Bingcang, who is moving to the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA).

Nepomuceno confirmed his transfer on Wednesday, November 11, the same day President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed his appointment, which took immediate effect.

The change comes as BCDA prepares long-term management arrangements for Camp John Hay’s golf course and hotel facilities, following the completion of an updated master development plan for the former American military reservation.

Under Bingcang, BCDA pursued plans to attract private investors to manage and improve the facilities after regaining control of disputed properties from former developer Camp John Hay Development Corporation in January 2025, following a Supreme Court ruling. (READ: Camp John Hay: A 3-decade saga of turf wars, court drama, and a new beginning)

The agency also extended interim management arrangements for the golf course through 2026 while preparing for a long-term concession.

Beyond Baguio, Nepomuceno inherits the proposed 4,000-acre Pax Silica industrial hub in New Clark City, Tarlac, part of a US-led initiative aimed at strengthening supply chains for semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, and technologies supporting artificial intelligence.

The proposal has faced scrutiny over its potential environmental impact, land rights, and consultation with affected communities, including indigenous peoples. (READ: [In This Economy] Pax Silica: What’s the Philippines’ trump card?)

Capas Mayor Roseller Rodriguez questioned the lack of prior consultation with local officials and sought greater disclosure of the project’s scope and potential effects. In August, the Department of Environment and Natural Resources confirmed that it had not received or processed an environmental impact assessment application for Pax Silica.

BCDA, however, has maintained that the proposed development would occupy designated buildable areas, would not displace Indigenous communities, and would comply with Philippine environmental laws. (READ: Pax Silica: BCDA’s claims and the counterarguments)

Questions over national sovereignty also surfaced during a House hearing on Wednesday, November 11, when lawmakers raised concerns about a proposed joint-governance arrangement with the United States.

Bingcang assured legislators that Philippine laws would prevail, stressing that negotiations on the project’s legal framework were still ongoing, with no confirmed signing date.

Following the announcement of his transfer to PEZA, Bingcang said Pax Silica remained a national government initiative.

Nepomuceno now takes over BCDA with both projects at critical planning stages. The agency has yet to announce whether the leadership change will affect Camp John Hay’s proposed management contracts or the timetable for the Pax Silica agreement. – Rappler.com

World.title: Chua on defense wanting longer trial: We call it ‘masochism’
World.content:
Manila Rep. Joel Chua —Screengrab from an INQUIRER.net video

MANILA, Philippines — The supposed preference of Vice President Sara Duterte’s camp for a longer trial comes off as masochism for Manila Rep. Joel Chua, as the defense lawyers seem to enjoy seeing themselves ‘beaten and bloodied’ continuously.

Chua, a member of the prosecution panel, said this during a press briefing on Friday as he believes the defense has been beaten badly already, even as they have just started presenting their own set of witnesses.

If the defense is already beaten badly, Chua asked why it appears that members of Duterte’s camp, like her spokesperson Atty. Paolo Panelo, question the prosecution’s yearning to finish the trial before the year ends.

Article continues after this 

READ: Luistro: Sara Duterte trial ‘bloodbath’ real, but it’s on defense’s side

“Kanina tinatanong po ninyo ‘yong explanation ng bloodbath. ‘Yong paliwanag po ni Chair Jinky (Luistro) ganito po: naglabas po ng ebidensya ang prosecution, bugbog po sila. Naglabas po ng ebidensya at testigo ang defense, mas lalo po silang na bugbog at duguan na po sila,” Chua said.

(A while ago you were asking for an explanation on the bloodbath statement. What Chair Jinky (Luistro) tried to say is this: the prosecution came up with evidence, they got beaten. The defense came up with its own witnesses and evidence, and still got beaten, they are now bloodied.)

“Ngayon ayaw pa nilang matapos? Eh masokista na po ang tawag d’yan,” Chua added.

(Yet they do not want to end this? We now call this as masochism.)

Article continues after this 

Chua’s statement came after Panelo, in an ambush interview on the sidelines of the trial on Thursday, said that Duterte herself expects the trial not to reach Christmas Day as the prosecution is allegedly rushing to end the proceedings.

READ: Prosec: Duterte’s camp in panic, still no answer to ill-gotten wealth allegations

Article continues after this 

Panelo said Duterte believes the prosecution is aiming for a conviction near Christmas so that the people’s emotions would be simmered.

“Inaasahan niya talaga at yan ang nakikita niyang hinahabol ng prosecution, or ng mga tao sa likod nitong impeachment. Dahil ang sabi niya sa akin noon, ang parang pakay ng mga nagmamadali para habulin itong Christmas break is para daw kung may conviction at magalit yung mga tao, hindi sila makapag-express masyado ng galit nila dahil Pasko na,” Panelo said.

(She really expects that and knows that the prosecution is going after that, or the people behind this impeachment. Because what she told me before, their goal in rushing things is to settle things before the Christmas break so that if there is a conviction and the people are mad, they cannot be mad because it’s Christmas.)

READ: Prosec: Defense withdrew BPI exec to prevent ‘Pandora’s box’ opening

“At kung acquittal naman, eh di makakalimutan na sa susunod na taon. So, ‘yon ang information na natanggap niya,” he added.

(And if it’s an acquittal, then it will be forgotten next year. So, that is the information that she received.)

Earlier in the press briefing on Friday, lead public prosecutor and Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro said that Duterte’s yearning for a bloodbath in her impeachment trial came true, but it happened on the side of the defense.

“May bloodbath nga (There is a bloodbath), but the bloodbath is happening in the defense and not in the prosecution,” Luistro said after being asked about Duterte’s previous statements.

Chua, also a public prosecutor who was with Luistro during the briefing, explained that the bloodbath happened because the defense panel has been bombarded by punches from the prosecution, yet it has not been able to land any of its attacks when it was their turn to present evidence.

Luistro said he wanted to give the defense the benefit of the doubt, but he also understands why people believe the defense has been absorbing punches in bunches — because the prosecution’s accusations for Article II of the Articles of Impeachment remain unanswered.

“With all due respect to the defense, let us give them the benefit of the doubt sapagkat ako man ay naghihintay sa kasagutan ng respondent vice president to these specific allegations of unexplained wealth. Kaya lang siyempre, ang tagal nating hinintay ito eh, kaya ang anticipation namin mataas, ang expectation namin na explosive ang testigo, ang ebidensya, is very high,” Luistro said.

(With all due respect to the defense, let us give them the benefit of the doubt because even I await the vice president’s answers to these specific allegations of unexplained wealth. But of course, we have been waiting for so long, that’s why our anticipation is great, our expectation that there would be explosive testimonies, evidence, is very high.)

“That’s what they kept on saying since the proceedings in the justice committee. Palaging ang sinasabi, we will answer; we will address in the proper forum. Now we are in the proper forum, it’s your time to answer, wala pa tayong nakikitang convincing na sagot. Again the disparity of the amount is so big — P817 million ang hina-hanapan natin ng explanation,” she added.

(That’s what they kept on saying since the proceeding in the justice committee. They always said that they will answer in the proper forum. Now we are in the proper forum, it’s your time to answer, but you have not given us any convincing answer. Again the disparity of the amount is so big — we are looking for an explanation on the P817 million unexplained wealth.)

After the defense panel presented six witnesses since Monday, different members prosecution have been adamant that their testimonies failed to counter the evidence against Duterte — adding that in some ways, even bolstered the prosecutors’ arguments.

On Thursday, prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said that the allegations raised under Article II have not been disputed, and therefore causing panic within its ranks.

Alonto Adiong said he is basing this on the defense panel’s decision to withdraw the presentation of several witnesses, which he said may be a sign of a change in their strategy.

During the 43rd day of Duterte’s trial, the defense manifested that they will no longer be calling several witnesses, including Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) senior vice president and lawyer Paul Roderick Ysmael.

Chua, meanwhile, said that the defense’s withdrawal of banking officials may have been brought by a yearning to play safe, as pushing with their plan may have led to more information against their client.

Chua said this after being asked whether the alleged presence of dollar accounts under the vice president’s name was the reason why the defense begged off from presenting BPI senior vice president and lawyer Paul Roderick Ysmael.

Chua said he cannot say for certain whether this was the case, but he believes the decision aimed to prevent the opening of a Pandora’s box.

Article II deals with allegations that Duterte amassed unexplained wealth and failed to properly declare her wealth in her Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth (SALN).

One of the key allegations under Article II is the report of financial forensic analyst Atty. Alexander Cabrera, who testified before the Senate Impeachment Court last October 9 as a prosecution witness.

According to Cabrera, the vice president has failed to declare P817 million worth of assets in her SALN from 2022 to 2025.

Cabrera said this was a conservative figure, as the total may reach around P1.5 billion.

Since Monday, six witnesses have been presented by the defense to counter the prosecution’s allegations in Article II. However, none of the witnesses discussed Cabrera’s P817 million figure. /mr

World.title: 9 private hospitals in Caraga sign ‘No Balance Billing’ pact
World.content:
PhilHealth Acting President and CEO Dr. Beverly Lorraine Ho (center) and PhilHealth Caraga Regional Vice President Michael Jibson Hernandez (fourth from left) sign a memorandum of agreement with nine private hospitals in Caraga on Nov. 12, 2026, at Watergate Hotel in Butuan City to implement the No Balance Billing policy. (Photo courtesy of Butuan City PIO)

BUTUAN CITY — More patients in the Caraga region can now avail of hospital care without out-of-pocket expenses after nine private hospitals signed a memorandum of agreement (MOA) with the Philippine Health Insurance Corporation (PhilHealth) and the Department of Health (DOH) to implement the ‘No Balance Billing’ (NBB) policy.

Dr. Beverly Lorraine Ho, PhilHealth acting President and Chief Executive Officer and PhilHealth Caraga Regional Vice President Michael Jibson Hernandez led the signing ceremony alongside representatives from the participating private health facilities.

Among the nine signatories are three major hospitals in Butuan City, namely, Manuel J. Santos Hospital, Allied Care Experts (ACE) Medical Center-Butuan, and Butuan Doctors’ Hospital.

Article continues after this 

READ: Solon says Caraga may soon get first Level III hospital

Under the NBB policy, qualified PhilHealth members admitted to basic or ward accommodations will not be charged any additional fees beyond their PhilHealth benefit packages for covered medical services.

To ensure compliance and accommodate eligible beneficiaries, participating private hospitals are mandated by law to allocate at least 10 percent of their total bed capacity for basic or ward accommodations in accordance with PhilHealth guidelines.

Beyond zero out-of-pocket billing, the agreement establishes a framework for regular program monitoring, streamlined benefit delivery, and joint data collection between PhilHealth and the private hospitals to guide future healthcare policy improvements.

Officials said the partnership clarifies the operational responsibilities of both the state health insurer and private providers in expanding access to affordable, quality healthcare across the region. INQ

World.title: 20 charging points for EVs now available at NLEX
World.content:
EV charging bay at Shell Mexico, Km 76 southbound. —Photo from NLEX Corp.

MANILA, Philippines — Twenty charging points were added across the North Luzon Expressway (NLEX) amid a growing number of electric and hybrid vehicles, its operator announced Friday.

According to NLEX Corp. in a statement, six of its service stops have been equipped with 20 EV charging points as of November 2026.

READ: Toll board orders NLEx operator to address flooding in Pampanga

Article continues after this 

These facilities, said the corporation, provide power ratings ranging from 22 kilowatt (kW) to 240 kW.

“NLEX Corporation is responding to this shift by expanding the availability of electric vehicle charging facilities along its expressway network, giving EV owners more opportunities to recharge during their journeys between Metro Manila and Central Luzon,” NLEX Corp. said.

NLEX said the exact location of the charging facilities are at Petron Marilao, Total San Simon and Shell Mexico for northbound motorists, and Shell Mexico, Petron Bocaue and Drive & Dine for those travelling southbound.

Its facility in Drive & Dine features seven charging units, including 240-kW DC fast chargers, which is currently the highest-rated charging units on the NLEX network.

Additionally, all charging facilities support “CCS2 and Type 2 connectors”, while “GB/T connectors” are also available at Total San Simon and Drive & Dine.

Article continues after this 

NLEX Corp. said two Shell Recharge facilities are also scheduled to open in December 2026, which will be located at Shell Burol, kilometer 32 northbound, and Shell of Asia, kilometer 36 southbound.

Meanwhile, apart from EV infrastructure, NLEX said it is implementing additional service facilities and amenities, with four service stops currently offering free Wi-Fi, namely Drive & Dine, Shell Burol and both Shell Mexico locations.

Article continues after this 

The corporation said the Toll Regulatory Board has also approved six additional service facilities along NLEX and SCTEX, from Bocaue to Concepcion. /ms

World.title: Luistro: Sara Duterte trial ‘bloodbath’ real, but it’s on defense’s side
World.content:
Rep. Gerville Luistro. INQUIRER PHOTO / NIÑO JESUS ORBETA

MANILA, Philippines — The “bloodbath” that Vice President Sara Duterte imagined would happen in her impeachment trial came true, but it was not in the way she would have wanted, Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro said on Friday.

Luistro, lead public prosecutor for the impeachment, said in a press briefing that the bloodbath happened instead within Duterte’s camp, or the defense panel, as their witnesses’ testimony favored the prosecution.

“May bloodbath nga (There is a bloodbath), but the bloodbath is happening in the defense and not in the prosecution,” Luistro said after being asked about Duterte’s previous statements.

Article continues after this 

READ: VP Duterte on impeach trial: ‘I want a bloodbath’

Manila Rep. Joel Chua, also a public prosecutor who was with Luistro during the briefing, explained that the bloodbath happened because the defense panel has been bombarded by punches from the prosecution, yet it has not been able to land any of its attacks when it was their turn to present evidence.

“Duguan na sila eh, ‘di ba? So, so far hanggang ngayon di pa sila tumatama, ‘yong suntok nila sa prosecution. Bugbog-bugbog na sila eh,” he added.

(It’s because they are already bloodied, right? So, so far, up to now, they have yet to land their punches against the prosecution. But they are already beaten up.)

Luistro and Chua were referring to Duterte’s several statements pertaining to a bloodbath during the trial.

Article continues after this 

The first time Duterte mentioned blood in relation to the impeachment proceedings against her was during a thanksgiving mass in Davao City after the May 2025 elections. According to Duterte, she is eager for a “bloodbath” once the impeachment trial for the first set of complaints starts at the Senate.

This was for the first set of impeachment complaints filed against Duterte. However, the trial did not push through as the Supreme Court declared the first set of Articles of Impeachment against Duterte unconstitutional, based on a petition filed by the vice president herself.

Article continues after this 

Several lawmakers and lawyers supportive of Duterte’s impeachment poked fun at the Vice President’s alleged contradicting statements, as she had been vocal about a bloodbath but supposedly acted towards avoiding it.

Last March, House prosecutor and Mamamayang Liberal party-list Rep. Leila de Lima asked Duterte twice as to where her aspiration for a “bloodbath” is as her statements back then allegedly show a bid to evade accountability.

De Lima said that instead of answering the questions and issues hurled against her, Duterte is resorting to diverting discussions by questioning moves to protect documents and witnesses that may be vital to the impeachment proceedings.

READ: Where’s ‘bloodbath’ now? De Lima says Duterte scared of impeachment

After the start of her trial in July, Duterte once again referred to her impeachment trial as a “bloodbath,” this time adding that she expects to be “bloodied but unbowed.”

Duterte said this in a short statement, when she met with her lawyers in the Senate. In response, another House prosecutor — this time Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon — urged Duterte to personally face the impeachment court, as she cannot participate in a bloodbath but at the same time field proxies for her.

After the defense panel presented six witnesses since Monday, different members prosecution have been adamant that their testimonies failed to counter the evidence against Duterte — adding that in some ways, even bolstered the prosecutors’ arguments.

On Thursday, prosecution spokesperson and Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said in a separate press briefing that the allegations raised under Article II have not been disputed, and therefore causing panic within its ranks.

Alonto Adiong said he is basing this on the defense panel’s decision to withdraw the presentation of several witnesses, which he said may be a sign of a change in their strategy.

On the 43rd day of Duterte’s trial, the defense stated that it would no longer call several witnesses, including Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) senior vice president and lawyer Paul Roderick Ysmael.

Chua, meanwhile, said during Thursday’s briefing that the defense’s withdrawal of banking officials may have been brought by a yearning to play safe, as pushing with their plan may have led to more information against their client.

Chua said this after being asked whether the alleged presence of dollar accounts under the vice president’s name was the reason why the defense begged off from presenting BPI senior vice president and lawyer Paul Roderick Ysmael.

World.title: De Lima files new reso seeking probe on Zambales dredging
World.content:
Rep. Leila de Lima —Screengrab from an INQUIRER.net video

MANILA, Philippines — A new resolution which reiterates the need for a congressional investigation on the large-scale dredging operations in Zambales has been filed by Mamamayang Liberal party-list Rep. Leila de Lima, saying that the ecosystem damage continues if this issue remains unchecked.

In a statement, de Lima said she filed House Resolution No. 1601 calling on the House of Representatives to conduct an inquiry on the dredging operations in Zambales’ rivers and coastal waters, and the alleged presence of Chinese vessels in the area.

According to de Lima, the investigation should result in a stronger legal framework governing dredging, which will safeguard coastal areas and marine resources.

Article continues after this 

“With large-scale dredging unabated, coastal erosion and loss of livelihoods unresolved, and questions regarding the foreign vessels involved, the volume of materials dredged and their destination still unaddressed, every day of delay in conducting an inquiry into the matter poses greater risks of further and potentially irreversible damage to coastal areas, fishing grounds, and the communities that depend on them,” de Lima said on Thursday.

“The findings of such probe should guide the formulation of stronger environmental safeguards, transparency mechanisms, and accountability measures to ensure that all dredging and reclamation activities are conducted in accordance with law, and the right of the people to a balanced and healthful ecology,” she added.

De Lima said several issues involving dredging — from environmental damage to security concerns — remain unanswered while their calls to investigate the matter have not been addressed.

“Marami tayong mga tanong ukol sa nakababahalang dredging na ito sa Zambales na kailangan ng agarang tugon. We won’t allow this alarming issue to be ignored or left unaddressed,” she said.

(We have a lot of questions about this concerning dredging in Zambales which we have to address. We won’t allow this alarming issue to be ignored or left unaddressed.)

Article continues after this 

“Kailangan nating malaman ang totoo hindi lang para matukoy kung may nangyayaring pag-abuso, pagkukulang o kapabayaan, nang hindi na magpatuloy o maulit pa ang ganitong operasyon na banta sa kalikasan, seguridad, buhay at kabuhayan ng marami nating mga kababayan,” she added.

(We need to know the truth behind this not only to pinpoint whether there was abuse, shortcomings, or neglect, but also to ensure that these operations will no longer happen again as it threatens the safety, security, lives, and livelihood of many Filipinos.)

Article continues after this 

As early as November 2025, de Lima had already called for an investigation on a Chinese company’s dredging operations near Zambales, filing House Resolution No. 424 as there are different issues brought by such an activity.

De Lima said Malacañang should check the dredging operations, as residents claimed that this endanger communities and the overall ecosystem, with fisherfolk and residents of San Felipe town in Zambales being affected.

READ: De Lima wants probe into Chinese firm’s dredging in Zambales

Last September, de Lima again renewed her call for a congressional investigation on the matter, claiming that the vessels involved have questionable records.

De Lima raised the matter during the House committee on appropriations’ hearing on the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) proposed 2027 budget, saying that the agency made “conflicting explanations” on the nature of operations conducted by vessels that had Chinese names.

At one point, the lawmaker said a regional director told him that no Chinese firm was involved in dredging activities. However, she also recalled that DENR previously acknowledged that there were Chinese vessels used, but were merely rented.

De Lima cited a Philippine Ports Authority (PPA) list issued in September 2025 showing that there are 67 vessels conducting dredging activities in Botolan and San Felipe towns in Zambales from 2020 to 2025 — including some that had questionable records and identities.

But regardless of the DENR’s explanation, the Minority solon Lima said the department has not denied the presence of dredging operations — stressing the need for an investigation especially since residents of coastal communities have complained about seas coming closer to the coastline.

READ: De Lima renews call for probe into Zambales dredging

During the 2026 southwest monsoon season, several residents have complained about seas creeping closer to their homes, which they believe to have happened after dredging activities started in 2022.

READ: Sea inches closer as dredging worries Zambales folk

In an interview with INQUIRER last September, a woman who has been a long-time resident of the area said that the shoreline continues to erode, with waves now reaching homes during high tide.

World.title: Eating out, commuting get pricier in Baguio, Cordillera in October
World.content:
Dining out and commuting by public transportation were a bit pricey in October, as shown by inflation rates of 9.3 percent in Baguio City and 9.2 percent in the Cordillera region.

BAGUIO CITY — Dining out and commuting by public transportation were a bit pricey in October, as shown by inflation rates of 9.3 percent in Baguio City and 9.2 percent in the Cordillera region.

The October inflation was the highest rate yet this year for the mountain resort city and the highland provinces of Ifugao, Abra, Apayao, Benguet, Mountain Province, and Kalinga, and its component Tabuk City, said Aldrin Federico Bahit Jr., chief statistician of the Philippine Statistics Authority for the Cordillera, during a briefing on Thursday.

With the 1.9 percent inflation rate at the start of the year, Cordillera commodity prices became so expensive that inflation initially peaked at 7.6 percent in April, he said. But Cordillera inflation followed a sustained upward trajectory, climbing to 8.3 percent in September and 9.2 percent last month.

Article continues after this 

READ: Inflation jumps to three-year high of 7.8% in October

Inflation in the summer capital followed a similar trend, from 4 percent in January to 7.8 percent in September before high prices pushed it to 9.3 percent last month.

A weakened peso in October, when the exchange rate traded at P63-64 per US dollar, and global uncertainties over the protracted war in Iran have directly impacted the Cordillera, Bahit said.

Philippine transactions are dollar-based, so when the peso depreciates, commodities purchased abroad, like gasoline, become expensive, as does the domestic supply chain when truckers deliver Benguet vegetables to Manila and contend with high fuel costs. “The compounding effect of high-priced gas and a depreciating peso on Cordillera households is high,” Bahit said.

Food like rice remained a major contributor to upland inflation, with the inflation rate at 20.2 percent in October, up from “an already double-digit rate” of 18.2 percent in September, he said.

Article continues after this 

Restaurants and cafes with full service helped accelerate October inflation, with an 11.4 percent rate last month, which was up from the 10.2 percent rate recorded in September, Bahit said. Utility expenses, rent and LPG prices also helped jack up Cordillera inflation.

READ: Fuel prices drive highest Philippine inflation in years

Article continues after this 

But last month’s decision to raise passenger fees for jeepneys (a provisional hike from P13 to P15) and taxicabs (a flagdown rate of P65 from the original P50) in Baguio and public utility vehicles like tricycles in Abra or Mountain Province reflected a “second round of risk” confronting families, Bahit said.

Gasoline sold in the Cordillera posted an inflation rate of 48.4 percent in October from 41 percent in September.

The Strong El Niño would worsen inflation because of its effect on food supplies like rice, Bahit pointed out. The prolonged dry spell came at a time when regions like the Cordillera are affected by the Middle East war and the closure of the trade route through the Strait of Hormuz, he said.

Your subscription could not be saved. Please try again. Your subscription has been successful. Subscribe to our daily newsletter SIGN ME UP

The outlook has not dampened travel to the highlands. Drawing an average of 250,000 to 300,000 visitors every December, which is the start of Baguio’s peak tourist season, the city “remains a favorite destination during Christmas despite any crisis,” said Aloysius Mapalo, Baguio tourism operations officer. With a report from Maureen Matayew, Contributor./coa

World.title: ASEAN Should Accept Myanmar Back at Diplomat Level: Bangkok
World.content:
BANGKOK—Myanmar’s foreign minister should be allowed back into meetings of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) regional bloc, Thailand’s top diplomat said on Thursday after a visit to the war-torn country.

Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said his meetings with regime leader Min Aung Hlaing and others had revealed “a desire on the part of Myanmar to engage, to return to ASEAN.” But he said there was no talk of specific steps.

Myanmar has been excluded from high-level meetings of the 11-nation ASEAN since a 2021 military coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and triggered an ongoing civil war.

Thailand has been leading efforts to normalize ties since coup leader Min Aung Hlaing was installed as civilian president earlier this year following elections dismissed by monitors as a charade.

“For Thailand, we believe that the next step is to have the foreign minister of Myanmar participate in the ASEAN meetings at the level of foreign minister,” Sihasak told reporters.

His comments came ahead of a meeting of ASEAN leaders starting Sunday in the Philippines.

Sihasak said he had also raised the “very urgent problem” of water pollution among tributaries of the Mekong River, which straddles five Southeast Asian countries and China, saying a working group would meet later this month.

Last week, authorities in northern Thailand suspended tap water production after arsenic levels at the waterworks intake was found to be 30 times higher than the safety standard. More than a dozen villages were affected by the suspension.

A subsequent field sample from the nearby Sai River measured arsenic at 25 times the safety standard, the government said.

Thai officials previously pinned the toxic sediment on wastewater from mining activity upstream in Myanmar.

Sihasak said he also raised the issue of a spillover of violence into Thailand.

World.title: Myanmar Faces Year of Blackouts as Regime Admits 30% Power Shortfall
World.content:
Myanmar’s rotating power cuts will remain in place through 2027, with generation expected to meet only 70 percent of national demand, Deputy Energy Minister Aye Kyaw announced Wednesday.

Addressing the regime’s rubber-stamp parliament, he said next summer’s 24-hour electricity demand is forecast at 5,010 MW, while generation capacity is only 3,540 MW.

“That’s why we need to continue the load shedding measures,” he said.

Despite having the poorest electricity access in the region, Myanmar made significant progress in grid connectivity under the National League for Democracy’s 15-year National Electrification Plan in 2015. By 2020, more than half of households had electricity access, and the NLD’s World Bank-backed plan aimed to achieve nationwide electrification by 2030.

However, the plan was scrapped after the 2021 coup, and regime mismanagement has since triggered rolling power outages across the country.

The World Bank says reliable supply has dropped sharply since the military takeover, affecting nearly half of connected households — with 41.6 percent receiving only enough electricity for basic lighting and phone charging, and 9.1 percent getting no electricity at all.

It blames the deepening generation crisis on the suspension of LNG power plants, declining domestic gas production, hydropower stress, infrastructure damage, and stalled investment.

In response, the regime reintroduced nationwide rolling blackouts, leaving residents in even major cities struggling to manage households and livelihoods.

“We have to be ready to fill up the water, cook meals, and iron our clothes the moment the power comes back on,” Ko Thant Zin from Insein Township in the suburbs of Yangon told the Irrawaddy.

He said the electricity supply rotates between four hours on and four hours off.

“Under the civilian government, the roads were bright with lights. Now, I have to open my eyes wide to see the way ahead while driving at night,” he commented.

The deputy energy minister told citizens to install solar panels if they want a reliable supply. However, import curbs and surging prices have put solar options out of reach for most urban residents.

“Forget about solar panels, most people can’t even afford a portable power pack,” a resident of downtown Yangong’s Botahtaung Township told The Irrawaddy. “Prices have been skyrocketing because of import restrictions.”

He added that power cuts would cause major suffering during the El Niño heatwave forecast for November through January.

“I can’t imagine how we will get through next summer,” he said, reacting to the rationing announcement. “It will be especially tough for young children and the elderly.”

Demand driven by outages has seen the price of solar panels surge to a record high. Yangon residents said a household solar power system now costs at least 10 million kyats (around US $4,760), putting it beyond the reach of ordinary families.

Last month, Yangon City authorities mandated that all commercial projects and high-rise buildings must install solar power systems to operate elevators and emergency lighting, as part of a nationwide push for solar amid deepening power blackouts.

The World Bank says chronic power shortages remain one of the main constraints on Myanmar’s economy, limiting its recovery and keeping poverty persistently high.

The deputy energy minister also announced plans to develop two 55 MW small-modular-reactors in cooperation with Russia’s atomic agency, ROSATOM, starting in fiscal 2028-29. The project is slated for completion in fiscal 2035-36 but locations have yet to be announced.

World.title: Three Years After Operation 1027, Hopang Transformed Under Wa Rule
World.content:
Friday marks three years since Hopang in the Wa Self-Administered Zone experienced its first taste of the joint ethnic offensive known as Operation 1027, when drones deployed by the Brotherhood Alliance bombed a monastery sheltering retreating Myanmar military personnel from nearby Kunlong base.

For the Myanmar military, which had controlled Hopang for decades, the drone strike was an early warning that its grip on the town was nearing an end. For the United Wa State Army (UWSA), it presented an opportunity to gain one of the most important towns in Wa territory without firing a shot.

Less than two months after the Nov. 13 drone attack, forces of the Brotherhood Alliance—which grouped the Arakan Army, Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) and Ta’ang National Liberation Army (TNLA)—and allied groups entered Hopang with little resistance. Rather than holding the town themselves, they quickly handed it over to their ally, the UWSA.

Operation 1027, which inflicted one of the most devastating military setbacks in the Myanmar military’s history, had begun on Oct. 27, 2023, in Chinshwehaw, a border town just 8 km from Hopang. Just 19 km away, Kunlong, a key town on a China-Myanmar trade route, also fell after sustained drone attacks by alliance forces.

As Kunlong collapsed, its commander, officers and wounded soldiers fled to Hopang.

“A battalion commander and a soldier entered the monastery building and pleaded for shelter,” recalled a witness who was in the compound. “They told the abbot they had been under drone attacks for four days, and had only managed to retreat after receiving supporting fire.”

That same night, drones struck the monastery.

For Hopang residents, who had watched the fighting around Kunlong from hilltop pagodas, the attack on the monastery signaled that war was coming closer. By the next morning, many were fleeing the town, leaving their homes and shops behind.

Some local drivers found themselves ferrying displaced families back and forth, while others stayed behind to guard their properties. Residents feared not only a potential urban battle similar to the fighting in Kunlong, but also the prospect of Myanmar military airstrikes.

One restaurant owner recalled watching looters load crates of beer from his shop onto vehicles through CCTV cameras while he was fleeing.

Among those who fled were a monk who was injured in the November 13 drone attack, as well as health workers from a public hospital in Hopang.

Hopang was home to a military battalion and a police station, but all the surrounding towns including Kunlong and Chinshwehaw were controlled by the Brotherhood Alliance. At this point, Hopang was effectively isolated.

When MNDAA troops entered Hopang in early January 2024, the remaining military and police units reportedly surrendered with little resistance. Under a prior arrangement between the MNDAA and the UWSA, control of the town was then transferred to the Wa army.

Unlike Lashio, Laukkai, Chinshwehaw or Kunlong, Hopang largely escaped major battle damage. Yet residents say the town has since undergone a different kind of transformation, one increasingly shaped by Chinese capital and Wa administration.

The ethnically diverse town, home to Shan, Wa, Bamar, Kachin, Ta’ang and other communities, was once known for its Buddhist, Christian and traditional ethnic festivals. Today, residents say casinos, bars, hotels, massage parlors and prostitution-related businesses funded by Chinese investors have proliferated.

Some residents also complain of heavy taxation and a justice system that includes public executions, practices rarely seen under previous administrations.

The yuan now dominates much of the local economy, with residents increasingly pricing goods in the Chinese currency rather than kyats. In the healthcare arena, expensive Chinese-run private hospitals have emerged alongside the only public hospital.

Over the past three years, rumors have repeatedly surfaced that the UWSA will return Hopang to the regime. Residents say they see no sign that this is imminent, however.

The town, which participated in the 2010, 2015 and 2020 elections, did not take part in the regime-organized 2025 poll and is absent from the list of constituencies scheduled to be put to a vote in additional elections scheduled for April 2027.

Recently, regime Defense Minister and peace negotiator Lieutenant General Yar Pyae visited Panghsang, the UWSA headquarters. There was no indication that Hopang’s status was discussed during his meetings with Wa leaders, however.

While the UWSA remained officially neutral during Operation 1027, it emerged among the campaign’s biggest beneficiaries. Without openly joining the offensive, it gained full control of Hopang and Panlong, while also securing partial control along with the Myanmar military over Tangyan, a strategically important town on the route to Lashio, the largest town in northern Shan.

Three years after the first drone bombs fell on Hopang, the town has changed beyond recognition for longtime residents.

During Operation 1027, the MNDAA and TNLA went on to seize almost the whole of northern Shan State including the capital Lashio and all vital trade routes with China.

However, under strong Chinese pressure, in 2025 the ethnic armies were forced to halt fighting the Myanmar military and hand back several liberated towns to the regime.

World.title: Myanmar’s Coup President Barred From Upcoming 49th ASEAN Summit
World.content:
The Philippines announced Wednesday that Myanmar regime leaders remain barred from joining the 49th ASEAN summit and high-level meetings in Manila from November 15 to 17, upholding a ban imposed after the 2021 military coup.

Myanmar will instead be represented by the Director-General of its ASEAN affairs department, according to a statement issued by Manila’s Department of Foreign Affairs.

“We welcome this official confirmation that there is no place [at the summit] for junta leader Min Aung Hlaing,” Khin Ohmar, a prominent Myanmar democracy activist and founder of the Progressive Voice human rights foundation, told The Irrawaddy.

“ASEAN made the right decision in line with its principles. We have been demanding that no junta member be permitted to join the summit.”

She added that ASEAN would have sacrificed its credibility and responsibility to the people of Myanmar by inviting the junta leader, who faces a genocide ruling at the international court later this month.

Confirmation that the ban remains in place came after domestic and international rights groups warned the regional bloc against legitimizing a regime that is intensifying violence against civilians.

On Monday, the Special Advisory Council for Myanmar (SAC-M) and ASEAN Parliamentarians for Human Rights urged regional leaders “to immediately confirm” that Min Aung Hlaing and his junta cohorts would be excluded from the summit.

It also called on ASEAN leaders to adopt “measurable benchmarks for compliance” with the bloc’s Five-Point Consensus (5PC), along with “a series of escalating punitive steps” if the junta continues to defy the peace plan.

Regime leaders were barred from regional summits for failing to implement the April 2021 consensus, including an immediate end to violence and constructive dialogue with the opposition.

The regime largely ignored the 5PC before formally rejecting it in a July 2026 vote by its rubber-stamp parliament. However, it continues to pay lip service to the plan.

During his latest talks with ASEAN special envoy Theresa Lazaro in Naypyitaw in October, Foreign Minister Tin Maung Swe claimed the regime was implementing the 5PC “without compromising its national interests and sovereignty in accordance with its own roadmaps and objectives.”

The UN reports that at least 8,384 civilians have been killed by regime forces since the coup, in an escalating military campaign that has also left over 4 million displaced. Meanwhile, nearly 23,000 political prisoners remain in detention, including deposed democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi.

However, ASEAN members began bilateral engagement with the regime after it rebranded in civilian clothing in April following elections widely condemned as a sham. Since then, coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing has been invited on official visits to bloc members Laos, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia.

Both Malaysia—once a vocal critic of the regime—and Thailand drew widespread condemnation from rights groups for hosting the junta leader.

Both nations defended the visits as pragmatic re-engagement in search of solutions to challenges they face, such as refugee repatriation for Malaysia and transborder issues for Thailand.

Critics have warned that bi-lateral engagement may sway a collective ASEAN decision to reintegrate the regime.

However, the move to uphold the summit ban marks a major setback for a junta desperate for legitimacy on the international stage.

“This is a huge blow to the junta. I am sure it has not expected this kind of decision,” Khin Ohmar commented. “It also signals that the junta’s election farce failed to confer legitimacy, since even those advocating its return to the international stage want to avoid being seen as complicit in its violence.”

World.title: Myanmar Junta Seeks Record Military Budget as Millions Struggle With Poverty
World.content:
The Myanmar regime plans to increase the military budget to a record high for the 2026-27 fiscal year, even as approximately one-third of the country’s population lives in poverty.

Since 2021, the regime has been waging war against several established ethnic armed organizations as well as newly emerged resistance forces, including the People’s Defense Force, across the country, spending a large portion of its budget on military expenses.

Last Thursday, the regime’s rubber-stamp Union Parliament (Pyidaungsu Hluttaw), where the military-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party (USDP) and its allies hold a majority of seats, debated a supplementary budget allocation bill.

The proposed allocation would bring total defense spending to 10.53 trillion kyats (US$5.01 billion), combining the initial 2026-27 fiscal year estimate of 7.95 trillion kyats with a supplementary grant of 2.58 trillion kyats.
