Russia’s foreign ministry said Ukraine was responsible for the attack, but Baku did not publicly identify the party responsible.

Russia has so far made no official comment on the meeting between the Azerbaijani and Ukrainian presidents in Dublin.

What does Ukraine expect from Azerbaijan?

Alongside drone cooperation, Zelensky made another request concerning energy supplies. After meeting Aliyev, he wrote:

“We would be grateful if Azerbaijan could also find a way to support Ukraine’s critical infrastructure and logistics now, ahead of winter.”

Speaking at the summit the same day, Zelensky described energy support as one of Ukraine’s three main priorities:

“We need it now, in November, and throughout the winter.”

Zelensky also thanked Azerbaijani companies for continuing to operate in Ukraine despite Russian attacks. Azerbaijan has previously donated five electric buses to the city of Irpin and helped rebuild a school and a hospital.

During Bayramov’s visit in August, it was reported that Azerbaijan’s total humanitarian assistance to Ukraine had exceeded $50 million.

How long can Azerbaijan maintain this balance?

Following the meeting in Gabala, analysts described Azerbaijan’s foreign policy as “balanced” and “multi-vector”. Baku is signing defence agreements with Kyiv while simultaneously restoring relations with Moscow.

The Dublin meeting illustrates how this approach works: Kyiv speaks openly about military cooperation, while Baku’s official statements focus on economic ties and humanitarian assistance.

But as the scale of the contracts grows, maintaining this balance may become increasingly difficult.

World.title: Who runs Poland? Why the president and the government cannot agree
World.content:
Political crisis in Poland



A sharp political crisis has erupted in Poland. The president and the government are accusing each other of violating the Constitution, while the opposition is speaking of a coup. What is happening in a country that has become one of the main immigration hubs in Central Europe, and should foreigners be worried about their future there?

What happened in Warsaw

On October 30, police appeared outside the building of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal. Judges elected by the parliamentary majority but not sworn in by President Karol Nawrocki attempted to take up their duties. One of them, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, announced the removal of the tribunal’s president, Bogdan Święczkowski, and his deputy.

The tribunal’s leadership refused to recognise the legality of what was happening. Opposition supporters gathered outside the building, and a standoff with police began.

President Nawrocki, who was on his way to Senegal for an official visit, turned his plane around and returned to Warsaw. He went to the tribunal building and accused the government of attempting to seize control of a state institution.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk, by contrast, said the government intended to ensure that the Constitutional Tribunal could operate independently and lawfully.

The events of October 30–31 were reported by Reuters and Euroradio.

The word “coup” has once again entered Poland’s political debate. But is this really an attempt to seize power?

“If we are to say that a coup took place on Friday, then we must also say that it began back in 2015, when the struggle over the Constitutional Tribunal started to move beyond legal boundaries,” says Michał Potocki, a political commentator for the Polish newspaper Dziennik Gazeta Prawna, in an interview with Euroradio.

In his view, the events of October 30 are simply the latest episode in a conflict that has been going on for eleven years.

Why politicians are fighting for control of the constitutional tribunal

Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal reviews whether laws comply with the Constitution. Its rulings can constrain the actions of parliament and the government, making control over the institution politically significant.

The current crisis began in 2015, when the conservative Law and Justice party (PiS) came to power. Its judicial reforms sparked protests at home and a confrontation with the European Union. European institutions accused the Polish authorities of undermining judicial independence.

In 2023, a coalition led by Donald Tusk took office. It pledged to restore the independence of the courts and reverse controversial decisions made by its predecessors. But delivering on those promises proved difficult: initially, its initiatives were blocked by President Andrzej Duda and, since 2025, by Karol Nawrocki, who is politically aligned with PiS.

As a result, different branches of government are challenging the legality of one another’s actions.

“At its core, this is a struggle for control of the Constitutional Tribunal, which can either help the government or obstruct its legislative agenda,” Potocki says.

The expert, however, does not consider either side beyond reproach.

“Both sides have violated the Constitution. Law and Justice did so more often and to a greater extent. But, unfortunately, the Civic Coalition has its own share of wrongdoing,” he notes.

Polish legal experts have also raised questions about the methods used by Tusk’s government. As The Guardian reports, constitutional law specialists are divided over the legality of the decision to remove the tribunal’s president. Some critics of PiS also consider the legal grounds for the move questionable.

Could the crisis paralyse the state?

Despite the dramatic events in Warsaw, Poland is not yet facing a breakdown of its system of government.

According to Potocki, the Constitutional Tribunal has effectively been unable to function normally for about two years. Nevertheless, the country’s other state institutions continue to operate.

The danger lies elsewhere: prolonged confrontation is eroding public trust in the courts, politicians and the state itself.

The Constitutional Tribunal is supposed to act as an independent arbiter, resolving disputes over the legality of government actions. But when judges and politicians themselves challenge one another’s authority, that mechanism ceases to function.

Potocki notes that some Polish political forces are calling for a complete overhaul of the tribunal and the appointment of a new panel of judges through compromise. So far, however, no agreement has been reached.

That is why the current conflict matters not only to Polish politicians but also to the millions of people who live in the country and depend on decisions made by its public institutions.

What the political crisis means for migrants

In recent years, Poland has become one of the main immigration destinations in Central Europe. Hundreds of thousands of foreigners live and work there, including people from Ukraine, Belarus, Georgia and other countries. They include migrant workers, students, people who have moved for family reasons, and refugees who cannot safely return to their home countries.

To varying degrees, all of them depend on Polish state institutions: they apply for residence and work permits, renew their documents and seek international protection. A prolonged conflict between branches of government is therefore bound to cause concern.

However, the political crisis does not mean that migration services will stop operating or that foreigners will automatically lose their right to reside in Poland.

“This will have no direct impact, because the Constitutional Tribunal does not deal with the legalisation of residence, Pole’s Cards or other issues faced by citizens of Belarus and other countries,” Michał Potocki explains in an interview with Euroradio.

At the same time, Poland’s migration system was already under considerable strain before the current crisis.

As Euroradio reported, Olga Dobrovolska, a lawyer at the Belarusian Solidarity Centre, said that more than 190,000 applications for legalisation of foreigners’ residence were awaiting consideration in the Mazovian Voivodeship alone. The situation is also particularly difficult in the Lower Silesian and Pomeranian Voivodeships. The introduction of the MOS electronic application system has so far failed to reduce the queues.

For refugees, these difficulties are compounded by the question of international protection. According to Dobrovolska, Polish authorities assess applications individually, examining whether a person would face danger if they returned to their home country. References to political events from previous years alone may not be sufficient.

There is no direct link between these problems and the events surrounding the Constitutional Tribunal. But, as Potocki points out, a constitutional oversight body that is not functioning properly limits the opportunities to seek systemic solutions to problems involving violations of rights.

The expert cites lengthy delays in processing residence applications as an example. When statutory deadlines are not met, a properly functioning Constitutional Tribunal could potentially examine whether such practices comply with constitutional guarantees.

When the legitimacy of the tribunal itself is being contested, however, it becomes much harder to use this mechanism.

The main risk for migrants, therefore, is not the immediate loss of their documents or legal status, but the weakening of the legal safeguards intended to protect their interests in dealings with the state.

Who benefits from the conflict?

The political crisis in Poland is being actively exploited by Russian and Belarusian state propaganda.

As Euroradio reported, the events surrounding the Constitutional Tribunal have provided an opportunity to claim that a coup is supposedly taking place in the country.

According to Potocki, the propaganda campaign has several objectives. Above all, it seeks to portray Poland as a country engulfed in chaos and undermine public trust in democratic institutions.

Belarusian propaganda is also using the conflict to challenge Poland’s right to criticise violations of democracy in Belarus.

Another objective is to deepen divisions between Poland’s political camps, including by exploiting disagreements over Ukraine and relations with the European Union.

However, Potocki stresses that the Polish government and the president remain broadly aligned on fundamental issues concerning Russia and the need to support Ukraine. Their differences are primarily about political approaches and individual decisions.

What happens next?

Experts do not expect the crisis to be resolved quickly.

Parliamentary elections are due to take place in Poland in 2027. The confrontation between the ruling coalition and PiS is already becoming part of the election campaign, leaving politicians with fewer and fewer incentives to compromise.

“Unfortunately, I do not see much chance of a compromise. Polarisation in Poland will only intensify,” Potocki predicts.

For foreigners living in Poland, this means, above all, keeping an eye on government and parliamentary decisions that directly determine the rules governing residence, employment and state assistance.

For now, there are no grounds to claim that the conflict surrounding the Constitutional Tribunal threatens migrants’ right to remain in the country.

But Poland’s crisis illustrates a broader problem: even in a democratic state, political confrontation can weaken institutions for a prolonged period, undermining the mechanisms that protect human rights. For migrants, particularly refugees whose status often depends heavily on decisions made by the authorities, this has very practical implications.

World.title: Singer fined over song. What other forms of dissent can be punished in Georgia
World.content:
Singer in Georgia fined over song

Georgian singer Sofо Batilashvili has been fined 3,000 lari (about $1,150) for posting a video on social media of herself performing the song “Ole Ola”, which contains profanity directed at the ruling party. The ruling was issued by Judge Koba Chagunava.

After the hearing, Batilashvili told journalists that restrictions on forms of protest were becoming increasingly widespread in Georgia and that the issue had now extended to censorship of music.

“A year ago, it would have seemed absurd to arrest people for standing on the pavement. But now, in Georgia, we have reached a point where people are arrested for almost anything if they express resistance, take part in protests or show solidarity with protesters.

“We have reached a point where we could be handed a list of songs. They have already started drawing up lists of songs that cannot be performed. We are now dealing with censorship of musicians,” the singer said.

What happened

The song “Ole Ola”, which contains profanity directed at the ruling Georgian Dream party, has become an unofficial anthem of mass pro-European protests that have continued in Tbilisi for more than two years.

The protests began after Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze announced on November 28, 2024, that Georgia, which has EU candidate status, would put its EU accession process on hold until 2028.

Sopho Batilashvili is not the first person to face punishment for performing the song in public.

On October 7, activist Tornike Toshkhua and student Sandro Sekhniashvili were summoned to court over performing “Ole Ola” in the street.

Batilashvili posted her video on October 8.

In her accompanying post, she said she objected to people being summoned to court over a song and was posting the video in protest, at 10 p.m. – the time when participants in the pro-European protests sing “Ole Ola” at rallies.

“People are being prosecuted in Georgia in 2026 over this song – I repeat, over a song. And I, who got tired of ‘Ole Ola’ a long time ago and have not even felt like humming it for years, suddenly decided: here you go,” Batilashvili wrote.

In her post, she also expressed solidarity with Georgian musician Kordz, the author of “Ole Ola”, who has openly opposed the authorities and faced attacks and threats from municipal officials, members of the ruling Georgian Dream party and pro-government media.

Kordz, whose real name is Aleksandre Kordzaia, has reported twice that attempts had been made to attack him.

As a result, the Kamara music festival in the town of Gori, where Kordz was due to perform, had to be postponed indefinitely in September. The organiser, the Danish Cultural Institute, said it considered it unsafe to hold the event.

In her Facebook post, Batilashvili stressed the importance of society refusing to accept such treatment of people.

“I know that many things have become normalised. I also know how people turn against you if you speak out. But we must remind ourselves that treating people this way is not normal, and that we still have each other’s backs. Otherwise, there is simply no point,” she wrote.

Unprecedented case

The fine imposed on Sopho Batilashvili may be considered an unprecedented case in Georgia.

One notable international parallel is Russia. In 2025, members of the band Stoptime were arrested in St Petersburg for performing songs by musicians critical of the Ukrainian and Russian authorities in public.

The band’s lead singer, Diana Loginova, known as Naoko, was fined on charges of “discrediting the Russian armed forces”, while the musicians were placed in administrative detention several times.

From social media to pavements: Georgia’s crackdown on protests

Since late 2024, the government led by Georgian Dream has tightened administrative and criminal legislation several times. As a result, people have faced penalties both for taking part in protests and for criticising government officials on social media.

● In February 2025, parliament added a new provision, Article 173, Part 16, to the Code of Administrative Offences. It defines verbal insults, abusive language and offensive behaviour towards state and political officials, civil servants and people holding equivalent positions as administrative offences.

The penalties range from a fine of 1,500 lari (about $600) to 4,000 lari (about $1,500), or administrative detention for up to 45 days.

The provision was soon used against people who posted statements and comments on Facebook criticising the government. In 2026, monitoring of social media posts became even more active.

● According to Human Rights Watch, a special unit set up within the interior ministry had referred around 300 cases of alleged administrative offences to the courts by August 2026.

● The legislative crackdown also extended to street protests. Amendments adopted in October 2025 increased penalties for obstructing roads and banned protesters from covering their faces. In some cases, fines were replaced with administrative detention, while repeat offences became subject to criminal prosecution.

● Further amendments adopted on December 12, 2025, extended restrictions to pavements and pedestrian areas. Under the new rules, organisers must notify the interior ministry in advance if an assembly or demonstration obstructs pedestrian movement.

Police were given broad powers to demand that protesters change the location or route of a gathering. Failure to comply can result in administrative detention of up to 15 days for participants and up to 20 days for organisers. Repeat violations may lead to criminal prosecution.

After the amendments came into force, police began detaining people standing on pavements and treating them as participants in protest rallies.

● Human rights organisations say the legislative changes disproportionately restrict freedom of assembly and expression and have become a tool for punishing peaceful protesters.

Human Rights Watch’s 2026 World Report also says that the human rights situation in Georgia has deteriorated sharply and that the government is using administrative and criminal measures to suppress critical voices.

World.title: Azerbaijan recovers $62.8M through state financial controls
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. Azerbaijan’s State Financial Control Service recovered 106.9 million manats ($62.88 million) and prevented 100.9 million manats ($59.35 million) in expenditure following inspections conducted in January-September 2026, according to a report by the Ministry of Finance.

The report said the service completed inspections at 84 organizations during the nine-month period.

Of these, 52 organizations were inspected on the basis of decisions received from law enforcement agencies, while the remaining 32 underwent scheduled inspections.

Meanwhile, financial assessments of public investment and infrastructure projects are being carried out under an action plan to improve the efficiency of public investment projects in Azerbaijan’s liberated territories.

The assessments aim to ensure the efficient implementation of projects and compliance with execution discipline, promote the economical use of public funds, optimize project scope and strengthen preventive oversight.

A total of 91 projects have been submitted for financial assessment. Assessments of 59 projects have been completed, while work on the remaining 32 is ongoing. The combined value of the 59 projects that have completed the assessment process stands at 1.038 billion manats ($610.59 million).

The financial assessments cover the prices of goods, materials and equipment, as well as costs related to labor, machinery and mechanisms. In particular, the process identifies discrepancies between costs included in project estimates and applicable standards and prevailing market prices.

World.title: Azerbaijan Railways passenger traffic rises 19%, cargo 13% (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. In the period from January through October 2026, Azerbaijan Railways CJSC (ADY) transported 9.8 million passengers and 15.7 million metric tons of cargo; compared to the same period last year, passenger traffic increased by 19%, and cargo traffic by 13%.

According to Azerbaijan Railways, this information was presented at a meeting between the company’s management and experts in the fields of public transportation, international transport corridors, logistics, and tourism.

In addition, it was noted that more than 1.3 million passengers were transported in October, marking the highest monthly passenger count on record. Daily passenger traffic on the Absheron Circular Railway route has increased from 36,000 to 52,000 people over the past two years.

The meeting included a presentation on the restoration of the Baku–Balaken and Baku–Aghdam routes, the extension of the Baku–Agstafa route to Gazakh, the organization of daily passenger service on the Ganja–Gabala route, and the resumption of the Baku–Tbilisi–Baku international rail service.

In addition, discussions focused on reducing passenger volume (passenger density) in Absheron, optimizing the schedule, upgrading infrastructure along the Khirdalan route, and improving the Baku–Khirdalan–Sumgayit and Baku–Pirsaghi–Sumgayit lines. Information was also provided regarding work being carried out to restore new commuter lines and the procurement of 20 new passenger trains.

At the meeting, it was noted that transit freight volume had increased by 20% over the first 10 months of this year. As a result of the modernization of the Baku–Tbilisi–Kars railway, the line’s annual capacity was increased from 1 million to 5 million metric tons.

At the Baku Port, container transshipment volumes rose by 31% from January through October, totaling more than 112,000 TEU. It was emphasized that this is a record figure.

During the meeting, participants exchanged views on the development of the Middle Corridor and the North–South International Transport Corridor, the construction of the Horadiz–Aghband railway line, the construction of the Astara Terminal, and the expansion of the Baku Port's capacity.

Rovshan Rustamov, Chairman of the Azerbaijan Railways, stated that increasing passenger satisfaction, improving service quality, and ensuring safe and sustainable transportation are among the top priorities.

The discussions also addressed issues related to improving digital services, eliminating “bottlenecks” in the logistics chain, expanding the railcar fleet, simplifying border crossing procedures, and the role of rail transport in the development of tourism.

World.title: Azerbaijan showcases Livable Baku project at COP31 in Türkiye (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. Azerbaijan has presented the Livable Baku project at the 31st session of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, the Ministry of Economy reported.

According to the report, the ministry organized a panel discussion titled "From Cleanup to Livable Cities: Azerbaijan’s Livable Baku Model and Shared Green Priorities in the Region" at the Azerbaijani Pavilion during COP31.

Asgar Alakbarov, Advisor to the Minister of Economy, participated in the discussions and highlighted the importance of efforts aimed at strengthening the environmental sustainability of cities, restoring contaminated areas, and creating more favorable living environments, while also sharing Azerbaijan’s experience in this field. He also addressed the application of a comprehensive approach in this area, as well as opportunities for mitigating the impacts of climate change and expanding regional cooperation.

During the event, information was presented regarding the Livable Baku project, which is currently being developed in collaboration with the World Bank. The significance of the project was underscored in terms of waste management, the restoration of polluted lakes and land areas, the improvement of the ecological situation, and the development of a sustainable urban environment.

Information concerning the "Livable Baku" project was also showcased at the Azerbaijani Pavilion.

World.title: Uzbekistan discovers gas well with 300,000-cubic-meter daily potential
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. Uzbekistan has discovered a new commercially viable natural gas flow at the Kultak field in the Kashkadarya region, with exploratory well No. 39R recording an initial estimated production rate of 300,000 cubic meters per day, according to Uzbekneftegaz.

The gas flow was obtained ahead of a visit to the region by the chairman of the company's board.

The discovery marks progress in exploration at a field that has been in operation for decades. The Kultak field was discovered in 1963 and brought into production in 1978. Despite nearly 50 years of industrial gas production, ongoing geological exploration has identified additional wells capable of producing commercially viable volumes of natural gas.

Well No. 39R was drilled at a location selected based on the processing and analysis of data from the Alan 3D seismic exploration project. Drilling began on September 1, 2026, and reached a depth of 3,020 meters.

During testing, the well produced a commercially significant gas flow from carbonate Jurassic deposits at depths of 2,868 to 3,020 meters.

Further studies are underway to determine the reservoir's natural characteristics and conduct gas-dynamic and gas-condensate assessments. The company noted that the reported daily production rate is preliminary and may be revised after these tests are completed.

During his visit to the well, the chairman emphasized the importance of preparing it for operation and incorporating its output into the country's existing production figures as soon as possible.

Exploration at the Kultak field is continuing beyond well No. 39R. Drilling is underway at exploratory well No. 40R, while work has also begun at well No. 41R. The company plans to start drilling well No. 42R by the end of 2026.

World.title: US discusses Central and South Asia policy priorities with UK officials
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. The United States has discussed its policy priorities in South and Central Asia with UK officials, regional experts and business leaders during meetings in London, according to a post by the US Department of State’s Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs on its X account.

The meetings focused on US engagement with South and Central Asia and brought together representatives of the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), regional specialists and business leaders.

“Last week in London, I met with representatives from the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office and engaged with South and Central Asia experts and business leaders to discuss US policy priorities in the region,” S. Paul Kapur, Assistant Secretary of the US Department of State’s Bureau of South and Central Asian Affairs, said.

The United Kingdom has maintained a diplomatic presence in all five Central Asian countries for more than three decades, with embassies in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. This network provides London with direct access to regional governments and local developments.

The FCDO also holds regular strategic consultations with Central Asian governments, covering political, security, economic and trade issues.

London has also developed a network of institutions and specialists focused on the region. These include the Russia and Eurasia Program at Chatham House, whose researchers examine Central Asia's domestic developments and foreign policy, as well as its relations with Russia, China and Western countries.

In September 2026, the International Institute for Central Asia, London-based ODI Global and the British Embassy in Uzbekistan jointly organized the first Central Asia-UK Think Tank Forum in Tashkent. The event brought together more than 100 representatives of think tanks, diplomatic missions, international organizations, businesses and academic institutions to discuss transport connectivity, critical minerals, investment and other areas of cooperation.

World.title: Iran reports downing of US-owned MQ-1 drone in Hormozgan
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. A US-owned MQ-1 unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) has been shot down by a new Iranian Navy air defense system in Kuhestak, Sirik County, in Iran's southern Hormozgan Province, according to the public relations department of the Iranian army.

"A few hours ago, a US-owned MQ-1 UAV was shot down and destroyed by fire from a new air defense system belonging to the Iranian Navy," the report said.

The Iranian army stated that it would take all necessary measures to protect the country's territorial integrity, maritime borders and national interests.

The incident comes amid renewed escalation of tensions between the United States and Iran, which intensified on July 8. On that day, US forces launched several waves of strikes against Iranian territory, saying they were responding to an attack on a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes marked the first US military action against Iran since the signing of a memorandum between Washington and Tehran.

On the same day, US President Donald Trump announced the termination of the ceasefire with Iran. In response, Tehran began striking US facilities in Bahrain, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

The conflict has brought maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz to a standstill.

World.title: bp expects ACG oil output to rise by year-end despite natural decline
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. Oil production at the Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli (ACG) field is expected to increase by the end of 2026 compared to the beginning of the year, despite the natural decline in production at mature fields, Vice President for Subsurface in Azerbaijan, Georgia, and Türkiye at bp, Dan Sparkes, said, Trend's correspondent reports.

He made the remark during the information session “Supporting Production from ACG: New Approaches and Technology,” held as part of the SOCAR and bp Energy Dialogue Platform on Friday.

According to him, the potential for further increasing investment in drilling is constrained by inherent operational conditions.

"With simultaneous well-intervention work and drilling operations underway, and all available drilling rigs already in use, it is not possible to rapidly increase the number of rigs and platforms," Sparkes said.

He noted that, as a result, companies have focused on enhancing productivity.

"Efforts are being directed along two paths: increasing the number of wells drilled annually using the existing rig fleet, and extending the length of the reservoir sections penetrated by each well.

To achieve this, new well designs have been developed to improve drilling efficiency and expand access to productive reservoir zones. Specifically, technologies are being employed that allow the wellbore to be steered along the reservoir, tracking its productive interval and adjusting the drilling trajectory in real time," Sparkes said.

He pointed out that the drilling of horizontal and multilateral wells is one example of this approach. The company first successfully tested the technology over sections spanning several hundred meters, before drilling a well with a 1,000-meter horizontal section within the reservoir.

"Subsequently, the technology was applied in a more complex, previously untapped area of the field, where the length of the reservoir section reached 2,000 meters. This well has become one of the most productive at ACG in over a decade," he added.

Sparkes explained that these productivity gains are driven by a combination of new drilling technologies, longer reservoir penetration, and insights from 4D seismic surveys, which help identify areas where oil remains following earlier stages of development.

According to him, the number of wellbore intervals drilled within productive formations this year has increased by approximately 50% compared to last year. He remarked that the company has managed to simultaneously increase both the number of such intervals and the total length of the reservoir sections penetrated.

He also informed that, thanks to the measures taken, the rate of natural production decline at the ACG field complex has been reduced from approximately 12% to 3%.

"Having managed to reduce the production decline rate from about 12% to 3%, it appears that we’ll finish the year at ACG with higher production levels than we started with. This is an incredible result for a mature field," Sparkes highlighted.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Azerbaijan plan joint environmental projects for 2027–2029
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 13. Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan discussed developing a portfolio of joint environmental projects for 2027–2029, focusing on water resource management, air quality, waste management, and the environmental aspects of the Central Asia–Azerbaijan energy corridor, on November 13.

According to Uzbekistan's National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change, the discussions took place on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, on Friday.

The meeting brought together Aziz Abdukhakimov, Adviser to the President of Uzbekistan on Environmental Issues and Chairman of the National Committee on Ecology and Climate Change, and Azerbaijan's Minister of Ecology and Natural Resources, Rashad Ismayilov.

The sides discussed shared environmental and climate challenges and explored opportunities to strengthen bilateral cooperation through joint initiatives.

Particular attention was paid to the shrinking Aral Sea and declining water levels in the Caspian Sea, which have contributed to desertification, soil degradation, salinization and an increase in sand, dust and salt storms. The participants noted that, despite differences in scale and geographical conditions, both countries face similar environmental threats that require coordinated regional responses.

Abdukhakimov outlined Uzbekistan's efforts to restore ecosystems in the Aral Sea region, noting that protective forest plantations have been established across more than 2 million hectares of the dried seabed.

He also presented a proposal to establish a regional research center for combating desertification at Green University in Uzbekistan. The planned center would include 15 specialized laboratories, a digital monitoring system using satellite data and geographic information systems (GIS), and a genetic bank of drought-resistant plants.

The parties also discussed a potential joint initiative to protect inland seas and other water bodies affected by declining water levels. The proposed cooperation could include data exchange, joint environmental monitoring, restoration of coastal and dried-up areas, and coordinated engagement on international platforms.

Uzbekistan invited Azerbaijani scientists to participate in research activities at the planned center, including field studies, monitoring of the Aral Sea's dried seabed and the development of early warning systems for dust storms.

Another focus was coordination of their positions at COP31, particularly on climate change adaptation and expanding access to climate financing for landlocked developing countries.

At the end of the meeting, Abdukhakimov invited Azerbaijan to participate in the Eco Expo Central Asia 2027 international exhibition, scheduled to take place in Tashkent on June 15–17, 2027. He also invited the Azerbaijani delegation to visit Uzbekistan and Green University.

World.title: Spectacular try helps England to Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup glory
World.content:
England is Wheelchair Rugby League World champion for a third time after triumphing in a fiery, exhilarating final against France in Wollongong.

A spectacular try on the cusp of half-time proved pivotal for the English, with superstar Jack Brown rolling half the length of the pitch to collect a perfectly weighted Rob Hawkins kick and put his side ahead.

England kept the advantage for most of a hotly contested second half before surging clear late to triumph 50-38 and prompt a rousing rendition of the English sporting anthem Three Lions.

Earlier, Australia's Wheelaroos finished their campaign on a high, beating Ireland 70-24 in the third-place play-off.

Brown's superb effort came after a topsy-turvy first-half between wheelchair rugby league's two great powers, who have now combined for all five World Cup titles to date.

England raced to a 10-0 lead within the first 10 minutes, but was pegged back quickly, with French livewire Leo Hivernat scoring a try and providing a brilliant no-look pass to set up Damien Dore.

Tempers flared in the first period when England's Mason Billington shoved Hivernat to the ground, prompting a mid-court coming-together between the two teams.

Being a non-disabled player in elite wheelchair sport Leading out Australia at this month's Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup will be a dream come true for Bayley McKenna, the Wheelaroos first non-disabled skipper.

A flurry of quick points followed for the French, but England eventually regained its composure, with Hawkins levelling things up in the right corner before setting up Brown in the half's dying moments.

France's Dany Denuwelaer crossed for a second-half hat-trick, but England proved too strong, with Brown scoring twice to complete his treble and Joe Coyd finishing with four tries.

Wheelaroos finish campaign on a high

Still licking their wounds from the 86-18 loss to England in Tuesday's semifinal, the Wheelaroos were out to finish their campaign on a high against an Irish side ranked one place ahead of them in the world rankings.

And Australia raced out of the blocks in the evening's curtain raiser, with Cory Cannane crossing within a minute and Toby Popple completing a quickfire double to have the tournament hosts 16-0 ahead after just seven minutes of play.

Ireland's Cian Horgan proceeded to hit back barely 60 seconds later, but his four-pointer would prove to be Australia's only concession in a dominant first half.

Wheelaroos captain Bayley McKenna was a surprise omission from coach Brett Clark's starting five, but returned early on to score his ninth try of the competition as the Australians reached the break with a 36-point advantage.

Ireland's Oran Spain, forced to rely on the kindness of an Irish tourist to replace a wheelchair broken on the eve of the tournament, suffered a heavy first-period fall but returned after half-time to score his side's second try in an improved showing from his side.

However, McKenna continued to influence the game, providing a deft assist for Daniel Anstey before tumbling over for two late tries to complete both his hat-trick and Australia's 70-24 victory.

Anstey also finished with a treble as the Wheelaroos secured a third-place finish, their equal, second-best finish in tournament history.

World.title: Floreat gunman's daughter condemns 'entitled' father intent on control
World.content:
The daughter of a gunman who murdered two women in one of Western Australia's most horrific cases of family violence has delivered a powerful apology at the inquest into their deaths, condemning him as a "powerful, privileged entitled man" intent on control and revenge.

WARNING: This story contains details that may distress some readers.

Jennifer Petelczyc, 59, and her daughter Gretl, 18, were killed by Mark Bombara as he stormed their home in the Perth suburb of Floreat in May 2024, in pursuit of his estranged wife, Rowena.

Bombara then turned the gun on himself.

His daughter Ariel told the inquest her father was a "devious, ruthless manipulator" who when he could not find his wife, decided murdering her best friend "would be the next best punishment".

"I am so sorry that some feel the need to excuse his behaviour as medical or mental health issues, as opposed to acknowledging that these were planned choices he made to murder," Ariel Bombara told the court.

"Killing her [Rowena Bombara] was the only thing that would have truly satisfied him.

Jennifer and Gretl Petelczyc were shot dead by Mark Bombara at their Floreat home. (Supplied)

"Make no mistake; he viewed her as his property and, [medical] strokes or not, in my opinion, he never would've let mum leave him without a death penalty."

Warnings unheeded

Ms Bombara addressed Liesl Petelczyc, Jennifer's daughter and Gretl's sister, who was sitting in the public gallery.

Liesl was out at a babysitting job when Bombara stormed her family home.

"Your mum and sister did not deserve to be killed," she said.

"I am so sorry, Liesl, that so many people let you and your family down."

Ariel Bombara tried to warn police at least four times that her father was a real and imminent threat and had access to firearms, when she helped her mum escape the family home, weeks before the murders.

The inquest continues into the Floreat murder-suicide. (ABC News: Ruby Littler)

Appropriate action was not taken, according to an internal police investigation, and eight officers have since faced disciplinary action.

"I would do anything to go back and scream "fit and proper" into the faces of a hundred police officers, hoping that one would finally believe us; help us; and take his lethal weapons away," Ms Bombara said.

Ariel Bombara says her father was a "devious, ruthless manipulator". (ABC News: Lucy Murray)

"I have thought about these events every single day for the last two and a half years, wondering what more I could've done to convince everyone of the danger, and knowing that for the rest of my life I will feel like I pulled the pin on the grenade that landed on someone else's family.

"I am so sorry to my mum for not being able to protect her from him better … I am so sorry that she had to hear her best friend be murdered by her abusive husband over the phone.

"Her scream after hearing those shots, and her wails long after that Triple Zero call ended, are sounds that will haunt me for the rest of my life."

Tribute to a best friend

Speaking publicly for the first time since the murders, Rowena Bombara told the court she was heartbroken at the loss of her best friend Jennifer Petelczyc, and Jennifer's daughter Gretl.

Gunman recorded himself during shooting, inquest hears The inquest into the deaths of Jennifer and Gretl Petelcyzc hears new details about the day they died and the gunman's interactions with police weeks before the shooting.

She said Gretl "had a wonderful sense of humour and her whole life ahead of her".

She also spoke of her fear of her husband.

"I knew what would happen if Mark found me," she said.

"That's why I deliberately never stayed with Jenny in her home.

"I am heartbroken."

The court has issued suppression orders preventing media outlets publishing images of Rowena Bombara and Liesl Petelczyc.

Floreat double-murderer Mark Bombara. (Supplied)

Acting state coroner Sarah Linton said there was "not a dry eye" in the room at the conclusion of her statement, adding she did not have "the words to express her sorrow" for the families involved.

The findings are expected to be handed down next year.

World.title: Prisoner who bolted from brother's funeral caught after months on the run
World.content:
A prisoner who escaped custody while attending his brother's funeral in Melbourne's north-west seven months ago has been arrested in Far North Queensland.

Orijol Rukaj, 47, was on remand at Marngoneet Correctional Centre, near Geelong, when he was escorted to Keilor Cemetery on April 25.

Despite wearing handcuffs and helping carry the casket, Rukaj was able to escape from the service.

Police said there was about 300 people at the funeral.

After almost seven months on the run, Rukaj was arrested in Bamaga, near Cape York, on Friday.

Police said he was in custody and Queensland and would be interviewed in the coming days.

Police will seek to extradite him back to Victoria.

World.title: Teens committed to trial over alleged murder of Sunshine Coast soccer coach
World.content:
Two Sunshine Coast teenagers charged with fatally stabbing a man in his home last year have been committed to face a jury trial in the Supreme Court in Brisbane.

They are charged with murdering 57-year-old soccer coach Zdravko Bilic at his Warana home in July 2025.

A 15-year-old West Woombye boy was arrested in Brisbane, while a 17-year-old Beerwah boy was arrested disembarking a bus in Toowoomba, before being charged with murder on July 17, 2025.

Now 16 and 18, the teens faced Maroochydore Children's Court on Friday.

Neither entered a plea nor made applications for bail.

Zdravko Bilic was fatally stabbed at his home in July 2025. (ABC Sunshine Coast: Owen Jacques)

The 18-year-old's lawyer Simon Lewis questioned four witnesses, three police officers, and a justice of the peace (JP).

Mr Lewis asked why his Indigenous client was not provided with the opportunity to talk to a support person of his choice on the evening he was arrested.

Mr Lewis told the court that police should have contacted his parents or guardians first, then family or a friend, before calling a support person from a list available at the police station.

The JP, who was at the Toowoomba watchhouse that evening as a support person, told the court he should have been a "last resort" for the officers.

The two Sunshine Coast teenagers charged cannot be identified under Queensland law. (Supplied: Queensland Police)

The court heard that at some stage while the teen was in the watchhouse he spoke on the phone with a legal representative from the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Legal Service (ATSILS) in Maroochydore.

Police told the court the teen was questioned twice that night: once after 10pm and another time just before midnight.

The lead arresting and interviewing Sunshine Coast officer told the court he was aware the 18-year-old's parents were in custody and unavailable but believed a JP was "appropriate" as a support person.

Zdravko Bilic was known as "Coach Zed". (Supplied: Ginger Sport)

The teenager was not given the opportunity to speak with the JP alone without police, the court heard.

The senior constable admitted he was unaware of the hierarchy of support persons for an Indigenous minor, and that he did not know there was a list at the Toowoomba Police Station.

"That's a gap in my knowledge," he told the court.

The second teenager's lawyer, Adrian Braithwaite, questioned three witnesses.

Media were excluded from the cross-examining of the first witness.

The second witness was an interviewing police officer, and the third a support person.

Zdravko Bilic with his wife Gry Tømte. (Supplied)

The court heard the teenager asked to make a phone call, but police said he could not until the next morning, after the interview, because the person he wanted to call was underage.

The court heard he wanted to tell her that he loved her.

Police promised he could call her in the morning after the police interview.

The court heard the teen was given a support person who sat in the interview with him and was able to speak with him alone during the two interview breaks, the second being about 1am.

Police told the court they attempted to call a legal aid hotline for juveniles but because it was outside hours there was no answer.

The support person told the court that during the police interview breaks she gave words of comfort, asked the boy to tell the truth, and promised to sit with him throughout the process and the rest of his life.

She agreed that during the last break the accused told her he was going to tell police what they wanted to hear so he could call the underage girl.

The public prosecutions office will set the trial date.

World.title: Accused killer allegedly used phone while he said he was sleeping, jury hears
World.content:
A former Queensland RAAF pilot accused of killing his wife, allegedly "interacted" with his phone during the time he told investigators he was sleeping and she accidentally died, a jury has heard.

Robert Crawford is on trial in Brisbane charged over the murder of 49-year-old Frances Crawford in Upper Lockyer in July 2024.

The 49-year-old has pleaded not guilty, and maintains his wife died in a tragic accident.

A Supreme Court jury has already heard Mr Crawford called Triple Zero (000) in the early hours to report he found Ms Crawford trapped underneath their ride on lawnmower at the bottom of a retaining wall.

He told officers he had been asleep at the time when he believed his wife was fatally injured trying to move the machine away from sprinklers, the jury has heard.

Robert Crawford says his Frances Crawford's death was a tragic accident. (ABC News: Tara Cassidy)

On the final day of prosecution evidence, an investigative computer analyst from the Queensland Police Service took the witness stand.

Sean Dalton detailed to the jury how he analysed data extracted from both phones and explained the tests he carried out.

For Mr Crawford's phone, he told the jury he was asked to analyse usage between 1:09am to 3:20am.

"I developed a hypothesis being that the mobile phone was manually interacted with during the time periods," he said.

The jury heard according to Mr Dalton's analysis, Mr Crawford's phone was unlocked at 1:09am, 1:50am, twice at 2:35am and finally at 3:20am.

His analysis found all five times the phone was unlocked, the Signal messenger application was open, the jury heard.

The jury heard the independent testing could not conclude what was being done within the application.

Investigative computer analyst Sean Dalton told the court his testing was "incredibly clinical". (ABC News: Talissa Siganto)

However the jury heard the analysis did show Mr Crawford's phone keyboard was last accessed at 12:35am.

Mr Dalton said there were limitations to his findings.

"My testing is incredibly clinical, very structured," he said.

The jury heard the analysis of Ms Crawford's phone showed an exchange of messages between her and one of her sons from 6:31pm until 7:44pm.

At 9:23pm, a message was received on Ms Crawford's phone from her other son, whose conversation had been previously muted, the jury heard.

The analysis the jury heard showed that message was not opened until the following morning.

The house where Frances Crawford was found dead in 2024. (Queensland Police Service)

At 11:20pm, the jury heard Ms Crawford's phone was unlocked, and one minute later a signal message was sent to Mr Crawford's phone.

The jury has already heard that message said "hey are you going to put mower away soon?".

At 11:22pm, the jury heard Mr Crawford made a call to a work colleague which ended at 11:25pm.

Between 11:24 and 11:26pm, the jury has already heard Ms Crawford's phone received three messages from Mr Crawford's phone.

In them he explained he was dealing with a work issue, asked her to "wait a sec", and suggested she turn the sprinklers off, the jury heard.

At 11:26pm, the jury heard the analysis showed Ms Crawford's phone was locked, and was not accessed again until 4:45am, when the screen's back light was activated.

The jury has already heard the final messages from Mr Crawford were sent to his wife's phone about an hour later, in which he asked her to come to bed, and the analysis showed they were not opened until the following morning.

Prosecutors allege the messages sent and received after 11:21pm between both phones were authored by Mr Crawford, in a bid to set the scene that his wife died in an accident.

Mr Crawford has denied using his phone after sending his last message at 12:35pm.

The prosecution closed has now closed its case, and the defence has opened its.

They are expected to call three expert witnesses when the trial continues next week.

World.title: Australia's next fast bowling star blows England away on ODI debut
World.content:
Mahli Beardman has stamped his reputation as the next big thing in Australian cricket by slicing his way through England during a memorable ODI debut in Perth.

On a day when Australian cricket was still knee-deep dealing with the ghosts of Sandpapergate, Beardman snared 6–24 as England was skittled for 131 in 33.4 overs at Perth Stadium.

Australia chased the runs down with ease, led by captain Mitch Marsh's explosive 50 from 30 balls at the top of the order.

The 21-year-old Beardman was nearly unplayable at times, with England collapsing from 2–38 to 7–60 on the back of Beardman's burst.

It marked just the second time an Australian has produced a five-wicket haul in their ODI debut, following on from Tony Dodemaide's haul of 5–21 against Sri Lanka at the WACA Ground in 1988.

Only some late handy runs from Gus Atkinson (29 not out off 32 balls) and Will Jacks (25) ensured England made it to triple figures, with the visitors 8–65 at one stage.

"It all happened very quickly," Beardman told Fox Cricket when asked about his big haul.

"It's just a great privilege and honour to be able to represent my country. And to go out and take a few wickets as well is the cherry on top.

"Harry Brook was a nice wicket to get off the mark. Anytime you get your first one it's a weight off your shoulders, so that was awesome."

The right-arm paceman snared his first ODI wicket in his second over when he found the edge of England captain Brook (1).

Hitting speeds of up to 145.4 kilometres per hour, Beardman was able to entice 200-game milestone man Joe Root (17 off 36 balls) to drive on the up to gift wicketkeeper Josh Inglis his third catch of the innings.

And Beardman was on a hat-trick when he collected the scalp of Jordan Cox at the start of his fourth over — again with another pearler of a delivery that caught the edge.

Sam Curran's attempted pull off Beardman's bouncer gave Adam Zampa a catch on the boundary rope and Beardman his fourth wicket.

And Beardman's five-wicket haul was complete when Liam Dawson was caught at gully, giving the West Australian figures of 5–13 off 4.4 overs at that point.

Spencer Johnson (3–42) ensured the party continued by jumping high in the air to pull off a one-handed catch off his own bowling to send Jamie Overton packing.

Atkinson and Jofra Archer (11) struck a series of boundaries in a 29-run last-wicket stand before Beardman completed the demolition job by having Archer caught at gully.

Beardman's figures were the fourth best by a debutant in ODI world cricket, with Charlie Cassell's effort of 7–21 for Scotland against Oman in 2024 still the best.

Marsh's early burst made sure the result was never in doubt for Australia, despite Travis Head being bowled for a golden duck by Gus Atkinson.

Marsh hit a series of enormous sixes in a thrilling but brief knock, before Cooper Connolly (27), Matt Renshaw (26*) and Josh Inglis (23*) helped steer Australia home in just the 24th over.

The ABC of SPORT Sports content to make you think... or allow you not to. A newsletter delivered each Saturday.

ABC/AAP

World.title: Man who burned shoebox of tax records fined for resulting bushfire
World.content:
A Tasmanian man has been fined for lighting a fire that destroyed two houses and burnt through 1,200 hectares of vegetation in the state's upper east coast.

Michael John Davis, 56, was found guilty in the Launceston Magistrates Court this week of lighting a fire on December 9 last year without taking reasonable precautions to prevent it from spreading.

He also pleaded guilty to a low-range drink-driving charge.

The bushfire at Stieglitz could be seen across the water from St Helens. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

According to his lawyer, James Oxley, Davis could not appear in person as he lives in Indonesia, and so appeared via videolink.

The prosecution said on December 9, 2025, Mr Davis was at his parents' property burning a shoebox filled with tax records inside a fire pit while smoking cigarettes.

Davis sat with the fire until the box had burnt completely, then went inside to prepare lunch for his father, who was bedridden at the time.

The December 9 bushfire was captured by a NASA satellite. (Supplied: NASA/MODIS)

When he went back outside 30 minutes later, he discovered bushland on the northern boundary of the home, metres from where he burnt the receipts, was on fire.

Davis attempted to extinguish the fire with buckets of water and asked his mother to call the fire brigade when she returned home.

The fire had spread through bushland to the north, and as a result, two residences on St Helens Point Road were destroyed.

TasNetworks and Telstra infrastructure were also damaged as a result of the fire.

Mr Oxley said he confirmed with the Tasmania Fire Service that a total fire ban had not been issued on the day, and no fire permits were required in that area.

He said the total number of documents burnt had fit into a shoebox, and that the fire was not large.

"At its most intense it was about a foot high (30 centimetres) while the documents burned," Mr Oxley said.

"He did everything he could once he saw the fire had spread to put it out."

The bushfire sent plumes of smoke over St Helens. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Concerns over visa status

Mr Oxley asked Magistrate Simon Brown to consider Davis' visa status in his decision, and asked for Davis to be fined without a conviction, as that could hamper his chances at renewing his visa with the Indonesian government.

"That process will involve him producing his Tasmanian record to the Indonesian government," he said.

"His plan is to remain there with his wife for the foreseeable future, and in my submission there is a real risk that this could come back to haunt him in that application process."

Two houses were destroyed in the blaze at Stieglitz. (Supplied: John Sullivan)

However, Magistrate Brown said there had been "catastrophic consequences" as a result of Davis' negligence.

"In fairness, I don't think I'm minded to not convict," he said.

"I accept the defendant's degree of negligence. His moral culpability here is plainly at the lower end of the scale.

"Of course, lighting a fire outside in Tasmania in the summer months in December is something that should be done with real care.

"Whilst the defendant did watch the fire and believed it to be out, he took no steps to ensure it could go absolutely nowhere by wetting down or stamping on it."

Magistrate Brown convicted Davis and fined him $1,000 for the drink driving charge, as well as suspended his licence for six months.

He was fined $2,000 in relation to the fire, totalling $3,000.

World.title: Hung jury in trial of man accused of Busselton 'love triangle' murder
World.content:
The jury in the trial of a man accused of murdering a woman whose body was found stuffed in a wardrobe at a house in WA’s South West has been unable to reach a verdict.

WARNING: The following story contains details that may distress some readers.

James Anthony Sorgiovanni, 29, had been on trial for the murder of Tara Morrison, whose body was found in his Busselton house in 2024.

Ms Morrison had been visiting the house Mr Sorgiovanni shared with his girlfriend Hannah Louise Glover, who had also been charged with murder but pleaded guilty part-way through the trial.

Her guilty plea followed the evidence of an inmate who said Glover — who was formerly Ms Morrison's girlfriend — had confessed to the killing in prison.

A court sketch of Hannah Louise Glover and James Anthony Sorgiovanni, (ABC News: Anne Barnetson)

The court was earlier told Ms Morrison was killed in a frenzied attack arising from a “love triangle”.

The jury started deliberating on Monday afternoon but after days of discussing the case, could not reach a unanimous verdict on the charge of murder and was discharged today.

Stabbed multiple times

Glover gave evidence describing how she stabbed her former girlfriend multiple times, in several locations inside the house she shared with Mr Sorgiovanni.

She told the jury Mr Sorgiovanni held Ms Morrison while Glover attacked her, but that he was the last one to stab the victim.

The court had heard Ms Morrison was planning to stay at the house, and methylamphetamine and GHB were used on the night of the murder.

James Sorgiovanni’s defence lawyer, Lisa Boston. (ABC News: David Weber)

Mr Sorgiovanni’s lawyer Lisa Boston told the jury he was under the influence of drugs at the time, woke to find Glover attacking Ms Morrison, and could not effectively prevent it.

Under cross-examination by Ms Boston, the prisoner who Glover confessed to said Glover made "no mention" of Mr Sorgiovanni initially.

Tara Morrison was stabbed multiple times. (Supplied: Facebook)

She said Glover told her Mr Sorgiovanni had grabbed her in a "bear hug" and tried to drag her away.

'Ongoing struggle'

During closing submissions to the jury, prosecutor Michael Cvetkoski showed a photo of Tara Morrison's left hand, with a serious injury which he described as a defensive wound.

Mr Cvetkoski put it to the jury that Ms Morrison's right hand was being restrained and could not be used as a "defensive mechanism".

Woman admits murder after court told of victim's final moments Hannah Louise Glover pleads guilty to stabbing Tara Morrison to death in Western Australia's South West after a murder trial hears about her prison confessions.

"Likely, this was an ongoing struggle," Mr Cvetkoski told the jury.

The court was shown crime scene photos with blood on the floor and walls of the house.

Mr Sorgiovanni now faces a retrial.

It is not known when Glover will be sentenced.

World.title: Albanese and Bowen caught in hot mic gaffe
World.content:
PoliticsFederalAnthony Albanese Albanese and Bowen caught in hot mic gaffe Natassia Chrysanthos November 13, 2026 — 10:42pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen have been recorded making small talk about phone radiation and “dicks” in a candid moment caught on camera at this year’s global climate conference. The exchange was picked up with a hot mic on Friday as the pair chatted while waiting to start a roundtable discussion about business investment at this year’s COP31 climate conference in the Turkish town of Antalya. The prime minister and Chris Bowen in the moment when the conversation was captured by a TV microphone. Seven News The prime minister’s office brushed off the incident after Channel Seven was first to broadcast the clip on Friday evening (AEDT), having picked up on the conversation during the production process. According to the footage, which started recording before Albanese and Bowen made their official remarks, the prime minister put his phone in his jacket pocket and asked Bowen whether he was right-handed. He then told Bowen that he should store his phone away from his heart because “it can interfere with your rhythm”.



Bowen jokingly asked whether it was because it was “a little bit radioactive?” to which Albanese said yes, “it makes absolute sense”. Related Article Updated

Climate policy ‘She’s entitled to her views’: Albanese defends himself after Thunberg’s ‘snail’ jibe The climate change minister said he was more conscious of putting his phone in his pants pocket. The prime minister asked: “Because of your dick?” Bowen agreed. “Arguably more important than the heart,” he said. A spokesman for the prime minister said: “They were having a joke in between meetings.”



Friday’s event was held to discuss business opportunities with Australian agencies and both current and potential investors in the country’s renewable energy transition. “Trade and investment components of these annual climate meetings are absolutely critical,” Albanese said in his opening remarks. “It’s how we turn the commitments that we want to make into actions and outcomes, and capitalise on the opportunity which is before us.” Anthony Albanese (left) with Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen (right) greeting Andrew “Twiggy” Forrest at COP31. AAP Australia’s involvement in this year’s COP has attracted heightened scrutiny because the federal government is co-hosting the event with Turkey. Bowen has taken on a new role as president of negotiations – a position he secured after Australia lost its bid to host the event in Adelaide. Albanese arrived in Antalya on Wednesday for the conference leaders summit. He left Turkey shortly after Friday’s business roundtable, and will head straight to the Philippines for the ASEAN summit. Bowen will stay in Antalya and lead negotiations between 190 countries until the end of next week.



Hot mic moments involving the Australian prime minister have drawn attention since former prime minister Tony Abbott and then home affairs minister Peter Dutton were caught in 2015 joking about “water lapping” at Pacific islands threatened by rising sea levels. While the pair didn’t know they were being recorded, the comments were damaging to Australia’s reputation in the Pacific. World.title: Microsoft’s attempts to resolve major outage ‘not working as expected’
World.content:
Updated TechnologyNetwork outage Microsoft’s attempts to resolve major outage ‘not working as expected’ Elias Visontay, Jack Gramenz and Emily Kaine Updated November 13, 2026 — 9:01pm ,first published November 13, 2026 — 7:46am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Tech giant Microsoft scrambled for solutions and prioritised restoring government services in Australia during its global outage on Friday, conceding its attempt at a broad fix for users around the world hadn’t worked as expected. The widespread server-related outage – which Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke has insisted is not the result of a cyberattack – hit Microsoft Outlook, Teams and Copilot early on Friday morning in Australia, causing users to have issues accessing or sending emails, while other errors affected the tech giant’s apps. Microsoft users were hit with a widespread outage overnight. AP Nearly 130,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook and other Microsoft services, beginning just before 5am (AEDT). At one point, reports to the platform reached almost 20,000 per minute, stemming from outages across five Microsoft services in 74 countries. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they still couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes.



Related Article Exclusive

Telecommunications ‘Didn’t foot the bill’: Telstra outage cost the economy half a billion dollars, modelling finds By afternoon, Microsoft email access was still patchy, while other Microsoft platforms such as Teams appeared functional – prompting memes on social media from frustrated workers lamenting the split-level of functionality. A swath of corporate Australia and government departments and agencies were among those affected. They included the Australian Federal Police and the ABC. While they were still able to function, email issues also plagued national supermarket chain Coles as well as government agencies in NSW, Victoria, Queensland, Tasmania and Western Australia. Australia Post suspended its phone payment system and suppliers were unable to send delivery notices to supermarket distribution centres. The cost to Australia would be billions of dollars, said Ashwin Pal, of accounting firm RSM Australia.



Related Article Exclusive

Telecommunications ‘Didn’t foot the bill’: Telstra outage cost the economy half a billion dollars, modelling finds “That’s not just direct, but indirect costs as well,” he said. “But a protracted event like this can easily be the straw that breaks the camel’s back for smaller entities.” The Australian Computer Society renewed its call for a national review of sovereign risk in Australian IT. “Australians who couldn’t get paid, couldn’t send an invoice, or couldn’t reach a government service are entitled to be worried,” chief executive Prins Ralston said. “Where were the direct updates to Australian customers and media - and who will answer for the lost productivity and the cost to the economy?”



Such a widespread and prolonged global outage highlighted the dangers of reliance on a very small number of tech firms, University of Melbourne professor Toby Murray said. “And to find ourselves many hours later still in the same position that we were when we got up this morning, it really is surprising,” he said. The US tech company was reported to be focusing on restoring services to government first given its large user base. In a statement on Friday afternoon, Microsoft said: “We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed that change is not taking as expected. “We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances.”



Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services. Loading To fix the issue, Microsoft said it had so far attempted to restart its servers, and validate a change. But initial efforts to fully restore services proved unsuccessful. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the company said. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” An update issued on Friday morning said the company had “observed limited recovery in some regions”, but its efforts for a quick fix proved unsuccessful. Microsoft later said it was implementing “protective traffic management measures” region by region to test if it helped with restoring its services.



“[We are] fully isolating a portion of our service infrastructure, restarting the affected components, and gradually reintroducing traffic to confirm our services remain stable before applying this approach more broadly. “We’re also analysing traffic patterns across our entire service infrastructure and evaluating whether isolating traffic within each region may allow affected regions to recover independently.” At a press conference in Sydney on Friday morning, Burke said he had been briefed by Australia’s cybersecurity coordinator and the head of Microsoft Australia and that they did not believe they were dealing with a cyber threat. “The perspective of Microsoft at this stage … they believe in some ways [similar] to what we saw with CrowdStrike where there is an update that has gone awry,” Burke said. View post on X



Microsoft said it was “also investigating why affected servers are experiencing elevated processor usage while handling requests”. In updates posted earlier, it said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes”. Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load”, which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”. The company determined several servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks. “We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X. The company earlier said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

World.title: Debutant fires Aussies to huge win over England after Warner slams Cummins comments
World.content:
Mahli Beardman has stamped his reputation as the next big thing in Australian cricket by producing a sizzling ODI debut in his team’s crushing seven-wicket victory over England in Perth.

On a day when Australian cricket was still knee-deep dealing with the ghosts of sandpapergate 2018, Beardman snared 6-24 as the tourists were skittled for 131 in 33.4 overs at Optus Stadium.

In reply, Mitch Marsh smashed 50 off 30 balls as Australia reached the victory target with a whopping 159 balls to spare. Matt Renshaw (26 not out) and Josh Inglis (23 not out) finished the job.

The result gave Australia a 1-0 lead in the three-match series before game two in Adelaide on Sunday.

While Marsh provided the fireworks with four sixes and four fours before holing out in the deep, it was Beardman’s performance that will live long in the memories of the 27,313 fans at the stadium on Friday.

Mahli Beardman walks off after a six-wicket haul. Getty Images

The 21-year-old was near unplayable at times, with England collapsing from 2-38 to 7-60 on the back of Beardman’s devastating burst.

It marked just the second time an Australian has produced a five-wicket haul in their ODI debut, following Tony Dodemaide’s 5-21 against Sri Lanka at the WACA Ground in 1988.

Only some late handy runs from Gus Atkinson (29 not out off 32 balls) and Will Jacks (25) ensured England made it to triple figures, with the visitors 8-65 at one stage.

“It all happened very quickly,” Beardman told Fox Cricket when asked about his big haul.

“It’s just a great privilege and honour to be able to represent my country. And to go out and take a few wickets as well is the cherry on top.

“Harry Brook was a nice wicket to get off the mark. Anytime you get your first one it’s a weight off your shoulders, so that was awesome.”

Loading

Beardman, who was handed his ODI cap by Test legend Mike Hussey, received a big cheer from his home town crowd when he was introduced into the attack for the 10th over – a maiden.

The right-arm paceman snared his maiden ODI wicket in his next over when he found the edge of England captain Brook (1).

That was just a taste of things to come.

Hitting speeds of up to 145.4km/h, Beardman was able to entice 200-game milestone man Joe Root (17 off 36 balls) to drive on the up to gift wicketkeeper Josh Inglis his third catch of the innings.

And Beardman was on a hat trick when he collected the scalp of Jordan Cox at the start of his fourth over – again with another pearler of a delivery that caught the edge.

Beardman’s hat-trick ball was anticlimactic – a wide down the leg side.

But while his first three wickets came courtesy of fuller deliveries that featured swing and seam, Beardman’s next wicket proved his pace and bounce is also a major weapon.

Sam Curran’s attempted pull off Beardman’s bouncer gave Adam Zampa a catch on the boundary rope.

Spencer Johnson (3-42) ensured the party continued by jumping high in the air to pull off a one-handed catch off his own bowling to send Jamie Overton packing.

Atkinson and Jofra Archer (11) struck a series of boundaries in a 29-run last-wicket stand before Beardman completed the demolition job by having Archer caught at gully.

Beardman’s figures were the fourth best by a debutant in ODI world cricket, with Charlie Cassell’s effort of 7-21 for Scotland against Oman in 2024 still the best.

Mitch Marsh of Australia and Harry Brook of England at the coin toss in Perth. Getty Images

And Beardman’s five-wicket haul was complete when Liam Dawson was caught at gully, giving the West Australian figures of 5-13 off 4.4 overs at that point.

To mark the special moment, the Australian team formed a circle around Beardman as the rising star raised the ball in the air.

Whether it’s a modern or period home, a standout facade can include features such as textural contrast, visual anchors, dramatic rooflines and architectural lighting, leaving a striking impression and setting the home apart. These Sydney homes not only have great street appeal, but their interiors back it up, making them standouts both inside and out. Here are five of the best Sydney homes with facades we love. 72 Oxford Street, Woollahra NSW



This terrace has a width of 8.2 metres with a striking facade featuring a lacework balcony. Inside, the home is just as impressive, with interiors by Phoebe Nicol featuring oak, natural stone and a textural palette. The open-plan living, dining and kitchen areas feature high ceilings and engineered flooring, opening onto an undercover al fresco with an integrated barbecue and landscaped gardens. With two bedrooms, 2½ bathrooms and basement car parking with an internal lift, there is plenty to enjoy. 92 Balfour Road, Bellevue Hill NSW



Featuring curves, an arched window and contrasting materials, the facade of this home makes a statement. This design continues inside with high ceilings, sculptural curves, skylights and an interplay of oak, glass and Arabescato Corchia marble. Highlights include the central atrium, all-weather al fresco, lower-level media room and considered design features such as brushed gold tapware, rainwater showers, underfloor heating in the bathrooms, an integrated Bose sound system and an AV security intercom with keypad and swipe entry. 207 Bridge Road, Glebe NSW



With a jasmine-framed filigree facade, this Victorian terrace features an iron lacework balcony and plenty of period charm. This continues inside with the timber floors, high ceilings and archways. Modern updates include skylights, glazing and a bistro-style kitchen with a servery bar that connects to a wraparound deck. The home is set over three levels, with an additional attic.



The dual-access block offers double garaging, while the terrace itself is one of a historic row of four. 29 Pacific Parade, Manly NSW This c.1922 bungalow’s tuck-pointed brick facade, high gables and covered north-facing porch with tessellated-tile floors have been beautifully preserved. There are modern updates including the fence and undercover carport. One family has owned the home for 62 years, and it was renovated in 2015.



The home features abundant natural light, a stone-crafted kitchen, a formal lounge with a gas log fireplace, and a rear entertainer’s terrace with a landscaped garden. Only a short walk from Manly Beach, in leafy “Manly Flat”, the location is a definite drawcard. 9 O’Connor Street, Haberfield NSW This Federation home located in the inner west has an elegant facade framed by jacaranda and immaculate landscape gardens, with level lawns and established greenery.



Sitting on a prized 720-square metre corner position on a tree-lined street, the home features ornate ceilings, leadlight windows, original fireplaces and a wraparound verandah. Alongside its period craftsmanship, the four-bedroom, three-bathroom home has had a contemporary extension with a covered al fresco terrace overlooking its gardens and pool. Other features include generous attic storage, ducted reverse-cycle air-conditioning and an elegant lounge with floor to ceiling bookshelves.
